## 0. Source Documents and Provenance

- **Primary source (unrefined stakeholder input):** `specs/QFIELD_PROJECT_BUILDER_REQUIREMENTS_EN.md` ("the Requirements Draft"). This document is treated as raw stakeholder input, not as an approved specification. It has not been modified by this specification.
- **Clarification record:** the requirements-elicitation conversation between the spec-writer and the human stakeholder (three rounds, all dated 2026-08-10), consolidated into the Decision Log (Section 19) and Open Questions (Section 20) below. Every requirement, constraint, and acceptance criterion in this document traces either to the Requirements Draft or to an explicit stakeholder answer recorded in the Decision Log — nothing here is invented.
- Cross-references to the Requirements Draft use the notation `(Req §n)` where `n` is the Requirements Draft's own section number.
- **Implementation-phase reconciliation record:** two explicit, direct stakeholder instructions given during a post-MVP-approval "macOS release checkpoint" implementation phase — not part of the original Requirements Draft or the six pre-implementation clarification rounds (D-1–D-23) — are reconciled into this specification as Decision Log D-24 (the drawing-canvas OpenStreetMap visual-aid exception to the network boundary) and D-25 (deferral of a built Windows package to a subsequent release, while the cross-platform source/packaging-configuration requirement remains unchanged). Per this project's own change-control discipline, an unambiguous, explicit, direct prior stakeholder instruction is treated as approval of that specific product decision; both are layered in as dated amendments, not silent rewrites of the sections they touch.
- **Second reconciliation record (2026-08-14):** three further, independently classified stakeholder items are reconciled into this specification as Decision Log D-26 (VWorld layer-discovery endpoint — Category C, supersedes the layer-list portion of FR-QPB-071), D-27 (Korean survey-type explanations at Step 2 — Category B, closes a specification omission), and D-28 (full Korean localization of this application's own UI — Category C, new NFR). Each is traced to a verbatim stakeholder instruction quoted in its own Decision Log entry and is layered in as a dated amendment; none of D-1–D-25 is reworded, deleted, or renumbered.
- This specification supersedes, for deployment/architecture purposes only, any impression given by `README.md` that this is a browser-based web application. Per the Decision Log this specification records an explicit, stakeholder-made technology decision (Python + PySide6/Qt native desktop app, with a separate PyQGIS worker process and a QGIS 3.44 LTR MVP runtime dependency) for this product. As of this revision, `README.md`, `docs/product.md`, and `docs/architecture.md` have been updated to reflect this decision (Decision Log D-20); this specification remains the authoritative source for the detailed requirements.

## 1. Summary

QField Project Builder is a locally installed, single-user native desktop application (Python + PySide6/Qt, Windows and macOS) that automates the end-to-end creation of a self-contained, QField-ready ecological survey project: selecting a survey type, generating the correct local GeoPackage schema, importing or drawing sites/plots/offline-map extents, generating and configuring a QGIS project (relations, forms, constraints, symbology, attachments, relative paths), configuring an online VWorld basemap or generating a bounded offline MBTiles basemap, and producing a portable project folder for direct transfer to and from a smartphone running QField (iOS or Android). An optional, **post-MVP** subsystem adds Pl@ntNet photo identification, Korean taxon-name resolution (KTSN), and raster-based occurrence-probability lookup. The application removes the need for ecologists to write SQL or hand-configure QGIS/QField project files.

## 2. Product Goals and Non-Goals

### 2.1 Goals

- G-1: Let an ecologist with no database/GIS-configuration background produce a correct, QField-ready local survey project through a guided wizard. (Req §1)
- G-2: Guarantee the generated project is portable as a single folder, copyable directly between a computer and a smartphone, without any cloud service or QFieldSync packaging step. (Req §1, §2.1, §10)
- G-3: Guarantee data integrity in the generated GeoPackage: UUID domain identifiers distinct from the hidden GeoPackage physical key, enforced foreign keys, and QGIS relations that mirror them. (Req §3)
- G-4: Support ecologically meaningful survey structures out of the box: simple inventory, temporary plots, permanent plots, and vegetation mapping. (Req §6)
- G-5 (post-MVP): Assist species identification and Korean-name/accepted-name/occurrence-probability enrichment from field photos, without transmitting survey data to external services. (Req §9, §11)

### 2.2 Non-Goals

- NG-1: This product is not a database server, a multi-user platform, or a hosted web application (Decision Log D-1, D-9).
- NG-2: This product does not replace QFieldSync as a *general* QField packaging tool — QFieldSync is explicitly excluded from the required workflow because of reported GeoPackage relation/key issues (Req §2.2, §10).
- NG-3: This product does not perform ecological analysis, dashboards, or publication-ready reporting (Req §2.2).
- NG-4: This product does not choose an application stack on the implementer's behalf beyond what the stakeholder has explicitly decided (Decision Log D-9) — no further stack decisions are made here.

## 3. Target Users and User Journeys

**Primary user:** ecological field researchers who need to run structured vegetation/species surveys but should not need to write SQL or configure QGIS/QField manually (Req §1).

### User journeys

- **J-1 — Build a new project (desktop, MVP).** The user opens the desktop app, runs the six-step wizard (Section 7), and produces a self-contained project folder without touching a database or `.qgs` XML.
- **J-2 — Field data collection (QField, outside this application's runtime boundary).** The user copies the generated folder to an iOS or Android phone, opens it in QField, collects sites/plots/surveys/observations/community polygons and photos, then copies the complete folder back to the desktop (Req §10).
- **J-3 — Desktop validation after fieldwork (MVP).** The user re-opens the returned project folder on the same or a different computer and confirms it still opens without a missing-layer or repair warning (Req §12.2, §12.5).
- **J-4 — Assisted identification in the field (post-MVP).** After the identification subsystem is enabled and the feasibility spike (Section 13) has confirmed a workable interaction, the user triggers "Identify attached photos" on an observation, reviews top-three Pl@ntNet candidates enriched with KTSN/probability data, and selects or manually overrides the result (Req §9).

## 4. MVP and Post-MVP Boundary

This boundary is a direct transcription of the stakeholder's explicit answer in the Decision Log (D-3, D-13) and must not be re-derived or reinterpreted by any later role.

### 4.1 MVP (required for first acceptance)

- The locally installed native desktop application (Windows + macOS) and its guided wizard UI.
- All four survey types (Section 8).
- GeoPackage generation using UUID domain identifiers, distinct from the hidden GeoPackage `fid` (Section 8.1).
- QGIS `.qgs` project generation (Section 9).
- Database constraints and QGIS relations (Section 9).
- QGIS/QField attribute-form configuration (Section 9).
- Site, plot, and bounding-box input by drawing or spatial-file upload (Section 7.4).
- Online VWorld basemap configuration (Section 10).
- Offline VWorld-sourced MBTiles generation for a selected bbox and zoom range, including the 1 GiB hard limit and pre-generation size estimation (Section 11).
- Relative project paths throughout the generated project (Section 12; Section 14.2, NFR-QPB-020).
- Generation of the self-contained transfer folder (Section 12).
- Project validation and a validation report (Section 12).
- Computer-to-smartphone and smartphone-to-computer whole-folder transfer instructions, for both iOS and Android (Section 12, Decision Log D-11).
- Manual species/taxon name entry as the guaranteed data-entry path for all survey types (Decision Log D-14). Photo attachment is available only where defined in the schema — Types 1–3 (Section 8.1–8.3) — and in every case is optional: zero photos is valid and never blocks an ordinary save, project validation, field completion, or project generation/transfer. Type 4 (`community`) has no photo field, photo table, or photo requirement (Decision Log D-23; see also DR-QPB-050).

### 4.2 Post-MVP / future scope (described here, does not block MVP acceptance)

- Pl@ntNet API integration (Section 13).
- The QField project plugin/sidecar required for in-field identification actions (Section 13).
- Manual "Identify attached photos" action and any automatic/silent attachment-triggered identification (the latter conditional on a feasibility spike passing on **both** iOS and Android) (Section 13, Decision Log D-14).
- KTSN Korean-name and accepted-name enrichment (Section 13.4–13.5).
- Occurrence-probability raster sampling (Section 13.6).
- Offline identification request queue and retry (Section 13.7).
- On-device (smartphone) probability-map packaging (Section 13.8).

Acceptance of the MVP must not be blocked by, or require completion of, any post-MVP item above.

## 5. System Architecture and Boundaries

### 5.1 Deployment model

- FR-QPB-001: The application must be a locally installed, single-user native desktop application implemented in Python using PySide6/Qt. It must not require a remote application server and must not depend on a browser-hosted UI. (Decision Log D-9)
- FR-QPB-002: The application must run and be distributed as first-class, MVP-supported builds on both Microsoft Windows and macOS. (Decision Log D-9)
- FR-QPB-003: All project-generation work — GeoPackage creation, QGIS project generation/configuration, layer/relation setup, QField form configuration, input GIS file validation/import, offline MBTiles generation, and final project-folder assembly — must execute on the user's local computer. (Decision Log D-9, D-10)
- FR-QPB-004: The user must select a local output directory; the application must assemble the generated QGIS project, GeoPackage, attachments, styles, and offline basemap into a self-contained folder at that location. (Req §4 Step 1, Decision Log D-9)
- FR-QPB-005: The application must not require any remote PostgreSQL database, hosted backend, or mandatory cloud storage. (Req §2.2, Decision Log D-9)
- FR-QPB-006: A previously generated project must remain fully usable without the desktop application being connected to the Internet. (Decision Log D-9)
- FR-QPB-131 (new; Decision Log D-81; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — application display name corrected): The application's own display name is ~~**"QFieldKit"**~~ **"FieldBuild Kit"** (name corrected by Decision Log D-86; originally decided as "QFieldKit" per Decision Log D-81), superseding "QField Project Builder" as the name shown in this application's own UI (window titles and any other user-visible product-name string), `README.md`, and the PyInstaller packaging configuration's own bundle name (`packaging/*.spec`). Locating and updating every remaining literal occurrence of the prior name across this codebase — beyond the credential-storage directory name this decision's own consequential side effect already addresses explicitly (NFR-QPB-018 (further revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (further revised)/NFR-QPB-081, Section 14.1) — is `test-designer`/`implementer` discovery work; this requirement does not itemize every file-by-file occurrence. This specification's own document title and prose are not renamed by this entry (mirroring NFR-QPB-070's own carve-out that this specification's prose is a distinct artifact from the shipped application's own UI strings); a separate, later administrative decision would be required to rename the specification document itself.
- FR-QPB-132 (new; Decision Log D-82; example text corrected, Decision Log D-86): The application must display its own currently running version (the existing `qfield_builder.__version__` constant, `qfield_builder/__init__.py`) somewhere visible in the desktop wizard UI, without requiring the user to inspect a file or run a command to discover it. **Proposed default location, per the orchestrator's own proposal, not yet contested by the stakeholder:** the wizard's own window title, e.g. ~~"QFieldKit v0.1.0"~~ **"FieldBuild Kit v0.1.0" (corrected by Decision Log D-86)** once FR-QPB-131 (further revised, Decision Log D-86)'s rename lands. The exact placement/format is not dictated character-for-character by this requirement and is left to implementer discretion if a different, equally visible placement (e.g. an About dialog) is judged more consistent with this document's existing UI-detail conventions — mirroring Decision Log D-27's own precedent that exact UI copy/placement is implementer-authored detail unless the stakeholder has specifically dictated it.

### 5.2 QGIS/GDAL runtime dependency

- FR-QPB-007: For the MVP, the application must require a compatible QGIS Desktop installation on the user's computer. The MVP target is the **QGIS 3.44 LTR series**, using the latest available patch release in that series from the official QGIS distribution, on both Windows and macOS. The application installer is not required to bundle the QGIS runtime in the first release. QGIS 4.2 (or any later 4.x release) is explicitly **not** an MVP requirement; migration to a 4.x LTR is a post-MVP decision to be reassessed once QGIS publishes a supported 4.x LTR and generated projects have been validated on QField for both iOS and Android. (Decision Log D-19; closes the product-level "which QGIS series" question, formerly Open Question O-6.)
- FR-QPB-007a: PyQGIS must not be installed separately (e.g., via `pip`); it must be supplied by, and used from, the detected QGIS Desktop installation's own Python/PyQGIS environment. (Decision Log D-19)
- FR-QPB-008: The application must attempt automatic detection of a supported QGIS installation, and must allow the user to select the QGIS installation path manually when automatic detection fails. (Decision Log D-10)
- FR-QPB-009: The application must verify the QGIS, PyQGIS, GDAL, and required data-provider environment before starting project generation, and must show a clear, non-technical error message when the required runtime is missing or incompatible. (Decision Log D-10)
- NFR-QPB-001: The product-level choice of QGIS series is resolved (QGIS 3.44 LTR; FR-QPB-007). The exact tested patch version, Windows versions, macOS versions, GDAL version, and QField (iOS/Android) versions remain an implementation prerequisite and release-gate compatibility matrix, tracked as Open Question O-9 — these specific version numbers must not be invented by this specification or by any later role without verification. (Req §14, §15.6; Decision Log D-6, D-10, D-19)

### 5.3 Process separation

- FR-QPB-010: The application must not assume the PySide6 UI and the QGIS Python environment can safely share one process, because the UI and QGIS runtime may use different Qt Python bindings and versions. The process model is: (1) the main UI runs independently using Python and PySide6; (2) the application detects the supported QGIS Desktop installation; (3) it launches a separate local GIS worker process using the Python/PyQGIS environment supplied by that QGIS installation; (4) the GIS worker initializes `QgsApplication` without a QGIS GUI and performs all QGIS/PyQGIS/GDAL project-generation operations; (5) results, progress, warnings, and errors are returned to the PySide6 UI through the still-unresolved IPC mechanism (Open Question O-1). No data may be sent to a remote worker or server. (Decision Log D-11, D-19)
- A-QPB-001 (assumption): The exact inter-process communication mechanism between the UI process and the GIS worker process is an implementation decision not fixed by this specification, per explicit stakeholder direction. (Decision Log D-11)

### 5.4 External integrations and network boundary

- FR-QPB-011 (further revised; Decision Log D-65; adds clause (d); further revised, Decision Log D-76, extending clause (d) with a second, independently scoped permission): The only network requests the MVP application may make are: (a) VWorld online basemap tile requests when online mode is selected; (b) VWorld tile downloads when generating an offline MBTiles basemap; (c) OpenStreetMap (OSM) XYZ raster tile requests, strictly and only as an ephemeral visual aid rendered behind the wizard's interactive site/plot/bbox drawing canvas (Section 6.3, FR-QPB-025's "or drawing features on an interactive map" clause) — clause (c) is a narrow, UI-only carve-out: OSM tiles are fetched only for on-screen display while the user is actively drawing; fetched tile imagery is never written into, or referenced by, the generated project output (no `.mbtiles` file, no `.qgs` reference, nothing persisted by a build); and OSM is **not** an approved basemap source for the project's actual online (Section 10) or offline (Section 11) basemap-generation pipeline, both of which remain VWorld-only and are entirely unaffected by this exception — clause (c) must never be read as authorizing OSM as an alternative or substitute basemap provider anywhere outside the drawing-canvas visual aid; and **(d) (new; Decision Log D-65) fetching a single, specifically selected Tabler icon's SVG file from Tabler's public icon source (`github.com/tabler/tabler-icons`), strictly and only when the user has already selected that icon by name from an offline, build-time-bundled static icon-name index in the wizard's Step 6 symbol-styling configuration (FR-QPB-121, revised; FR-QPB-123, new) — ~~this clause never authorizes any live search/autocomplete network request against any Tabler endpoint; searching the bundled icon-name index is always offline~~ **(superseded, not deleted, by Decision Log D-76, for the narrow case immediately below only: the client-side name-filtering/search mechanism FR-QPB-121 describes remains entirely offline and unchanged; what changes is that a *separate, additional* live preview-image fetch is now also permitted during search, scoped precisely as follows)** — **and (d)(ii) (new; Decision Log D-76): fetching preview SVG content, live, for the currently visible/matched results of an in-progress search** — i.e., only for icon names actually returned by the user's current search query and currently rendered on screen in the Step 6 results list, debounced as the user types (see NFR-QPB-080, further revised, below for the operational safeguards this requires) — **strictly never an unbounded background prefetch of the full, ~5,130-name bundled index, and never fetched for a result that is not currently visible on screen.** This is an *additional*, narrower permission for showing an image preview alongside each visible search result; it does **not** replace, alter, or duplicate the separate, already-approved final SVG fetch-on-selection mechanism the first sentence of clause (d) above describes, which remains completely unchanged: a user's final icon selection still triggers its own single fetch exactly as FR-QPB-121 already requires, regardless of whether a preview for that icon was already fetched during search.** No other network access is permitted in the MVP — clauses (a)–(d) above are exhaustive (clause (d) now has two internal fetch triggers, (d)(i) fetch-on-selection and (d)(ii) fetch-during-search-preview, but remains one lettered clause of the same exhaustive list). (Req §2.3; OSM carve-out per Decision Log D-24; Tabler carve-out per Decision Log D-65; live search-preview-fetch carve-out per Decision Log D-76) ~~**Cross-reference (new, Decision Log D-61 — draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved):** a proposed new network destination (Tabler SVG icon search/download for point-symbol configuration, draft FR-QPB-121) is under consideration and is explicitly **not** yet an approved exception to this requirement's "No other network access is permitted" rule — see Open Question O-24 and draft NFR-QPB-080 below. This requirement's own approved clauses (a)/(b)/(c) above, and its "no other network access" closing sentence, are unchanged by that proposal; no clause (d) is added until O-24 is resolved.~~ **(superseded, not deleted, by this entry: O-24 is resolved, Decision Log D-65, and clause (d) above is that resolution.)**
  - Clarification (Decision Log D-26): the single VWorld capabilities-metadata request required by revised FR-QPB-071 (Section 10) — a request to the same VWorld host already referenced by clauses (a)/(b), made to discover the currently advertised layer set rather than to fetch a map tile — falls within this existing VWorld network allowance. It is not a fourth permitted network destination or purpose; it is the same provider, serving the same basemap-configuration function as (a)/(b). This clarification does not change clauses (a), (b), or (c), or the "no other network access" closing sentence, in any other respect.
- FR-QPB-012: Post-MVP, the only additional network requests permitted are Pl@ntNet identification requests, explicitly disclosed to the user (Section 13; Req §2.3).
- FR-QPB-013: The UI must clearly disclose, before any network request that transmits user photos, that those photos are sent to an external service (Pl@ntNet), post-MVP only (Req §2.3).
- NFR-QPB-060 (new; Decision Log D-24): For the drawing-canvas OSM visual aid permitted by FR-QPB-011(c): (1) every OSM tile request must carry a compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header (never a generic/default HTTP client string); (2) at most one fetch attempt may be made per tile per application session — a tile that fails to fetch (network error, non-200 response, timeout, or empty response body) must not be retried automatically within that session (cache-or-fail-once; no retry storms); (3) a permanently visible "© OpenStreetMap contributors" attribution label (the ODbL-required attribution) must be shown whenever OSM tiles are the active canvas background; and (4) the canvas's drawing/geometry-producing functionality (polygon, point, and bbox capture per FR-QPB-025/FR-QPB-080) must remain fully correct and usable with zero network access, falling back to a plain coordinate graticule for any tile that has not yet loaded or has failed to fetch.
- NFR-QPB-080 (revised; Decision Log D-65; confirmed, no longer provisional; further revised, Decision Log D-76, adding new clauses (5)–(8) for the live search-preview-fetch permission added to FR-QPB-011(d)(ii)): All rules from NFR-QPB-080 (Decision Log D-61) above remain correct in kind, restated here as confirmed rather than provisional, with clause (3) removed: (1) the single SVG-fetch request permitted by FR-QPB-011(d) must carry a compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header; (2) that request must not retry automatically in an unbounded loop on failure — one attempt per user selection, surfaced as a clear, non-blocking failure to the user on error (FR-QPB-121, revised); ~~(3) a permanently visible attribution/license notice for the Tabler Icons project must be shown wherever a downloaded Tabler icon is actually used as a symbol, matching whatever attribution Tabler's own current license terms require (Open Question O-24(b))~~ — **removed, not merely struck (Decision Log D-65): Tabler Icons is confirmed MIT-licensed; no attribution/license notice is legally required anywhere in the generated project or this application's own UI for a used Tabler icon, and none is required by this specification.** (4) the minimalist default styling (FR-QPB-120) must remain fully available and usable with zero network access at all times, regardless of whether the Tabler feature is reachable. **New (Decision Log D-76), directly mirroring NFR-QPB-060's own OSM-carve-out safeguards — this specification's own established structural template for every network-boundary carve-out it has ever granted:** (5) every live search-preview-fetch request permitted by FR-QPB-011(d)(ii) must carry the same compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header clause (1) above already requires of the selection-fetch request — this extends, rather than invents anew, the identical existing discipline to this second fetch trigger; (6) preview fetches must be debounced as the user types — a fetch must not be issued on every keystroke, only after the user's input has briefly settled (the exact debounce interval is an implementation detail, not dictated here, mirroring this specification's existing convention of leaving exact UI-timing mechanics to the implementer, e.g. Decision Log D-27/D-75); (7) concurrency for in-flight preview fetches must be bounded to a small, reasonable number at any one time — never one unbounded, simultaneous request fired per every currently visible result at once; and (8) — critically — search itself, and the ability to select an icon by name, must remain fully functional with zero network access at all times, mirroring NFR-QPB-060(4)'s and this requirement's own existing clause (4)'s identical offline-fallback discipline: a preview fetch that fails (no network, non-200 response, timeout, empty body) or has not yet completed must simply result in that one result showing no image (or a name-only/placeholder row), never blocking search, never blocking selection, and never crashing the application; the offline, build-time-bundled name index and its client-side substring/prefix filtering (FR-QPB-121) remain entirely unaffected and continue to require no network access of their own.
- NFR-QPB-002: No survey database records (attribute data, geometries, relations) may be transmitted to any external API, in MVP or post-MVP (Req §2.3, §11).

### 5.5 Packaging

- FR-QPB-014 (revised; Decision Log D-25): For this MVP release, the application must be delivered as a macOS `.app` distributed via an appropriate installer or disk image; macOS is the first platform packaged and delivered. A Windows installer or packaged executable is a **required subsequent-release task**, explicitly deferred by direct stakeholder instruction — not descoped and not indefinitely postponed — and must be producible from the same, already cross-platform-clean source and packaging configuration described in NFR-QPB-030 (revised), without requiring a rewrite of either. Code signing, macOS notarization, and Windows signing are release-plan concerns and do not need to be fully designed in this specification. (Decision Log D-9, D-25)

## 6. Functional Requirements — Shared Project-Building Workflow (Req §4)

~~The wizard must present the following six steps in order, matching the Requirements Draft.~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-65, 2026-08-26, closes O-27): the wizard now presents the following seven steps in order.** Steps 1–5 (Sections 6.1–6.5) and Step 7 (Section 6.7, "Review and build") trace to the Requirements Draft exactly as before, unchanged in substance; the new Step 6 (Section 6.6, "Symbol styling configuration") does not, and is a purely additive insertion — Step 7's own requirement content (FR-QPB-040/FR-QPB-041) is unaffected by this insertion, only its position/number.

### 6.1 Step 1 — Project basics (Req §4 Step 1)

- FR-QPB-020: The wizard must collect: a Unicode `project_display_name` (free-form, user-facing project name), output directory, optional project description, project CRS (defaulting to EPSG:5186), and storage CRS for survey GeoPackage geometry layers (defaulting to EPSG:4326).
- FR-QPB-021 (revised; closes former Open Question O-2; Decision Log D-22): The application must derive a filesystem-safe `project_slug` from `project_display_name`, kept as a separate value from the Unicode display name. `project_slug` must contain only ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores; must not exceed 64 characters; and must never be blank. Slug derivation/validation must reject: blank input, path-traversal components (e.g. `..`, `/`, `\`) and separators generally, and Windows-reserved filenames (e.g. `CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`–`COM9`, `LPT1`–`LPT9`) — none of these may be produced as, or accepted as, the slug.
- FR-QPB-021a (new; Decision Log D-22): Every generated project must carry an internal `project_id` (UUID v4) that is independent of, and never derived from, `project_display_name` or `project_slug`.
- FR-QPB-022: The UI must show the final folder and file names, derived from `project_slug`, that will be created, before creation begins.
- FR-QPB-022a (new; Decision Log D-22): An existing project output folder must never be silently overwritten (this restates and cross-references E-QPB-008).
- ~~A-QPB-002~~: **Removed.** The project-naming/sanitization rules are no longer an open implementation assumption; see FR-QPB-020–FR-QPB-022a and Decision Log D-22.

### 6.2 Step 2 — Survey type selection (Req §4 Step 2)

- FR-QPB-023: The wizard must require the user to select exactly one of: (1) Simple species inventory, (2) Temporary plots at defined sites, (3) Permanent plots at defined sites, or (4) Vegetation mapping.
- FR-QPB-024 (revised; Decision Log D-23): The selected survey type must determine the generated GeoPackage schema, relations, editable layers, form layout, photo configuration (which optional photo tables/fields, if any, exist for that survey type), and symbology, per Section 8. No survey type's photo configuration is a mandatory-photo rule; see Section 8 for which optional photo relations exist per type.
- FR-QPB-024a (new; Decision Log D-27; closes a specification omission, not a reversal of FR-QPB-023/024): At the survey-type-selection step (Step 2), and before the user makes a selection, the wizard must display a brief Korean-language explanation for each of the four survey types — (1) Simple species inventory, (2) Temporary plots at defined sites, (3) Permanent plots at defined sites, and (4) Vegetation mapping. Each explanation must describe, specifically for that survey type, how survey information is collected, structured, and recorded — i.e. it must be substantively differentiating content grounded in that type's actual schema (Section 8: Type 1's relation-free point inventory per Section 8.1; Type 2's site→survey→observation temporary-plot structure per Section 8.2; Type 3's site→plot→survey→observation permanent-plot structure per Section 8.3; Type 4's site→survey→community polygon-mapping structure per Section 8.4) — not generic or interchangeable filler that could describe more than one type equally well. The exact displayed Korean wording is not specified by this requirement; it is an implementation-authored, domain-facing detail to be reviewed once built (see this specification's completion note to the user).

### 6.3 Step 3 — Site and plot input (Req §4 Step 3)

- FR-QPB-025: When applicable to the selected survey type, the wizard must allow either: upload of a GeoPackage layer, upload of a zipped Shapefile (containing at minimum `.shp`, `.shx`, `.dbf`, and preferably `.prj`), or drawing features on an interactive map.
- FR-QPB-026: Site data must be validated as Polygon or MultiPolygon; permanent-plot data must be validated as Point.
- FR-QPB-027: The input CRS must be detected or explicitly supplied by the user.
- FR-QPB-028: Invalid geometry must be reported to the user and must be repaired only with explicit user approval.
- FR-QPB-029: Imported geometry must be transformed to the configured storage CRS.
- FR-QPB-030: The user must map source attributes to required fields (e.g., `site_name`, and `plot_size` where applicable).
- FR-QPB-031: Imported values must be previewed before being written to the generated project.
- FR-QPB-032: Project creation must be atomic: invalid input must never leave a partially generated project on disk (see also E-QPB-009, NFR-QPB-010).
- FR-QPB-033: For temporary-plot projects, an uploaded plot-point layer may be used as a set of proposed survey locations; each point becomes a seed survey record whose date and surveyor fields remain empty until field collection.
- FR-QPB-129 (new; Decision Log D-75; further revised, Decision Log D-79, extending scope to Type 4; Category C, stakeholder-directed workflow/UX change — does not alter `site`'s own geometry column, DR-QPB-008, which stays a single Polygon/MultiPolygon column): ~~For Type 2 and Type 3 (the survey types whose `site` layer this page collects seed locations for)~~ **For Type 2, Type 3, and Type 4 (Decision Log D-79: every survey type whose `site` layer this page collects seed locations for — originally Type 2/3 only per the struck-through text immediately preceding, extended to Type 4 by explicit stakeholder confirmation)**, the drawing alternative in FR-QPB-025 must support drawing **multiple, separate polygons in one drawing session**, with each finished polygon individually, manually named by the user — never merged into one `site` record with a multi-part `MultiPolygon` geometry, and never sharing one single name applied to all of them. Concretely: (1) the drawing canvas (`qfield_builder/ui/map_canvas.py`'s `MapCanvas`) must let the user finish one polygon, then either start drawing a new, separate polygon (preserving every previously finished polygon and its assigned name) or end the drawing session entirely; (2) `SiteInputPage` (`qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py`) must let the user assign or confirm a distinct name for each individual finished polygon, defaulting to a non-blank, per-polygon fallback name (mirroring the existing single-shape default, "그려진 사이트") when left blank — no uniqueness constraint across these names is required, mirroring the existing upload-path precedent (`_resolve_sites_from_upload`'s own "가져온 사이트" fallback, already applied to every unnamed uploaded feature without deduplication); (3) the wizard's config-collection step must build `config["sites"]` as a list containing one `{"site_name", "geom_wkt"}` entry per named, finished polygon — reusing the exact, already-existing list contract `qfield_builder/build.py`'s `_resolve_seed_sites()`/`_resolve_sites_from_upload()` already implement for the upload path, requiring **no** change to `qfield_builder/build.py` itself; (4) zero, one, or many named polygons are all valid outcomes of one drawing session, mirroring `SiteInputPage.validatePage()`'s existing "drawing is optional" behavior, unchanged by this requirement. The exact UI mechanics for "finish this polygon and start a new one" versus "finish drawing entirely" (e.g. button labels/placement) are not dictated by this requirement and are left to the implementer, mirroring Decision Log D-27's own precedent for implementation-authored UI copy. ~~This requirement's scope is Types 2 and 3 only, per the stakeholder's own instruction; whether it also extends to Type 4's site-input step (which reaches this identical `SiteInputPage`/`MapCanvas` mechanism but was not named by the stakeholder) is not decided here — see Open Question O-38.~~ **(superseded, not deleted, by Decision Log D-79): the stakeholder has since explicitly confirmed, verbatim, "Yes apply to Type 4 as well" — this requirement's scope is now Types 2, 3, and 4, per Decision Log D-79; Open Question O-38 is CLOSED.**

### 6.4 Step 4 — Connectivity and basemap mode (Req §4 Step 4)

- FR-QPB-034: The wizard must ask the user, as a self-reported choice, whether the field site has sufficient connectivity for an online map.
- FR-QPB-035: Online mode must configure a VWorld WMTS/XYZ layer using the user-supplied API key (Section 10).
- FR-QPB-036: Offline mode must require a bounded area and generate a local MBTiles basemap for that area (Section 11).

### 6.5 Step 5 — Optional photo identification toggle (Req §4 Step 5; MVP behavior only)

- FR-QPB-037: The wizard must ask whether photo-based plant identification is desired for this project.
- ~~FR-QPB-038 (original): For the MVP, if the user declines (or since the subsystem is post-MVP, by default), the application must not request a Pl@ntNet API key and must not add any identification runtime component.~~ **Superseded, not deleted — “any identification runtime component” was ambiguous once the shared sidecar also became the unconditional home of the identification-independent HTML-report feature; see FR-QPB-038 (revised; Decision Log D-87) immediately below.**
- FR-QPB-038 (revised; Decision Log D-87): For the MVP, if the user declines photo identification (or since the subsystem is post-MVP, by default), the application must not request a Pl@ntNet API key and must not add or activate **identification-specific** runtime content. In particular, the "Identify attached photos" reminder button and the identification write-back polling `Timer` must appear inside `<project_slug>.qml` only when `identification_enabled = true`. This does not suppress the sidecar itself or its identification-independent Export HTML Report button/report mechanism: those are present in every generated project, with no wizard/config on/off field, per FR-QPB-090/FR-QPB-133 and Decision Log D-87.
- FR-QPB-039 (post-MVP): If the user opts in once the identification subsystem exists, the application must request a Pl@ntNet API key, validate it without logging it, and enable the workflow in Section 13. (Decision Log D-45: the concrete key-collection step, its secret-masking/no-logging treatment, and the separate, further embedding-consent flow this key collection may lead to are now stated explicitly as new FR-QPB-117 and new FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-116, Section 13.1a; this entry's own general statement is unchanged in substance and remains accurate.)
- FR-QPB-138 (new; Decision Log D-95; independent of `identification_enabled`): For a Type 1–3 project, Step 5 must resolve the canonical taxonomy workbook before the build review can be completed. The wizard must freshly search `storage/reference/tables/` for `.xlsx` candidates, including `Rpt_2026-08-29_List.xlsx` when present, and show each candidate's filename plus a bounded sample of parsed data rows and the detected sheet/header layout. The user must explicitly confirm one candidate. If no candidate is suitable, or the user reports that the preview does not match the intended source, the wizard must provide a manual `.xlsx` upload path and show the same preview/validation result before confirmation. Candidate selection is not a secret/credential flow and must not be coupled to the Pl@ntNet key toggle. The final review must identify the confirmed source filename, source kind (repository candidate or user upload), and validation status. Type 4 does not require a taxonomy reference for its existing schema, but if the always-present HTML report is requested by the generated project, it must report that no observation taxonomy aggregation is applicable rather than inventing one.
- E-QPB-001: Until the post-MVP subsystem is implemented, the wizard must present this step honestly (e.g., "coming in a future release") rather than implying a working feature that does not yet exist.

### 6.6 Step 6 — Symbol styling configuration (Req n/a; new; Decision Log D-65, closes O-27)

- FR-QPB-123: See Section 9 for this step's own requirement text (FR-QPB-123, cross-referencing FR-QPB-120/FR-QPB-121). At this step, for the survey type already selected at Step 2 (FR-QPB-023), the wizard must let the user accept the minimalist default point/polygon styling (FR-QPB-120) with no further action, or search for and select one Tabler SVG icon (FR-QPB-121) to replace the default point-marker symbol for every point layer of the project being generated. This step is inserted between Step 5 (Section 6.5) and the renumbered Step 7 (Section 6.7, immediately below).

### 6.7 Step 7 — Review and build (Req §4 Step 6; renumbered from Step 6 to Step 7 by Decision Log D-65/O-27 to accommodate the new Step 6 above; FR-QPB-040/FR-QPB-041's own substance is unaffected by this renumbering)

- FR-QPB-040: The final review screen must show: selected survey type; schema summary; number of imported sites/plots; basemap mode; offline extent, zoom/resolution, and estimated size where applicable; whether the post-MVP identification subsystem is enabled; output folder; and warnings about embedded VWorld credentials and smartphone folder transfer.
- FR-QPB-041: The build must run as an observable job with progress reporting, cancellation, rollback on failure or cancellation, and a final validation report (Section 12).

## 7. Data Requirements — Common GeoPackage and UUID Rules (Req §3, §5)

- DR-QPB-001: Every domain entity's user-facing and relational identifier must be a UUID v4 — never a sequence or user-visible autoincrementing number.
- DR-QPB-002: Each GeoPackage table may contain a hidden physical key such as `fid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` where required by the GeoPackage/QGIS standard. `fid` must never be displayed to the user, copied into business exports as the domain identifier, or used by any domain relation.
- DR-QPB-003: Every domain table must contain a UUID field (e.g., `site_id`, `plot_id`, `survey_id`, `observation_id`, `community_id`) that is `TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, holding a canonical lowercase UUID with hyphens and without braces.
- DR-QPB-004: All application-generated records must receive a UUID v4.
- DR-QPB-005: In QGIS forms, the UUID field must use the UUID Generator widget or the default expression `uuid('WithoutBraces')`, must be read-only, and should normally be hidden.
- DR-QPB-006: Every foreign key must reference a UUID field, never `fid`. Both a database-level foreign-key constraint and a matching QGIS project relation must exist for each such reference.
- DR-QPB-007: Database format: one local `.gpkg` file per generated project; no remote database connection strings may ever be generated.
- DR-QPB-008: Default geometry storage CRS is EPSG:4326. Site and community layers use `MULTIPOLYGON`; plot/inventory layers use `POINT`.
- DR-QPB-009: Spatial indexes must exist on every geometry column. Ordinary indexes must exist on all UUID foreign-key columns and commonly searched name fields.
- DR-QPB-010: UUID foreign keys must use `ON UPDATE CASCADE`. Composition-owned child records must use `ON DELETE CASCADE` unless a later domain decision requires restrictive deletion. `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` must be used where the storage engine supports it.
- DR-QPB-011: Every application-managed SQLite connection must execute `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`. `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` must return no rows before project delivery.
- DR-QPB-012: Photo files must never be stored as database BLOBs; only paths relative to the project folder may be stored. Absolute paths must never be written into the GeoPackage or QGIS project.
- DR-QPB-013: Date fields use ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; timestamps, where present, use ISO 8601 with timezone. Required text fields must be trimmed and must reject empty strings.
- DR-QPB-014: Each generated database must include schema-version metadata (survey type, schema version identifier, creation timestamp) so that future schema migrations — in particular, enabling the post-MVP identification subsystem — can be managed explicitly rather than by ad hoc inspection. (Decision Log D-12) The exact storage mechanism (dedicated metadata table vs. GeoPackage extension metadata) is left to the implementer as a low-risk, reversible choice.
- DR-QPB-015: Users must never be required to regenerate or manually restructure an existing project merely to enable the later, optional Pl@ntNet identification feature. (Decision Log D-12)
- DR-QPB-079 (new; Decision Log D-95; canonical taxonomy-reference schema): The canonical source is materialized in the generated project's GeoPackage as the non-spatial `ktsn_taxonomy_reference` attributes table. Its logical columns, in this order, are: `ktsn` (TEXT, required, unique), `source_no` (TEXT, source `No`, preserving numeric values as strings and synonym `-`), `taxon_status` (TEXT, source `정이명여부`, exactly `정명` or `이명`), `korean_name` (TEXT nullable, source `대표국명`, display alias `국명`), `scientific_name` (TEXT required, source `학명`, the exact original cell value), `scientific_name_normalized` (TEXT required, whitespace/parenthesis-normalized comparison form), `scientific_name_without_authority` (TEXT required, Pl@ntNet comparison key), `authority` (TEXT nullable/empty when absent), `naming_year` (TEXT nullable, source `명명년도`), `phylum_scientific_name`, `phylum_korean_name`, `class_scientific_name`, `class_korean_name`, `order_scientific_name`, `order_korean_name`, `family_scientific_name`, `family_korean_name`, `genus_scientific_name`, `genus_korean_name` (all nullable, from the corresponding `Phylum`, `Class`, `Order`, `Family`, and `Genus` `Name`/`국명` subcolumns), `accepted_ktsn` (TEXT required), `source_url` (TEXT required, original `URL`), `content_available` (TEXT/boolean normalized from `콘텐츠 여부`), and `source_row` (INTEGER, 1-based workbook row). The two-row header is metadata, not a data record; data starts at workbook row 3. All source rows are retained, in source order. For a `정명` row, `accepted_ktsn = ktsn`; each following `이명` row belongs to the most recent preceding `정명` row and retains its own KTSN and raw name while pointing `accepted_ktsn` to that accepted row. A synonym may not be promoted or selected as a second accepted record. Blank hierarchy cells remain NULL; they are not copied from another row during ingestion.
- DR-QPB-080 (new; Decision Log D-95; compatibility projection and indexing): The existing `ktsn_accepted_name_lookup` table remains in new projects for the current `ValueRelation` contract. It is an accepted-only projection of `ktsn_taxonomy_reference` (`taxon_status = '정명'`) with the existing physical columns `fid`, `ktsn`, `taxon_kor_nm`, and `taxon_full_nm`; `taxon_kor_nm` is sourced from `korean_name`, and `taxon_full_nm` is sourced from the preserved raw `scientific_name`. It must not be a second source of truth. `ktsn_taxonomy_reference` must be indexed on `ktsn`, `accepted_ktsn`, and `scientific_name_without_authority`; the compatibility table keeps its existing KTSN/name indexes. Neither table is a survey domain entity and neither participates in a `QgsRelation` or foreign-key write-back relation.
- DR-QPB-081 (new; Decision Log D-95; reference-layer contract): The QGIS `Reference` group must contain a read-only, non-identifiable table layer named `ktsn_taxonomy_reference`, displayed to users as `식물 분류 참조표`, and the existing accepted-only layer `ktsn_accepted_name_lookup`, displayed as `인정 국명 조회표`. The new layer exposes the canonical logical fields above with Korean aliases (`KTSN`, `원본 No`, `정/이명`, `국명`, `원문 학명`, `학명(명명자 제거)`, `명명자`, `명명년도`, and rank-specific `문/강/목/과/속` aliases). It is a lookup/reference layer, not an editable observation layer; no domain UUID or `fid` is exposed as a user identifier.
- DR-QPB-071 (new; Decision Log D-56 — **draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved**): Extending DR-QPB-005's existing "should normally be hidden" rule for UUID fields, every field on every layer of every generated project must carry a Korean-language display alias, set via QGIS's field-alias mechanism, **except** a UUID field in its primary-key role (`col.is_uuid_pk` in `qfield_builder/schemas.py`; configured `Hidden`/read-only by `_configure_widget_for_column` in `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py` per DR-QPB-005/FR-QPB-057) — a Korean label for a field a surveyor never sees in the form would be meaningless. A UUID field in its foreign-key role (`_fk_uuid_col`), which is not hidden and remains visible as a `RelationReference` picker widget (FR-QPB-057/DR-QPB-006/AC-QPB-013), is explicitly **in scope** and must receive a Korean alias like any other visible field. The hidden GeoPackage physical key `fid` (DR-QPB-002) is likewise out of scope: ~~it is never modeled as a `ColumnDef` in `qfield_builder/schemas.py` and is already excluded from the attribute-editor form tree entirely (see the `_build_drag_and_drop_form` comment in `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`), so no alias applies to it.~~ **(corrected by Decision Log D-59, 2026-08-26 — the struck-through clause above incorrectly implied `fid` is also absent from a layer's own field collection, the same way geometry columns are above; it is not.)** `fid` is not modeled as a `ColumnDef` in this codebase's own Python schema classes (`qfield_builder/schemas.py`) — that part of the original clause remains true — but it **is** a genuine member of a real generated layer's `layer.fields()`: every generated GeoPackage table is created with an explicit `"fid" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` physical column (per the OGC GeoPackage specification's own required named integer primary key), which OGR/QGIS's GeoPackage driver exposes as an ordinary attribute field, unlike a Shapefile's synthetic, non-attribute FID. `fid` receives no Korean alias not because it is absent from `layer.fields()`, but because it is a non-domain physical key that this section's alias proposal simply does not assign one to, and because it is separately excluded from the *visible* attribute-editor form tree by the pre-existing, unrelated `_build_drag_and_drop_form` mechanism (`qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`), which actively clears QGIS's default flat field list — which already includes `fid` — and rebuilds it without an `fid` entry. See Decision Log D-59 for the full correction record. The specific proposed Korean alias for each in-scope field is recorded, per survey type and table, in new Section 8.5 — a draft proposal pending the stakeholder's own domain-expert review and correction, not an approved translation.
- DR-QPB-072 (new; Decision Log D-66; closes part of Open Question O-32): For every generated project of Types 1–3, a real, queryable, indexed database table — the "KTSN accepted-name lookup table" — containing at minimum the Korean name, scientific name, and KTSN identifier of every currently accepted (non-synonym) taxon (row-derivation rule stated by FR-QPB-126) must be bundled as an additional non-spatial table inside the generated project's own existing survey `.gpkg` file — **not** a second `.gpkg` file, preserving DR-QPB-007's "one local `.gpkg` file per generated project" rule. This table must be loaded into the generated project's `.qgs` file as the first layer to actually populate the pre-existing, previously-always-empty "Reference" layer-tree group (FR-QPB-055), configured non-identifiable and read-only where appropriate, per FR-QPB-059's existing "Reference/extent layers" convention. **Indexing (closes O-32):** a real, build-time `CREATE INDEX` statement must exist on this table's own Korean-name and scientific-name columns, mirroring DR-QPB-009's existing "ordinary indexes must exist on... commonly searched name fields" convention — not the in-memory JavaScript index technique (`nameIndex`/`ktsnIndex`) this codebase already uses for the Pl@ntNet identification widget, which is unrelated to this table. This table is reference/lookup data, not a domain survey entity in DR-QPB-001's sense; its own key column is the source data's own natural `ktsn` identifier, not a newly generated UUID, and DR-QPB-001's UUID-identifier rule does not apply to it. Scope: Types 1–3 only; the Type 4 `community` layer is explicitly unaffected (DR-QPB-050's existing exclusion is confirmed unchanged, Decision Log D-66/O-29).
- DR-QPB-078 (new; Decision Log D-80; ~~**general capability confirmed by the stakeholder; the specific proposed layer names in Section 8.7 remain a draft, not yet stakeholder-approved**~~ — **confirmed by Decision Log D-84: Section 8.7's proposed domain-layer names (with one correction, `site` → 조사지) and the KTSN-lookup-layer bonus-row name are now stakeholder-confirmed; `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against this requirement and Section 8.7's confirmed names**): Extending DR-QPB-071's Korean-alias discipline to a layer's own identity rather than its individual fields, every generated domain survey-data layer — i.e. every layer created from a `TableDef` in `qfield_builder/schemas.py`, across all four survey types — must receive a Korean-language display name, set via `QgsMapLayer.setName()`, in place of the raw GeoPackage table name QGIS/QField otherwise shows by default in the Layers panel/legend (e.g. `inventory_observation`). This is a distinct, third UI surface from, and does not alter, DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119 (a field's own display alias, Section 8.5) or FR-QPB-128 (an embedded relation widget's own display name, Section 8.6) — a layer's own name, a field's alias, and a relation widget's group label are three separately configured QGIS/QField concepts. This requirement does not extend to non-domain layers outside `qfield_builder/schemas.py`'s own `TableDef` set (the bundled KTSN accepted-name lookup table, DR-QPB-072; the online/offline basemap layer; or any uploaded extent/reference layer) ~~— whether any of those should also receive this treatment is not decided here; see Section 8.7 and Open Question O-39~~ — **narrowed by Decision Log D-84: the bundled KTSN accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) specifically is now confirmed in scope for this same Korean-display-name treatment, with name 인정 국명 조회표 (Section 8.7's bonus row); this requirement's own governed scope is extended in place to include that one additional layer alongside every domain survey-data layer. The online/offline basemap layer and any uploaded extent/reference layer remain outside this requirement's scope, undecided — see Open Question O-39 (narrowed).** The specific proposed Korean name for each in-scope layer is recorded, per survey type, in new Section 8.7 — ~~a draft proposal pending the stakeholder's own review and confirmation, not an approved translation~~ **now a stakeholder-confirmed translation, per Decision Log D-84 (with one correction, `site` → 조사지).**

## 8. Data Requirements — Survey Schemas by Type (Req §6)

A hidden integer `fid` may additionally exist per DR-QPB-002, but every displayed ID and every relation must use the UUID columns below.

### 8.1 Type 1 — Simple species inventory (Req §6.1, reworked per Decision Log D-5, D-12)

This survey type has one editable Point layer, `inventory_observation`, and no parent-child domain relation.

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `inventory_id` | TEXT UUID | yes | logical identifier; unique; read-only |
| `observed_at` | DATETIME | yes | default current date/time |
| `surveyor` | TEXT | yes | non-empty |
| `selected_korean_name` | TEXT | no | final user-selected Korean name; active in MVP — entry mechanism changed by Decision Log D-66/FR-QPB-124 (new) from free text to a constrained, filterable `ValueRelation` selection against the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072); the field itself and its "active in MVP" status are otherwise unchanged |
| `selected_scientific_name` | TEXT | no | ~~final user-selected/entered scientific name; active in MVP for manual entry~~ — **superseded for Types 1–3 by Decision Log D-67/FR-QPB-125 (new), 2026-08-26: now a fully derived, read-only field, auto-populated from `selected_korean_name`'s `ValueRelation` selection via a `QgsDefaultValue`/`applyOnUpdate` expression; direct manual free-text entry is no longer possible once this feature is present** |
| `selected_ktsn` | TEXT | no | ~~reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP identification subsystem ships~~ — **superseded for Types 1–3 by Decision Log D-67/D-68/FR-QPB-125/FR-QPB-127 (new), 2026-08-26: now an active, auto-derived field (same `applyOnUpdate` mechanism as `selected_scientific_name` above), independent of the post-MVP identification subsystem's own `identification_enabled` toggle (Decision Log D-68/O-31)** |
| `identification_score` | REAL | no | reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP; 0–1 when populated |
| `occurrence_probability` | REAL | no | reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP; valid range 0.0–1.0 inclusive when populated (`0.0` is a valid value), `NULL` means unavailable; see Section 13.6 for the underlying raster's `-9999` NoData handling (Decision Log D-17) |
| `leaf_photo_path` | TEXT | no | relative Attachment path; optional |
| `flower_photo_path` | TEXT | no | relative Attachment path; optional |
| `fruit_photo_path` | TEXT | no | relative Attachment path; optional |
| `identification_status` | TEXT | yes | `not_requested` in MVP; post-MVP adds `pending`, `complete`, `failed`, `manual` (added; Decision Log D-43 — `manual` is reserved for a manually-entered identification, distinct from `complete`, which remains reserved for a real, persisted Pl@ntNet candidate selection) |
| `identification_timestamp` | DATETIME | no | new (DR-QPB-052; Decision Log D-38); reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP identification subsystem ships; ISO 8601 with timezone per DR-QPB-013's timestamp-format rule; when populated, records when the persisted candidate's identification was performed |
| `identification_model_version` | TEXT | no | new (DR-QPB-052; Decision Log D-38); reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP identification subsystem ships; records the Pl@ntNet API/model version string when available, verbatim as returned by the API |
| `notes` | TEXT | no | multiline text |
| `geom` | POINT | yes | feature location |

- DR-QPB-052 (new; Decision Log D-38; closes a `test-designer`-identified specification gap in FR-QPB-109): Following the Types 1–3 forward-compatibility rule (Decision Log D-12) that already governs `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn`/`identification_score`/`occurrence_probability`/`identification_status`, `inventory_observation` (Type 1) must additionally include two nullable, reserved, inactive-until-post-MVP columns: `identification_timestamp` (DATETIME; ISO 8601 with timezone, per DR-QPB-013's timestamp-format rule) and `identification_model_version` (TEXT). These are the storage columns FR-QPB-109 (revised; Decision Log D-38)'s "identification timestamp/API-model version when available" persistence requirement writes to; no such column existed prior to this entry.
- DR-QPB-020: `inventory_observation` must provide exactly three optional, nullable, relation-free photo-path fields — `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, `fruit_photo_path` — each storing at most one relative attachment path. The field name identifies the organ, so no separate organ-tag column is required. (Decision Log D-16; closes former Open Question O-3, superseding the five-slot/organ-enum design.)
- DR-QPB-021: A Type-1 observation may be saved with zero, one, two, or three of these photo fields populated. Photo attachment is **not** a validation requirement for completing a Type-1 observation. (Decision Log D-16)
- DR-QPB-022: This layer must remain relation-free. If at least one of the three photo fields is populated, that photo (or photos) may later be used by the post-MVP Pl@ntNet identification feature. (Decision Log D-16)
- DR-QPB-023: The attribute form for `inventory_observation` must present three separately labeled Attachment widgets — "Leaf photo", "Flower photo", and "Fruit photo" — bound to `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, and `fruit_photo_path` respectively. (Decision Log D-16)

### 8.2 Type 2 — Temporary plots at defined sites (Req §6.2)

Core relationship: `site (1) → (many) survey (1) → (many) observation`.

**`site`** — MultiPolygon, EPSG:4326: `site_id` (UUID, unique), `site_name` (searchable display field), `site_geom`.

**`survey`** — Point, EPSG:4326: `survey_id` (UUID, unique), `site_id` (UUID FK → `site.site_id`), `survey_date` (default current date), `surveyor` (non-empty), `plot_size` (human-readable), `plot_geom` (temporary plot location).

**`observation`** — no geometry: `observation_id` (UUID, unique), `survey_id` (UUID FK → `survey.survey_id`), `selected_korean_name` (active in MVP; entry mechanism changed by Decision Log D-66/FR-QPB-124 from free text to a constrained `ValueRelation` selection against the bundled accepted-name lookup table, DR-QPB-072), `selected_scientific_name` (~~active in MVP for manual entry~~ — **superseded by Decision Log D-67/FR-QPB-125, 2026-08-26: now a fully derived, read-only field auto-populated from `selected_korean_name`; direct manual entry is no longer possible once this feature is present**), `selected_ktsn` (~~reserved, nullable/inactive until post-MVP~~ — **superseded by Decision Log D-67/D-68/FR-QPB-125/FR-QPB-127, 2026-08-26: now an active, auto-derived field, independent of the post-MVP identification subsystem's `identification_enabled` toggle**), `cover` (INTEGER 0–100 inclusive, required), `identification_score` (reserved, nullable/inactive), `occurrence_probability` (reserved, nullable/inactive; valid range 0.0–1.0 inclusive when populated, `0.0` is valid, `NULL` means unavailable — Decision Log D-17), **`leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` (new; DR-QPB-074; Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28): three optional, nullable, relation-free photo-path fields, mirroring Type 1's `inventory_observation` exactly (Section 8.1, DR-QPB-020), replacing the now-removed `observation_photo` child-table relation for this survey type — see below**, `identification_status` (`not_requested` in MVP; post-MVP adds `pending`, `complete`, `failed`, `manual` — `manual` added by Decision Log D-43, reserved for a manually-entered identification, distinct from `complete`, which remains reserved for a real, persisted Pl@ntNet candidate selection), `identification_timestamp` (new; DR-QPB-053; Decision Log D-38; reserved, nullable/inactive until post-MVP; DATETIME, ISO 8601 with timezone per DR-QPB-013), `identification_model_version` (new; DR-QPB-053; Decision Log D-38; reserved, nullable/inactive until post-MVP; TEXT), `notes`.

**Photo tables (active in MVP):**
- `survey_photo(photo_id UUID, survey_id UUID FK, path TEXT, captured_at DATETIME, notes TEXT)`.
- ~~`observation_photo(photo_id UUID, observation_id UUID FK, path TEXT, organ TEXT, captured_at DATETIME)`.~~ — **removed entirely for Type 2, not deleted from this historical record (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28): this table no longer exists anywhere in a generated Type 2 project. See DR-QPB-074/076 below for its replacement (three inline photo-path fields on `observation` itself) and DR-QPB-032's matching strikethrough for the now-moot `organ` enum.**

- DR-QPB-030 (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior "at least one" misinterpretation): A temporary `survey` may have zero or more related `survey_photo` records. Zero is valid and never blocks an ordinary save, project validation, field completion, or project generation/transfer. (Req §6.2; see AC-QPB-009.)
- ~~DR-QPB-031 (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior "at least one" misinterpretation): A Type 2 `observation` may have zero or more related `observation_photo` records. Zero is valid and never blocks an ordinary save or project validation. (Req §6.2; see AC-QPB-009.)~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28): `observation_photo` no longer exists for Type 2 (or Type 3) — see new DR-QPB-074/075 below, which replace this cardinality rule with the same fixed, optional, relation-free three-field pattern DR-QPB-020/021 already establish for Type 1's `inventory_observation`.**
- ~~DR-QPB-032: `organ` must be one of `leaf`, `flower`, `fruit`, `bark`, or `auto`. (Req §6.2)~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28): the `organ` column existed only on `observation_photo`, which no longer exists for Type 2/3 (DR-QPB-076). No table anywhere in this specification retains an `organ` column after this revision, so this rule is now moot everywhere it previously applied.**
- ~~DR-QPB-033: Up to five selected observation photos may later be submitted in one identification request (post-MVP); all submitted photos must represent the same individual plant. (Req §6.2)~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28): once Type 2/3's `observation` is limited to the same fixed three photo-path fields as Type 1 (DR-QPB-074), there is no longer a variable-cardinality "selection" of observation photos to bound for Type 2/3 either — mirroring Type 1, which never had an analogous DR rule. FR-QPB-104's existing, general "no more than five JPEG/PNG photos... per request" cap (Section 13.2) is unaffected and continues to apply as the sole governing ceiling, already satisfied by three or fewer photos.**
- DR-QPB-034: `identification_score`, `occurrence_probability`, `selected_ktsn`, and `identification_status`'s post-MVP status values must remain nullable and inactive in the MVP build, per the Types 1–3 forward-compatibility rule (Decision Log D-12).
- DR-QPB-053 (new; Decision Log D-38; closes a `test-designer`-identified specification gap in FR-QPB-109): Following the same rule DR-QPB-034 states, the Type 2 `observation` table — and, by cross-reference, the Type 3 `observation` table (Section 8.3, which shares Type 2's fields) — must likewise include `identification_timestamp` (DATETIME; ISO 8601 with timezone, per DR-QPB-013) and `identification_model_version` (TEXT), both nullable, reserved, and inactive until the post-MVP identification subsystem ships. This extends DR-QPB-034's existing nullable/inactive list to also cover these two new columns by name; DR-QPB-034's own text above is unchanged.
- DR-QPB-074 (new; Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28; Category C, stakeholder-directed — supersedes DR-QPB-031/DR-QPB-042's cardinality rule for Type 2/3's `observation` table specifically, and the `organ`-column concept DR-QPB-032 governed, both struck through and annotated above/below, not deleted): Following Type 1's own DR-QPB-020 precedent for `inventory_observation` exactly, Type 2/3's shared `observation` table (this section; Section 8.3, which inherits this table by cross-reference) must provide exactly three optional, nullable, relation-free photo-path fields — `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, `fruit_photo_path` — each storing at most one relative attachment path. As with Type 1, the field name identifies the organ, so no separate organ-tag column is required, and no `organ` column exists anywhere in this table.
- DR-QPB-075 (new; Decision Log D-74; mirrors DR-QPB-021 for Type 2/3's `observation`): A Type 2/3 `observation` record may be saved with zero, one, two, or three of these photo fields populated. Photo attachment is **not** a validation requirement for completing an observation of either type — unchanged in substance from the cardinality rule DR-QPB-031/DR-QPB-042 previously stated for the now-removed `observation_photo` relation; only the storage mechanism changes.
- DR-QPB-076 (new; Decision Log D-74): The `observation_photo` table is **removed entirely** for Type 2 and Type 3 — it no longer exists anywhere in a generated Type 2 or Type 3 project's GeoPackage. `observation` itself remains otherwise unaffected: it is still a required child of `survey` via `rel_observation_survey` (FR-QPB-056, DR-QPB-006), and its `cover`/identification-related columns are all unchanged; it simply no longer has any child relation of its own — unlike Type 1's relation-free `inventory_observation` (DR-QPB-022), which has never had one at all. If at least one of the three photo fields is populated, that photo (or photos) may later be used by the post-MVP Pl@ntNet identification feature, mirroring DR-QPB-022's identical Type-1 rule. **Consequence for the "Identify attached photos" mechanism (Section 13.1, FR-QPB-101; cross-reference only, no FR-QPB-101 text change required):** `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_identification_photo_paths_expression` function, confirmed by direct code reading to branch by table name (`inventory_observation` already reads its three inline columns directly; every other table previously read via a `relation_aggregate()` expression over `rel_observation_photo_observation`), must now treat `observation` (Type 2/3) identically to `inventory_observation` (Type 1) — reading the same three inline columns directly, with no `relation_aggregate()` branch remaining for any table in `IDENTIFICATION_TARGET_LAYERS` (unchanged: `("inventory_observation", "observation")`). This is confirmed, by direct code reading, to require no change to the embedded QML itself — `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `render_identification_widget_qml()`/`qpbCurrentPhotoPaths()` already treat `photo_paths_expression` as an opaque, pre-built comma-separated-path expression string, and already submit every photo with a hardcoded `organ="auto"` regardless of source table — only `_identification_photo_paths_expression`'s own Type-2/3 branch needs to change.
- DR-QPB-077 (new; Decision Log D-74; mirrors DR-QPB-023 for Type 2/3's `observation`): The attribute form for Type 2/3's `observation` table must present three separately labeled Attachment widgets — bound to `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, and `fruit_photo_path` respectively — using the **exact same Korean aliases already stakeholder-confirmed for Type 1's `inventory_observation`** (Section 8.5; Decision Log D-56–D-58): 잎 사진 / 꽃 사진 / 열매 사진. No new Korean-terminology decision or stakeholder confirmation is required for this specific wording, since these are the identical column names Section 8.5 already aliases for Type 1.

### 8.3 Type 3 — Permanent plots at defined sites (Req §6.3)

Core relationship: `site (1) → (many) plot (1) → (many) survey (1) → (many) observation`.

**`site`** — same as Type 2.

**`plot`** — Point, EPSG:4326: `plot_id` (UUID, unique), `site_id` (UUID FK), `plot_name` (searchable), `plot_size`, `plot_geom` (fixed location).

**`survey`** — no geometry: `survey_id` (UUID, unique), `plot_id` (UUID FK → `plot.plot_id`), `survey_date` (default current date), `surveyor` (non-empty).

**`observation`** — same fields and forward-compatible-but-inactive Pl@ntNet columns as Type 2 (including the new `identification_timestamp`/`identification_model_version` columns added by DR-QPB-053; Decision Log D-38, and the `manual` `identification_status` value added by Decision Log D-43), with `survey_id` referencing the permanent-plot survey. Type 3 likewise inherits Type 2's `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn` treatment as revised by Decision Log D-66/D-67/D-68 (Section 8.2 above): a constrained `ValueRelation` selection for `selected_korean_name`, and fully derived, read-only, identification-toggle-independent values for `selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn`. **Type 3 likewise inherits Type 2's `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` fields and its removed `observation_photo` relation (new; DR-QPB-074–077; Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28) in place of the fields' prior absence and the relation's prior presence — see Section 8.2 above for the full rule; this is a shared-table cross-reference, not a separate decision for Type 3.**

**Photo tables (active in MVP):**
- `plot_photo(photo_id UUID, plot_id UUID FK, path TEXT, captured_at DATETIME, notes TEXT)`.
- ~~`observation_photo(photo_id UUID, observation_id UUID FK, path TEXT, organ TEXT, captured_at DATETIME)`.~~ — **removed entirely for Type 3, not deleted from this historical record (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28), mirroring Type 2's identical removal above (Section 8.2). `plot_photo` immediately above is a structurally distinct table (photos of the permanent `plot` itself, not of an individual `observation`) and is completely unaffected by this change.**

- DR-QPB-040 (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior "at least one" misinterpretation): A permanent `plot` may have zero or more related `plot_photo` records. Zero is valid and never blocks an ordinary save, project validation, field completion, or project generation/transfer. (Req §6.3; see AC-QPB-009.)
- DR-QPB-041: Plot photos belong to the permanent plot, not to each repeated survey; this remains true regardless of whether zero or more plot photos exist. (Req §6.3)
- ~~DR-QPB-042 (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior "at least one" misinterpretation): A Type 3 `observation` may have zero or more related `observation_photo` records. Zero is valid and never blocks an ordinary save or project validation. (Req §6.3; see AC-QPB-009.)~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28), mirroring DR-QPB-031's identical Type-2 treatment above: `observation_photo` no longer exists for Type 3 — see DR-QPB-074/075 (Section 8.2, shared by cross-reference) for its replacement.**

### 8.4 Type 4 — Vegetation mapping (Req §6.4)

Core relationship: `site (1) → (many) survey (1) → (many) community`.

**`site`** — same as Type 2.

**`survey`** — no geometry: `survey_id` (UUID, unique), `site_id` (UUID FK), `survey_date` (default current date), `surveyor` (non-empty).

**`community`** — MultiPolygon, EPSG:4326: `community_id` (UUID, unique), `survey_id` (UUID FK → `survey.survey_id`), `community_name` (searchable), `dominant_species` (manually entered/selected), `is_field_checked` (BOOLEAN, default false), `community_geom`, `notes`.

- DR-QPB-050: `community` must **not** include Pl@ntNet-specific identification fields (`selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn`/`identification_score`/`occurrence_probability`/`identification_status`) unless a later requirement explicitly introduces them. This is an intentional deviation from the Types 1–3 forward-compatibility rule. (Decision Log D-12)
- DR-QPB-054 (new; Decision Log D-38; non-destructive extension of DR-QPB-050, not a reopening of it): Per DR-QPB-050's existing intentional deviation from the Types 1–3 forward-compatibility rule, `community` (Type 4) must also **not** include `identification_timestamp` or `identification_model_version` — the two new columns added to Types 1–3 by DR-QPB-052/053 — unless a later requirement explicitly introduces them. This confirms Type 4 continues to be excluded from the forward-compatibility treatment for these two new columns as well; DR-QPB-050's own text above is unchanged.
- DR-QPB-051: Rule-based symbology must render `is_field_checked = true` as a green hatch/pattern and all other values as a red hatch/pattern. (Req §6.4)

### 8.5 Korean field aliases (Req n/a; new, Decision Log D-56 — **draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved**)

> **Status of this section: ~~DRAFT PROPOSAL.~~ ~~CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (Decision Log D-57), 2026-08-26 — with one narrow, explicitly-flagged exception noted below.~~ FULLY CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (Decision Log D-57/D-58), 2026-08-26 — the one previously narrow, explicitly-flagged exception (the Type-3 `plot_id` foreign-key label's "고정" prefix) has since itself been explicitly confirmed by the stakeholder; see Decision Log D-58. No exception remains.** This section responds to the stakeholder's verbatim instruction, reported by the orchestrator: **"Add Korean aliases to the fields in the form."** Per DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119, every field below except a table's own UUID primary key receives the listed Korean alias via QGIS's field-alias mechanism (e.g. `QgsVectorLayer.setFieldAlias`). ~~**Every alias below is a proposal requiring the stakeholder's own domain-expert review and correction — none of it is decided.**~~ ~~**The stakeholder has explicitly confirmed every alias below exactly as proposed (Decision Log D-57), except one narrow, related sub-question that was not itself separately addressed: whether the Type-3 `survey.plot_id`/`plot_photo.plot_id` foreign-key label should also carry the "고정" prefix used in `plot.plot_name`'s confirmed alias. That sub-question is resolved, for now, only as the orchestrator's own interpretation (leave it as the already-proposed plain "조사구," unchanged) — not a stakeholder confirmation — and remains individually correctable; see Decision Log D-57 and Open Question O-22's closure note (Section 20).**~~ **The stakeholder has explicitly confirmed every alias below exactly as proposed (Decision Log D-57), including the one previously narrow, related sub-question left open by D-57 — whether the Type-3 `survey.plot_id`/`plot_photo.plot_id` foreign-key label should also carry the "고정" prefix used in `plot.plot_name`'s confirmed alias — which the stakeholder has since explicitly confirmed, verbatim, **"'고정' added there too"** (Decision Log D-58). No field below remains at Medium confidence or otherwise unconfirmed.** Each proposed term was originally marked with a confidence level at proposal time; the table below now also records each term's confirmation status:
> - **High** — either it already appears verbatim, or very close to verbatim, in this application's own already-drafted Korean UI copy (`qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py`'s Step 2 survey-type explanations, FR-QPB-024a/Decision Log D-27, and Step 5 identification-toggle text), or it is an unambiguous, single-common-rendering literal translation.
> - **Medium** — a reasoned, grounded proposal with no verified precedent elsewhere in this project, where more than one common Korean rendering exists, or where the exact institute-preferred phrasing/register is unverified. Every Medium-confidence term is also listed in new Open Question O-22 (Section 20) for explicit stakeholder confirmation or correction.
>
> Geometry columns (`geom`, `site_geom`, `plot_geom`, `community_geom`) are not listed: they are not modeled as `ColumnDef` entries in `qfield_builder/schemas.py` and are not part of a QGIS vector layer's attribute-field collection (`layer.fields()`), so the field-alias mechanism this section proposes does not apply to them. ~~The hidden physical key `fid` (DR-QPB-002) is likewise not listed, for the same reason (see DR-QPB-071).~~ **(corrected by Decision Log D-59, 2026-08-26)** The hidden physical key `fid` (DR-QPB-002) is likewise not listed in the table below, but **not** for the same reason as the geometry columns above: unlike a geometry column, `fid` **is** a genuine member of a real generated layer's `layer.fields()` (see the corrected DR-QPB-071, Section 7, for the full technical basis). It is omitted from the table below because it is a non-domain physical key that this proposal simply does not assign a Korean alias to, and because it is already excluded from the *visible* attribute-editor form entirely by the separate, pre-existing `_build_drag_and_drop_form` mechanism (DR-QPB-002; DR-QPB-071) — not because the alias-setting mechanism this section proposes is structurally inapplicable to it the way it is for geometry columns. This proposal does **not** address translating the *values* of enumerated/status fields (e.g. `identification_status`'s `not_requested`/`pending`/`complete`/`failed`/`manual`, or `organ`'s `leaf`/`flower`/`fruit`/`bark`/`auto`) — only the field *label* (alias) itself; value-level Korean display (e.g. via `ValueMap`) is a related but separate, out-of-scope concern this section does not propose.
