### 8.6 Korean relation-widget display names (Req n/a; new, Decision Log D-73 — **draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved**)

> **Status of this section: ~~DRAFT PROPOSAL.~~ CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (Decision Log D-77), 2026-08-28 — six of the seven proposed names below are confirmed exactly as proposed; the seventh (`rel_observation_survey`) is corrected from the originally proposed "관찰" to the stakeholder's actual confirmed term, "식물관찰."** This section responds to the stakeholder's direct report, quoted in full in Decision Log D-73: **"Widget에 relation을 추가할 때 rel_observation_survey와 같은 이름으로 추가하지 말고 적절한 한국어 alias를 적용할 것"** ("When adding a relation to a widget, don't add it with a name like 'rel_observation_survey' — apply an appropriate Korean alias instead"). Per new FR-QPB-128, every relation embedded as a `QgsAttributeEditorRelation` widget in a parent record's own attribute form (FR-QPB-056/FR-QPB-057) — the mechanism that currently displays the raw relation ID, e.g. `rel_observation_survey`, confirmed by direct reading of `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_add_relations()`/`_build_drag_and_drop_form()` — must instead receive the Korean display name listed below, via the relation's own separate, human-facing "name" property (`QgsRelation.setName()`, currently set to the same raw ID as the relation's own stable `id()`) — never the stable ID itself, which is unchanged and continues to govern every existing cross-reference (`relation_aggregate()` calls, FR-QPB-056's own "stable relation IDs" requirement, etc.). ~~**Every name below is a proposal requiring the stakeholder's own confirmation or correction — none of it is decided; see Decision Log D-73 for the full investigation record (including a disclosed, not-yet-independently-verified caveat about exactly which QGIS mechanism drives the widget's rendered label) and Open Question O-36 for the confirmation request.**~~ **Every name below is now stakeholder-confirmed (Decision Log D-77; Open Question O-36 CLOSED) — the one disclosed, not-yet-independently-verified caveat about exactly which QGIS mechanism drives the widget's rendered label (`QgsRelation.setName()`, most plausible, per Decision Log D-73) remains open on its own terms and is unaffected by this terminology confirmation; confirming that mechanism is separate implementer-verification work.** `rel_observation_photo_observation` is deliberately **excluded** from the table below: Decision Log D-74 (this same round, Section 8.2/8.3) removes the `observation_photo` table — and therefore this relation — entirely for Type 2/3, so proposing a Korean name for it here would be moot.

> Each proposed name reuses this specification's own already-confirmed Section 8.5 vocabulary for the **child** table the widget lists (the widget's role, on the parent record's own form, is to show that parent's related child records) — grounded in existing precedent, but not itself independently confirmed, since a relation-widget group label is a different UI element from an ordinary field alias.

| `rel_survey_site` | Type 2, Type 4 | `site` | `survey` | 조사 | **Confirmed** (Decision Log D-77); ~~Medium — reuses the already-confirmed "조사" root term (Section 8.5), but its use as a *relation-widget group label*, rather than a field alias, is new and unconfirmed~~ |
| `rel_observation_survey` | Type 2, Type 3 | `survey` | `observation` | ~~관찰~~ 식물관찰 (Decision Log D-77) | **Confirmed** (Decision Log D-77); ~~Medium — reuses the already-confirmed "관찰" term (Section 8.5's `observation_photo.observation_id` FK alias, historical); same relation-widget-vs-field-alias caveat as above~~ |
| `rel_survey_photo_survey` | Type 2 | `survey` | `survey_photo` | 조사 사진 | **Confirmed** (Decision Log D-77); ~~Medium — a new compound term, not previously proposed anywhere in Section 8.5; a bare "사진" (matching `survey_photo.path`'s own alias) is a plausible, simpler alternative~~ |
| `rel_plot_site` | Type 3 | `site` | `plot` | 고정조사구 | **Confirmed** (Decision Log D-77); ~~Medium — reuses the already-confirmed "고정조사구" term (Section 8.5, Decision Log D-58); same relation-widget-vs-field-alias caveat~~ |

### 8.7 Korean layer display names (Req n/a; new, Decision Log D-80; ~~**draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved**~~ — **CONFIRMED by the stakeholder, with one correction (Decision Log D-84), 2026-08-28**)

> **Status of this section: ~~DRAFT PROPOSAL. Not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder.~~ CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (Decision Log D-84), 2026-08-28 — every proposed name in both tables below (the domain-layer table and the KTSN-lookup-layer bonus row) is confirmed exactly as proposed, except the `site` layer's own proposed name (three occurrences, Types 2/3/4), which is corrected from "사이트" to "조사지."** This section responds to the stakeholder's direct question, confirmed as a "yes, do this" instruction, reported by the orchestrator: **"레이어가 표시되는 이름을 한국어로 변경할 수 있나? 예를 들어, 테이블 이름은 inventory_observation이더라도 QField에서 표시되는 이름은 식물관찰 이라던지"** ("Can the displayed layer name be changed to Korean? For example, even if the table name is inventory_observation, the name displayed in QField could be 식물관찰"). Per new DR-QPB-071's sibling, DR-QPB-078, and new FR-QPB-130, every generated domain survey-data layer must receive the Korean display name listed below, set via `QgsMapLayer.setName()` — a real, standard QGIS API that sets a layer's own name in the Layers panel/legend, completely independent of the underlying GeoPackage table name; this is a confirmed, well-known technical capability, not one requiring the live-research disclosure caveats this specification has needed for some other capabilities (e.g. Decision Log D-36/D-46). This is distinct from, and does not alter, two related but separate, already-confirmed proposals: Section 8.5/DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119 (a field's own display alias) and Section 8.6/FR-QPB-128 (an embedded relation widget's own display name) — neither sets the layer's own name as it appears in the Layers panel/legend. ~~**Every proposed name below is a draft requiring the stakeholder's own review and confirmation, mirroring Decision Log D-56/D-73's identical precedent for a draft Korean-terminology proposal** — no `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against this section or AC-QPB-118 until the stakeholder has reviewed it.~~ **Every proposed name below is now stakeholder-confirmed (Decision Log D-84; Open Question O-39 narrowed, not closed) — `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against this section and AC-QPB-118.** Each proposed name below reuses this document's own already-confirmed Section 8.5 (field-alias) or Section 8.6 (relation-display-name) vocabulary for the same underlying table wherever one exists — grounding it, but not itself confirming it for this distinct new UI element, since a layer's own name is a different UI surface from a field alias or a relation-widget group label (mirroring Section 8.6's own identical caveat about reusing Section 8.5 vocabulary) — and is marked **High** on that basis; a proposed name with no such precedent to reuse is marked **Medium**, using the same confidence-level definitions as Section 8.5/8.6.
>
> **A note on this proposal's own currency relative to `qfield_builder/schemas.py`:** the table below enumerates every domain survey-data layer per this specification's own current, approved schema (Section 8, which already reflects Decision Log D-74's approved removal of `observation_photo` for Types 2/3) — not the literal contents of `qfield_builder/schemas.py` as it exists in the repository as of this writing, which has not yet been updated by an `implementer` round to reflect Decision Log D-74 and therefore still defines an `observation_photo` `TableDef` for Types 2/3. This proposal deliberately follows the specification's own approved schema, consistent with this document's own discipline of treating the specification, not a not-yet-caught-up implementation, as the source of truth for what a later `implementer` round must build.

Whether either should also receive Korean-language treatment is not decided here; see Open Question O-39.

## 9. Functional Requirements — QGIS/QField Project Configuration (Req §7)

- FR-QPB-050: The application must generate the QGIS project through supported QGIS/PyQGIS APIs where possible, and must not rely on fragile string replacement of `.qgs` XML as the primary implementation method.
- FR-QPB-051: The application must generate an uncompressed `.qgs` project unless a compatibility test explicitly approves `.qgz`.
- FR-QPB-052: The `.qgs` and `.gpkg` must live inside the same project folder tree, referenced by relative paths — likewise for attachments, basemap, plugin (post-MVP), and reference assets (post-MVP).
- FR-QPB-053: The generated project must set the configured project CRS and enable on-the-fly transformation.
- FR-QPB-054: Every required GeoPackage layer, including non-spatial tables used by relations, must be loaded into the project; internal GeoPackage metadata tables must not be loaded into the layer tree.
- FR-QPB-055 (revised; Decision Log D-71 — original text retained and extended in place; this is a purely additive clarification of stacking/rendering order, not a reversal of the original sentence's own meaning, which remains true and unchanged): Layers must be grouped into `Survey data`, `Basemap`, and `Reference` groups. **`Basemap` must be the last of these three groups within the root layer tree's own children order** — concretely, within the root `QgsLayerTreeGroup`'s `children()` list (the same list that determines both the on-screen Layers-panel position and the rendering/z-order QGIS and QField actually use), `Basemap`'s own index must be greater than both `Survey data`'s index and `Reference`'s index. This is stated in terms of that single governing index deliberately, so "last" cannot be read three different ways ("last added" vs. "last in the visual list" vs. "bottom of the rendering stack") — in a correctly ordered QGIS layer tree these always coincide, and children-index order is what governs all three simultaneously. The practical effect: `Survey data` and `Reference` must both render on top of (in front of, visually above) `Basemap`, so the actual survey data and reference/extent layers remain visible above the basemap rather than being obscured by it. This requirement states nothing about, and does not constrain, the relative order between `Survey data` and `Reference` themselves — no requirement in this specification does; that relative order remains unconstrained.
- FR-QPB-056: One QGIS project relation must be created for every database foreign key, using stable relation IDs (e.g., `rel_survey_site`, `rel_observation_survey`, `rel_photo_observation`). Composition strength must be used for owned child records (observations, photo rows). Child relations must be added to parent forms so users can create observations/photos from the parent feature. Foreign-key fields must use Relation Reference widgets with a human-readable display expression.
- FR-QPB-057: Attribute forms must be built with the Drag and Drop Designer, organized into clear tabs/groups, and must: hide `fid` and UUID fields from normal entry; keep UUID values non-editable; use Date/Time widgets with current date/time defaults; use Relation Reference widgets for foreign keys with the option to open referenced forms; use a Range widget for `cover` (min 0, max 100, step 1); use a Checkbox for `is_field_checked` (default false); use Value Map for controlled categorical values; use Attachment widgets for photo-path fields configured with relative paths; enforce mandatory attributes with hard constraints, not only UI labels; use multiline text widgets for notes; and add embedded relation widgets for child observations and photo galleries. **Cross-reference (new, Decision Log D-56 — draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved):** new FR-QPB-119 below proposes that every field this requirement describes as visible to the user must also carry a Korean-language display alias; see Section 8.5 for the proposed per-field mapping, still awaiting the stakeholder's own domain-expert review.
- FR-QPB-058: For related photo tables, the child `path` field must use the Attachment widget, and the relation must be included in the parent form, to support the QField gallery relation behavior.
- FR-QPB-059: Each layer's display expression must be set to a useful human-readable field (e.g., `site_name`, `plot_name`, `survey_date`, `selected_korean_name`, `community_name`). Reference/extent layers must be non-identifiable and read-only where appropriate; survey data must be searchable where useful.
- FR-QPB-060: The project must enable transaction behavior appropriate for related edits, and must enable evaluation of provider-side/default values where required, while ensuring UUID generation also works correctly in QField.
- FR-QPB-061: The application must validate, before delivery, that a parent and its new child records can be created and saved together in one field workflow.
- FR-QPB-119 (new; Decision Log D-56 — **draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved**): Every attribute field on every layer of the generated QGIS project must have a Korean-language display alias set via QGIS's field-alias mechanism (e.g. `QgsVectorLayer.setFieldAlias`) — rather than showing the raw, snake_case column name — **except** a UUID field in its primary-key role, per DR-QPB-071 (already `Hidden`/read-only per DR-QPB-005/FR-QPB-057 above). This explicitly includes UUID foreign-key fields, which remain visible as Relation Reference picker widgets (FR-QPB-057/DR-QPB-006/AC-QPB-013) and therefore need a human-readable Korean label like any other visible field. The specific proposed Korean alias for each field, per survey type and table, is recorded in new Section 8.5 — a **draft proposal pending explicit domain-expert review and correction by the stakeholder**, not an approved translation; where Section 8.5 flags a field's proposed alias as Medium confidence, that flag is part of this requirement's own text and must not be silently resolved by any later role — the exact wording for every flagged field must be confirmed with the stakeholder (see Open Question O-22) before any `test-designer`/`implementer` work proceeds against this requirement.
- FR-QPB-120 (revised; Decision Log D-65; confirmed minimalist definition and per-survey-type scope): Every generated point layer must receive a minimalist default point-marker symbol, and every generated polygon layer must receive a minimalist default fill-and-outline symbol, set as that layer's `QgsSingleSymbolRenderer`/`QgsSymbol` at build time, replacing QGIS's own undifferentiated default symbol — **except** the Type 4 `community` layer, which keeps its existing rule-based renderer (DR-QPB-051) unaffected. **"Minimalist" (confirmed; closes O-25):** a single flat fill color plus a thin, contrasting outline for every polygon layer; a small, solid circle marker for every point layer; no gradient, pattern, label callout, or per-category color-coding by default. **Scope (confirmed; closes O-26; stakeholder's verbatim reasoning: "because we can define the number of layers and types of layers only after determining survey type"):** styling is decided once per generated project, as a whole, at the wizard's new Step 6 (FR-QPB-123) — after the survey type is already selected at Step 2 (FR-QPB-023) and its full layer set is therefore already known. Within one generated project, the resulting choice applies uniformly to **every** point layer of that project and, separately, uniformly to **every** polygon layer of that project — never a different style per individual layer within the same project, and never persisted or reused automatically as a global default for a later, separately generated project (even of the same survey type). How a user configures this in the wizard is stated by new FR-QPB-123 below (closes O-27).
- FR-QPB-121 (revised; Decision Log D-65; confirmed Tabler mechanism, license/attribution, offline behavior, and embedding — closes O-24): For point layers specifically, the wizard's Step 6 (FR-QPB-123) must let the user search, by name/keyword, an offline, build-time-bundled static index of Tabler icon names (~6,184 names at time of research; MIT-licensed, `github.com/tabler/tabler-icons`), with results filtered live as the user types via a simple client-side substring/prefix filter over the bundled name list — no network request for searching. Upon the user selecting one icon, the application must fetch that icon's SVG content from Tabler's public source (the single network request FR-QPB-011(d) permits), and, on success, use it as the point-marker symbol for every point layer of the generated project (FR-QPB-120's confirmed per-survey-type/not-per-layer scope), replacing the minimalist default marker for that project, and must embed the downloaded SVG file into the generated project's own output folder (e.g. a new `symbols/` subfolder of the project root), referenced only by a project-relative path from the `.qgs` symbol definition — never an absolute path, and never a path outside the generated project's own folder tree (FR-QPB-091/DR-QPB-012). No attribution/license notice is required anywhere in the generated project or this application's own UI (MIT license, confirmed). If the fetch fails (no network, non-200 response, timeout) or the user does not select an icon, the minimalist default (FR-QPB-120) remains the project's point-marker symbol and project generation is not blocked; the minimalist default remains fully usable with zero network access at all times (NFR-QPB-080(4)).
- FR-QPB-122 (new; Decision Log D-63, ~~draft~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-69**): The `identification_status` field (Section 8.1's `inventory_observation`; Section 8.2/8.3's `observation`) must be configured with a `ValueMap` (or a functionally equivalent fixed-list-selection) editor widget listing exactly its five existing enum values (`not_requested`, `pending`, `complete`, `failed`, `manual`) as the only selectable options — replacing the plain default text-edit widget it currently receives in `_configure_widget_for_column` (`qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`), the gap Section 8.5 (Decision Log D-56) already named and explicitly left out of scope. The value written to the GeoPackage on selection must remain exactly the existing raw enum string; this requirement changes only the editor's presentation/entry-constraint behavior, not the column's SQL type, `CHECK` constraint (`_identification_status_col`, `qfield_builder/schemas.py`), default value, or any rule governing which code path may write which value (FR-QPB-109, Decision Log D-38/D-43/D-50/D-51, unaffected). **Confirmed (Decision Log D-69, closes O-33):** the dropdown's displayed option text keeps the existing raw English enum strings as its values (`not_requested`/`pending`/`complete`/`failed`/`manual`), with no Korean-language value-label translation, matching the existing `organ` `ValueMap` widget's own precedent (identical English keys/values) — this is distinct from, and does not alter, the field's own already-confirmed Korean *label* alias (Section 8.5, Decision Log D-56–D-58).
- FR-QPB-123 (new; Decision Log D-65; closes O-27): a new wizard **Step 6, "Symbol styling configuration"**, inserted immediately after the existing Step 5 (optional photo identification toggle, Section 6.5) and immediately before the renumbered Step 7 "Review and build" (Section 6.7, originally Section 6.6, FR-QPB-040/FR-QPB-041). At this step, for the survey type already selected at Step 2 (FR-QPB-023), the wizard must let the user accept the minimalist default point/polygon styling (FR-QPB-120) with no further action, or search for and select one Tabler SVG icon (FR-QPB-121) to replace the default point-marker symbol for every point layer of the project being generated. See Section 6.6 for this step's own requirement text.
- FR-QPB-124 (new; Decision Log D-66; closes part of O-28/O-29): `selected_korean_name` (Types 1–3 only — `dominant_species`, Type 4, is explicitly out of scope, Decision Log D-66/O-29) must be configured with a native QGIS `ValueRelation` editor widget referencing the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072), configured for a filterable, typeahead selection experience using QGIS's own `ValueRelation` "use completer"/filter-expression configuration; where QGIS's widget configuration allows it, the number of simultaneously displayed matches should be capped at five. **Disclosed technical-feasibility caveat (mirrors FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-36):** whether QGIS's/QField's actual `ValueRelation` widget implementation supports a live, as-you-type filter capped at exactly five displayed results is not independently verified by this specification; verifying and, if necessary, adjusting this display-count behavior to whatever QGIS's real widget configuration actually supports is implementer work to report back. The value written to `selected_korean_name` on selection is the plain Korean-name text itself — this is a constrained-value-selection widget, not a true relational foreign key in the DR-QPB-006/FR-QPB-056 sense; no GeoPackage-level foreign-key constraint and no QGIS project relation is created for it.
- FR-QPB-125 (new; Decision Log D-67; closes part of O-30): for Types 1–3, `selected_scientific_name` and `selected_ktsn` must each be configured with a `QgsDefaultValue` expression that has `applyOnUpdate = true` (QField's "apply default upon update"), referencing `selected_korean_name`'s current value to look up, in the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072), that row's own scientific name (for `selected_scientific_name`) and KTSN identifier (for `selected_ktsn`); both fields' own editor widgets must be configured non-editable (read-only). This mechanism works identically for a brand-new feature and for an existing, already-saved feature reopened later, via QGIS's/QField's own standard live-default-value re-evaluation — unlike the Pl@ntNet candidate-selection write-back mechanism (Decision Log D-50), this mechanism is not limited to brand-new/not-yet-saved features only.
- FR-QPB-126 (new; Decision Log D-67; closes remainder of O-30; states DR-QPB-072's row-derivation rule): the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) must be derived at build time by: (1) reusing the same deterministic Steps 1–4 row-filtering computation FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-48) already defines (Plantae-kingdom-subtree filter; species-level-and-below rank filter; vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist filter; duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution), invoked regardless of whether `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` output itself is written for a given build (see FR-QPB-127 for this table's own, decoupled trigger condition); then (2) applying a new Step 5: keeping only rows whose `taxon_jm_nm` value is exactly `정명` (the existing accepted-name-status flag, Decision Log D-4/15b), excluding every row for which it is not, including a row with a missing/blank `taxon_jm_nm` value. Resulting columns, at minimum: `ktsn`, `taxon_kor_nm` (Korean name), and `taxon_full_nm` with `<em>`/`</em>` tags removed (scientific name). No row count is asserted by this requirement; the count this Step 5 filter produces is unconfirmed and requires a build-time measurement (Decision Log D-67/D-68; NFR-QPB-001).
- FR-QPB-127 (new; Decision Log D-68; closes O-31): for every Types 1–3 generated project, the accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) and its build-time row-derivation (FR-QPB-126) must always run and always be bundled, independent of whether the post-MVP identification subsystem is enabled (`identification_enabled`, FR-QPB-037–039) — decoupled from FR-QPB-112 (revised; Decision Log D-47)'s own conditional-bundling trigger, which is unaffected and unchanged (it continues to govern only the larger, identification-subsystem-specific `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`/probability-raster bundle). This reuses FR-QPB-105's existing source-CSV-presence/required-column validation and fail-early discipline, now applying to every Types 1–3 project build, not only identification-enabled ones.
- FR-QPB-128 (new; Decision Log D-73 — ~~**draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved; not to be exercised by any `test-designer`/`implementer` work until Section 8.6's proposed relation display names are stakeholder-confirmed**~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-77 — Section 8.6's proposed relation display names are now stakeholder-confirmed (six as proposed, one corrected); `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against this requirement**): Every child relation embedded into a parent layer's attribute form as a `QgsAttributeEditorRelation` widget (FR-QPB-056/FR-QPB-057) must show a Korean-language display name instead of the raw relation ID (e.g. `rel_observation_survey`) currently shown. The relation's own stable ID (FR-QPB-056; `QgsRelation.setId()`) must remain completely unchanged by this requirement — only the relation's separate, human-facing display name (`QgsRelation.setName()`, the most plausible, code-grounded mechanism identified; see Section 8.6's disclosed, not-yet-independently-verified caveat about exactly which QGIS mechanism drives the widget's rendered label) is affected. The specific confirmed Korean name for each relation is recorded in new Section 8.6 — ~~a **draft proposal pending explicit stakeholder review and correction**, not an approved translation~~ **now a stakeholder-confirmed translation, per Decision Log D-77 (the disclosed `QgsRelation.setName()`-mechanism-verification caveat remains open on its own terms, unaffected by this terminology confirmation).** This requirement does not extend to, and is fully independent of, DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119/Section 8.5's separate, already-confirmed attribute-*field*-alias work, which this requirement does not reopen, reword, or alter in any way.
- FR-QPB-130 (new; Decision Log D-80; ~~**general mechanism confirmed by the stakeholder; the specific proposed layer names in Section 8.7 remain a draft, not yet stakeholder-approved**~~ — **confirmed by Decision Log D-84 — Section 8.7's proposed layer names are now stakeholder-confirmed (with one correction, `site` → 조사지); `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against this requirement**): Every generated domain survey-data layer (DR-QPB-078, **now also extended to the bundled KTSN accepted-name lookup table, DR-QPB-072, per Decision Log D-84**) must have its own display name set, at build time, via `QgsMapLayer.setName()`, to the Korean-language name recorded in Section 8.7 — replacing whatever name QGIS/OGR would otherwise default to from the underlying GeoPackage table name. This must be configured once per layer, for every layer added by this application's own layer-loading logic (`qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`) — it is unrelated to, and must not be confused with, that same module's existing display-*expression* configuration (FR-QPB-059), which governs which single field's value represents an individual *feature* of a layer, not the layer's own name as shown in the Layers panel. The specific Korean name for each in-scope layer is recorded, per survey type and table, in Section 8.7 — ~~a draft proposal pending the stakeholder's own review and confirmation; where Section 8.7 flags a layer's proposed name as Medium confidence, or flags a layer as possibly out of this requirement's own scope, that flag is part of this requirement's own text and must not be silently resolved by any later role (see Open Question O-39)~~ **now a stakeholder-confirmed translation (Decision Log D-84); the remaining, narrower scope question — whether the three English-named layer-tree groups and/or the basemap layer's own name should also receive this treatment — is unaffected by this confirmation and remains open (Open Question O-39, narrowed).**
- ~~**FR-QPB-136 (MVP; new; Decision Log D-91):** On the first open of every newly generated project, every layer that is present in the project layer tree must be enabled/checked (visible) by default. This includes all generated `Survey data` layers, all generated `Reference` layers (including the Type 1–3 accepted-name lookup table and any uploaded reference/extent layer), and every generated `Basemap` layer that applies to the selected online/offline mode. The saved `.qgs` layer-tree state must therefore contain no intentionally unchecked layer as a generation default. This requirement governs the initial generated-project state only: after opening, a user's deliberate visibility changes may be saved and must not be overwritten by this requirement.~~ **Superseded only in its blanket every-present-layer visibility scope, not deleted; see FR-QPB-136 (revised; Decision Log D-94) immediately below.**
- **FR-QPB-136 (MVP; revised; Decision Log D-94):** On the first open of every newly generated project, every present `Survey data` layer and every present `Basemap` layer must be enabled/checked (visible) by default. Every present `Reference` layer must likewise be enabled/checked by default unless it is the registered `occurrence_probability_multiband` multiband raster lookup source at `reference/rasters/occurrence_probability_multiband.tif`; that one lookup raster must be registered in the project and remain addressable by the project's probability-lookup expressions, but must be intentionally unchecked/default-hidden. The exception is limited to that lookup raster only: it does not permit hiding a survey, basemap, uploaded reference/extent, accepted-name lookup table, or any other non-lookup reference layer. This requirement governs the initial generated-project state only: after opening, a user's deliberate visibility changes may be saved and must not be overwritten by this requirement.
- **FR-QPB-137 (MVP; new; Decision Log D-94; offline layer-selection parity):** Offline VWorld basemap generation must use the same supported-layer selection model as online basemap generation: the selectable set is the supported VWorld layer set determined under FR-QPB-071 (revised), and the user must explicitly select one member of that set. The resulting offline build configuration must carry that selected layer identity explicitly; a missing, blank, stale, or unsupported selection must fail before tile retrieval and before project promotion, with no implicit `Base` (or any other) default. The selected identity must be used consistently for offline tile retrieval, MBTiles metadata, and generated-project source identity; this does not embed the VWorld API key in the delivered offline project and does not alter FR-QPB-078/NFR-QPB-058.
- **FR-QPB-140 (new; Decision Log D-95; canonical reference-layer creation):** For every new Type 1–3 project after the canonical workbook has been confirmed and validated, the build must create the `ktsn_taxonomy_reference` GeoPackage attributes table and load it into the `Reference` group as the read-only layer `식물 분류 참조표`, with the schema and aliases in DR-QPB-079/081. It must also create/load the accepted-only `ktsn_accepted_name_lookup` compatibility layer. Both layers use project-relative GeoPackage access, are available offline, and are visible by default under FR-QPB-136; neither is a survey-data layer, relation parent, foreign-key target, or editable write-back destination. The source workbook itself is not copied into the generated project.

## 10. Functional Requirements — Online VWorld Basemap (Req §8.1)

- FR-QPB-070: The application must collect the VWorld API key as a secret input, masked in the UI, and must never write it to logs or diagnostic exports.
- ~~FR-QPB-071 (original)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see FR-QPB-071 (revised; Decision Log D-26) immediately below.** ~~The application must support the documented VWorld layer set: `Base`, `gray`, `midnight`, `Hybrid`, `Satellite`.~~ (This text was copied directly from the Requirements Draft, `specs/QFIELD_PROJECT_BUILDER_REQUIREMENTS_EN.md:398-399`, which itself used the `gray`/lowercase-`midnight` spellings.)
- FR-QPB-071 (revised; Decision Log D-26): The application must obtain its supported VWorld layer set by querying the VWorld WMTS capabilities endpoint — `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml` — rather than trusting a hardcoded, Requirements-Draft-derived layer list, and must support every layer that endpoint advertises. As of this revision, the five layers currently known to be advertised by that endpoint are: `Base`, `White`, `Midnight`, `Hybrid`, `Satellite` — this corrects the prior `gray`/lowercase-`midnight` spellings in the original FR-QPB-071 above, which are now understood to have been an imprecise transcription in the Requirements Draft rather than VWorld's actual layer identifiers. This is a layer-discovery/naming correction to the existing VWorld online/offline basemap pipeline (Sections 10/11), not a new pipeline: the `{key}` placeholder and per-tile GetTile URL mechanics for actual tile retrieval (FR-QPB-072) are unchanged and unaffected; only the mechanism by which the application discovers/validates which layer names are legitimate is changed. The surrounding key-handling rules — FR-QPB-073, FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079, NFR-QPB-014, NFR-QPB-017–NFR-QPB-019, NFR-QPB-058 — are unaffected and continue to apply exactly as before. (Req §8.1; Decision Log D-26)
- ~~FR-QPB-072 (original)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see FR-QPB-072 (revised; Decision Log D-29) immediately below.** ~~The application must use the documented WMTS/XYZ GetTile URL pattern (`.../{key}/{layer}/{z}/{y}/{x}.png`) and must prefer HTTPS when the endpoint supports it. The URL scheme and template must be updatable via configuration, without a code change, because the external API may change.~~
- FR-QPB-072 (revised; Decision Log D-29): For the generated project's **online** VWorld basemap layer only (Section 10), the application must add that layer using QGIS's native WMTS provider, connected via the VWorld WMTS capabilities endpoint URL — `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml` (the same endpoint FR-QPB-071 (revised; Decision Log D-26) already uses for layer discovery) — rather than by the application itself constructing a per-tile XYZ URL template (`.../{key}/{layer}/{z}/{y}/{x}.png`) and adding it as a `type=xyz` raster layer. QGIS itself must negotiate the specific layer, tile matrix set, and tile format from the capabilities document at connection time; the application must not hand QGIS a manually built GetTile template for this online layer. The capabilities endpoint URL must remain updatable via configuration, without a code change, because the external API may change. **This revision applies only to the online layer's connection mechanism (Section 10).** It does not apply to Section 11 (offline MBTiles generation, FR-QPB-080–089): that pipeline downloads individual tiles itself via ordinary HTTP requests to assemble a `.mbtiles` file — a fundamentally different mechanism from a live, QGIS-managed layer connection — and must keep using concrete, individually-fetchable per-tile GetTile URLs exactly as before (FR-QPB-084 steps (1)/(3); the offline tile-downloader in `qfield_builder/mbtiles.py`/`vworld_tiles.py` is unchanged). It also does not apply to FR-QPB-071 (revised; Decision Log D-26), the layer-*discovery* mechanism — a separate concern (which layer names exist) from this decision (how the online layer connects at runtime) — which is unaffected in substance, even though both now reference the same capabilities endpoint URL for their respective purposes.
- **FR-QPB-072 (further clarified; Decision Log D-97 — supplements, and does not replace, the preceding native-WMTS connection requirement):** For an **online** project whose user selected the currently supported VWorld layer identifier `Satellite`, supplied a VWorld key that VWorld accepts for the selected WMTS service, and accepted the existing VWorld-key embedding consent (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076), the generated project must open in QField and load that selected `Satellite` imagery. QField must not show a missing-layer, repair-data-source, or equivalent source-repair warning for that layer. A correct-looking saved URI, a parsed `.qgs` datasource, or an offline/desktop-only structural assertion alone does **not** establish this result: the selected layer must render in QField on an iPhone under usable network connectivity. This clarification changes neither the native-WMTS mechanism above nor the supported-layer discovery, VWorld-key masking/consent boundary, offline MBTiles pipeline, or offline no-delivered-key rule.
- ~~FR-QPB-073 (revised; closes former Open Question O-10; Decision Log D-21; reviewed, not textually changed, under Decision Log D-29)~~ — **superseded in one clause only, not deleted; see FR-QPB-073 (further revised; Decision Log D-45) immediately below.** ~~Because an online VWorld WMTS layer requires the API key at QField runtime, the application **may** embed the user-provided VWorld API key in the online layer's URI inside the generated `.qgs` file — but only as a single, narrowly scoped exception, and only after the explicit informed-consent flow in FR-QPB-076. This is the **only** permitted generated-project exception for storing a provider API key in project output; it applies solely to the VWorld online-layer runtime requirement (FR-QPB-079). (Reviewed under Decision Log D-29: this wording refers generically to "the online layer's URI," not to any specific URL shape, so it remains accurate now that the online layer connects via the WMTS capabilities endpoint URL — where the key still appears as the same `{key}` path segment — instead of a per-tile GetTile URL; no textual revision was needed.)~~
- FR-QPB-073 (further revised; closes former Open Question O-10; Decision Log D-21; reviewed, not textually changed, under Decision Log D-29; further revised, one clause only, under Decision Log D-45): Because an online VWorld WMTS layer requires the API key at QField runtime, the application **may** embed the user-provided VWorld API key in the online layer's URI inside the generated `.qgs` file — but only as a single, narrowly scoped exception, and only after the explicit informed-consent flow in FR-QPB-076. **This was originally recorded (Decision Log D-21) as the *only* permitted generated-project exception for storing a provider API key in project output. Decision Log D-45 supersedes that specific "only" framing by adding a second, independently consent-gated exception for the Pl@ntNet API key (new FR-QPB-114/FR-QPB-115, Section 13.1a) — this VWorld exception is otherwise entirely unchanged and continues to apply solely to the VWorld online-layer runtime requirement (FR-QPB-079, revised).** (Reviewed under Decision Log D-29: this wording refers generically to "the online layer's URI," not to any specific URL shape, so it remains accurate now that the online layer connects via the WMTS capabilities endpoint URL — where the key still appears as the same `{key}` path segment — instead of a per-tile GetTile URL; no textual revision was needed.)
- FR-QPB-076 (new; Decision Log D-21): Before embedding the VWorld key, the application must present an explicit consent step that: explains the `.qgs` file will contain the API key in readable form; explains that anyone who receives or opens the project folder may be able to extract the key; requires an explicit confirmation checkbox (not merely an informational dialog) before the key is embedded; recommends using a dedicated VWorld key and any access restrictions the provider supports; and clearly distinguishes this online-layer exception from offline MBTiles generation, which does not retain the key in the delivered project (FR-QPB-078).
- FR-QPB-077 (new; Decision Log D-21): If the user declines the consent step in FR-QPB-076, the application must not embed the key and must not create an immediately usable online VWorld layer in the generated project. It may instead omit the online layer and explain to the user that it can be configured manually later.
- FR-QPB-078 (new; Decision Log D-21): For offline MBTiles generation, the VWorld API key may be used only during tile retrieval and must not remain in the generated project once the `.mbtiles` file has been completed; the offline project must reference only the local `.mbtiles` file, never a URL containing the key. (Reconciles with NFR-QPB-058.)
- ~~FR-QPB-079 (new; Decision Log D-21)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see FR-QPB-079 (revised; Decision Log D-45) immediately below.** ~~The FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076 exception applies only to the VWorld online-layer runtime requirement. It must **not** be automatically extended to the Pl@ntNet API key or to any other credential; no other generated-project artifact may contain a provider API key in any form.~~
- FR-QPB-079 (revised; Decision Log D-45): The FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-078 VWorld online-layer exception and the new FR-QPB-114/FR-QPB-115 Pl@ntNet-key exception (Section 13.1a) are each independent, narrowly scoped, consent-gated exceptions to this specification's general no-embedded-provider-credential rule. Per the stakeholder's explicit decision (Decision Log D-45), the Pl@ntNet API key is no longer categorically excluded from ever being embedded in a generated project — the prior blanket rule above ("must not be automatically extended to the Pl@ntNet API key") is superseded specifically for this one, narrowly scoped, consent-gated case (embedding solely as the `qpb_plantnet_api_key` QGIS project variable, FR-QPB-114). This remains a **closed, enumerated list of exactly two exceptions**: it must not be further, automatically extended to any other credential, or to any broader Pl@ntNet-related storage location than the single project variable named above, without its own explicit stakeholder decision and Decision Log entry. Outside these two enumerated exceptions, no other generated-project artifact may contain a provider API key in any form.
- FR-QPB-074: The generated QGIS project must include visible attribution to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) VWorld WMTS/TMS API, substantially equivalent to: *"This basemap uses the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport VWorld WMTS/TMS API under the Korea Open Government License Type 1 (attribution required). https://www.vworld.kr"* (Decision Log D-18).
- FR-QPB-075: The same attribution text must also appear in `MANIFEST.json` and in the user-facing transfer/validation documentation (Section 12), and must remain present and correct after the project folder is copied to and used on a QField device. (Decision Log D-18)

## 11. Functional Requirements — Offline MBTiles Generation (Req §8.2–§8.4)

- FR-QPB-080: Offline mode must accept either an extent drawn on the map or a Polygon/MultiPolygon from an uploaded GeoPackage or zipped Shapefile, and must use the bounding envelope/bbox of the selected geometry as the download extent. Every tile intersecting the bbox must be downloaded; edge tiles may extend to normal tile boundaries; polygon clipping is not required.
- FR-QPB-081: Before generation, the UI must show: bbox coordinates, area, selected min/max zoom levels, expected tile count, estimated output size, and a visible 1 GiB hard limit.
- DR-QPB-060: The final `.mbtiles` file must not exceed 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes). 900 MiB must be used as the pre-generation acceptance threshold, to preserve overhead/estimation error.
- FR-QPB-082: Size must be estimated from tile count and representative `Content-Length` samples where possible, using a conservative percentile and safety multiplier rather than only an average. If the estimate exceeds 900 MiB, the application must block creation and prompt the user to reduce bbox size, reduce max zoom, or choose a lower resolution.
- FR-QPB-083: Generation must occur into a temporary location with size monitored during creation. If final output exceeds 1 GiB, the application must abort, remove the incomplete temporary output, and return the user to extent/resolution selection.
- FR-QPB-084: The required pipeline is: (1) determine all VWorld tiles intersecting the approved bbox at every selected zoom level; (2) display tile count and conservative size estimate before downloading; (3) download/render tiles while respecting VWorld authentication, quota, rate-limit, retry, and caching requirements; (4) write tiles and required metadata into a standards-compatible `.mbtiles` file in a temporary build directory; (5) verify MBTiles coverage contains the approved bbox and that min/max zoom match the user's selection; (6) verify the final file does not exceed 1 GiB; (7) add the MBTiles layer to the QGIS project using a relative path.
- FR-QPB-085: QGIS/GDAL "Build Overviews" must **not** be run as a separate step; the MBTiles file's stored zoom levels already provide the multi-resolution pyramid.
- DR-QPB-061: MBTiles metadata must include at minimum a stable name, format, geographic bounds, minimum zoom, and maximum zoom. Tile-row orientation and metadata must be verified against the explicitly supported QGIS/QField versions (see NFR-QPB-001). The application must not report success until the generated MBTiles opens in the project and renders at representative locations/zoom levels.
- NFR-QPB-003 (resolved; Decision Log D-18; closes the licensing portion of former Open Question O-5): VWorld/MOLIT's WMTS/TMS API is published on the Korea Public Data Portal (https://www.data.go.kr/data/3046388/openapi.do) as free and licensed under the Korea Open Government License (KOGL) Type 1, and the published KOGL Type-1 terms (https://www.kogl.or.kr/info/licenseType1.do) permit online and offline use, modification, and commercial use of the licensed work provided the source is attributed. On this basis, offline MBTiles generation remains in MVP scope, subject to the operational conditions in FR-QPB-086–FR-QPB-089 and NFR-QPB-058–NFR-QPB-059 below. This is no longer treated as an unresolved release blocker.
- FR-QPB-086: The implementation must comply with the traffic quota, concurrency limits, and rate limits associated with the user's own VWorld API key; tile-download requests must use bounded concurrency and rate limiting rather than unbounded parallel requests. (Decision Log D-18)
- FR-QPB-087: The number of tile requests required for a given bbox/zoom selection must be estimated and shown to the user before generation begins (this restates and cross-references FR-QPB-081). (Decision Log D-18)
- FR-QPB-088: If the VWorld API returns a quota-exceeded, authorization, or rate-limit error during tile download, the application must terminate the download gracefully with a clear, non-technical message, and must leave no partial `.mbtiles` deliverable in the final output folder (see E-QPB-009, E-QPB-013). (Decision Log D-18)
- FR-QPB-089: The application must not attempt to bypass VWorld provider restrictions (quota, authentication, or rate limits) by any technical means. (Decision Log D-18)
- NFR-QPB-058 (reconciled; Decision Log D-18, D-21): During offline MBTiles generation, the VWorld API key must be used only for the tile-download requests themselves; it must not be written into the resulting `.mbtiles` file, `MANIFEST.json`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, or any other file placed in the mobile transfer folder. This is now explicitly reconciled with the narrowly scoped online-layer exception in FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079: this rule governs the offline MBTiles pipeline and its output; the online-layer exception governs only the `.qgs` online-layer URL, and only after explicit consent. Former Open Question O-10 is closed.
- NFR-QPB-059: Application/user documentation must state that VWorld/MOLIT provider terms, quotas, and licensing can change, and should be rechecked for each release. (Decision Log D-18)

## 12. Functional Requirements — Validation, Manifest, and Transfer (Req §10, §12.5, §13)

- FR-QPB-090 (further revised; Decision Log D-87 — closes O-42 and supersedes D-85's dual-trigger formulation without deleting it): The generated result must be a self-contained directory containing (names may be adjusted by later architecture decisions, but the structural roles below must exist): the `.qgs` project; `data/<project>.gpkg`; an `attachments/` tree; `basemap/` (offline mode only); `README_TRANSFER_KO.md`; `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`; `MANIFEST.json`; and a project-specific `<project_slug>.qml`/JS plugin sidecar (FR-QPB-100). ~~Under Decision Log D-85, the sidecar was generated whenever either `identification_enabled = true` or the HTML-report export feature was present/enabled.~~ **Superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-87):** the HTML-report export feature is always present/enabled, with no wizard/config toggle, so the sidecar must be generated for **every** generated project regardless of `identification_enabled`. The `reference/` folder remains conditional on `identification_enabled = true`; this clarification does not extend that folder's trigger. Identification-specific content inside the unconditional sidecar is also conditional: the "Identify attached photos" reminder button and identification write-back polling `Timer` must be included only when `identification_enabled = true`, while the Export HTML Report button/report mechanism is included unconditionally.
- FR-QPB-091: All references inside the generated project must remain relative; the folder must remain portable as a single unit.
- FR-QPB-092: `MANIFEST.json` must identify all required files and must be able to detect a missing attachment, plugin (post-MVP), database, or basemap before transfer.
- FR-QPB-093: The application must generate a Korean-language end-user transfer notice (`README_TRANSFER_KO.md`) instructing the user: do not package the project with QFieldSync (it can replace UUID-based primary-key/relation behavior with `fid`-based behavior and may remove or alter foreign-key-based relations); copy the entire generated folder (including `.qgs`, `.gpkg`, attachments, plugin if present, reference assets if present, and offline basemap if present) directly to the phone; open the local project in QField; after fieldwork, close the project and copy the entire folder back to the computer; do not copy only the GeoPackage, and do not rename or move files inside the folder. The notice must also explain Android and iOS transfer options in non-technical language and advise keeping a backup before replacing an older desktop copy.
- FR-QPB-094: The build must produce a final validation report (`VALIDATION_REPORT.json`) confirming the checks in Section 17 (Acceptance Criteria) that are applicable to the generated project.

## 13. Post-MVP Functional Requirements — Pl@ntNet / KTSN / Occurrence Probability (Req §9)

These requirements are recorded for completeness and future planning. **None of them are required for MVP acceptance** (Section 4.2).

The guaranteed-baseline **"Identify attached photos"** action (Decision Log D-13/D-14) remains a **`QML Widget` editor-widget type** embedded directly in the attribute form of the relevant layer — Type 1's `inventory_observation` layer, or Type 2/3's `observation` layer (Section 8.1–8.3) — built via the same `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField` mechanism (FR-QPB-057), giving the embedded QML direct read access to the currently-edited feature's attribute values. Within the embedded QML, the action must: request permission before activation as required by QField; **read the selected relative attachment file's byte content using QField's own native `QfFileUtils.readFileContent(filePath)` method — a QField-specific singleton exposed to QML via `import org.qfield.core`, restricted to files within the current project directory (which matches this application's own attachment files, since they live inside the generated project folder) — and must NOT rely on QML's own `XMLHttpRequest` object to open a `file://` URL directly for this purpose.** This corrects the D-45 text's claim, retained struck-through above, that "no separate QField networking component exists or is required for this": Qt's own QML `XMLHttpRequest` implementation cannot read local files by default, and QField's own application source code never lifts that restriction (confirmed by direct research; see Decision Log D-46 for the full citation), so a plain QML `XMLHttpRequest` genuinely cannot read a local attachment file inside QField. Read EXIF GPS when present; call Pl@ntNet via QML's own native `XMLHttpRequest` **for the network POST request itself** — this network-call mechanism is unaffected by the correction above, which concerns only reading the local file's bytes, not submitting the HTTP request — submitting the byte content already obtained via `QfFileUtils.readFileContent()` as the multipart request body, when connected — authenticating using the Pl@ntNet API key read from the `qpb_plantnet_api_key` project variable via `expression.evaluate("@qpb_plantnet_api_key")` when that variable has been embedded under the consent-gated exception in FR-QPB-114/FR-QPB-115 (Decision Log D-45), or otherwise prompting the field user to enter the key manually in QField per FR-QPB-116's decline-path fallback; queue the request when offline; display the top three candidates; run KTSN and probability enrichment (the ~247 MB combined KTSN/probability reference data this enrichment step depends on is bundled into the generated project's own `reference/` folder per FR-QPB-112 — Decision Log D-35, closing former Open Question O-16; see Open Questions O-17 and O-18 for a project-size consideration and a scope-conflict consideration this bundling decision raises but does not itself resolve); allow one candidate to be selected; and update the correct GeoPackage record without changing `fid` or breaking UUID relations.

  **Platform-scope caveat, explicitly disclosed and accepted (Decision Log D-46):** `import org.qfield.core`/`QfFileUtils` is a QField-specific QML module, registered only by QField's own native C++ application code; QGIS Desktop's plain PyQGIS-hosted QML engine never registers this module, and QML provides no conditional/optional import mechanism — so when this module cannot be resolved, the entire embedded QML component fails to load, not merely the file-read call within it. Adopting this mechanism to correctly fix real, confirmed on-device QField photo-reading is expected — and is accepted as a disclosed tradeoff, per the stakeholder's explicit decision (Decision Log D-46) — to make this same embedded widget fail to load/render at all when the same generated project is opened in QGIS Desktop specifically. QField is the confirmed, approved target platform for this guaranteed-manual "Identify attached photos" baseline (Decision Log D-31); QGIS Desktop has only ever served as a secondary, exploratory test surface for this specific widget, not a requirement this specification imposes on the photo-identification network-request capability specifically. This is a deliberate, disclosed, stakeholder-approved tradeoff (Decision Log D-46), not a defect, and does not reopen or alter this widget's other rendering/architecture requirements above.~~ (This text never specified any resize, compression, or size-limiting step for the photo bytes before they are embedded in the Pl@ntNet multipart request body — a genuine specification omission; real-device testing confirmed an unresized, full-resolution photo can trigger an HTTP `413 Request Entity Too Large` rejection. See FR-QPB-101 (further revised; Decision Log D-52) below.)
- FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-52; adds a mandatory photo-resize step only — does not reopen, reword, or alter D-31/D-35/D-43/D-45/D-46's other substance): All rules from FR-QPB-101 (further revised; Decision Log D-46) above remain correct and are restated here, unchanged in substance, except for one addition: a mandatory photo-resize step, inserted between reading the original attachment file's bytes and submitting those bytes to Pl@ntNet. The guaranteed-baseline **"Identify attached photos"** action (Decision Log D-13/D-14) remains a **`QML Widget` editor-widget type** embedded directly in the attribute form of the relevant layer — Type 1's `inventory_observation` layer, or Type 2/3's `observation` layer (Section 8.1–8.3) — built via the same `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField` mechanism (FR-QPB-057), giving the embedded QML direct read access to the currently-edited feature's attribute values. Within the embedded QML, the action must: request permission before activation as required by QField; read the selected relative attachment file's byte content using QField's own native `QfFileUtils.readFileContent(filePath)` method, restricted to files within the current project directory, and must NOT rely on QML's own `XMLHttpRequest` object to open a `file://` URL directly for this purpose (Decision Log D-46); read EXIF GPS when present; **before those original bytes are ever included in the Pl@ntNet multipart request body, resize the photo via a temporary copy — never the original attachment file (Decision Log D-52):** write the original photo's already-read bytes to a new temporary file using the already-confirmed `FileUtils.writeFileContent()`; call `FileUtils.restrictImageSize(tempFilePath, 1280)` on that temporary copy only — QField's native, confirmed method (`src/core/utils/fileutils.h`, real QField v4.2.4 C++ source) that restricts a given image file's width and height to a maximum size, resizing the file at the given path **in place**, with no separate output-path parameter and no return value; read back the now-resized bytes from the temporary file using the already-confirmed `FileUtils.readFileContent()`; use those resized bytes — not the original, unresized bytes — as the photo content submitted in the Pl@ntNet multipart request body; and clean up the temporary file afterward by overwriting it with empty content via `FileUtils.writeFileContent(tempFilePath, "")` — never via `FileUtils.deleteFiles()`, which Decision Log D-50 already found unreliable/silently-no-op on at least one tested device. **The original attachment file — the one referenced by the feature's own photo-path attribute and stored in the project's GeoPackage/attachments — must remain completely unmodified and at its original, full resolution at all times; only the temporary copy actually submitted to Pl@ntNet is ever downsized.** Call Pl@ntNet via QML's own native `XMLHttpRequest` for the network POST request itself — this network-call mechanism is unaffected by either this entry's or Decision Log D-46's corrections, both of which concern only how the submitted photo bytes are obtained/prepared, not how the HTTP request itself is submitted — submitting the resized byte content described above as the multipart request body, when connected — authenticating using the Pl@ntNet API key read from the `qpb_plantnet_api_key` project variable via `expression.evaluate("@qpb_plantnet_api_key")` when that variable has been embedded under the consent-gated exception in FR-QPB-114/FR-QPB-115 (Decision Log D-45), or otherwise prompting the field user to enter the key manually in QField per FR-QPB-116's decline-path fallback; queue the request when offline; display the top three candidates; run KTSN and probability enrichment (the ~247 MB combined KTSN/probability reference data this enrichment step depends on is bundled into the generated project's own `reference/` folder per FR-QPB-112 — Decision Log D-35, closing former Open Question O-16; see Open Questions O-17 and O-18 for a project-size consideration and a scope-conflict consideration this bundling decision raises but does not itself resolve); allow one candidate to be selected; and update the correct GeoPackage record without changing `fid` or breaking UUID relations.

  **Platform-scope caveat, explicitly disclosed and accepted (Decision Log D-46) — unchanged by Decision Log D-52's photo-resize addition, restated here unaltered:** `import org.qfield.core`/`QfFileUtils` is a QField-specific QML module, registered only by QField's own native C++ application code; QGIS Desktop's plain PyQGIS-hosted QML engine never registers this module, and QML provides no conditional/optional import mechanism — so when this module cannot be resolved, the entire embedded QML component fails to load, not merely the file-read call within it. Adopting this mechanism to correctly fix real, confirmed on-device QField photo-reading is expected — and is accepted as a disclosed tradeoff, per the stakeholder's explicit decision (Decision Log D-46) — to make this same embedded widget fail to load/render at all when the same generated project is opened in QGIS Desktop specifically. QField is the confirmed, approved target platform for this guaranteed-manual "Identify attached photos" baseline (Decision Log D-31); QGIS Desktop has only ever served as a secondary, exploratory test surface for this specific widget, not a requirement this specification imposes on the photo-identification network-request capability specifically. This is a deliberate, disclosed, stakeholder-approved tradeoff (Decision Log D-46), not a defect, and does not reopen or alter this widget's other rendering/architecture requirements above.

  **Naming note, disclosed not resolved (Decision Log D-52):** the resize step above uses the `FileUtils` singleton naming already established for the write-back mechanism in Decision Log D-50 (`FileUtils.writeFileContent()`), matching this entry's own confirmed v4.2.4 source-inspection finding for `restrictImageSize()`. This entry does not address or reconcile any naming difference between this and the `QfFileUtils`/`org.qfield.core` naming used above for the original file-read step (Decision Log D-46) — reconciling that naming question, if one turns out to be needed, is outside this entry's scope and is not decided here.
- ~~FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-90; Type 2/3 interaction correction)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-93) immediately below.** ~~For a Type 2 or Type 3 `observation` feature, the embedded **"Identify attached photos"** action must start the identification workflow immediately when the user clicks its Identify control. The application must not insert an application-authored consent/confirmation popup, modal, or other intermediate **OK** step between that click and the identification attempt; the existing "request permission before activation" behavior in the preceding FR-QPB-101 forms is superseded for this Type 2/3 interaction only, not deleted from the historical record. The action must remain usable while the plant-observation attribute form is open, so no dialog may be placed behind or underneath that form in a way that prevents the user from completing the action. This does not authorize automatic identification merely because a photo was attached (FR-QPB-102 remains unchanged), does not remove the separate desktop wizard's Pl@ntNet-key embedding consent (FR-QPB-115), and does not prohibit a permission prompt that QField itself unavoidably owns and requires at the operating-system/runtime level; the application must not add a second confirmation dialog around such a platform prompt.~~
- **FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-93; generated-widget direct-identification rule):** For every generated identification `QML Widget` that presents the **`사진으로 동정하기`** button, clicking that button must directly invoke the identification workflow. This applies to the Type 1 `inventory_observation` widget and the Type 2/3 `observation` widgets whenever they are generated; the application must not insert an application-owned consent/confirmation popup, modal, or intermediate **OK** step between the click and the identification attempt, nor render/open such a dialog behind or underneath the active attribute form. The handler either proceeds to the identification request or shows the existing request-level validation/error state. Type 4 (`vegetation_mapping`) is outside this interaction rule because its current `community` schema has no photo or identification fields and no identification widget/button is generated (DR-QPB-050/054); this decision neither adds one nor changes Type 4 behavior. This does not authorize automatic identification merely because a photo was attached (FR-QPB-102 remains unchanged), does not remove or weaken the separate desktop wizard's consent for embedding a Pl@ntNet API key (FR-QPB-115), and does not alter the declined-embedding manual-key path (FR-QPB-116). A permission prompt that QField or the operating system itself unavoidably owns is not an application-owned dialog under this rule; the application must not wrap it in a second confirmation dialog.
- FR-QPB-102 (post-MVP, conditional): Silent/automatic identification triggered immediately after a photo attachment is added must not be implemented, and must not be claimed to the user as available, unless a feasibility spike confirms it can be implemented reliably in QField on **both** iOS and Android (Decision Log D-14). Until that spike passes, the application must never claim automatic behavior that does not exist.

They must instead be verified empirically as a natural byproduct of implementing and testing the manual baseline correctly. ### 13.1a Pl@ntNet API key handling and embedding (post-MVP)

This subsection mirrors, for the Pl@ntNet API key, the VWorld online-layer consent-gated key-embedding pattern already established in Section 10 (FR-QPB-073, FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-078; Decision Log D-21). It records a new, explicit stakeholder decision (Decision Log D-45) that extends the same pattern to Pl@ntNet, superseding FR-QPB-079's prior blanket exclusion of Pl@ntNet from any embedding exception (see FR-QPB-079, revised, Section 10).

- FR-QPB-114 (new; Decision Log D-45; mirrors FR-QPB-073's VWorld online-layer exception): Because the embedded QField `QML Widget` identification action (FR-QPB-101) calls Pl@ntNet directly from the field device, in-field, via QML's `XMLHttpRequest`, and QField itself provides no separate secrets-management mechanism, the application **may** embed the user-provided Pl@ntNet API key into the generated project — but only as a second, narrowly scoped exception, mirroring the VWorld online-layer exception, and only after the explicit informed-consent flow in FR-QPB-115. The key must be embedded as a **QGIS project variable**, named exactly `qpb_plantnet_api_key`, set on the generated `.qgs` project, matching the exact variable name the embedded `QML Widget` identification action reads at runtime via `expression.evaluate("@qpb_plantnet_api_key")` (this read-side mechanism was confirmed/fixed in a separate, already-completed implementation round; this requirement only obligates the build pipeline to write the same variable name, so the two sides stay consistent). The key must **not** be embedded in any other generated-project artifact: not the GeoPackage, not the `<project_slug>.qml` plugin file's own literal source text, not `MANIFEST.json`'s content beyond the boolean flag in new NFR-QPB-071, not `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, not application logs, and not any temporary filename. Per Decision Log D-45, this is now the second of exactly two enumerated, narrowly scoped generated-project provider-credential exceptions this specification permits — the other being FR-QPB-073's VWorld online-layer exception (Section 10) — and FR-QPB-079 (revised) records that this list is closed and must not be further, automatically extended without its own explicit stakeholder decision.
- FR-QPB-115 (new; Decision Log D-45; mirrors FR-QPB-076's VWorld consent flow): Before embedding the Pl@ntNet key, the application must present an explicit consent step — presented once the user has opted in to photo identification at Step 5 (FR-QPB-037/FR-QPB-039) and supplied the key (FR-QPB-117) — that: explains the generated project will contain the Pl@ntNet API key in readable form, as a QGIS project variable inside the `.qgs` file; explains that anyone who receives or opens the project folder may be able to extract the key; requires an explicit confirmation checkbox (not merely an informational dialog) before the key is embedded; recommends using a dedicated Pl@ntNet key, or a usage/quota-restricted key, if Pl@ntNet's own account settings support such a restriction; and clearly identifies this as the same category of disclosed, accepted risk already approved for the VWorld online-layer exception (FR-QPB-076), so the user is not asked to evaluate an unfamiliar risk in isolation.
- FR-QPB-116 (new; Decision Log D-45; mirrors FR-QPB-077's VWorld decline path): If the user declines the consent step in FR-QPB-115, the application must not embed the Pl@ntNet key anywhere in the generated project. The generated project's Pl@ntNet identification feature (the embedded `QML Widget` action, FR-QPB-101) must still be present and usable, but must require the field user to enter the Pl@ntNet API key manually within QField at the point of use — i.e., the application's current (pre-Decision-Log-D-45) behavior, in which the generated project's identification feature requires manual in-QField key entry, continues to exist as the decline-path fallback; it is not removed by this decision, only demoted to the non-default path taken when consent is withheld.
- FR-QPB-117 (new; Decision Log D-45; new wizard step/field extending Section 6.5's Step 5): When the user opts in to photo identification at the Step 5 toggle (FR-QPB-037), once the identification subsystem exists per FR-QPB-039, the wizard must collect the Pl@ntNet API key as a secret input, masked in the UI (mirroring FR-QPB-070's treatment of the VWorld key), and must never write it to logs or diagnostic exports (NFR-QPB-011). This collection step is a prerequisite to, and distinct from, the separate embedding-consent step required by FR-QPB-115: collecting the key does not, by itself, authorize embedding it in the generated project — only an accepted consent checkbox (FR-QPB-115) does that; if consent is declined, the collected key is used only for the desktop application's own local validation/session purposes (FR-QPB-039, NFR-QPB-012) and is not written into the generated project (FR-QPB-116).
