What changes is the storage mechanism: the key must be stored in an application-managed, locally-encrypted file (`credentials.enc`, placed in this application's own local application-data directory — a new convention this specification introduces here, since none previously existed anywhere in this specification: ~~macOS `~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\`~~ — superseded, not deleted, by Decision Log D-81: ~~macOS `~/Library/Application Support/QFieldKit/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\QFieldKit\`~~ — **further superseded, not deleted, by Decision Log D-86: macOS `~/Library/Application Support/FieldBuild Kit/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\FieldBuild Kit\`** — see new NFR-QPB-081 (further revised, Decision Log D-86) for the required one-time migration of any already-remembered key from the old, prior-name-derived directory into this new one), encrypted with a key derived from the password established per new NFR-QPB-073's first-launch encrypted-storage setup step, using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (at least 600,000 iterations, and a randomly generated, per-installation salt of at least 16 bytes, stored alongside the encrypted file since the salt is not itself required to be secret) to derive a 32-byte key, used with `cryptography.fernet.Fernet` (AES-128-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256, an authenticated symmetric-encryption scheme) — a real, complete, well-documented construction, not a custom/novel cryptographic scheme invented for this requirement. The operating system's credential store (the `keyring` package; macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager) must no longer be used anywhere in this application's own key-retention code path. Otherwise (no "Remember this key" opt-in selected, or no encrypted-storage password yet established/declined, per NFR-QPB-073) the key must be retained only for the current application session, exactly as before. **Disclosed trade-off (Decision Log D-53):** this moves the key's at-rest protection from a well-vetted, OS-hardened credential store — which, particularly on macOS, benefits from OS-level access controls and, in many configurations, hardware-backed protections — to an application-managed encryption-at-rest scheme whose protection depends only on the strength of the user's own chosen password and this KDF's work factor; this is recorded honestly as a real, accepted security trade-off, not asserted as a strictly-more-secure replacement.
- ~~NFR-QPB-019 (new; Decision Log D-21)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see NFR-QPB-019 (revised; Decision Log D-45) immediately below.** ~~The VWorld online-layer key-embedding exception (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079) applies only to the VWorld online-layer runtime requirement; it must not be automatically extended to the Pl@ntNet API key or to any other credential (see also FR-QPB-079).~~
- NFR-QPB-019 (revised; Decision Log D-45): The VWorld online-layer key-embedding exception (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-078) and the Pl@ntNet key-embedding exception (new FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-116, Section 13.1a) are each independently scoped: neither extends automatically to the other's credential, nor to any other credential. Per Decision Log D-45, the Pl@ntNet exception is now a second, explicitly and independently authorized case — not an automatic extension of the VWorld exception, and not a general precedent that any future credential receives the same treatment without its own explicit stakeholder decision and Decision Log entry (see also FR-QPB-079, revised). **Reviewed under Decision Log D-53 and confirmed unaffected in substance and not textually altered:** this entry governs which *generated-project embedding exception* extends to which credential (a distinct concern from the desktop application's own local "Remember this key" storage mechanism, which NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072, revised, govern) — it says nothing about, and is not in tension with, D-53's storage-mechanism change.
- NFR-QPB-071 (new; Decision Log D-45; mirrors NFR-QPB-017 for the Pl@ntNet key): `MANIFEST.json` may record only a boolean security-warning flag indicating that the generated project contains an embedded Pl@ntNet API key (as the `qpb_plantnet_api_key` project variable, FR-QPB-114); it must never contain the key itself. This flag is independent of, and additional to, the existing VWorld online-layer security-warning flag (NFR-QPB-017) — a generated project may carry either flag, both, or neither, depending on which consent step(s) the user accepted. **Reviewed under Decision Log D-53 and confirmed unaffected in substance and not textually altered:** this entry governs only the `MANIFEST.json` embedded-in-generated-project disclosure flag, not the desktop application's own local storage mechanism.
- ~~NFR-QPB-072 (new; Decision Log D-45; mirrors NFR-QPB-018 for the Pl@ntNet key)~~ — **superseded, not deleted, for its storage-mechanism clause only; its consent-gated "Remember this key" opt-in behavior is unchanged and restated below; see NFR-QPB-072 (revised; Decision Log D-53) immediately below.** ~~The desktop application may remember the user's Pl@ntNet API key across sessions only when the user explicitly selects a "Remember this key" option (mirroring the existing VWorld "Remember this key" option, NFR-QPB-018), in which case the key must be stored in the operating system's credential store; otherwise the key must be retained only for the current application session. This is consistent with, and does not alter, NFR-QPB-012's existing "stored outside the GeoPackage, preferably in the OS credential store" rule for the Pl@ntNet key generally.~~
- NFR-QPB-072 (revised; Decision Log D-53; mirrors NFR-QPB-018 (revised) for the Pl@ntNet key; further revised, Decision Log D-81 — directory renamed, see NFR-QPB-018 (further revised) for the exact new path and new NFR-QPB-081 for the migration requirement; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — directory name corrected, see NFR-QPB-018 (further revised) for the exact corrected path): The desktop application may remember the user's Pl@ntNet API key across sessions only when the user explicitly selects a "Remember this key" option (mirroring the existing VWorld option, NFR-QPB-018 (revised)) — this consent-gated opt-in behavior is unchanged from Decision Log D-45. The storage mechanism mirrors NFR-QPB-018 (revised) exactly: an application-managed, locally-encrypted `credentials.enc` file in this application's own local application-data directory, encrypted with a key derived via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (same parameters: at least 600,000 iterations, a randomly generated per-installation salt of at least 16 bytes) from the same first-launch password (new NFR-QPB-073), using `cryptography.fernet.Fernet` for the encryption itself — the VWorld and Pl@ntNet keys may be held within the same encrypted file or as independently encrypted entries, but neither uses the operating system's credential store, which must no longer be used anywhere in this application's own key-retention code path. Otherwise the key must be retained only for the current application session, exactly as before. This is consistent with, and updates, NFR-QPB-012's existing "stored outside the GeoPackage, preferably in the OS credential store" rule for the Pl@ntNet key generally — NFR-QPB-012 (revised; Decision Log D-53), above, reflects the same update. Subject to the same disclosed trade-off recorded under NFR-QPB-018 (revised)/Decision Log D-53. The application-data directory itself is the same one NFR-QPB-018 (further revised; Decision Log D-81; further corrected, Decision Log D-86) names — ~~`QFieldKit`~~-based **(corrected by Decision Log D-86: `FieldBuild Kit`-based)**, not `QField Project Builder`-based — and is migrated once, per new NFR-QPB-081, exactly as for the VWorld key.
- NFR-QPB-073 (new; Decision Log D-53; retrieval-time re-prompt trigger point confirmed by Decision Log D-55, closing Open Question O-21): On the first launch of the desktop application, or on any subsequent launch where no encrypted-storage password has yet been established (including after a prior decline — see below), the application must prompt the user to set a password used **solely** to derive the local encryption key described in NFR-QPB-018 (revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (revised), via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256. This prompt must not function as a general access-gate over any other application functionality — the wizard and every project-building capability must remain fully usable without ever supplying this password. **If the user declines/skips this prompt:** no password is established; the "Remember this key" option must be unavailable/disabled for that application session, falling back to the existing session-only retention already required by NFR-QPB-018 (revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (revised) for the non-remembered case; and this same setup prompt must be shown again at the next launch, since a password still has not been established. **If the user forgets a previously established password:** any previously remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key becomes permanently unrecoverable — decryption of `credentials.enc` fails, and no password-recovery mechanism exists or is implied by this requirement — the user must re-enter their API key(s) manually, and may establish a new encrypted-storage password to resume "Remember this key" behavior going forward. **Confirmed retrieval-time trigger point (Decision Log D-55, closing Open Question O-21):** the application must re-prompt for this password only at the specific point where a remembered VWorld or Pl@ntNet key would otherwise be auto-filled (e.g., the specific wizard step that would read a remembered key from `credentials.enc` to pre-populate a field) — never at general application startup, and never as a blanket access-gate shown before any other, unrelated part of the application is used. Outside that specific retrieval point, no password prompt is required to use the wizard or any project-building capability, consistent with this requirement's "not a general access-gate" rule above. The stakeholder's own choice, presented with a second, rejected alternative (a once-per-launch, upfront prompt before any wizard step), was explicit: prompt only at the point of use. If the user cannot supply the password correctly when prompted at that point, the forgotten-password consequence described above applies for that key.
- NFR-QPB-081 (new; Decision Log D-81; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — renamed-application/directory name corrected below): On first launch of the application after its rename to ~~"QFieldKit"~~ **"FieldBuild Kit" (corrected by Decision Log D-86)** (FR-QPB-131), the application must check whether the old, product-name-derived application-data directory (`~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/` on macOS; `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\` on Windows) exists and contains a `credentials.enc` file and its accompanying salt. If it does, **and** the new, ~~`QFieldKit`~~ **`FieldBuild Kit` (corrected by Decision Log D-86)**-named directory (NFR-QPB-018 (further revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (further revised)) does not yet contain its own `credentials.enc` file, the application must copy the old directory's `credentials.enc` file and salt into the new directory before any "Remember this key" retrieval is attempted for that session, so any already-remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key remains decryptable with the same, already-established encrypted-storage password (NFR-QPB-073) exactly as before the rename. **This migration copies; it never deletes.** The old directory (and every file within it) must be left completely untouched after a successful migration — a deliberate, disclosed choice (Decision Log D-81), not an oversight, given this project's own documented caution around destructive filesystem operations outside a generated project's own folder (see the QGIS-profile-isolation hardening recorded in `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, referenced in `CLAUDE.md`'s "Current status"); an automatic, unconditional deletion of a user's own Application-Support/AppData folder carries a real, avoidable risk for a small, one-time convenience gain, so this requirement deliberately does not delete it — a user or a later, separate cleanup pass may always remove the old, now-superseded folder manually. If the new directory already contains its own `credentials.enc` file (whether because migration already ran in a prior session, or because both directories happen to already exist independently), no migration is attempted, the new directory's own existing `credentials.enc` is treated as authoritative and left unmodified, and the old directory is, again, left completely untouched — no merge and no overwrite in either direction. If the old directory does not exist at all (a fresh install with no prior "QField Project Builder"-named installation), no migration is attempted and the application behaves exactly as NFR-QPB-018 (further revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (further revised) already describe for a project with no previously stored key.

### 14.2 Portability and offline behavior (Req §2.3, §12.5)

- NFR-QPB-020: All survey records, geometries, relations, selected identifications (post-MVP), and attachment paths must remain in the local project folder.
- NFR-QPB-021: The generated project must open without a missing-layer warning after the entire folder is moved to a different absolute path on disk.
- NFR-QPB-022: The generated project must remain fully functional after a computer → phone → computer round trip, with all attachment paths remaining relative and valid.
- NFR-QPB-023: No QFieldSync packaging step may be required or invoked anywhere in the supported workflow.

### 14.3 Compatibility (Decision Log D-9–D-11)

- NFR-QPB-030 (revised; Decision Log D-25): The application's **source code and packaging configuration** must remain genuinely cross-platform and support Windows and macOS as first-class MVP targets: no macOS-only (or Windows-only) assumption may be introduced into the application's own source, and the packaging configuration must remain usable, as-is, to produce a Windows build without a separate, divergent packaging setup. This source/configuration requirement is unchanged and unweakened by this revision. Actual **delivery of a built, installable Windows artifact** for this MVP release is a distinct concern, governed by FR-QPB-014 (revised; Decision Log D-25), which defers that specific deliverable to a required subsequent release.
- NFR-QPB-031: The generated project must support QField on both iOS and Android; it must not intentionally rely on iOS-only behavior or exclude Android. Required validation paths include macOS→iOS (primary), Windows→iOS, Windows→Android, and macOS→Android.
- NFR-QPB-032: The project must open in all explicitly supported QGIS and QField versions (see NFR-QPB-001).

### 14.4 Data integrity (Req §12.1)

- NFR-QPB-040: The generated GeoPackage must open in QGIS without a repair warning.
- NFR-QPB-041 (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior "required-photo" misinterpretation): Every domain UUID must be valid, unique, and non-null; no domain relation may reference `fid`; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` must return no rows; geometry types and CRS must match the selected survey template; spatial indexes must exist for all geometry layers; `cover` values outside 0–100 must be rejected; Type 1–3 photo relations must remain optional as specified in Section 8 — validation must never require a minimum photo count for any survey type, and the absence of any photo record must never be treated as an error or as blocking field completion.

### 14.5 Localization (Req §1; Decision Log D-28)

- NFR-QPB-070 (new; Decision Log D-28): All user-facing text produced by this application's own PySide6 desktop wizard UI — explicitly including labels, buttons, instructions, validation messages, warnings, progress messages, dialogs, and error messages — must be presented in Korean, because the application's intended end users are Korean. This requirement is scoped strictly to the application specified here (the PySide6 desktop wizard, its dialogs, and its own generated user-facing messages); it does not, and cannot, govern the third-party UI language of QGIS Desktop or QField themselves, both of which are outside this project's control, and this requirement must not be read as a broader promise about those applications' own displayed language. Internal identifiers, source-code symbols, file-format terms, and proper names may remain unchanged where translation would be inappropriate. Concrete examples of this carve-out: (1) file-format/technical terms such as `.gpkg`, `.qgs`, `MANIFEST.json`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, and `README_TRANSFER_KO.md`; (2) proper names such as VWorld, QField, QGIS, and Pl@ntNet; and (3) internal field/column identifiers (e.g. `site_id`, `fid`, `project_slug`) that are not displayed to the end user. This requirement does not apply to this specification document itself — the specification's own FR/NFR/DR/AC prose remains in English; only the shipped application's own UI strings are in scope.

### 14.6 Distributed reference-bundle integrity (Decision Log D-89)

- **NFR-QPB-082 (new; Decision Log D-89):** The final distributed application must be self-contained for the filtered reference-data workflow without shipping the raw source tables. Its packaged contents must contain only the validated filtered lookup artifacts required by FR-QPB-135/DR-QPB-073 and the required probability-raster set; no end user may need to download the source CSV/XLSX files or manually install them. Raw reference sources may be read by a release-build staging job, but they are build inputs, not distributable application data. The package's filtered bundle and manifest must be internally consistent and reproducible from the recorded pipeline revision; a package containing a raw table, an unvalidated/stale filtered artifact, or a missing required raster is not a releasable build.
- **NFR-QPB-083 (new; Decision Log D-95):** The canonical workbook is non-secret reference data, but it must be processed locally only: no workbook content, source path outside the project, sample rows, or uploaded file bytes may be sent to Pl@ntNet, VWorld, or any other external service. Candidate/upload handling accepts `.xlsx` only, does not execute macros or formulas, bounds preview size, preserves KTSN as text, and records only the provenance metadata in DR-QPB-079 (not the workbook itself) in the generated project. Logs and validation reports may include filenames, row/column checks, counts, and hashes, but must not contain API keys, photo bytes, or full workbook rows.

## 15. Edge Cases and Error Handling (Req §13)

- E-QPB-001: (see Section 6.5) Wizard must not imply post-MVP identification is available before it exists.
- E-QPB-002: Missing or incompatible QGIS/PyQGIS/GDAL runtime must produce a clear, non-technical, actionable error before any generation work begins (FR-QPB-009).
- E-QPB-003: Invalid or unverifiable VWorld API key must be surfaced as an actionable error without blocking the rest of project setup unnecessarily.
- E-QPB-004: Malformed spatial upload (corrupt Shapefile/GeoPackage, missing required components, unreadable CRS) must produce an actionable error and must not partially write a project.
- E-QPB-005 (post-MVP): Invalid KTSN CSV schema, invalid `correct_list` JSON, or a missing probability raster must produce an actionable error; a failure in optional Pl@ntNet validation must not destroy an otherwise valid project draft and must allow the user to disable identification and continue.
- E-QPB-006: Offline-map size overflow (estimate > 900 MiB, or actual output > 1 GiB) must block/abort generation, remove any incomplete temporary output, and return the user to extent/resolution selection (FR-QPB-082, FR-QPB-083).
- E-QPB-007: Disk-space shortage during generation must be detected and surfaced as an actionable error rather than producing a silently truncated project.
- E-QPB-008: If the chosen output directory already exists, the application must not overwrite it silently; it must offer a new name or an explicit replace workflow with backup.
- E-QPB-009: The application must never leave a partially generated project at the final output path; it must write to a temporary build directory, validate, and atomically promote to the final directory only on success.
- E-QPB-010: User-initiated cancellation mid-build must leave no partial deliverable in the final output folder.
- E-QPB-011: Invalid geometry in an uploaded layer must be reported and repaired only with explicit user approval (never auto-repaired silently) (FR-QPB-028).
- E-QPB-012: A required text field submitted empty or whitespace-only must be rejected (DR-QPB-013).
- E-QPB-013: Network loss during VWorld tile download for offline MBTiles generation must be handled by retry/backoff consistent with VWorld's terms (NFR-QPB-003), without producing a corrupt or partial `.mbtiles` file in the final output.
- E-QPB-014 (post-MVP): Loss of connectivity during an in-field identification request must queue the request and mark it pending rather than losing the underlying observation/photo data (FR-QPB-110).
- E-QPB-015: Failure or crash of the local GIS worker process must be surfaced to the UI as an actionable error rather than leaving the UI hung or the build silently incomplete.
- E-QPB-016: A user manually renaming or moving files inside a generated project folder (contrary to the transfer instructions in FR-QPB-093) is explicitly out of the application's ability to prevent once the folder leaves its control; the transfer notice must warn against this, but the application is not required to detect or recover from it after the fact.
- **E-QPB-017 (post-MVP; new; Decision Log D-89):** A failed or incomplete filtered-reference extraction/validation during application release packaging is a release-blocking error: the pipeline must report the failing artifact/check, produce no usable packaged deliverable, and never substitute a raw CSV/XLSX or an unvalidated previous artifact. During ordinary project generation, the same condition must produce an actionable error and no partially promoted project.
- ~~**E-QPB-018 (new; Decision Log D-91):** If a generated project's initial layer-tree state contains a missing, unchecked, or invalid node for a layer that was successfully created, project validation must report the layer and fail before promotion; it must not silently ship a project whose survey, reference, or basemap layer is hidden by default. This does not treat a deliberately user-saved post-open visibility change as a generation error.~~ **Superseded only for the designated probability-lookup visibility exception, not deleted; see E-QPB-018 (revised; Decision Log D-94) immediately below.**
- **E-QPB-018 (revised; Decision Log D-94):** If a generated project's initial layer-tree state contains a missing or invalid node for a layer that was successfully created, or a checked-state contrary to FR-QPB-136 (revised), project validation must report the layer and fail before promotion. It must not silently ship a project with a hidden survey layer, basemap layer, or non-lookup reference layer, nor a project in which the required `occurrence_probability_multiband` lookup raster is absent or visible by default. The intentional unchecked state of that one registered lookup raster is valid and must be excluded from the ordinary visible-layer assertion. This does not treat a deliberately user-saved post-open visibility change as a generation error.
- **E-QPB-019 (new; Decision Log D-95):** If canonical-workbook candidate discovery, preview, upload, schema validation, or provenance hashing fails, the build must stop before creating or promoting the GeoPackage/project. It must identify the failed source check, offer re-selection or `.xlsx` upload, and never fall back to the legacy CSV/XLSX pipeline or emit a mixed-source reference layer. If a taxonomy lookup is missing during report generation, the report must retain ordinary records and emit the defined limitation instead of failing the whole export.

## 16. Assumptions

- A-QPB-001: The exact IPC mechanism between the PySide6 UI process and the local GIS worker process is an implementation decision (Section 5.3).
- ~~A-QPB-002~~: **Removed.** The project-naming/sanitization rules are now a confirmed decision (`project_display_name`/`project_slug`/`project_id` split, ASCII-only slug, 64-char limit, rejection rules) — see Section 6.1 and Decision Log D-22.
- ~~A-QPB-003~~: **Removed.** The Type-1 photo design is no longer an assumption; it is a confirmed decision (three fixed `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` fields, no organ-tag column, no photo required) — see Section 8.1 and Decision Log D-16.
- A-QPB-004 (updated): `README.md`, `docs/product.md`, and `docs/architecture.md` have been updated as part of this revision (Decision Log D-20) to reflect the native-desktop/PySide6 decision, the PySide6-UI/PyQGIS-worker process separation, and the QGIS 3.44 LTR MVP runtime dependency recorded here.
- A-QPB-005 (new; Decision Log D-53): The exact platform-appropriate application-data-directory location and name (`~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/` on macOS; `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\` on Windows; the `credentials.enc` filename) is a new convention introduced by this specification, since no local, writable, per-installation application-state-directory location existed anywhere in this specification before this entry. It is not fixed by any prior stakeholder decision; an implementer may need to confirm the exact directory name with the stakeholder if a different convention is already in use elsewhere in the shipped application.
- A-QPB-006 (new; Decision Log D-53) — **confirmed correct and promoted to a decided requirement; no longer a live assumption (Decision Log D-55, closing Open Question O-21):** Whether the encrypted-storage password must be re-supplied specifically at the point of retrieving an already-remembered key during a later application session (as opposed to some other mechanism) is not specified by the stakeholder's decision. This specification assumes the narrowest interpretation consistent with the stakeholder's explicit "not a general access-gate" instruction — a targeted prompt only when the application actually needs to decrypt a remembered credential, not a blanket login screen at every launch — but this remains an assumption, not a confirmed decision. ~~See also Open Question O-21.~~ **The stakeholder has since been asked directly, and confirmed this exact reading is correct — a targeted prompt only at the point of use, not a once-per-launch upfront prompt. This assumption's own content required no correction, only confirmation; NFR-QPB-073 (revised, Decision Log D-55, Section 14.1) now states it as a decided requirement, and Open Question O-21 is CLOSED (Section 20).**
- ~~A-QPB-007 (new; Decision Log D-90)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see A-QPB-007 (revised; Decision Log D-93) immediately below.** ~~The Type 2/3 immediate-identification change removes only an application-authored pre-identification consent/OK gate. Any permission prompt that QField or the operating system independently requires for a protected runtime capability is treated as platform-owned behavior; the application must not add another modal around it. The change does not alter the separate project-generation Pl@ntNet-key embedding consent (FR-QPB-115) or the prohibition on automatic identification after attachment (FR-QPB-102).~~
- **A-QPB-007 (revised; Decision Log D-93):** The Type 1–3 generated-widget direct-identification rule removes only an application-authored pre-identification consent/OK gate. Any permission prompt that QField or the operating system independently requires for a protected runtime capability is platform-owned behavior; the application must not add another modal around it. This rule does not alter the separate desktop project-generation Pl@ntNet-key embedding consent (FR-QPB-115), its declined-embedding manual-key path (FR-QPB-116), or the prohibition on automatic identification after attachment (FR-QPB-102). Type 4 is excluded because it has no generated identification widget/button under the current schema (DR-QPB-050/054).
- **A-QPB-008 (new; Decision Log D-94):** The `occurrence_probability_multiband` exception is identified by its dedicated generated-project lookup role and `reference/rasters/occurrence_probability_multiband.tif` source identity, not merely by being in `Reference` or by being a raster. No future reference layer inherits its hidden-by-default treatment unless an explicit stakeholder decision records it. For acceptance coverage, a valid offline fixture models the product contract by supplying an explicit, currently supported VWorld layer selection; a test-only implicit selection is not representative of a valid offline build.
- **A-QPB-009 (new; Decision Log D-95):** The current workbook's 8,042 rows, 4,673 `정명` rows, and 3,369 `이명` rows are observed fixture facts, not permanent business invariants. Future canonical workbook revisions may change counts and values, but must pass the same schema/value checks and carry a new provenance hash; acceptance tests must use both the real fixture and small synthetic fixtures.

## 17. Out of Scope

- OS-1: PostgreSQL, PostGIS, or any other remote database (Req §2.2).
- OS-2: QFieldCloud or another cloud database/synchronization service (Req §2.2).
- OS-3: QFieldSync packaging as the final transfer workflow (Req §2.2).
- OS-4: General ecological analysis, dashboards, or publication-ready reporting (Req §2.2).
- OS-5: Requiring users to edit the generated `.qgs` XML manually (Req §2.2).
- OS-6: Choosing further application technology beyond what the stakeholder has already explicitly decided (Section 5) (Req §2.2; CLAUDE.md hard boundary).
- OS-7: All post-MVP identification-subsystem behavior (Section 13) is out of scope for MVP acceptance, though it is specified for future planning.
- OS-8: Bundling the QGIS runtime inside the application installer (Section 5.2, FR-QPB-007) — deferred beyond MVP.
- ~~OS-9~~: ~~On-device (smartphone) probability-map packaging (Section 13.8).~~ **Superseded, not deleted; see Decision Log D-36 and revised FR-QPB-111.** This item is no longer out of scope: per the stakeholder's explicit, direct Category C instruction, in-field, on-device probability-raster sampling is now a first-class in-scope capability for this phase (subject to the recorded, not-yet-confirmed technical-feasibility caveat in Decision Log D-36/FR-QPB-111 (revised)), closing former Open Question O-18.
- OS-10: Fuzzy KTSN name matching (Req §9.4 — explicitly deferred by the source draft itself).

## 18. Acceptance Criteria

Each criterion is independently testable and PASS/FAIL. MVP criteria are listed first; post-MVP criteria are explicitly marked and do not block MVP acceptance.

### 18.1 Database acceptance (MVP)

- **AC-QPB-001**: Given a generated project for any of the four survey types, when it is opened in the explicitly supported QGIS Desktop version, then it opens without a repair warning.
- **AC-QPB-002**: Given a generated GeoPackage, when every domain UUID column is inspected, then every value is valid, unique, and non-null.
- **AC-QPB-003**: Given a generated GeoPackage, when its relations are inspected, then no domain relation references `fid`.
- **AC-QPB-004**: Given a generated GeoPackage, when `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` is run against it, then it returns zero rows.
- **AC-QPB-005**: Given a generated project of a given survey type, when its geometry layers and CRS are inspected, then they match the schema in Section 8 for that type.
- **AC-QPB-006**: Given a generated GeoPackage, when its geometry columns are inspected, then a spatial index exists for each.
- **AC-QPB-106** (new; Decision Log D-66; closes O-32): Given a generated Type 1, 2, or 3 project's GeoPackage, when the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) is inspected, then a real, build-time-created index exists on its Korean-name column and on its scientific-name column.
- **AC-QPB-007**: Given an attempted `cover` value outside 0–100, when the record is saved, then it is rejected.
- **AC-QPB-008** (revised; Decision Log D-16): Given a Type 1 inventory record with zero, one, two, or three of `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` populated, when the record is saved, then it is accepted in every case — no photo is required to complete a Type-1 observation.
- **AC-QPB-009** (revised; Decision Log D-23; corrects a prior mandatory-photo misinterpretation, and removes the undefined "marked field-complete" photo-validation concept; further revised, Decision Log D-74, 2026-08-28 — narrows scope to reflect `observation_photo`'s removal for Type 2/3, struck through and annotated below, not deleted): Given a Type 2 survey ~~or observation~~, or a Type 3 plot ~~or observation~~, with zero related photo records, when the record is saved and the project is validated, then it is accepted. Given one or more related photo records, each photo record must contain a valid relative attachment path, and a referenced file that is missing from the project folder must be reported as a broken attachment. **(Decision Log D-74): the struck-through "or observation" references above no longer apply — Type 2/3's `observation` no longer has any related child photo table (`observation_photo` is removed entirely); see new AC-QPB-112 (schema shape) and AC-QPB-114 (mirrors AC-QPB-008's optionality assertion) below for its replacement.**
- **AC-QPB-112** (new; Decision Log D-74): Given a generated Type 2 or Type 3 project, when its GeoPackage schema is inspected, then no `observation_photo` table exists anywhere in it, and the `observation` table instead has exactly three optional, nullable columns — `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, `fruit_photo_path` — each configured with the Attachment (`ExternalResource`) editor widget and the Korean-language alias already confirmed for Type 1's identical column names (잎 사진/꽃 사진/열매 사진, Section 8.5, Decision Log D-56–D-58); and given the same project's Type 3 `plot_photo` table (if applicable) or Type 2 `survey_photo` table, when inspected, then each remains fully present and unaffected by this criterion.
- **AC-QPB-114** (new; Decision Log D-74; mirrors AC-QPB-008 for Type 2/3): Given a Type 2 or Type 3 `observation` record with zero, one, two, or three of `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` populated, when the record is saved, then it is accepted in every case — no photo is required to complete an observation of either type, mirroring AC-QPB-008's identical Type-1 assertion.
- **AC-QPB-115** (new; Decision Log D-75; ~~Type 2 or Type 3~~ **scope extended to Type 4, Decision Log D-79**): Given a ~~Type 2 or Type 3~~ **Type 2, Type 3, or Type 4** project built after the user draws and individually names two or more separate polygons in one site-input drawing session, when the generated GeoPackage's `site` table is inspected, then it contains exactly one record per named polygon, each with the geometry and `site_name` value the user assigned to that specific polygon — never one record with a merged multi-part geometry, and never every record sharing one single shared name.

### 18.2 QGIS/QField acceptance (MVP)

- **AC-QPB-010**: Given a generated project folder moved to a different absolute path, when the `.qgs` is opened, then no missing-layer warning appears.
- **AC-QPB-011**: Given a parent feature form with a related child table, when a new child record is created from the parent form, then it is saved and displayed correctly.
- **AC-QPB-012**: Given a new feature in QGIS Desktop and in QField, when the UUID field is inspected, then it was generated automatically and cannot be edited through the normal form.
- **AC-QPB-013**: Given a foreign-key field rendered via a Relation Reference widget, when displayed, then it shows a human-readable name, not a raw UUID.
- **AC-QPB-014**: Given a generated project copied computer → phone → computer, when attachment paths are inspected, then they remain relative and valid.
- **AC-QPB-015**: Given a Type 4 `community` feature, when `is_field_checked` is toggled, then its symbology switches between red and green hatch accordingly.
- **AC-QPB-016**: Given the project opened in each explicitly supported QGIS and QField version (per NFR-QPB-001, once pinned), then it opens successfully in each.
- **AC-QPB-098** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-56 — **draft proposal, not yet stakeholder-approved; not to be exercised by any `test-designer`/`implementer` work until Section 8.5's proposed aliases are stakeholder-confirmed**): Given a generated project for any of the four survey types, when every layer's fields are inspected, then every field except a table's own UUID primary key (DR-QPB-071) has a non-empty, Korean-language alias set matching Section 8.5's approved mapping (or a stakeholder-corrected equivalent) — not the raw column name; and given the same layers, when a table's own UUID primary-key field specifically is inspected, then it has no alias set and remains configured `Hidden`/read-only exactly as before (DR-QPB-005/FR-QPB-057), unchanged by this criterion.
- **AC-QPB-100** (new; Decision Log D-61, ~~draft~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-65**): Given a generated project for any survey type, when a point layer's and a polygon layer's renderer are inspected (excluding the Type 4 `community` layer, which retains its existing DR-QPB-051 rule-based renderer), then each has been assigned a deliberately configured default `QgsSingleSymbolRenderer`/`QgsSymbol` at build time — not QGIS's own undifferentiated default symbol — matching the confirmed "minimalist" definition (FR-QPB-120, revised: single flat fill plus thin outline for polygons; small solid circle marker for points).
- **AC-QPB-101** (revised; Decision Log D-65, confirmed, closes remainder of O-24; **annotated, not altered in substance, by Decision Log D-76 below**): Given the wizard's Step 6 (FR-QPB-123) with zero network access, when the user types into the Tabler icon search field, then matching icon names are filtered live from the offline, build-time-bundled static index, with no network request made **(this asserts only the client-side name-filtering/matching step itself, unchanged by Decision Log D-76; a separate, independently permitted live preview-image fetch may now also occur while typing — see new AC-QPB-117 for that fetch trigger's own graceful-degradation behavior, which this criterion does not test)**; given the user then selects one icon while online, when the selection completes, then that icon's SVG is fetched (**one of two now-independently-permitted fetch triggers per Decision Log D-76 — this is the pre-existing, unchanged fetch-on-selection trigger, FR-QPB-011(d)(i)**) and, on success, every point layer of the generated project uses it as its marker symbol, and the SVG file is embedded into the generated project's own output folder at a project-relative path; and given the user selects an icon while offline, or the fetch otherwise fails, then the minimalist default marker (FR-QPB-120) remains in use for every point layer, and project generation is not blocked.
- **AC-QPB-102** (revised; Decision Log D-65, confirmed, closes remainder of O-24): Given the single Tabler SVG-fetch request permitted by FR-QPB-011(d), when it is inspected, then it carries a compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header and does not retry automatically in an unbounded loop on failure; and given a downloaded icon is actually used as a symbol, then **no** attribution/license notice is shown anywhere in the generated project or this application's own UI (MIT license, confirmed — NFR-QPB-080, revised) — this reverses AC-QPB-102 (original)'s provisional "attribution notice is visibly present" expectation, which this revision supersedes.
- **AC-QPB-103** (new; Decision Log D-63, ~~draft~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-69**): Given a generated `inventory_observation` or `observation` layer, when the `identification_status` field's editor widget setup is inspected, then it is configured as `ValueMap` (or an equivalent fixed-list-selection widget) listing exactly the five values `not_requested`, `pending`, `complete`, `failed`, `manual` as the only selectable options, displayed using those same raw English strings (no Korean-language value-label translation, confirmed — closes O-33); and given a value is selected and saved, then the GeoPackage record's stored value is exactly the corresponding raw enum string, unchanged from today.
- **AC-QPB-105** (new; Decision Log D-66; closes part of O-28/O-29): Given a generated Type 1, 2, or 3 project, when `selected_korean_name`'s editor widget configuration is inspected, then it is a `ValueRelation` widget referencing the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072), configured with a filter/completer setting rather than a plain text-edit widget; and given the Type 4 `community` layer's `dominant_species` field, when its editor widget is inspected, then it is unaffected (not a `ValueRelation` widget) — confirming the O-29 scope exclusion.
- **AC-QPB-107** (new; Decision Log D-67; closes O-30): Given a feature (either a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature, or an existing, already-saved feature reopened later) with `selected_korean_name` selected via the `ValueRelation` widget, when the form is inspected, then `selected_scientific_name` and `selected_ktsn` are automatically populated with the corresponding accepted values from the lookup table in both cases, and both fields' editor widgets are configured non-editable (read-only) — confirming this mechanism is not limited to brand-new/not-yet-saved features the way Decision Log D-50's Pl@ntNet write-back mechanism is; and given the bundled accepted-name lookup table's row set, when it is inspected, then no row with `taxon_jm_nm != '정명'` (a synonym or original-combination name) appears in it.
- **AC-QPB-108** (new; Decision Log D-68; closes O-31): Given a generated Type 1, 2, or 3 project with the post-MVP identification subsystem disabled (`identification_enabled = false`), when the project's GeoPackage and `.qgs` file are inspected, then the accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) is present, indexed, and referenced by the "Reference" layer-tree group, and `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn` are configured exactly as FR-QPB-124/FR-QPB-125 require — unaffected by the identification subsystem being disabled.
- **AC-QPB-109** (new; Decision Log D-70; closes O-34; makes FR-QPB-105's newly clarified second, independent trigger condition — added per FR-QPB-127/Decision Log D-68 — independently testable, distinct from AC-QPB-108 above, which assumes valid reference data is present): Given an attempted Types 1–3 project build with `identification_enabled = false` and no valid raw KTSN reference data present (the raw CSV file missing entirely, or present but lacking one or more of its required columns — `ktsn`, `taxon_full_nm`, `taxon_kor_nm`, `taxon_jm_nm`, `correct_list`), when the build is run, then it still fails early with a clear message, exactly as FR-QPB-105 already requires when `identification_enabled = true` — confirming this fail-early validation is not bypassed merely because the identification subsystem itself is disabled, since FR-QPB-127's unconditional accepted-name-lookup-table derivation (FR-QPB-126) depends on this same raw source data regardless of that toggle.
- **AC-QPB-110** (new; Decision Log D-71; makes FR-QPB-055 (revised)'s stacking/rendering-order requirement independently testable): Given a generated project's `.qgs` file for any survey type, when the root layer tree's group children are inspected in their own stored children-index order, then `Basemap` is the last (highest-index) of the three required groups (`Survey data`, `Basemap`, `Reference`) — i.e., both `Survey data`'s and `Reference`'s own child index within the root group are less than `Basemap`'s index, confirming `Basemap` is positioned to render beneath (behind) both other groups. This criterion does not assert, and must not be read as asserting, any particular relative order between `Survey data` and `Reference` — only `Basemap`'s own last position is checked.
- **AC-QPB-111** (new; Decision Log D-73, ~~draft — **not to be exercised until Section 8.6's proposed relation names are stakeholder-confirmed**~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-77 — the seven proposed relation names in Section 8.6 are now stakeholder-confirmed (six as proposed, one corrected); this criterion may now be exercised**): Given a generated project for any survey type, when each embedded child-relation widget's underlying `QgsRelation` is inspected, then its `id()` is unchanged from the existing stable relation-ID convention (FR-QPB-056; e.g. `rel_observation_survey`) and its `name()` is the corresponding Korean display name from Section 8.6's approved mapping (or a stakeholder-corrected equivalent) — never the raw relation ID string. This criterion asserts only the `QgsRelation` object's own configured `id()`/`name()` values, independently of the disclosed, not-yet-verified question of exactly which mechanism drives the widget's on-screen rendered label (Section 8.6); confirming that the rendered label actually reflects this configured name is implementer verification work, mirroring the existing convention for this class of uncertainty (Decision Log D-36/FR-QPB-111).
- **AC-QPB-117** (new; Decision Log D-76; closes the "offline-safe, graceful degradation" half of Open Question O-35): Given the wizard's Step 6 Tabler icon search with no network access available (or every live preview fetch failing/timing out), when the user types a search query, then matching icon names are still filtered live from the offline, build-time-bundled static index exactly as before (FR-QPB-121), each visible result shows no image (or a name-only/placeholder row) in place of a preview, and the user can still select any result by name without being blocked, and without the application crashing; given the user then selects an icon while offline, then the existing, unchanged offline/failed-fetch fallback (AC-QPB-101) applies — the minimalist default marker remains in use and project generation is not blocked. This criterion asserts only the offline/failure-safe degradation behavior; it does not assert that a preview image is actually shown when the application is online and a fetch succeeds (see AC-QPB-101, revised, for the two independently permitted fetch triggers this feature now exercises).
- **AC-QPB-118** (new; Decision Log D-80, ~~**not to be exercised by any `test-designer`/`implementer` work until Section 8.7's proposed layer names are stakeholder-confirmed**~~ **confirmed by Decision Log D-84 — Section 8.7's proposed layer names are now stakeholder-confirmed (with one correction, `site` → 조사지); this criterion may now be exercised**): Given a generated project for any of the four survey types, when every domain survey-data layer's own name (as configured via `QgsMapLayer.setName()`) is inspected in the Layers panel, then it is a non-empty Korean-language name matching Section 8.7's approved mapping (or a stakeholder-corrected equivalent) for that layer's underlying table — never the raw, unmodified GeoPackage table name (e.g. `inventory_observation`); and given the same project, when a layer's individually configured display *expression* (FR-QPB-059) is inspected, then it is unaffected by this criterion, which governs only the layer's own name, not which field represents an individual feature. **Extended scope (Decision Log D-84):** and given a Type 1–3 project specifically, when the bundled KTSN accepted-name lookup layer's (DR-QPB-072) own name is inspected, then it likewise matches Section 8.7's confirmed name (인정 국명 조회표) — not the raw table name `ktsn_accepted_name_lookup` — per DR-QPB-078 (revised)/FR-QPB-130 (revised)'s own scope extension to this one additional layer.

### 18.3 Basemap acceptance (MVP)

- **AC-QPB-017** (reviewed, not textually changed, under Decision Log D-29): Given a valid VWorld API key and online mode selected, when the project is opened, then the VWorld layer loads successfully. (This criterion does not itself name a specific layer spelling; see AC-QPB-065, new below, for the layer-discovery/naming behavior required by revised FR-QPB-071. It also does not itself assume any specific connection mechanism, so it remains accurate under revised FR-QPB-072/Decision Log D-29; see new AC-QPB-068 below for the connection-mechanism-specific behavior.)
- **AC-QPB-018**: Given an approved bbox and zoom range for offline mode, when the MBTiles file is generated, then its tile coverage contains the approved bbox at every selected zoom level.
- **AC-QPB-019**: Given a generated `.mbtiles` file, when its metadata is inspected, then it contains the correct bounds, format, minimum zoom, and maximum zoom.
- **AC-QPB-020**: Given a generated `.mbtiles` file, when its size is measured, then it does not exceed 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes).
- **AC-QPB-021**: Given a size estimate exceeding 900 MiB before generation, when the user attempts to proceed, then generation is blocked and the user is prompted to reduce scope.
- **AC-QPB-022**: Given the MBTiles layer opened in each explicitly supported QGIS/QField version, then it renders correctly at representative locations and zoom levels.
- **AC-QPB-023**: Given an in-progress offline basemap build that is cancelled, when the final output folder is inspected, then no partial deliverable is present.
- **AC-QPB-054** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-21; closes former Open Question O-10): Given the user declines the online-layer key-embedding consent step (FR-QPB-076), when the project is generated, then no VWorld API key is embedded anywhere in the project and the online layer is omitted, with an explanation that it can be configured manually later.
- **AC-QPB-055** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-21): Given the user accepts the consent step and checkbox (FR-QPB-076), when the project is generated, then the `.qgs` online-layer URL contains the key, but the GeoPackage, `.mbtiles` file, `MANIFEST.json`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, application logs, and temporary filenames contain no copy of the key.
- **AC-QPB-056** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-21): Given a completed offline MBTiles build, when the generated project is inspected, then it references only the local `.mbtiles` file and contains no VWorld API key anywhere in the delivered project.
- **AC-QPB-057** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-21): Given `MANIFEST.json` for a project with an embedded online-layer key, when inspected, then it contains only a boolean security-warning flag and never the key value itself.
- ~~**AC-QPB-058** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-21)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see AC-QPB-058 (MVP; revised; Decision Log D-53) immediately below.** ~~Given the user selects "Remember this key," when the application is restarted, then the key is retrieved from the OS credential store rather than from any plaintext application file; given the user does not select this option, then the key is not retained beyond the current application session.~~
- **AC-QPB-058** (MVP; revised; Decision Log D-53): Given the user selects "Remember this key" for the VWorld key and an encrypted-storage password has already been established, when the application is restarted and the same password is supplied, then the key is retrieved by deriving the decryption key via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from the supplied password and the stored salt and decrypting `credentials.enc` — **never** by any call into the `keyring` package or an OS credential store, and never read back as plaintext from any application file (the file's on-disk bytes never contain the plaintext key). Given the user does not select "Remember this key," then the key is not retained beyond the current application session, unchanged from before. Given no encrypted-storage password has yet been established (first launch, or previously declined per NFR-QPB-073), then "Remember this key" is unavailable for that session and the key is retained only for the current session.
- **AC-QPB-089** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-53): Given `qfield_builder/credential_store.py` (or whatever module implements this application's own key-retention logic after this decision), when its source is inspected for any import of, or call into, the `keyring` package, then none is found anywhere in the "Remember this key" retention code path.
- **AC-QPB-090** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-53): Given a VWorld or Pl@ntNet key has been remembered via "Remember this key," when the on-disk `credentials.enc` file's raw bytes are inspected, then the plaintext API key string does not appear anywhere in the file's contents.
- **AC-QPB-091** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-53): Given the key-derivation code path is inspected, when the KDF call is located, then it is a named PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 call with an explicit iteration-count argument of at least 600,000 and a randomly generated, per-installation salt of at least 16 bytes — not a fixed/hardcoded salt and not a default/unspecified iteration count.
- **AC-QPB-092** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-53): Given the application is launched with no encrypted-storage password yet established, when the main window would otherwise appear, then the first-launch password-setup prompt (NFR-QPB-073) is shown first; given the user declines/skips it, then no password is established, "Remember this key" is unavailable/disabled for that session, and the same prompt is shown again at the next launch.
- **AC-QPB-093** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-53): Given a previously established encrypted-storage password that the user can no longer supply correctly, when the application attempts to decrypt `credentials.enc` using the re-derived key, then decryption fails, the previously remembered key is treated as unrecoverable (never silently guessed, brute-forced, or bypassed), and the user is prompted to re-enter their API key(s) manually.
- **AC-QPB-097** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-55; closes former Open Question O-21; makes NFR-QPB-073 (revised)'s confirmed retrieval-time password-re-prompt trigger point independently testable): Given a VWorld or Pl@ntNet key has previously been remembered via "Remember this key" and the encrypted-storage password has not yet been supplied in the current application session, when a wizard step is reached that does not itself need to auto-fill that remembered key, then no encrypted-storage password prompt is shown; given the wizard subsequently reaches the specific step that would auto-fill the remembered key, then the password prompt is shown at that point, and not at general application startup or before any other, unrelated part of the application is used.
- **AC-QPB-065** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-26): Given a valid VWorld API key, when the application determines its supported VWorld layer set, then it does so by querying `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml` rather than reading a hardcoded list, and the resulting supported-layer set matches the layers the capabilities response advertises (currently `Base`, `White`, `Midnight`, `Hybrid`, `Satellite`) rather than the superseded `Base`/`gray`/`midnight`/`Hybrid`/`Satellite` spellings.
- **AC-QPB-068** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-29): Given a generated project in **online** basemap mode, when the `.qgs` file's online VWorld layer datasource is inspected, then it is configured through QGIS's native WMTS provider connected to the capabilities endpoint URL `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml`, and it does **not** contain a manually constructed per-tile XYZ URL template (`.../{key}/{layer}/{z}/{y}/{x}.png`) as a `type=xyz` layer datasource. Given the equivalent **offline** MBTiles pipeline (Section 11) is exercised instead, then its own tile-download requests continue, unaffected, to use concrete per-tile GetTile URLs exactly as before (see AC-QPB-018, FR-QPB-084) — this criterion does not apply to, and must not be read as changing, the offline pipeline.

- **AC-QPB-146** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-97; iPhone-QField online `Satellite` verification): Given an online project generated after the user selected `Satellite`, supplied a VWorld key that VWorld accepts for that WMTS service, and accepted the existing VWorld-key embedding consent, when that unchanged project is transferred to and opened in QField on an iPhone with usable VWorld network access, then the map renders the selected `Satellite` layer and QField shows no missing-layer, repair-data-source, or equivalent source-repair warning for it. Inspection of a URI, XML, or offline/desktop-only fixture cannot pass this criterion by itself. This criterion requires recorded iPhone visual/manual verification because no local test runner emulates QField iOS; the record must identify the app/project build and selected layer but must not expose the key.

### 18.4 Portability acceptance (MVP)

- **AC-QPB-024**: Given a generated project folder copied to a new local path, when opened, then it opens successfully.
- **AC-QPB-025**: Given a generated project folder copied to a test smartphone, edited (data/photos added) in QField, closed, and copied back, when reopened in desktop QGIS, then it opens successfully with the edits present.
- **AC-QPB-026**: Given the supported transfer workflow, when it is followed end-to-end, then no QFieldSync packaging step is invoked or required.
- **AC-QPB-027**: Given `MANIFEST.json` for a project missing an attachment, plugin (if applicable), database, or basemap file, when validated, then the missing item is detected before transfer.
- **AC-QPB-028**: Given the macOS→iOS, Windows→iOS, Windows→Android, and macOS→Android transfer paths, when each is exercised end-to-end, then the project opens and functions correctly in QField on the target platform.

### 18.5 Application/runtime acceptance (MVP)

- **AC-QPB-029**: Given no compatible QGIS installation on the host machine, when the application starts a build, then a clear, non-technical error is shown instead of a crash or silent failure.
- **AC-QPB-030**: Given an existing directory at the chosen output path, when the user attempts to build into it, then the application does not overwrite it silently and instead offers a rename or explicit replace-with-backup path.
- **AC-QPB-031**: Given a build that fails partway through, when the output folder is inspected, then no partially generated project exists at the final path.
- **AC-QPB-032** (revised; Decision Log D-25): Given the application built and packaged for macOS, when the package is installed and launched on macOS, then the application starts and completes the wizard successfully. The equivalent Windows-package criterion is **not evaluated for this MVP release**: delivery of a built Windows installer/executable is explicitly deferred to a required subsequent release (FR-QPB-014, revised; Decision Log D-25) by direct stakeholder instruction — this is a stakeholder-directed delivery-timing decision, distinct from "not yet automatable" — and must be reinstated as an active, MVP-blocking criterion once that subsequent release's Windows package exists. The underlying cross-platform source/packaging-configuration requirement (NFR-QPB-030, revised) remains in force and is not itself deferred.
- **AC-QPB-059** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-22; closes former Open Question O-2): Given a `project_display_name` containing Unicode characters, spaces, or punctuation, when the project is created, then a valid ASCII `project_slug` (letters/digits/hyphens/underscores only, ≤64 characters) is derived and used for all generated folder/file names.
- **AC-QPB-060** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-22): Given a blank name, a name that reduces to a path-traversal sequence, or a Windows-reserved filename, when slug derivation runs, then it is rejected with an actionable error rather than silently producing an unsafe or reserved name.
- **AC-QPB-061** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-22): Given two different generated projects, when their `project_id` values are inspected, then each is a valid, distinct UUID v4, independent of `project_display_name`/`project_slug`.
- **AC-QPB-066** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-27): Given Step 2 (survey-type selection) is displayed, when the user views the step before making a selection, then four distinct Korean-language explanations are shown, one for each of the four survey types, and each explanation's content corresponds to that specific type's own data-collection/structuring/recording model per Section 8 (i.e. no two of the four explanations are generic or interchangeable with one another).
- **AC-QPB-067** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-28): Given any screen, dialog, validation message, warning, progress message, or error message produced by the application's own wizard UI, when it is displayed to the user, then its text is in Korean, with the sole exception of the internal identifiers, file-format terms, and proper names explicitly carved out by NFR-QPB-070.
- **AC-QPB-062** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-24): Given the wizard's drawing canvas is displayed, when it renders and fetches its background, then the only host it may issue tile requests to is `tile.openstreetmap.org` (or the configured OSM endpoint) for the ephemeral drawing-aid background described in FR-QPB-011(c), and no request is made to any other host as part of rendering that canvas.
- **AC-QPB-063** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-24): Given the drawing canvas is shown with no OSM tiles yet cached, when the canvas paints, then a plain graticule is shown immediately rather than blocking on the fetch; and given any OSM tile fetch fails (network error, timeout, non-200 response, or empty body), then the affected tile continues to show the graticule fallback and the canvas's polygon/point/bbox drawing functionality (FR-QPB-025/FR-QPB-080) remains fully correct and unaffected.
- **AC-QPB-064** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-24): Given a generated project in either online or offline basemap mode, when its `.qgs` file, `.mbtiles` file (if any), and `MANIFEST.json` are inspected, then none of them reference `tile.openstreetmap.org` or contain any OSM tile imagery — the FR-QPB-011(c) drawing-aid exception never appears in delivered project output, and the VWorld-only basemap-generation requirements of Sections 10/11 remain fully satisfied and unaffected.
- **AC-QPB-104** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-65; closes O-27): Given the wizard reaches the end of Step 5 (optional photo identification toggle), when the user proceeds, then a new Step 6, "Symbol styling configuration" (Section 6.6, FR-QPB-123), is displayed before the renumbered Step 7 "Review and build" (Section 6.7); and given a single generated project, when its point layers' and, separately, its polygon layers' symbols are inspected, then all point layers of that project share one identical styling choice and all polygon layers of that project share one identical styling choice (never a different style per individual layer within the same project); and given two separately generated projects of the same survey type, when their symbology is compared, then neither project's Step 6 styling choice is automatically carried over to the other — each build's styling choice is made fresh.
- **AC-QPB-116** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-75; ~~Type 2 or Type 3~~ **scope extended to Type 4, Decision Log D-79**): Given the site-input wizard step (`SiteInputPage`) in drawing mode for a ~~Type 2 or Type 3~~ **Type 2, Type 3, or Type 4** project, when the user finishes a polygon, assigns it a name, and then starts drawing a second, separate polygon without clearing the first, then the first polygon's own finished shape and assigned name are preserved (not discarded or merged into the second), and the canvas correctly begins a new, independent shape; given the user finishes the second polygon and ends the drawing session, then both named polygons are available for inclusion in the generated project, mirroring AC-QPB-115's own GeoPackage-level assertion.
- **AC-QPB-119** (new; Decision Log D-81; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — directory name corrected): Given a fresh install of the renamed application with no pre-existing `QField Project Builder`-named application-data directory anywhere on the machine, when the application is launched for the first time, then no migration is attempted, no error or warning about a missing old directory is shown, and only the new, ~~`QFieldKit`~~ **`FieldBuild Kit`**-named application-data directory is ever created (once a key is first remembered).
- **AC-QPB-120** (new; Decision Log D-81; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — directory name corrected): Given an old, `QField Project Builder`-named application-data directory that exists and already contains a valid `credentials.enc` file and its accompanying salt (from a prior version of this application, before the rename), and no ~~`QFieldKit`~~ **`FieldBuild Kit`**-named directory exists yet, when the renamed application is launched for the first time, then the old directory's `credentials.enc` file and salt are copied into the new, ~~`QFieldKit`~~ **`FieldBuild Kit`**-named directory before any "Remember this key" retrieval is attempted, the old directory and its contents remain completely unmodified and undeleted, and a previously remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key remains retrievable using the same, already-established encrypted-storage password.
- **AC-QPB-121** (new; Decision Log D-81; further revised, Decision Log D-86 — directory name corrected): Given both an old, `QField Project Builder`-named application-data directory and a new, ~~`QFieldKit`~~ **`FieldBuild Kit`**-named application-data directory already exist, each already containing its own `credentials.enc` file, when the application is launched, then no migration is attempted, the new directory's own existing `credentials.enc` file is left completely unmodified (never overwritten or merged with the old directory's contents), and the old directory is likewise left completely unmodified.
- **AC-QPB-122** (new; Decision Log D-82): Given the application is launched, when the wizard's UI (its window title, or wherever the implementer places it per FR-QPB-132) is inspected, then the application's own currently running version string (matching `qfield_builder.__version__`) is visibly present somewhere in the UI without requiring the user to inspect a file or run a command.

### 18.6 Post-MVP acceptance criteria (do not block MVP)

- **AC-QPB-040** (post-MVP): Given a valid one-plant identification request, when submitted, then exactly the top three results are returned and displayed, ordered by descending Pl@ntNet score.
- **AC-QPB-041** (post-MVP): Given a `taxon_full_nm` containing `<em>` tags, when normalized for matching/display, then the tags are removed correctly.
- **AC-QPB-042** (post-MVP): Given a synonym (non-`정명`) fixture with a `correct_list` entry, when accepted-name resolution runs, then it resolves to the correct accepted KTSN row.
- **AC-QPB-043** (post-MVP): Given missing, malformed, or conflicting (`KTSN` vs `KTNS`) accepted-name entries, when resolution runs, then each case is handled deterministically and visibly, including flagging conflicting values as ambiguous rather than silently choosing one.
- ~~AC-QPB-044 (post-MVP; original)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see AC-QPB-044 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-49) immediately below.** ~~Given a photo with EXIF GPS in WGS 84, when probability lookup runs, then the coordinate is transformed to the raster CRS before sampling.~~ (This text does not disclose that, on QField running on iOS specifically, its own precondition — "a photo with EXIF GPS" — can never actually be met for an attached photo, because QField's own iOS attachment-saving step strips GPS EXIF before this project's code reads the file; Decision Log D-49.)
- **AC-QPB-044** (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-49 — adds a disclosed QField-iOS platform-limitation qualification; the underlying transform assertion is unchanged and is restated below, unaltered): Given a photo with EXIF GPS in WGS 84, when probability lookup runs, then the coordinate is transformed to the raster CRS before sampling. **Disclosed platform limitation (Decision Log D-49):** on QField running on iOS specifically, this criterion's precondition — an attached photo actually carrying EXIF GPS by the time this project's code reads it — cannot be met for any attached photo, regardless of acquisition method (native camera, QField's own internal camera, or an existing gallery/camera-roll photo), because QField's own iOS attachment-saving mechanism strips GPS EXIF metadata before this project's code ever reads the file. This is a confirmed QField-iOS platform limitation, not a defect in this project's own `qpbReadPhotoGps`/`qpbReadExifTag` implementation, which is independently confirmed (via this project's sanctioned QGIS-isolation probe) to correctly read and parse GPS EXIF when it is actually present in the file it is given. This criterion therefore cannot be exercised/verified against a real QField-iOS device as written; it remains verifiable via desktop-side/simulated fixtures that supply a photo file already carrying EXIF GPS (bypassing QField's iOS attachment-save step), and, per the cited report, via QField on Android, where this stripping behavior is reported — not independently confirmed by this project — not to reproduce.
- **AC-QPB-045** (post-MVP; revised, Decision Log D-17): Given a sampled raster value of exactly `-9999`, a coordinate outside the raster extent, a missing raster file, or no photo GPS, when probability lookup runs, then the UI displays "No probability data" (or the no-GPS equivalent message), never a numeric zero.
- ~~AC-QPB-046 (post-MVP; revised, Decision Log D-43 — addition only, prior substance unchanged)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see AC-QPB-046 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-50) immediately below.** ~~Given a user selecting one of three candidates, when the selection is saved, then only the intended observation is updated, its UUID relations remain intact, and `identification_status` is persisted as `"complete"` — never `"manual"`, which is reserved for a manually-entered identification per new AC-QPB-078.~~ (This text asserted persistence unconditionally, without disclosing that whether the selection is actually saved at all depends on the current feature's own save-state, confirmed by real-device testing and direct source inspection; Decision Log D-50.)
- **AC-QPB-046** (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-50 — restructured into two independently testable branches by feature save-state; supersedes the unconditional D-43 assertion above, which is retained, struck through, immediately above):
  - **(a) Brand-new, not-yet-saved feature — real candidate selection or manual identification entry (Decision Log D-51 extends this branch, originally scoped under Decision Log D-50 to real candidate selection only, to also cover manual entry):** Given a user creates a new feature via QField's "Add feature" flow and, before saving, either (i) selects one of three candidates, or (ii) rejects all three candidates and enters a name manually, when the user then performs the normal save action, then the GeoPackage record for that feature is actually updated: only the intended observation is affected, its UUID relations remain intact, and `identification_status` is persisted as `"complete"` for scenario (i) — never `"manual"` — or as `"manual"` for scenario (ii) — never `"complete"`, with `identification_score`, `occurrence_probability`, and `identification_model_version` all remaining `NULL` for scenario (ii) — per AC-QPB-078. Both scenarios are verifiable only via real-device manual QA (no QField/QML runtime exists in this project's automated harness), following this document's existing convention for device-dependent criteria (Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072). ~~This branch tests only the real-candidate-selection mechanism Decision Log D-50 confirms and requires; whether the identical persistence result also holds for a manual entry on a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature is not asserted by this branch — see Open Question O-20.~~ — **superseded, not deleted (Decision Log D-51, closes former Open Question O-20):** this branch now asserts both scenario (i) and scenario (ii) above, per the stakeholder's confirmed, verbatim instruction, **"Yes, extend it to manual entry too."**
  - **(b) Existing, already-saved feature, reopened later:** Given a user reopens an existing, already-saved feature (not the same "Add feature" session) and selects one of three candidates (or confirms a manual entry), when the selection/entry is made, then the application displays its disclosed "not saved" message and the feature's previously-saved GeoPackage values remain unchanged. This is a **confirmed, permanent limitation** (Decision Log D-50), not a gap awaiting resolution, and must not be treated as a defect by any future reviewer.
- **AC-QPB-047** (post-MVP): Given an offline device, when an identification request is made, then it is queued without data loss and can later be retried.
- **AC-QPB-048** (post-MVP, feasibility-gated): Given the feasibility spike has not yet confirmed reliable automatic attachment-triggered identification on both iOS and Android, when a user attaches a photo, then the application does not claim or perform automatic identification and instead requires the explicit "Identify attached photos" action.
- **AC-QPB-049** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-17): Given a sampled raster value of exactly `0.0`, when probability lookup runs, then it is treated and displayed as a valid probability, not as "No probability data."
- **AC-QPB-050** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-17): Given a sampled raster value outside `0.0`–`1.0` that is not exactly `-9999`, when probability lookup runs, then the value is recorded as a validation warning and is never clamped into `0.0`–`1.0`.
- **AC-QPB-051** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-18): Given an online VWorld basemap or an offline MBTiles basemap generated into a project, when the project and its `MANIFEST.json` are inspected, then the required MOLIT/VWorld KOGL Type-1 attribution text is present in both, and remains present after the project is copied to a QField device.
- **AC-QPB-052** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-18): Given an offline MBTiles build during which the VWorld API returns a quota, authorization, or rate-limit error, when this occurs, then the build terminates gracefully with a clear message and no partial `.mbtiles` deliverable remains in the final output folder.
- **AC-QPB-053** (MVP; new, Decision Log D-19): Given the application launched with a detected QGIS 3.44 LTR installation on Windows or macOS, when the runtime-verification step runs, then it succeeds without requiring a separate `pip`-installed PyQGIS.
- **AC-QPB-069** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-31; closes former Open Question O-13): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, when the output folder is inspected, then it contains a `<project_slug>.qml` file (matching `project_slug`, not `project_display_name`) placed alongside the `.qgs` file, at the same folder level, consistent with QField's documented project-plugin discovery convention.
- ~~**AC-QPB-070** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-31; closes former Open Question O-13)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see AC-QPB-070 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-46) immediately below.** ~~Given a Type 1 `inventory_observation` feature, or a Type 2/3 `observation` feature, with its attribute form inspected in the generated project, then the "Identify attached photos" action is present as a `QML Widget` editor-widget embedded within that feature's own attribute form (built via the same `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField` mechanism as the rest of the form, FR-QPB-057), not as a separate, disconnected plugin surface — and the embedded QML has read access to that feature's own photo-path and identification/result attribute values.~~ (This text did not scope which host application — QField or QGIS Desktop — inspects the attribute form; Decision Log D-46 makes clear this criterion cannot be relied upon to hold in QGIS Desktop specifically. See AC-QPB-070 (further revised) below.)
- **AC-QPB-070** (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-46 — scopes the criterion explicitly to QField and discloses a QGIS-Desktop-rendering caveat; the underlying architecture requirement is otherwise unchanged): Given a Type 1 `inventory_observation` feature, or a Type 2/3 `observation` feature, with its attribute form inspected **in QField** — the confirmed target platform for this capability (Decision Log D-31) — then the "Identify attached photos" action is present as a `QML Widget` editor-widget embedded within that feature's own attribute form (built via the same `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField` mechanism as the rest of the form, FR-QPB-057), not as a separate, disconnected plugin surface, and the embedded QML has read access to that feature's own photo-path and identification/result attribute values. **This criterion is scoped to QField only.** Per Decision Log D-46, adopting QField's native `org.qfield.core`/`QfFileUtils` module (FR-QPB-101, further revised) to correctly read local attachment files is expected to make this same widget fail to load/render at all when the same generated project is opened in QGIS Desktop specifically — this is an accepted, disclosed tradeoff (Decision Log D-46), not a defect, and this criterion does not assert or require QGIS-Desktop rendering to succeed.
