- **AC-QPB-072** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-36; closes former Open Question O-18): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled and its bundled `reference/rasters/bce_inverse_corrected_probability_maps/` folder present (FR-QPB-112), when the embedded `QML Widget` identification action (FR-QPB-101) performs an occurrence-probability sample for a photo with valid EXIF GPS while the field device is disconnected from the desktop, then the sampled/displayed result correctly follows FR-QPB-108/DR-QPB-070's rules (valid `0.0`–`1.0` range; `-9999` displayed as "No probability data", never as zero or a probability; out-of-extent-coordinate and missing-raster cases both displaying "No probability data"; any other out-of-range value recorded as a validation warning and never silently clamped) using only the raster files already bundled on-device — without requiring the field project folder to first be copied back to a desktop computer. This criterion is subject to the technical-feasibility caveat recorded in Decision Log D-36/FR-QPB-111 (revised): if on-device raster sampling proves infeasible within QField's actual plugin API, this criterion cannot be satisfied on-device, and that infeasibility must be reported as a concrete implementer finding — not silently worked around by falling back to desktop-only sampling without disclosure.
- **AC-QPB-073** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-38): Given a candidate is selected and persisted for an `inventory_observation` (Type 1) or `observation` (Type 2/3) record, when the underlying identification-API response supplies timestamp and/or model-version information, then that information is persisted into the record's `identification_timestamp` (DR-QPB-052/053) and/or `identification_model_version` (DR-QPB-052/053) columns respectively; when the API response supplies neither, both columns remain `NULL` rather than being fabricated.

- **AC-QPB-075** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-40; supersedes AC-QPB-074's `correct_list[0]` criterion): Given a real KTSN CSV row whose `correct_list` JSON array contains more than one candidate accepted-taxon entry, and exactly one of those candidates' KTSN values appears in the extracted National Institute of Biological Resources (NIBR) accepted-taxa lookup list (sourced from `storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx`, sheet `62,604종`, column `KTSN`), when accepted-name resolution runs, then that one matching candidate is treated as the canonical entry and is resolved without being flagged ambiguous — regardless of that candidate's position in the `correct_list` array. This is independent of, and must not be confused with, AC-QPB-043's existing `KTSN`-vs-`KTNS` conflict-flagging behavior, which continues to apply, unaffected, to a genuine key-value conflict found within whichever single entry is resolved as canonical.
- **AC-QPB-076** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-40; makes former Open Question O-19's fallback behavior independently testable; O-19 is now closed per Decision Log D-42, which confirms this fallback is the stakeholder's confirmed intent): Given a real KTSN CSV row whose `correct_list` JSON array contains more than one candidate accepted-taxon entry, and either none, or more than one, of those candidates' KTSN values appear in the NIBR accepted-taxa lookup list, when accepted-name resolution runs, then the record is flagged ambiguous rather than resolved silently, and the now-superseded `correct_list[0]` rule (Decision Log D-39) is not applied as a silent tie-breaker.
- **AC-QPB-077** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-41): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, when the output folder is inspected, then it contains a lookup-list file under `reference/` containing only the extracted `KTSN` column values from the `62,604종` sheet (62,604 distinct values, no other xlsx column, row, or metadata retained), and any reference to that file from the `.qgs` project, the `<project_slug>.qml` plugin, or `MANIFEST.json` uses only a path relative to the project folder — never an absolute path and never a path outside the project folder — mirroring FR-QPB-091/DR-QPB-012's existing no-absolute-paths discipline as extended to this new artifact.
- **AC-QPB-078** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-43; makes FR-QPB-109 (further revised)'s manual-identification distinction independently testable): Given the user rejects all three Pl@ntNet candidates and enters a name manually, when the record is persisted, then `identification_status` is `"manual"` (not `"complete"`), and `identification_score`, `occurrence_probability`, and `identification_model_version` all remain `NULL`.
- **AC-QPB-079** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-45; mirrors AC-QPB-054 for the Pl@ntNet key): Given the user declines the Pl@ntNet key-embedding consent step (FR-QPB-115), when the project is generated, then no Pl@ntNet API key is embedded anywhere in the project — not the `.qgs` project variables, not the GeoPackage, not `MANIFEST.json`, not `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, not the `<project_slug>.qml` plugin, not application logs, and not any temporary filename — and the generated project's Pl@ntNet identification feature falls back to requiring manual key entry in QField, per FR-QPB-116.
- **AC-QPB-080** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-45; mirrors AC-QPB-055 for the Pl@ntNet key): Given the user accepts the Pl@ntNet key-embedding consent step and checkbox (FR-QPB-115), when the project is generated, then the `.qgs` file's project variables contain a variable named exactly `qpb_plantnet_api_key` holding the key, and the GeoPackage, `MANIFEST.json`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, application logs, and temporary filenames contain no copy of the key.
- **AC-QPB-081** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-45; mirrors AC-QPB-057 for the Pl@ntNet key): Given `MANIFEST.json` for a project with an embedded Pl@ntNet key, when inspected, then it contains only a boolean security-warning flag for the Pl@ntNet embedding (independent of, and in addition to if also present, the existing VWorld online-layer security-warning flag) and never the key value itself.
- ~~**AC-QPB-082** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-45; mirrors AC-QPB-058 for the Pl@ntNet key)~~ — **superseded, not deleted; see AC-QPB-082 (post-MVP; revised; Decision Log D-53) immediately below.** ~~Given the user selects "Remember this key" for the Pl@ntNet API key, when the application is restarted, then the key is retrieved from the OS credential store rather than from any plaintext application file; given the user does not select this option, then the key is not retained beyond the current application session.~~
- **AC-QPB-082** (post-MVP; revised; Decision Log D-53; mirrors AC-QPB-058 (revised) for the Pl@ntNet key): Given the user selects "Remember this key" for the Pl@ntNet API key and an encrypted-storage password has already been established, when the application is restarted and the same password is supplied, then the key is retrieved by deriving the decryption key via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from the supplied password and the stored salt and decrypting `credentials.enc` — never by any call into the `keyring` package or an OS credential store, and never read back as plaintext from any application file. Given the user does not select "Remember this key," then the key is not retained beyond the current application session, unchanged from before. Given no encrypted-storage password has yet been established, then "Remember this key" is unavailable for that session and the key is retained only for the current session.

- **AC-QPB-083** (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-48, complete five-step-pipeline form — extends the three-step entry immediately above, in place, to reflect the full four-step filtering pipeline (Steps 1–4) and the final 20,914-row count; the column-set and CSV-failure-mode assertions are unchanged and restated here unaltered): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled and a source `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` that exists and passes FR-QPB-105's required-column validation, when the output folder is inspected, then it contains the build-time-extracted lookup file at exactly `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`, whose header row lists exactly the 5 columns `ktsn`, `taxon_full_nm`, `taxon_kor_nm`, `taxon_jm_nm`, `correct_list`, in that order — no other column present, and none of these 5 missing — with the same number of data rows as the fully-filtered (Steps 1–4) subset of the source CSV computed per FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-48, complete five-step form) (**not** the same number of rows as the complete, unfiltered source CSV, and **not** the same as any single step's intermediate output alone) — see new AC-QPB-084 (Step 1), AC-QPB-085 (Step 2), AC-QPB-087 (Step 3), and AC-QPB-086 (Step 4) immediately below for the independently testable per-step assertions. Given the real, full source CSV and the real NIBR xlsx workbook (`storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx`, sheet `관속식물류`) as fixtures, when Steps 1–4 are run against them in sequence, then `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` contains exactly **20,914** data rows (matching the orchestrator-verified combined computation cited in Decision Log D-48) — not 212,397 (unfiltered), not 32,251 (Step 1 alone), not 26,763 (Steps 1–2 alone), and not 21,025 (Steps 1–3 alone). Given instead that the source `tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` is missing, or is present but fails FR-QPB-105's required-column validation, when a build with the identification subsystem enabled is attempted, then the build fails early with a clear message (the same failure FR-QPB-105 already requires for this condition) — it does not silently skip the extraction step, does not silently fall back to bundling the complete raw CSV, and does not produce a partial or truncated `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`.
- **AC-QPB-084** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-48; makes FR-QPB-118 (further revised)'s Step 1 row-filtering sub-step independently testable; unchanged in substance from this entry's original form, now explicitly scoped as "Step 1 of 5"): Given the complete, unfiltered `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` and a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, when the bundled `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` is inspected, then every row it contains corresponds to a source-CSV row that is a transitive descendant of `ktsn=120000098391` (Plantae) via the `p_ktsn` parent-pointer chain, and no row corresponding to a source-CSV row outside that subtree (e.g. a row belonging to the Animalia, Fungi, Bacteria, or Protista kingdoms, where such rows exist in the source CSV) is present. Given the real, full source CSV as fixture data, when Step 1's filtering runs against it in isolation, then it produces exactly 32,251 surviving rows (matching the orchestrator-verified transitive-closure computation cited in Decision Log D-48) — not the source file's full 212,397 data-row count, and not the 212,398-row (including header) raw row count either. (This assertion covers Step 1's own output only; Steps 2–4 further reduce this to 20,914 — see AC-QPB-085 (Step 2), AC-QPB-087 (Step 3), and AC-QPB-086 (Step 4).)
- **AC-QPB-085** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-48; makes FR-QPB-118 (further revised)'s Step 2 rank-filter sub-step independently testable; unaffected in substance and row counts by this entry's later insertion of Step 3, since Step 2 still runs immediately after Step 1 and before the new Step 3): Given the 32,251 rows surviving Step 1 (AC-QPB-084) as fixture input, when Step 2's `rank_id >= 700` filter is applied, then exactly **26,763** rows survive (matching the orchestrator-verified computation cited in Decision Log D-48), every surviving row's `rank_id` parses as an integer `>= 700`, and no surviving row has a `rank_id` value at or below any genus/family/order/etc.-level rank code (e.g. `600` Genus, `500` Family, `400` Order). Given a row whose `rank_id` value is missing, blank, or does not parse as an integer, when Step 2's filter is applied to it, then that row is excluded — it must never be guess-included on the theory that a malformed value might represent a qualifying rank. (This assertion covers Step 2's own output only; the new Step 3, AC-QPB-087, further reduces this to 21,025, and Step 4, AC-QPB-086, further reduces that to 20,914.)
- **AC-QPB-087** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-48; makes FR-QPB-118 (further revised)'s new Step 3 vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist sub-step independently testable): Given the 26,763 rows surviving Step 2 (AC-QPB-085) as fixture input, when Step 3's seven-phylum allowlist filter (`Magnoliophyta`, `Pteridophyta`, `Pinophyta`, `Filicophyta`, `Lycopodiophyta`, `Psilophyta`, `Sphenophyta`, matched against the `r200_nm` column) is applied, then exactly **21,025** rows survive (matching the orchestrator-verified computation cited in Decision Log D-48), and every surviving row's `r200_nm` value is one of those seven phyla. Given a synthetic fixture whose rows span several phyla, including at least one of the three bryophyte phyla (`Bryophyta`, `Marchantiophyta`, or `Anthocerophyta`) and at least one of the three algae-related phyla classified under Plantae by this dataset (`Charophyta`, `Chlorophyta`, or `Glaucophyta`), together with rows in one or more of the seven allowlisted vascular-plant phyla, when Step 3's filter is applied, then only the rows in the seven-phylum allowlist survive — every bryophyte-phylum row and every algae-related-phylum row is excluded, regardless of having survived Steps 1–2. Given a row whose `r200_nm` value is missing or blank, when Step 3's filter is applied to it, then that row is excluded — it must never be guess-included on the theory that a missing value might represent an allowlisted phylum.
- **AC-QPB-086** (post-MVP; further revised, Decision Log D-48 — renumbered from "Step 3" to "Step 4" and recomputed over the narrower row set surviving the new Step 3, changing its specific counts from this entry's prior form; makes FR-QPB-118 (further revised)'s Step 4 duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution sub-step independently testable, both at the real-fixture combined-result level and at the synthetic-fixture per-outcome level): Given the 21,025 rows surviving Step 3 (AC-QPB-087) as fixture input, together with the real NIBR xlsx workbook's `관속식물류` sheet, when Step 4's duplicate-resolution rule is applied, then exactly **20,914** rows survive overall (matching the orchestrator-verified computation cited in Decision Log D-48: 7 of 58 duplicated normalized scientific names each reduced to exactly one surviving row; the remaining 51 of 58 dropped entirely, along with all of their duplicate rows — 118 total duplicated rows going in, 104 rows removed). Independently of that real-fixture combined count: given a synthetic fixture in which two rows share the same normalized `taxon_full_nm` but have two different `ktsn` values, and a synthetic `관속식물류`-equivalent lookup fixture in which that same normalized name maps to exactly one distinct `KTSN` value equal to one of those two rows' own `ktsn` values, when Step 4's resolution rule is applied, then exactly one row survives for that name, and its `ktsn` equals the `KTSN` value found in the lookup fixture — the other duplicate row is dropped. Given instead a second synthetic fixture pair in which the duplicated name, in the synthetic lookup fixture, either (a) does not appear at all, (b) maps to more than one distinct `KTSN` value, or (c) maps to a `KTSN` value that matches neither duplicate row's own `ktsn`, when Step 4's resolution rule is applied to any of these three variants, then zero rows survive for that name in `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` — both original duplicate rows are dropped, and no fallback heuristic (file order, `taxon_jm_nm` accepted/synonym status, or any other tie-break) is applied to rescue one of them.
- **AC-QPB-088** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-52; makes FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-52)'s photo-resize-via-temporary-copy mechanism independently, structurally testable, mirroring how AC-QPB-069/AC-QPB-070 make FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-101's other structural mechanism details independently testable, and how AC-QPB-046 (Decision Log D-50) made FR-QPB-109's write-back mechanism independently testable at the mechanism level): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, when the embedded identification widget's QML source (the `QML Widget` attribute-editor content, FR-QPB-101) is inspected, then it contains: (1) a call writing the original photo's already-read bytes to a new temporary file (`FileUtils.writeFileContent()`), distinct from the original attachment file's own path; (2) a subsequent call to `FileUtils.restrictImageSize()` against that temporary file's path only, with a maximum width/height argument of `1280` — and never against the original attachment file's own path; (3) a subsequent call reading the resized bytes back from that same temporary file (`FileUtils.readFileContent()`) for use as the Pl@ntNet multipart request body, in place of the original, unresized bytes; and (4) a temporary-file cleanup call that overwrites the temporary file with empty content (`FileUtils.writeFileContent(tempPath, "")`), not a call to `FileUtils.deleteFiles()`. This criterion is independently testable via static/structural inspection of the generated QML source and does not require a real QField device.
- **AC-QPB-094** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-54; makes FR-QPB-104 (further revised)'s new request-parameter addition independently testable, mirroring AC-QPB-040's request-shape-adjacent framing): Given a valid one-plant identification request, when the outgoing Pl@ntNet request is inspected, then its query parameters include `include-related-images=true`, alongside the existing `api-key` and `nb-results=3` parameters (FR-QPB-104, further revised; Decision Log D-54).
- **AC-QPB-095** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-54; makes FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-54)'s candidate-card image-display/attribution/graceful-degradation requirements independently, structurally testable, mirroring how AC-QPB-046/AC-QPB-088 make other FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-109 mechanism details independently testable via structural QML inspection): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, when the embedded identification widget's QML source (the `QML Widget` attribute-editor content, FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-109) is inspected, then it contains, for each of the three displayed candidates: (1) an `Image` QML element whose `source` property is bound to that candidate's own small (`s`) size-variant representative-image URL, structurally distinct per candidate; (2) an attribution-text construction bound to that same candidate's image data, combining the contributor's name (`author`), the literal text "Pl@ntNet", and the literal text "CC BY-SA," conditioned on that candidate actually having image data; and (3) a conditional/guard construction such that, when a candidate's image field is absent or empty, neither the `Image` element's `source` nor the attribution-text construction renders any content for that candidate (no broken-image placeholder, no attribution text for a nonexistent image), while that candidate's other existing display content (scientific name, confidence, KTSN/probability enrichment, etc., FR-QPB-109) is unaffected. This criterion is independently testable via static/structural inspection of the generated QML source and does not require a real QField device or network connectivity.
- **AC-QPB-096** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-54; manual-QA-only placeholder, mirroring Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072's existing convention for device-dependent criteria that cannot be confirmed via structural inspection alone): Given a generated project with the identification subsystem enabled, a real device (or QGIS Desktop, subject to the existing QField-vs-QGIS-Desktop rendering-scope caveat, Decision Log D-46) with network connectivity, and a real Pl@ntNet identification response that includes related images for at least one candidate, when the "Identify attached photos" action runs and the candidate cards render, then: (a) the representative image actually renders on screen for each candidate for which the response supplied one, alongside its required CC BY-SA attribution text; and (b) given a subsequent, isolated failure to load a specific candidate's image (e.g. a network hiccup occurring after the initial identify response has already succeeded), that candidate's existing textual content remains fully displayed and unaffected. - **AC-QPB-129** (new, Decision Log D-88; recursive-resolution safety/failure handling): Given a recursive chain with a repeated KTSN (including a self-reference), a missing target row, a missing/blank/malformed/non-array or empty `correct_list`, a candidate with neither usable `KTSN` nor `KTNS`, a differing `KTSN`/`KTNS` pair, or a chain requiring more than 64 transitions, when accepted-name resolution runs, then it terminates deterministically without looping, does not return any non-`정명` row as accepted, retains the direct match, and exposes the existing unresolved or ambiguous indication. A chain that reaches an exact `taxon_jm_nm == '정명'` row within 64 transitions resolves successfully from that terminal row; no arbitrary candidate or intermediate row is returned.

- **AC-QPB-135** (MVP; revised; Decision Log D-94; initial layer visibility): Given a newly generated project for each supported survey type and each selected basemap mode that produces a layer, when the project is opened for the first time and its root layer tree is inspected, every present layer node in `Survey data` and `Basemap`, and every present non-lookup layer node in `Reference`, is checked/enabled (`isVisible() == true`) — including non-spatial reference tables and any generated/uploaded reference or extent layer. Every synonym has `source_no = '-'`, follows a preceding accepted row, retains its own KTSN/raw `학명`/URL, and has an `accepted_ktsn`; every accepted row has a nonblank source No and `accepted_ktsn = ktsn`. No QGIS relation, foreign key, or survey write-back target is created for either table.

Given any invalid/missing/mutated source condition in FR-QPB-138/13.3a, then no partial table or promoted project exists and the UI offers re-selection/upload with an actionable error.
- **AC-QPB-142** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-95; lookup/write-back compatibility): Given a Pl@ntNet name matching an accepted or synonym row, when matching and selection persistence run, then matching uses `scientific_name_without_authority`, a synonym resolves to its `accepted_ktsn`, the stored `selected_scientific_name` is the accepted row's preserved raw `학명` (including authority), and no ambiguous comparison-key collision writes a guessed value. - **AC-QPB-143** (post-MVP; new, Decision Log D-95; taxonomy report): Given saved Type 1–3 observations with accepted and synonym KTSNs, when Export HTML Report runs, then the report retains the existing schema/domain-record sections and adds Phylum/Class/Order/Family/Genus aggregation rows sourced from the accepted reference row, with correct observation and distinct-KTSN counts and no count multiplication from the lookup join. Given generated output inspection, then no raw canonical workbook, old CSV, old NIBR workbook, Pl@ntNet response, photo bytes, API key, or absolute source path is present in the project; existing old projects are not migrated in place.

Given a generated project from that application, when its output is inspected, then only the validated/materialized reference tables and provenance are present; the source workbook itself is absent.

## 19. Decision Log

All entries below are dated 2026-08-10 and derive from the three-round clarification conversation between the spec-writer and the human stakeholder that preceded this specification.

- **D-1**: Round-1 answer — deployment model was initially "locally installed desktop app with a local web UI." **Superseded by D-9.**
- **D-2**: Spec granularity — one integrated product specification covering the whole product, organized into modular sections; no separate per-feature specs at this stage (they may be derived later from this approved document).
- **D-3**: MVP boundary explicitly enumerated by the stakeholder (Section 4.1); Pl@ntNet/KTSN/probability/plugin/offline-queue/on-device-raster items explicitly placed post-MVP (Section 4.2).
- **D-4**: Section 15 items (a)–(h) of the Requirements Draft resolved or explicitly deferred as recorded throughout Sections 8, 13, and 20 of this specification.
- **D-5** — **SUPERSEDED by D-16 (for Type 1) and D-23 (for the Type 2/3 leak this entry's "at least one" framing caused)**: Type 1 photo requirement reworked: at least one plant photo in total (not one each of leaf/flower/fruit), each photo tagged with an organ from a fixed enum, relation-free, compatible with up to five identification photos. This entry's own "at least one" framing was later superseded for Type 1 by D-16 (three optional, unrelated photo fields, no photo required), but the "at least one required" phrasing had evidently leaked into the unrelated Type 2/3 requirements (DR-QPB-030/031/040/042) and AC-QPB-009, which incorrectly carried a mandatory-photo rule for Type 2/3 that was never confirmed by the stakeholder. That leak is identified and corrected by D-23.
- **D-6**: Exact QGIS/QField/GDAL version matrix left open, recorded as an implementation prerequisite and release gate (NFR-QPB-001), not invented here.
- **D-7**: VWorld offline-caching terms compliance left open, recorded as a release-blocking external compliance decision (NFR-QPB-003), not blocking specification drafting.
- **D-8**: Probability rasters need not ship to the smartphone for MVP or the first post-MVP increment; on-device lookup deferred to a later, separately evaluated feature (FR-QPB-111). **Clarified/superseded by D-36 (2026-08-15):** D-36 supersedes this entry's on-device-deferral framing for this phase specifically — in-field, on-device probability sampling is now in scope per an explicit, direct stakeholder instruction. This entry's own text above is unchanged and remains the historical record of the original decision; it is annotated, not reworded or deleted, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-13/D-33).
- **D-9** (supersedes D-1): Corrected deployment model — locally installed, single-user **native desktop application** built with Python + PySide6/Qt, not a web application; first-class support for Windows and macOS; no remote application server; all project-generation work runs locally; user selects a local output directory (Section 5.1, 5.5).
- **D-10**: QGIS/GDAL runtime is a host dependency (not bundled in MVP), with automatic detection, manual path override, environment verification, and non-technical error messaging (Section 5.2).
- **D-11**: Provisional architecture direction — UI (PySide6) and QGIS/PyQGIS/GDAL operations (local GIS worker process) run in separate local processes with job/progress/result exchange; no remote worker; exact IPC mechanism left to implementation (Section 5.3).
- **D-12**: Schema forward-compatibility — Types 1–3 include nullable, inactive Pl@ntNet-related columns in MVP schemas to avoid a later breaking migration; Type 4 (`community`) is explicitly excluded from this treatment unless a later requirement introduces such fields; every generated database must carry schema-version metadata (Sections 7, 8).
- **D-13**: Pl@ntNet is a guaranteed-manual, explicit "Identify attached photos" action at minimum for its first post-MVP implementation; automatic/silent identification is conditional on a feasibility spike passing on both iOS and Android (Section 13.1). **Clarified, not reworded, by D-33 (2026-08-14):** D-33 narrows *how* this entry's feasibility-spike requirement is satisfied for the guaranteed-manual baseline specifically (four of five spike areas verified as a byproduct of implementing that baseline correctly); this entry's own text above is unchanged and remains the governing statement that automatic/silent identification stays conditional on the spike passing on both platforms.
- **D-14** (this entry duplicates/confirms D-13's wording as given verbatim by the stakeholder in round 2/3): manual species entry and photo attachment are the guaranteed MVP behavior; the application must never claim automatic identification behavior that does not actually exist.
- **D-15**: QField mobile scope — both iOS and Android are required targets; iOS is the primary validation platform (stakeholder's field device), but the generated project must not use iOS-only behavior or exclude Android. Required validation paths: macOS→iOS (primary), Windows→iOS, Windows→Android, macOS→Android. Resolves round-2 open question on iOS scope.

All entries below are dated 2026-08-10 and derive from a fourth clarification round in which the stakeholder revised the Draft specification directly.

- **D-16** (closes former Open Question O-3): The Type-1 five-slot, organ-tagged photo design is incorrect and is superseded. `inventory_observation` instead has exactly three optional, nullable, relation-free photo-path fields — `leaf_photo_path`, `flower_photo_path`, `fruit_photo_path` — each storing at most one relative attachment path; the field name identifies the organ, so no separate organ-tag column exists. The form must present three separately labeled Attachment widgets ("Leaf photo", "Flower photo", "Fruit photo"). No photo is required to save or complete a Type-1 observation. If at least one photo is present, it may later be used by the post-MVP Pl@ntNet feature. This closes and removes the former five-slot assumption (A-QPB-003) and the acceptance criterion that required at least one Type-1 photo (AC-QPB-008, revised).
- **D-17** (closes former Open Question O-4): Probability raster encoding is confirmed: valid range `0.0`–`1.0` inclusive; NoData sentinel `-9999`. `0.0` is a valid probability and must not be treated as NoData. `-9999` displays as "No probability data," not as a probability. A coordinate outside the raster extent also displays "No probability data." Values outside `0.0`–`1.0` other than `-9999` are invalid raster data and must be recorded as a validation warning, never clamped into range. The stored/processed value stays on the 0–1 scale; the UI may additionally format it as a percentage.
- **D-18** (closes the licensing portion of former Open Question O-5): Based on the Korea Public Data Portal's listing of the MOLIT WMTS/TMS API as free under the Korea Open Government License (KOGL) Type 1 (https://www.data.go.kr/data/3046388/openapi.do), and the published KOGL Type-1 terms permitting online/offline use, modification, and commercial use with attribution (https://www.kogl.or.kr/info/licenseType1.do), offline MBTiles generation remains in MVP scope, subject to: visible VWorld/MOLIT attribution in the generated QGIS project and manifest, preserved through transfer to QField; use of the user's own API key only, never stored in the `.mbtiles`/manifest/validation-report/transfer-folder files produced by the offline pipeline; compliance with the key's traffic quota; bounded concurrency and rate limiting; pre-generation tile-count estimation; graceful termination with a clear message on quota/authorization/rate-limit errors; and no attempt to bypass provider restrictions. **Noted limitation**: the reviewed published sources do not use the specific phrase "bulk offline tile caching"; this is recorded as a documentation-precision limitation, not treated as a blocker for this internal offline-fieldwork use case. Application documentation must state that provider terms/quotas can change and should be rechecked each release (NFR-QPB-059). **Flagged, not silently resolved**: this decision's "no API key storage in the `.qgs`... " condition is scoped in this specification to the offline MBTiles pipeline/output (NFR-QPB-058); whether it is also intended to revoke the pre-existing round-1 exception allowing the VWorld key in the generated project's *online*-layer runtime URL (FR-QPB-073/NFR-QPB-014) is unresolved — see Open Question O-10.
- **D-19** (closes the product-level "which QGIS series" question, formerly part of Open Question O-6): QGIS 3.44 LTR (the latest available patch release in that series from the official QGIS distribution, e.g. 3.44.12 at the time of this decision) is the MVP target on both Windows and macOS. PyQGIS is supplied by the QGIS Desktop installation and must not be installed separately via `pip`. PyQGIS-based APIs (not direct `.qgs` XML editing) remain the required approach for creating/configuring layers, relations, forms, widgets, field constraints, relative paths, and processing operations. The process model is: PySide6 UI process → detects QGIS Desktop install → launches a separate GIS worker process using that install's Python/PyQGIS environment → worker initializes `QgsApplication` headlessly → communicates progress/results/warnings/errors back to the UI via the still-open IPC mechanism (O-1); this separation is required because the UI and QGIS runtime may use different Qt Python bindings/versions. QGIS 4.2/4.x is explicitly **not** an MVP requirement; migration will be reassessed once a supported 4.x LTR exists and QField iOS/Android validation of generated projects is complete. The exact tested patch version, Windows versions, macOS versions, GDAL version, and QField versions remain open as a narrower release-gate item — see Open Question O-9.
- **D-20** (closes former Open Question O-8): Updating shared documentation is authorized and has been carried out as part of this revision. `README.md`, `docs/product.md`, and `docs/architecture.md` have been updated to replace web-application framing with the native PySide6/Qt desktop application, state Windows and macOS as first-class MVP platforms, describe the local PySide6 UI plus separate PyQGIS worker process, state QGIS 3.44 LTR as the MVP runtime dependency, state that no remote application server or PostgreSQL database is used, describe local GeoPackage storage and self-contained folder transfer, and state that QField on iOS and Android is supported with iOS as the primary validation platform. The product specification itself remains marked Draft; no undecided implementation detail was added to the shared docs beyond what this specification already records.

This entry is dated 2026-08-10 and derives from a fifth clarification round in which the stakeholder resolved the conflict this specification had explicitly refused to resolve unilaterally (former Open Question O-10), and closed the project-naming question (former Open Question O-2).

- **D-21** (closes former Open Question O-10; deliberate security/usability tradeoff): the round-1 online-layer exception (originally FR-QPB-073/NFR-QPB-014) and this specification's own offline-MBTiles no-key-storage rule (NFR-QPB-058, introduced closing O-5) are reconciled, not left in tension, by the stakeholder's explicit decision: a single, narrowly scoped exception permits the VWorld API key to be embedded in the generated project's **online**-layer URI inside the `.qgs` file, and only after an explicit informed-consent flow (disclosure that the `.qgs` will contain the key in readable form, that recipients of the folder may extract it, a mandatory confirmation checkbox, a recommendation to use a dedicated/restricted key, and a clear distinction from offline MBTiles) — FR-QPB-073, FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079. If the user declines, no key is embedded and the online layer is omitted, with an explanation that it can be added manually later. Outside this one exception, the key must never appear in the GeoPackage, `.mbtiles`, manifest, validation report, logs, temporary filenames, or exported diagnostics (NFR-QPB-014, NFR-QPB-017); the manifest may record only a boolean security-warning flag. For offline MBTiles generation specifically, the key is used only transiently during tile retrieval and must not remain in the delivered project (FR-QPB-078, NFR-QPB-058). The desktop application may persist the key across sessions only via an explicit "Remember this key" opt-in stored in the OS credential store; otherwise it is session-only (NFR-QPB-018). This exception is scoped strictly to the VWorld online-layer case and must not be extended to Pl@ntNet or any other credential (FR-QPB-079, NFR-QPB-019). This is recorded as a deliberate security/usability tradeoff — accepting a disclosed, consent-gated, narrowly scoped risk for the online-layer case, in exchange for a working online basemap, while closing every other avenue by which a provider key could leak through the generated project.
- **D-22** (closes former Open Question O-2): project naming is resolved as a `project_display_name` (Unicode, free-form) / `project_slug` (ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores only; ≤64 characters; never blank; rejects path-traversal components and Windows-reserved filenames) / `project_id` (UUID v4, independent of both names) three-way split. The output-folder name (derived from `project_slug`) must be previewed before generation (restates FR-QPB-022), and an existing project folder must never be silently overwritten (restates E-QPB-008). This removes the former sanitization assumption (A-QPB-002).

This entry is dated 2026-08-10 and derives from a sixth clarification round in which the stakeholder corrected a misinterpretation of the Requirements Draft's photo language that had leaked into the Type 2/3 photo requirements.

- **D-23** (corrects a misinterpretation stemming from D-5; supersedes the "at least one" cardinality in DR-QPB-030, DR-QPB-031, DR-QPB-040, DR-QPB-042, NFR-QPB-041, FR-QPB-024, Section 4.1, and AC-QPB-009): The Requirements Draft's "allow one or more photos to be attached" language described a *capability* (photos may be attached), not a mandatory-photo rule. All Type 1–3 photo relationships are optional. Type 1's `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` fields were already correctly specified as optional (Decision Log D-16; unchanged by this entry). For Type 2, a `survey` may have zero or more related `survey_photo` records and an `observation` may have zero or more related `observation_photo` records. For Type 3, a `plot` may have zero or more related `plot_photo` records and an `observation` may have zero or more related `observation_photo` records; when plot photos exist, they remain associated with the permanent `plot`, not with each repeated `survey` (DR-QPB-041, unchanged). Type 4 (`community`) continues to have no photo field, photo table, or photo requirement (DR-QPB-050, unchanged). Photos are reference material; observation photos may optionally be used by the post-MVP Pl@ntNet workflow. The absence of photos must never prevent an ordinary save, prevent project validation, prevent field completion, convert an otherwise valid record into an error, or prevent generation or transfer of the project. The undefined "marked field-complete" photo-validation concept, which appeared only in the prior text of AC-QPB-009 and was never defined elsewhere in this specification, is removed entirely; no `Draft`/`Field complete`/`field_status`-style field is introduced solely for photo validation. If a photo child record is created, its `path` must be a valid, non-empty relative attachment path, and a referenced attachment later found missing from the project folder must still be reported as a broken attachment (this does not make the absence of a photo record itself an error). The post-MVP limit of up to five photos (DR-QPB-033) applies only to the photos selected for a single Pl@ntNet request; it is not a minimum and does not limit the number of reference photos stored in the related photo tables. This decision corrects DR-QPB-030, DR-QPB-031, DR-QPB-040, DR-QPB-042, NFR-QPB-041, FR-QPB-024, Section 4.1, and AC-QPB-009, all of which previously stated or implied "at least one photo required" for Type 2/3 photo relations; the existing photo tables (`survey_photo`, `observation_photo`, `plot_photo`), Attachment widgets, relative-path rules, and gallery/relation configuration for Type 2/3 photos are unchanged — only the "at least one required" cardinality constraint is removed.

This entry and D-25 below are implementation-phase amendments, recorded during a post-MVP-approval "macOS release checkpoint" implementation phase. They do not derive from the Requirements Draft or from the six pre-implementation clarification rounds recorded as D-1–D-23 above; they derive from explicit, direct, unambiguous stakeholder instructions given during that later implementation phase, reconciled back into this specification per this project's change-control discipline.

- **D-24** (implementation-phase amendment; carve-out to FR-QPB-011, not a reversal of it): The wizard's interactive site/plot/bbox drawing canvas (implementing FR-QPB-025's "or drawing features on an interactive map" clause) initially rendered only a plain coordinate graticule, with no geographic reference imagery. The original FR-QPB-011 constraint — "The only network requests the MVP application may make are: (a) VWorld online basemap tile requests when online mode is selected, and (b) VWorld tile downloads when generating an offline MBTiles basemap. No other network access is permitted in the MVP." — reflected a deliberate, real decision (the VWorld-only network boundary underlying D-9/D-10/D-11's architecture) and is **not** being retracted or judged wrong for the actual basemap-generation pipeline it governs; that pipeline (Sections 10/11) remains exactly as it was. However, the stakeholder found the graticule-only canvas hard to use in practice and, when offered a choice between (i) keeping the graticule-only fallback, (ii) using VWorld tiles for this UI purpose, or (iii) using free OpenStreetMap tiles for this UI purpose, gave the explicit, verbatim instruction: **"Use OpenStreetMap at this step."** This was implemented as real OSM XYZ raster tile fetching (`https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`, in `qfield_builder/ui/osm_tiles.py` and `qfield_builder/ui/map_canvas.py`), used strictly as an ephemeral visual backdrop while a user is drawing in the wizard's drawing canvas. The exact, narrow scope of this carve-out: (1) OSM tiles are fetched only for on-screen display during interactive drawing; (2) fetched tile imagery is never written into, or referenced by, the generated project output — no `.mbtiles` file, no `.qgs` reference, nothing persisted by a build; (3) OSM is not, and must not become, an approved basemap source for the generated project's actual online (Section 10) or offline (Section 11) basemap pipeline, both of which remain VWorld-only, governed by FR-QPB-070–FR-QPB-089/NFR-QPB-003/058/059 exactly as before, and entirely untouched by this decision; (4) the operational safeguards required of this exception — identifying `User-Agent`, fetch-at-most-once-per-session caching (no retry storms), permanently visible ODbL attribution, and zero-network-dependency drawing functionality with a graticule fallback — are recorded in new NFR-QPB-060. FR-QPB-011 is revised, not silently rewritten, to add this single carve-out as new clause (c); its original clauses (a) and (b), and the reasoning that produced them, are preserved unchanged and remain the governing rule for the actual basemap-generation workflow. New acceptance criteria AC-QPB-062–AC-QPB-064 make this boundary independently testable. This entry closes no prior Open Question and does not reopen O-9 or any other still-open item.
- **D-25** (implementation-phase amendment; distinguishes source/config cross-platform readiness from built-artifact delivery timing): During the same implementation phase as D-24, the stakeholder gave the explicit, verbatim instruction: **"Keep Windows packaging as a required subsequent release task, but ensure the source and packaging configuration remain cross-platform."** Only a macOS `.app` was built and delivered in this phase (via `packaging/build_macos_app.sh` and `packaging/qfield_builder.spec`); no Windows installer/executable was produced. Verified evidence supporting the cross-platform-configuration claim: the PyInstaller packaging configuration (`packaging/qfield_builder.spec`) contains exactly one `sys.platform == "darwin"`-guarded step — the `BUNDLE(...)` call that wraps the OS-agnostic PyInstaller onedir output into a macOS `.app` bundle; everything else in that spec is standard, OS-agnostic PyInstaller `Analysis`/`PYZ`/`EXE`/`COLLECT` output, already usable as-is to produce a Windows build; and no macOS-only assumption was introduced into the application's own source code. This draws an explicit distinction between two things this specification previously conflated under a single "Windows and macOS as first-class MVP platforms" statement: (a) the underlying source and packaging *configuration* remaining genuinely cross-platform — unchanged and unweakened as an MVP requirement (NFR-QPB-030, revised) — and (b) actual delivery of a *built* Windows installer/executable artifact for this MVP release, which is deferred to a required subsequent release (FR-QPB-014, revised), not descoped and not left ambiguous. macOS packaging is recorded as the first platform delivered. This reconciliation connects to, but does not duplicate the logic of, AC-QPB-032 (Section 18.5, revised above) and Open Question O-9 (the still-open, narrower exact release-gate compatibility matrix — tested QGIS/OS/QField versions — which remains a separate question from *whether* a Windows artifact has been built at all, and is unaffected by this entry).

**Closing note on durable UI/visual-design conventions:** category-D UX/visual-design refinements made during the same implementation phase (Qt Fusion style, `QWizard.WizardStyle.ModernStyle`, the refined neutral palette, page layout-margin/spacing conventions, and wizard window size bounds) are **not** recorded as numbered FR/NFR/AC items in this specification. Consistent with this project's documentation-structure conventions (durable UI rules belong in a UI/design guideline document, not the core data/functional specification), they are recorded in a new sibling document, `docs/ui-design-guidelines.md`.

The three entries below (D-26, D-27, D-28) are dated 2026-08-14 and derive from three separate, explicit stakeholder instructions given directly to the spec-writer, classified per this project's change-control discipline (`docs/change-control.md`) as, respectively, Category C (stakeholder-approved product change), Category B (specification clarification/omission), and Category C (stakeholder-approved product change). Each is its own independently traceable change; none reopens or silently rewrites D-1–D-25 above.

- **D-26** (Category C; supersedes the layer-list portion of the original FR-QPB-071, not the surrounding VWorld key-handling rules): Verbatim stakeholder instruction: **"Change the VWorld endpoint to: `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml`. This capabilities XML includes all five map layers: Base, White, Midnight, Hybrid, and Satellite. The application should obtain and support the available layers through this endpoint."** This supersedes the layer-list portion of FR-QPB-071 as it stood — the original text (copied verbatim from the Requirements Draft's `Base`/`gray`/`midnight`/`Hybrid`/`Satellite` list) is retained above, struck through and marked superseded, not deleted. This is a layer-discovery/naming correction to the existing VWorld online/offline basemap pipeline (Sections 10/11), not a new pipeline: the `{key}` placeholder and per-tile GetTile mechanics for actual tile retrieval (FR-QPB-072) are unchanged; only the mechanism by which the application discovers/validates which layer names are legitimate changes, from a hardcoded, Requirements-Draft-derived list to a query against VWorld's own capabilities endpoint. The surrounding key-handling rules — FR-QPB-073, FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079, NFR-QPB-014, NFR-QPB-017–NFR-QPB-019, NFR-QPB-058 — are unaffected and continue to apply exactly as before. FR-QPB-011's network-boundary enumeration is clarified (not altered in substance) to note that this capabilities request is within the existing VWorld network allowance, not a new destination or purpose. **Open compatibility question, flagged rather than silently resolved:** this specification cannot determine, from any artifact available to the spec-writer, whether any previously generated `.qgs` project already exists (in the field or otherwise) that references the superseded lowercase `gray`/`midnight` layer identifiers as literal layer names. No such generated project file was found in this repository, and the implementation-phase status notes in `CLAUDE.md` describe the current build as an uncommitted, not-yet-shipped "release checkpoint" — but the spec-writer has no visibility into whether the stakeholder has already used a prior build to generate real field projects. This is recorded as an open question (see Section 20, new O-11) for the stakeholder to confirm, rather than asserting there is no backward-compatibility impact.
- **D-27** (Category B; closes a specification omission, not a reversal of any existing requirement): Verbatim stakeholder instruction: **"Provide a brief Korean explanation for each survey type, describing how survey information is collected, structured, and recorded. These explanations should help users understand the differences between the four survey types before making a selection."** Prior to this entry, Section 6.2 (Step 2, FR-QPB-023/024) contained no requirement at all for explanatory/help content at the survey-type-selection step; this was a genuine specification gap, not a prior decision being reversed. New FR-QPB-024a requires a brief Korean-language, per-type explanation of each survey type's data-collection/structuring/recording model, grounded in each type's actual schema (Section 8), displayed before the user selects a type. The exact displayed Korean wording is implementation-authored, domain-facing content and is not dictated by this specification; per the change-control record, this is flagged for the stakeholder's review once the wording is drafted during implementation, since only the requirement and its acceptance criterion (AC-QPB-066) are specified here, not the literal copy.
- **D-28** (Category C; new NFR, distinct from this project's existing Korean *data*-content requirements): Verbatim stakeholder instruction: **"The application's intended end users are Korean. Change all user-facing text in the application to Korean, including labels, buttons, instructions, validation messages, warnings, progress messages, dialogs, and error messages. Internal identifiers, source-code symbols, file-format terms, and proper names may remain unchanged where translation would be inappropriate."** This is a new, broader requirement about the desktop application's own displayed UI strings, distinct from this specification's pre-existing Korean *data*-content requirements (`selected_korean_name`, `README_TRANSFER_KO.md`, KTSN Korean-name enrichment in Section 13), which govern domain/data content, not the application's own chrome. New NFR-QPB-070 (Section 14.5) records this requirement, its explicit carve-out (internal identifiers, source-code symbols, file-format terms, and proper names), and that it is scoped strictly to this application's own PySide6 wizard UI — it does not, and cannot, govern the third-party UI language of QGIS Desktop or QField, which are outside this project's control. This specification document's own prose (its FR/NFR/DR/AC text) remains in English and is not affected by this requirement; only the shipped application's UI is in scope.

This entry is dated 2026-08-14 and derives from a follow-up stakeholder exchange occurring after D-26 above. The stakeholder's report was first clarified with the stakeholder — because the mechanism D-26 already covers (per-tile GetTile URLs) is not itself malformed — before being confirmed as a deliberate architecture decision rather than treated as a defect.

- **D-29** (Category C; supersedes only the *connection-mechanism* portion of FR-QPB-072 — the online layer's runtime connection method — and does not touch Section 11's offline tile-downloading or FR-QPB-071's layer-discovery mechanism): Verbatim stakeholder report: **"Generated QGIS project file still has a wrong URL Vworld map. Map url should be `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml`."** Because the application's existing per-tile XYZ GetTile URL pattern (`.../{key}/{layer}/{z}/{y}/{x}.png`) is not itself malformed — it is a valid, documented VWorld REST tile-access convention, and this is what the original FR-QPB-072 required — this was clarified with the stakeholder before being treated as a specification/implementation defect (Category A). The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice, given after that clarification, was: **"Switch to QGIS's native WMTS connection."** This is recorded as a deliberate, real architecture change to how the generated project's online layer connects to VWorld (Category C), not a bug-fix and not merely a URL-string correction.
  - **Scope, confirmed narrow:** (1) This decision supersedes only the online VWorld layer's connection *mechanism* in the generated `.qgs` project (Section 10; FR-QPB-072, revised above) — the application must add that layer using QGIS's native WMTS provider, connected to the VWorld WMTS capabilities endpoint (`https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml`), letting QGIS itself negotiate the specific layer, tile matrix set, and tile format from the capabilities document, instead of the application manually constructing a per-tile XYZ URL template and adding it as a `type=xyz` raster layer. (2) It does **not** apply to Section 11's offline MBTiles generation (FR-QPB-080–089): that pipeline downloads individual tiles itself via ordinary HTTP requests to assemble a `.mbtiles` file — a fundamentally different mechanism from a live, QGIS-managed layer connection, which needs concrete, individually-fetchable per-tile URLs for its own programmatic bulk-download process — and must keep using concrete per-tile GetTile URLs exactly as before; `build_tile_request_url()`/the offline tile-downloader in `qfield_builder/mbtiles.py`/`vworld_tiles.py` are unchanged and unweakened by this decision. (3) It does **not** apply to FR-QPB-071 (revised; Decision Log D-26), the layer-*discovery* mechanism (querying the capabilities endpoint to learn which layer names/identifiers are currently supported) — that is a separate concern (which layers exist) from this decision (how the online layer connects at runtime); FR-QPB-071 is unaffected in substance, even though both now reference the same capabilities endpoint URL for their respective, distinct purposes.
  - **FR-QPB-073 reviewed, not changed:** the consent-gated key-embedding exception (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079, NFR-QPB-014/017–019/058) is unaffected in substance. The VWorld key still appears embedded in the online layer's datasource URI under the same narrowly scoped, consent-gated exception; only its location within that URI changes, from a GetTile URL's `{key}` path segment to the capabilities endpoint URL's `{key}` path segment. FR-QPB-073's existing wording refers generically to "the online layer's URI," not to any specific URL shape, so no textual revision to FR-QPB-073 was necessary; this is recorded explicitly here rather than silently.
  - **Open implementation question, flagged rather than guessed at:** this specification cannot determine, by static inspection, the exact TileMatrixSet identifier, CRS, and tile format that VWorld's real WMTS capabilities XML advertises per layer — values QGIS's native WMTS provider needs to construct a valid datasource connection string. The implementer must inspect VWorld's actual capabilities response (e.g. by fetching `https://api.vworld.kr/req/wmts/1.0.0/{key}/WMTSCapabilities.xml` with a real key) to determine these values through live inspection, rather than this specification asserting or guessing at any particular values. This is recorded as a new open question (see Section 20, new O-12), not silently assumed.

- **D-30** (confirmation/closure of Open Question O-12; does not reopen or alter D-29): Verbatim stakeholder report, given after building the application via `packaging/build_macos_app.sh`, entering a real VWorld API key, generating a project in online basemap mode, and opening the generated `.qgs` project in QGIS Desktop: **"Now Vworld map is well loaded."** This confirms that the WMTS-native-provider connection mechanism (FR-QPB-072, revised; Decision Log D-29) works correctly end-to-end against the real, live VWorld service with a genuine API key — the generated project's online VWorld basemap layer connects and renders successfully in QGIS Desktop. This closes Open Question O-12 in the sense that the underlying question this specification asked to have verified — whether the WMTS-native-connection mechanism actually produces a working online basemap layer against the real service — is now answered by direct stakeholder observation. This confirmation is scoped precisely: it is a mechanism-level, end-to-end result, not a report of which specific underlying values were involved. `resolve_wmts_layer_details()` (`qfield_builder/vworld.py`) attempts live capabilities discovery first and only falls back to the documented default values (`EPSG:900913`/`image/png`/`default`, `resources/config/vworld_layers.json`) if live discovery fails; the stakeholder's report does not indicate which of these two paths was taken in this instance, and both remain plausible. Accordingly, this entry confirms that the WMTS-native-provider connection mechanism (FR-QPB-072, revised D-29) works end-to-end for a real user with a real key; it does not confirm, and must not be read as confirming, that the specific fallback-default `TileMatrixSet`/CRS/tile-format constants were themselves exercised or validated in isolation. No change is made to `resources/config/vworld_layers.json` or `qfield_builder/vworld.py` on the basis of this report.

The four entries below (D-31–D-34) are dated 2026-08-14 and reconcile the stakeholder's answers to the four Open Questions (O-13, O-14, O-15, and a partial answer to O-7) raised by the spec-writer's readiness-review elicitation pass over Section 13. Each is its own independently traceable entry; none reopens, rewords, or renumbers D-1–D-30 above, or O-7/O-13/O-14/O-15 themselves (see Section 20 for the corresponding Open-Question annotations).

- **D-31** (Category C; closes former Open Question O-13; confirms a concrete architecture for FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-101, revised above): Verbatim stakeholder instruction: **"Develop the QField plugin based on the Latest iOS version QField. I have no idea how to use Pl@ntNet API to identify plant photo in QField input form. Read QField plugin documents and research it."** Acting on this instruction, live research was performed (via `WebFetch` against `api.qfield.org` and its subpages, plus a corroborating web search against `docs.qfield.org`) rather than the technology being assumed or invented. That research established, and the stakeholder subsequently approved, the following concrete architecture: (1) a **project plugin** — a `<project_slug>.qml` file generated alongside each project's `.qgs` file, matching QField's own documented project-plugin convention (auto-discovered/bundled by QFieldSync/QFieldCloud when the filename matches the project's own base name) and the Requirements Draft's own folder-layout citation (`<project_name>.qml # only when the QField plugin is enabled`, `specs/QFIELD_PROJECT_BUILDER_REQUIREMENTS_EN.md:598`); (2) the "Identify attached photos" action is a **`QML Widget` editor-widget type embedded in the relevant layer's attribute form** (Type 1's `inventory_observation`; Type 2/3's `observation`) — a real, existing QGIS/QField attribute-form editor-widget type (confirmed via web research, e.g. `docs.qfield.org/how-to/project-setup/attributes-form/`) giving the embedded QML direct access to the currently-edited feature's own attribute values, and connecting directly to infrastructure this codebase already has: `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py::_build_drag_and_drop_form()` already builds each layer's attribute form via `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField` (FR-QPB-057) — a `QML Widget` container/field is added the same way; (3) Pl@ntNet is called via QML's own native `XMLHttpRequest` (confirmed available in QML's JavaScript engine; no special QField networking component is required or exists for this); (4) no official minimum QField version is documented anywhere for this plugin API (confirmed by research) — this specification does not invent one. This closes Open Question O-13 at the architecture level; FR-QPB-100 and FR-QPB-101 above are revised accordingly, and new AC-QPB-069/AC-QPB-070 make this architecture independently testable. This entry does not resolve implementation-level details (e.g. the exact permission-request API call, or QML/QGIS version-specific syntax) not covered by the stakeholder's instruction or the cited research; those remain ordinary implementer work against the requirements above.
- **D-32** (Category C; partially closes former Open Question O-14 — unblocks, does not itself complete, live verification of FR-QPB-104): The stakeholder has supplied a real Pl@ntNet API key. Per the stakeholder's explicit instruction, this key is stored **only** in a local, gitignored `.env` file (never committed, never written to any tracked file) as `QPB_TEST_PLANTNET_API_KEY`, mirroring this project's existing `QPB_TEST_VWORLD_API_KEY` convention (confirmed already established in `.gitignore` and `tests/unit/test_vworld.py`). **This specification records only that a real key now exists and is available via that environment variable for live-network-gated implementer/test-designer verification — consistent with the boundary that a specification must never contain a literal credential value, this document does not, and must never, record the key itself.** This unblocks, but does not itself perform or certify, the live verification of FR-QPB-104's request shape (authentication scheme, endpoint base URL, rate-limit/quota behavior, response schema) against Pl@ntNet's real, current API — that verification remains implementer/test-designer work, per the note added to FR-QPB-104 above.
- **D-33** (narrows the *feasibility-spike* requirement's scope for the guaranteed-manual baseline only; closes former Open Question O-15; clarifies, and does not reword or delete, Decision Log D-13): The stakeholder approved folding the clean-room feasibility spike (D-13/FR-QPB-102/FR-QPB-103) into the manual-baseline build, rather than treating it as a separate, blocking, formal pre-step, on reasoning already presented to and approved by the stakeholder: building the guaranteed-manual "Identify attached photos" baseline (D-13's cleared first-phase scope) naturally exercises four of the five areas D-13/FR-QPB-103 required the spike to cover — multipart HTTP requests (the Pl@ntNet call itself), EXIF access (reading GPS from the attached photo), feature/attribute updates (persisting the selected candidate per FR-QPB-109), and raster sampling (FR-QPB-108's occurrence-probability lookup, itself part of the manual candidate-display flow) — as a natural byproduct of implementing the baseline correctly, to be verified empirically as part of that implementation work rather than as a separate, prior, standalone spike. Only **automatic attachment-change detection** (relevant only to *automatic/silent* triggering, FR-QPB-102) remains genuinely unproven and continues to gate that separate, still-not-approved future phase; this entry grants no approval whatsoever for FR-QPB-102 itself, which remains blocked exactly as D-13/FR-QPB-102 already require. FR-QPB-103 above is revised accordingly to state this narrowed scope; D-13's own original text (Section 19 above) is left completely unchanged and is annotated, not rewritten, to note that it is clarified by this entry.
- **D-34** (partially resolves — does not close — former Open Question O-7; authorizes starting KTSN validation work): The stakeholder has confirmed that both `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` and `storage/reference/rasters/bce_inverse_corrected_probability_maps/` are the authoritative, current reference datasets (resolving the elicitation-phase finding's open confirmation points (1) and (2), recorded under O-7 in Section 20), and has explicitly authorized starting the KTSN validation work (test-designer/implementer work against these now-confirmed-real fixtures). This is **not** a statement that the validation itself (the `correct_list`/KTSN loader's `KTSN`/`KTNS` precedence-and-ambiguity behavior, per FR-QPB-107 and confirmation point (3) under O-7) has been performed or has passed — only that it is now authorized to proceed. O-7 is annotated accordingly in Section 20 below and remains open, in a narrower sense, until that validation work is actually done and reported.

This entry is dated 2026-08-15 and reconciles the stakeholder's explicit answer to Open Question O-16, raised by the spec-writer's own readiness-review elicitation pass (see O-16's original text, Section 20, and the fourth-reconciliation traceability row, Section 21).

- **D-35** (Category C; closes former Open Question O-16; records a stakeholder-approved reference-data delivery decision, and flags two considerations it raises but does not itself resolve): Verbatim stakeholder instruction, given in direct answer to O-16's three-option reference-data delivery question: **"bundled into every generated project."** This selects option (a) of the three O-16 listed: the full KTSN reference CSV (`storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv`, ~183 MB) and the full probability-raster set (`storage/reference/rasters/bce_inverse_corrected_probability_maps/`, ~64 MB, several thousand `.tif` files) — combined, approximately 247 MB — must be copied into every generated project's own folder at build time, whenever the post-MVP identification subsystem is enabled for that project (FR-QPB-037–039). This is not installed once on the device and shared across projects (option (b) is rejected), and it is not reduced to a partial, cropped, or lazily-fetched subset (option (c) is rejected): the complete, unmodified dataset is copied every time. New FR-QPB-112 (Section 13.3) states this as a testable build-pipeline requirement, placing the copied data in the generated project's own `reference/` folder — the location FR-QPB-090 already anticipated ("a `reference/` folder containing only assets required at QField runtime") — using project-relative paths only, consistent with this project's existing no-absolute-paths portability discipline (FR-QPB-091, DR-QPB-012), which this decision confirms applies to reference-data paths and not only to photo-attachment paths. New AC-QPB-071 makes this independently testable. FR-QPB-101 is revised accordingly to reference this decision in place of the now-closed O-16.

  This decision also answers, in the affirmative, the related sub-question O-16 itself raised: because the full reference dataset now travels with every enabled project onto the device, FR-QPB-101's "run KTSN and probability enrichment" step can in principle be performed in-field with local, on-device data access, rather than necessarily waiting for the desktop-side path already described by FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-8. This entry does not itself specify *how* that in-field execution is implemented (e.g., whether the embedded QML performs the CSV lookup and raster sampling directly, or some other mechanism) — that remains ordinary implementer work against FR-QPB-101/106–108 once the reference data's presence on-device is established by FR-QPB-112.

  Two considerations are raised by this decision and are flagged here, not silently resolved:

  1. **Project-size/transfer-size risk (new Open Question O-17):** DR-QPB-060 already treats offline-basemap size as significant enough to warrant a hard 1 GiB limit, pre-generation size estimation, and an explicit user-facing warning (FR-QPB-081–083) — this specification already recognizes generated-project/transfer size as a real, examined constraint, not a detail to leave unexamined. This specification does not, anywhere, state an overall ceiling on total generated-project size (DR-QPB-060 bounds only the `.mbtiles` file specifically). Adding a fixed ~247 MB reference-data bundle to every identification-enabled project, on top of a `.mbtiles` file that can itself legitimately approach 900 MiB–1 GiB under DR-QPB-060/FR-QPB-082, means a single generated project's total on-disk/transfer size could approach or exceed roughly 1.25 GiB before even accounting for the GeoPackage, attachments, or the `.qml` plugin sidecar. This specification cannot determine, from any artifact available to the spec-writer, whether this is acceptable as-is (e.g., because modern phone storage and file-transfer methods comfortably accommodate it) or whether it warrants its own size estimate/warning/threshold analogous to FR-QPB-081/DR-QPB-060. This is not asserted to be a non-issue; it is recorded as an open, unresolved risk — see new Open Question O-17.
  2. **Apparent tension with FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-8 and Out-of-Scope item OS-9 (new Open Question O-18):** FR-QPB-111 currently states that probability rasters are "not required to be copied to the smartphone for the first post-MVP increment" and that probability enrichment "may run on the desktop after the complete field project folder is copied back," with on-device probability lookup described as "a later, separately evaluated feature" (Decision Log D-8); Section 17's Out of Scope list separately marks "On-device (smartphone) probability-map packaging (Section 13.8)" as OS-9. This new decision — bundling the full raster set into every generated project, which is then transferred to the phone per the standard workflow (Section 12) — appears, on its face, to place the probability rasters on the device for every enabled project, which is difficult to reconcile with FR-QPB-111's "not required" framing and OS-9's out-of-scope marking. This specification does not resolve whether D-35 is intended to supersede FR-QPB-111/D-8/OS-9 for the raster-delivery question specifically (in which case those would need their own explicit superseding treatment via a future Decision Log entry, not a silent rewrite here), or whether the two can coexist (e.g., the raster files are now physically present in `reference/` per this decision, but the first post-MVP increment's actual sampling/lookup logic still runs desktop-side only, with in-field/on-device *sampling* remaining the separately-evaluated later feature FR-QPB-111 already describes, and the bundled files sitting present-but-unused in-field until that later feature is separately approved). This is flagged, not silently resolved, as new Open Question O-18.

This entry is dated 2026-08-15 and reconciles the stakeholder's explicit answer to Open Question O-18, raised by Decision Log D-35 above (see O-18's original text, Section 20, and the fifth-reconciliation traceability row, Section 21).

- **D-36** (Category C; closes former Open Question O-18; supersedes the on-device-deferral portion of FR-QPB-111 (original)/the corresponding portion of Decision Log D-8, and removes Out-of-Scope item OS-9; records an explicit, not-yet-confirmed technical-feasibility caveat): O-18 asked, in effect, whether bundling the full raster set onto the device (Decision Log D-35/FR-QPB-112) means in-field, on-device probability sampling should now be built as part of this phase, or whether the bundled files should sit present-but-unused in-field while sampling stays desktop-only per FR-QPB-111 (original)/D-8's existing framing. The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed answer: **"Yes — build in-field, on-device probability sampling now."** This is a real, explicit Category C decision — not an inference — and it **supersedes**, for this phase specifically: (1) FR-QPB-111 (original) above's framing that probability rasters are "not required to be copied to the smartphone... probability enrichment may run on the desktop" and that on-device lookup is "a later, separately evaluated feature" — FR-QPB-111 is revised accordingly (Section 13.8 above), with the original text retained, struck through, and marked superseded, not deleted; (2) Decision Log D-8's original decision (Section 19 above), whose own text is left completely unchanged and is annotated, not rewritten, to note it is clarified/superseded by this entry for the on-device-sampling-in-scope question specifically — mirroring the same non-destructive annotation pattern already used for D-13/D-33; and (3) Out-of-Scope item OS-9 (Section 17), which is struck through and annotated as superseded by this entry, since on-device probability-map packaging/sampling is no longer out of scope for this phase.

  **Technical-feasibility caveat, recorded honestly and not overclaimed as settled:** based on the orchestrator's own preliminary web research (not exhaustive, not a confirmed working implementation), QField's plugin framework exposes some utility objects for map-layer access, and QField is itself built on QGIS core, which has real raster-sampling capability (e.g. `QgsRasterLayer`/`identify()`-style pixel sampling) at the C++/API level — this makes on-device raster sampling from within a QField plugin's QML context *plausible*. However, that research did **not** turn up a confirmed, concrete, working code example of sampling a raster pixel value from QField plugin QML specifically. This specification records this as a plausible-but-technically-unverified capability, to be verified empirically as implementer work — mirroring how this specification already handles Open Question O-12's WMTS-detail uncertainty and the D-13/D-33 "fold the spike into the baseline build" pattern. If it turns out infeasible within QField's actual plugin API, that becomes a concrete implementer finding to report back, not something this specification currently promises as certain. The existing desktop-side fallback path (probability enrichment run after the complete field project folder is copied back) may still exist as a secondary/fallback path if useful; on-device sampling itself is now a first-class in-scope capability for this phase, not deferred.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-8, D-13, D-33, or D-35, and does not alter FR-QPB-108's sampling-logic requirements (Section 13.6) — the NoData/`-9999`/valid-range/out-of-extent rules there already describe the sampling logic itself in a way that applies regardless of where it executes, so they are not duplicated here. New AC-QPB-072 (Section 18.6) makes the on-device execution distinction, and its feasibility caveat, independently testable. This entry does not affect Open Question O-17 (the project-size/transfer-size question): the ~247 MB reference-data bundle was already going to be included in every identification-enabled project's folder regardless of where sampling executes (Decision Log D-35/FR-QPB-112 already decided that); this entry only decides *where the bundled data is used*, not *whether it is present* — O-17 remains open, unchanged, on its own terms.

- **D-37** (confirmed technical fact from live verification of FR-QPB-104's request/response contract, established by a `test-designer` round's actual live API call against the real Pl@ntNet service — **not a stakeholder product decision**, and a materially different kind of entry than D-32 (which recorded only that the stakeholder had supplied a real key, unblocking but not performing verification); closes former Open Question O-14): Per `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`'s "Post-MVP: Section 13" section (functions 7 and 8, and function 8's "Live-verification note"), live verification against the real Pl@ntNet API was actually performed on 2026-08-15, using the real key already stored locally in the gitignored `.env` as `QPB_TEST_PLANTNET_API_KEY` (never written to any tracked file, exactly as Decision Log D-32 already established). Quoted verbatim from that note:

  - "Real endpoint: `https://my-api.plantnet.org/v2/identify/{project}` (POST, multipart form body with an `organs` field per photo and an `images` file per photo). `https://my.plantnet.org/...` returns HTTP 404 and must not be used."
  - "Auth scheme: `api-key` **query parameter** (not an `Authorization` header)."
  - "`nb-results` is also a query parameter; requesting `nb-results=3` returns exactly 3 results (confirmed with a synthetic, dependency-free-generated PNG test image — a real API account quota was not spent on a real plant photo for this schema-confirmation purpose)."
  - "Success response envelope keys (confirmed live): `query`, `predictedOrgans`, `language`, `preferedReferential`, `bestMatch`, `results`, `version`, `remainingIdentificationRequests`. Each `results[*]` entry has `score` (float, 0–1) and `species.scientificNameWithoutAuthor`/`scientificNameAuthorship`/`scientificName` (confirming FR-QPB-104's `species.scientificNameWithoutAuthor` field path is correct) plus `genus`/`family`/`commonNames`. Results were already returned in descending-`score` order by the real API itself — supporting AC-QPB-040's "ordered by descending Pl@ntNet score" as a property of the API response itself, not something the client must additionally sort."
  - "Auth-failure response (confirmed live, invalid key): HTTP `401`, JSON body `{"statusCode": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "message": "Bad token", "attributes": {"error": "Bad token"}}`."

  This corrects a genuine error in the specification's prior assumption: FR-QPB-104's original text and Open Question O-14's own framing traced only to the Requirements Draft's own citation (`specs/QFIELD_PROJECT_BUILDER_REQUIREMENTS_EN.md` §9.2, citing `https://my.plantnet.org/doc/api/identify`), a domain now confirmed, by live HTTP request, to 404. That prior text was an unconfirmed assumption inherited from the Requirements Draft, not a stakeholder decision being reversed here, and this entry corrects it as a confirmed technical fact — distinct in kind from a Category B/C stakeholder-directed change (compare the existing elicitation-finding/stakeholder-confirmation split already used for Open Question O-7 in Section 20, and the technical-feasibility-caveat framing in Decision Log D-36: a spec-writer/test-designer research or verification finding is recorded as such, not dressed up as a stakeholder instruction). FR-QPB-104 is revised accordingly above (Section 13.2; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded/corrected); Open Question O-14 is marked CLOSED below. This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber Decision Log D-32 — D-32's own text is left completely unchanged and remains the accurate record of when and how the real key was supplied; this entry only records that the verification D-32 unblocked has now actually been carried out, and what it found.
