The two entries below (D-38, D-39) are dated 2026-08-15 and reconcile the stakeholder's explicit answers to two remaining gaps a `test-designer` round found while building acceptance tests for Section 13's guaranteed-manual baseline (see `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder_post_mvp_identification.traceability.md`'s "Ambiguities / gaps found" section for the test-designer's original, read-only record of both gaps). Each is its own independently traceable Category B/C reconciliation; neither reopens, rewords, or renumbers D-1–D-37 above.

- **D-38** (Category B; closes a specification omission in FR-QPB-109, not a reversal of any existing requirement): A `test-designer` round found that FR-QPB-109 requires persisting "identification timestamp/API-model version when available" for each identification result, but confirmed, by a full read of Sections 7/8 and a targeted search of the whole specification for "timestamp"/"model version," that no schema column for either exists anywhere. Verbatim stakeholder instruction, given in direct answer to this gap: **"Yes — add two new nullable columns following the exact same forward-compatible pattern as the existing Pl@ntNet columns: an identification-timestamp column and an API-model-version column, added to every table that currently carries the existing Pl@ntNet-related columns... Use sensible names/types consistent with this project's existing conventions (e.g. `identification_timestamp` as an ISO-8601 DATETIME matching this project's existing date/timestamp conventions... and something like `identification_model_version` as a nullable TEXT column)."** Acting on this instruction: new columns `identification_timestamp` (DATETIME; ISO 8601 with timezone, per DR-QPB-013's existing timestamp-format rule) and `identification_model_version` (TEXT) are added, both nullable and reserved/inactive until the post-MVP identification subsystem ships, following the exact same Types 1–3 forward-compatibility pattern (Decision Log D-12) as the existing Pl@ntNet-related columns — to `inventory_observation` (Type 1, Section 8.1; new DR-QPB-052) and to the Type 2/3 `observation` table (Sections 8.2/8.3; new DR-QPB-053). Type 4 `community` continues to be excluded from this treatment, confirming no reason was found to depart from DR-QPB-050's existing exclusion for these two new columns specifically (new DR-QPB-054, a non-destructive extension of DR-QPB-050, not a reopening of it). FR-QPB-109 is revised accordingly (Section 13.7; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded) to reference these two new columns by name. New AC-QPB-073 makes this independently testable. This entry does not alter DR-QPB-014 (the separate, existing schema-version-metadata requirement — survey type, schema version identifier, creation timestamp — which is a project-level metadata concept, distinct from a per-record identification timestamp, and needs no change here).
- **D-39** (Category C; closes a specification omission/ambiguity in FR-QPB-107 regarding multi-entry `correct_list` arrays, distinct from and not a reversal of the existing `KTSN`/`KTNS` key-conflict rule): A `test-designer` round's full scan of the real, full KTSN reference CSV (~212,397 rows) found that ~402 rows have a `correct_list` JSON array containing more than one candidate accepted-taxon entry, each with its own distinct `KTSN` value, and confirmed that FR-QPB-107's existing text never defined which array entry is canonical in that case. Verbatim stakeholder instruction, given in direct answer to this gap: **"Always take the first entry in the array as canonical (`correct_list[0]`), without flagging ambiguity — this is different from how a genuine `KTSN`/`KTNS` key-value conflict within a single entry is handled (that remains flagged as ambiguous per the existing rule; this is specifically about which array entry is used when there are multiple, not a value conflict)."** FR-QPB-107 is revised accordingly (Section 13.5; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded) to state this `correct_list[0]`-is-canonical rule explicitly, scoped clearly as a distinct rule from the existing `KTSN`-vs-`KTNS` conflict-flagging rule (Decision Log D-4/15c), which is unaffected and remains unreworded. New AC-QPB-074 makes this independently testable and explicitly distinguishes it from AC-QPB-043's existing conflict-flagging criterion. **Superseded (2026-08-16) by Decision Log D-40, specifically for the `correct_list[0]`-is-canonical portion of this decision:** this entry's own text above is left completely unchanged and remains the historical record of the original decision; it is annotated, not reworded or deleted, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-13/D-33, D-8/D-36).

The two entries below (D-40, D-41) are dated 2026-08-16 and reconcile a further stakeholder instruction that supersedes D-39's `correct_list[0]`-is-canonical rule with a more precise, verifiable rule, plus a related delivery-mechanism decision for the new reference data that rule depends on. Neither reopens, rewords, or renumbers D-1–D-39 above.

- **D-40** (Category C; supersedes Decision Log D-39's `correct_list[0]`-is-canonical rule specifically for FR-QPB-107's multi-entry-`correct_list` case; does not reopen or reword D-39's own text, which remains visible above and is annotated, not rewritten): Verbatim stakeholder instruction: **"For FR-QPB-107, if correct KTSN is multiple, See 'storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx' and Sheet '62,604종'. If ktsn is enlisted in 'KTSN' column, then it is the correct one."** Orchestrator-verified facts about this file, cited here as confirmed ground truth (not independently re-verified by the spec-writer, and the underlying xlsx file was not itself read by the spec-writer): `storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx` exists in the repository and contains a sheet literally named `62,604종` (62,606 total rows: a two-row header spanning rows 1–2, followed by 62,604 data rows), whose column A is headed `KTSN` and contains that row's own KTSN identifier; this is Korea's official, government-curated National Institute of Biological Resources (NIBR) accepted-taxa list (confirmed by a URL column in that sheet linking to `species.nibr.go.kr`), and is a different, smaller (~62,604 rows), more authoritative "currently accepted" list than the ~212,397-row `tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` already used elsewhere in Section 13 (the broader raw reference/synonym dataset `correct_list` itself is drawn from). This instruction **explicitly supersedes Decision Log D-39's `correct_list[0]`-is-canonical rule** for the multi-entry-`correct_list` case: rather than always taking the first array entry as canonical, each candidate entry's KTSN value must now be cross-referenced against this national list's `KTSN` column, and whichever candidate is found in that list is canonical. D-39's own text above is left completely unchanged and is annotated, not rewritten, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention. FR-QPB-107 is revised accordingly (Section 13.5; the D-39 revision text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted); new AC-QPB-075/AC-QPB-076 make this independently testable. This entry does not resolve what happens when zero, or more than one, candidate's KTSN is found in the national list — that fallback case is addressed in FR-QPB-107 (further revised) above as a reasoned extension of this project's existing ambiguity-flagging discipline, and is separately flagged for the stakeholder's attention as new Open Question O-19, since this exact edge case was not part of the stakeholder's verbatim instruction quoted above.
- **D-41** (Category C; follows up on the same reference-data bundling question already resolved for the KTSN CSV/rasters, Decision Log D-35/FR-QPB-112; records how the new NIBR national-list reference data from Decision Log D-40 is delivered to generated projects): Following up on the same bundling question already resolved for the KTSN CSV/rasters, the stakeholder was asked whether to bundle the full `2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx` file or just the relevant column, and the stakeholder's explicit choice was: **extract only the `KTSN` column (column A) from the `62,604종` sheet into a small, simple lookup-list file (e.g. one KTSN per line, or a compact CSV/JSON) at build time, and bundle only that extracted list into every generated project** — not the full 31-column, 62,604-row xlsx file itself. This mirrors D-35's already-established "bundle into every generated project's own `reference/` folder, using project-relative paths only" delivery discipline (FR-QPB-091, DR-QPB-012), but narrows the source to a single extracted column rather than a complete source file, because — unlike the KTSN CSV/raster set, which FR-QPB-105/FR-QPB-108's resolution/sampling logic reads directly in full — only the `KTSN` column of this new xlsx sheet is actually needed at build or runtime for the FR-QPB-107 (further revised)/FR-QPB-113 cross-reference check; no other column of the source xlsx is used by any requirement in this specification. New FR-QPB-113 (Section 13.3) states this as a testable build-pipeline requirement; new AC-QPB-077 makes it independently testable. This entry does not alter FR-QPB-112, D-35, or their existing ~247 MB KTSN-CSV/raster bundling scope in any way — it adds a separate, much smaller reference-data artifact alongside them, and its size/transfer impact is separately assessed under Open Question O-17 (see O-17's D-41 interaction-check annotation, Section 20).

- **D-42** (Category C; confirmation/closure of Open Question O-19; does not reopen, reword, or supersede FR-QPB-107 (further revised), AC-QPB-076, or Decision Log D-40, whose substance is unchanged): Open Question O-19 asked whether the ambiguous-flagging fallback in FR-QPB-107 (further revised) — applied when zero, or more than one, candidate's KTSN value is found in the extracted NIBR accepted-taxa lookup list during multi-entry `correct_list` resolution — matches the stakeholder's actual intent, since this exact edge case was not part of the verbatim instruction quoted in Decision Log D-40. The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed answer: **"yes, flag as ambiguous."** This confirms that the ambiguous-flagging fallback already written into FR-QPB-107 (further revised) and made independently testable by AC-QPB-076 is the stakeholder's actual, approved intent — not merely a reasoned extension of this project's existing ambiguity-flagging discipline awaiting confirmation, as it was recorded when first written. No requirement text, acceptance criterion, or prior Decision Log entry is reopened, reworded, or renumbered by this entry; FR-QPB-107 (further revised)'s and AC-QPB-076's own text is updated only to remove now-outdated hedging language describing the fallback as unconfirmed, replacing it with a reference to this confirmation, consistent with this project's non-destructive confirmatory-update convention (mirroring Decision Log D-30's confirmation of D-29). Open Question O-19 is marked CLOSED below.

- **D-43** (Category B; adds an explicit `manual` `identification_status` enum value in response to a **reviewer-raised, non-blocking design finding — explicitly not a defect being retroactively corrected**, and not a reversal of any existing requirement): A fresh, independent `reviewer`, checking the just-implemented Pl@ntNet identification plugin's candidate-selection/manual-entry fix, found that `identification_status`'s documented values (`not_requested`/`pending`/`complete`/`failed`) have no distinct value for a manually-entered identification — the implementer's fix distinguishes "manual" only implicitly (a manual entry always persists `identification_score`/`occurrence_probability`/`identification_model_version` as `NULL`, whereas a real candidate selection always persists a numeric score), even though FR-QPB-109 (revised; Decision Log D-38) literally requires manual identification to be "marked as manual." The reviewer explicitly flagged this as a **non-blocking design concern, not a defect in the fix itself**, and recommended it be routed to spec-writer/stakeholder for an explicit decision rather than resolved unilaterally. The stakeholder's decision, given in direct response to this finding: add a new, explicit `identification_status` enum value, **`manual`** — reserved for a manually-entered identification (the user rejected all three Pl@ntNet candidates and typed a name directly). The existing `complete` value continues to mean "a real Pl@ntNet candidate was selected and persisted." `not_requested`/`pending`/`failed` are unaffected. This is a minimal, additive schema change — one more allowed enum value in an already-existing column (Section 8.1/8.2's `identification_status` column) — not a new column. Section 8.1's `inventory_observation` table and Section 8.2/8.3's `observation` table definitions are revised accordingly to list `manual` alongside `pending`/`complete`/`failed`. FR-QPB-109 is revised accordingly (Section 13.7; the Decision Log D-38 revision text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted; see FR-QPB-109 (further revised) immediately above it in Section 13.7). AC-QPB-046 is revised (addition only), and new AC-QPB-078 is added (Section 18.6), to make this distinction independently testable. DR-QPB-034 was checked against this change and found not to require an edit: its existing text refers generically to "`identification_status`'s post-MVP status values" (plural, unenumerated) remaining nullable/inactive in the MVP build, which already covers `manual` without naming it — a deliberate, examined conclusion, not an oversight. This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-42 above.

- **D-44** (Category E — packaging/build-mechanics decision, per this project's change-control policy; distinguishes the *distributed application's own bundle* from the *generated project's own folder*, which D-35/D-41 already govern): A fresh, independent reviewer, checking a packaging-configuration fix, found that `packaging/qfield_builder.spec` had been updated to bundle the full `storage/reference/` dataset (~247 MB: the KTSN reference CSV, the probability-raster set, and the NIBR national-species-list xlsx) into the *distributed packaged application itself* (i.e., into every copy of the built macOS `.app`, growing it from ~110 MB to ~379 MB), and that `README.md`'s note claiming this "mirrors" D-35/D-41's discipline was imprecise: D-35/D-41 only ever recorded a decision about bundling this same source data into each *generated project's own folder* (FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113), not a separate decision about the *distributed application's own installer/bundle size*. The reviewer correctly found no Decision Log entry recording that this specific app-bundle-size/distribution tradeoff had itself been put to, and approved by, the stakeholder — even though it genuinely had been. The stakeholder was asked directly, via a clarifying question presenting two options — bundle the full `storage/reference/` data into the packaged application (growing it to ~360 MB) versus ship it as a separate download/require manual setup — and gave the explicit, verbatim instruction: **"Bundle it into the packaged app (Recommended)"**, selecting the option described to the stakeholder as: "Add storage/reference/ to the PyInstaller .spec's datas, making the app fully self-contained. The packaged app grows from ~110MB to ~360MB, but identification works out of the box for any user who enables it — no separate download or manual setup step." This entry records the missing Decision Log entry the reviewer correctly identified was absent — a genuine, explicit stakeholder decision, not an unexamined packaging default.

  **What this decision covers, precisely, and how it differs from D-35/D-41:** D-35 (KTSN CSV + probability rasters) and D-41 (extracted NIBR KTSN-column lookup list) each govern bundling this same underlying source data from `storage/reference/` into every *generated project's own folder* at build time (FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113) — a per-project, per-build artifact, sized and reasoned about under Open Question O-17's project-size/transfer-size analysis. This entry, D-44, governs a different, related-but-distinct artifact: the *distributed packaged application* itself — the macOS `.app` bundle produced by `packaging/qfield_builder.spec`, i.e., the installer/build artifact a user downloads and installs once, before generating any project at all. Per this stakeholder decision, `packaging/qfield_builder.spec`'s PyInstaller `datas` now includes the full `storage/reference/` tree, so that the reference data needed by FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113's generated-project-bundling step is available locally on the machine running the packaged application, without requiring a separate download or manual setup step by the end user. This grows the packaged application's own installed/distributed size from ~110 MB to ~379 MB (a somewhat larger figure than the ~360 MB estimate presented to the stakeholder at decision time, reflecting the NIBR xlsx source file's actual on-disk size in addition to the KTSN CSV and rasters already estimated). No FR/DR/NFR/AC requirement changes as a result of this entry: FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113 continue to govern only what is copied into each generated project's own folder (unchanged in substance; see the minimal cross-reference notes added to each in Section 13.3); this entry separately records how the same underlying `storage/reference/` source data reaches the distributed application build pipeline in the first place, which is a build/packaging-mechanics decision, not a functional or data requirement change. `packaging/qfield_builder.spec` and `README.md` were already updated to reflect this decision by the time this entry closes the gap the reviewer found; neither file is modified by this entry.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-43 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-112, FR-QPB-113, Decision Log D-35, or Decision Log D-41 in any way.

This entry is dated 2026-08-18 and reconciles an explicit, direct stakeholder instruction extending the VWorld online-layer consent-gated key-embedding exception (Decision Log D-21) to the Pl@ntNet API key. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-44 above.

- **D-45** (Category C; stakeholder-approved product change superseding, for the Pl@ntNet key specifically, the blanket "never embed" rule stated by the original FR-QPB-079/NFR-QPB-019, Decision Log D-21): The application's post-MVP identification subsystem (Section 13) requires the field device itself to call Pl@ntNet at the point of use (FR-QPB-101's embedded `QML Widget`, calling Pl@ntNet directly via QML's `XMLHttpRequest`), which in turn requires the Pl@ntNet API key to be available on-device. Under the original FR-QPB-079/NFR-QPB-019 (Decision Log D-21), the Pl@ntNet key was categorically excluded from every generated-project embedding exception — a deliberate choice at the time, made in the same reconciliation that carved out the narrow, consent-gated VWorld online-layer exception (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-078) and, in the same breath, closed that door for every other credential, including Pl@ntNet. In practice this left the generated project's Pl@ntNet identification feature able to work in the field only via the user manually re-typing the key into QField for every project, every time — the current, pre-this-entry behavior.

  The stakeholder was presented with the exact tradeoff this specification had already accepted for VWorld — informed, verbatim: *"anyone who opens/copies/shares the generated project file can read the key in plain text, the same disclosed risk already accepted for VWorld"* — and asked to choose, via a direct multiple-choice confirmation, whether to mirror that same consent-gated exception for the Pl@ntNet key. The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice: **"Yes, mirror VWorld's consent-gated exception (Recommended)."**

  This **supersedes, for the Pl@ntNet key specifically**, FR-QPB-079 (original)/NFR-QPB-019 (original)'s blanket rule that the VWorld exception "must not be automatically extended to the Pl@ntNet API key or to any other credential" — both entries' own original text is retained above, struck through, and marked superseded, not deleted, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-13/D-33, D-8/D-36, D-39/D-40). The "or to any other credential" portion of that original rule is **not** superseded and remains in force: this decision authorizes exactly one additional, narrowly scoped exception (Pl@ntNet), not a general precedent for arbitrary future credentials.

  **What this decision adds, precisely, mirroring the VWorld pattern (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-078, NFR-QPB-017/NFR-QPB-018) established by Decision Log D-21:**
  1. The wizard's Step 5 photo-identification opt-in (Section 6.5, FR-QPB-037/FR-QPB-039) now has an explicit, concrete key-collection step — new FR-QPB-117 — collecting the Pl@ntNet key as a masked secret input, never logged.
  2. Before embedding, an explicit informed-consent step — new FR-QPB-115, mirroring FR-QPB-076 — discloses that the generated project will contain the key in readable form, that recipients of the project folder may extract it, requires an explicit confirmation checkbox (not merely an informational dialog), and recommends a dedicated/usage-restricted Pl@ntNet key if the provider supports one (the stakeholder's selected option itself explicitly called for this recommendation to be included).
  3. If the user declines consent, new FR-QPB-116 requires that no key be embedded and that the generated project's Pl@ntNet identification feature fall back to requiring manual key entry in QField — i.e., the current (pre-this-entry) behavior becomes the decline-path fallback, not a behavior that disappears.
  4. If accepted, the key is embedded as a **QGIS project variable** named exactly `qpb_plantnet_api_key` (new FR-QPB-114) — never in the GeoPackage, never in the `<project_slug>.qml` plugin's own literal source text, never in `MANIFEST.json` beyond a boolean flag, never in `VALIDATION_REPORT.json`, never in logs, never in a temporary filename. This exact variable name matches the name QField's embedded identification widget already reads at runtime via `expression.evaluate("@qpb_plantnet_api_key")` — a read-side mechanism confirmed/fixed in a separate, already-completed implementation round, which this decision does not itself re-verify; this decision only obligates the spec's build-pipeline requirement (FR-QPB-114) to write that same variable name, so the two sides of the mechanism stay named consistently.
  5. "Remember this key" (OS credential store) is extended to the Pl@ntNet key for wizard convenience across sessions, mirroring NFR-QPB-018 (new NFR-QPB-072).
  6. `MANIFEST.json` records only a boolean security-warning flag when a Pl@ntNet key has been embedded, mirroring NFR-QPB-017 (new NFR-QPB-071) — never the key value itself, and independent of the existing VWorld flag (a project may carry either, both, or neither).

  New FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-117 (Section 13.1a) and new NFR-QPB-071/NFR-QPB-072 (Section 14.1) state these rules as testable requirements; new AC-QPB-079–AC-QPB-082 (Section 18.6) make them independently testable, mirroring AC-QPB-054/AC-QPB-055/AC-QPB-057/AC-QPB-058's structure for the analogous VWorld criteria. FR-QPB-073 and FR-QPB-101 each receive a minimal, clearly marked textual correction/addition as a direct consequence of this decision (Section 10 and Section 13.1a respectively) — in FR-QPB-073's case, correcting a now-inaccurate "the only permitted exception" claim (original text retained, struck through, marked superseded in that one clause); in FR-QPB-101's case, adding the runtime key-retrieval mechanism this decision makes concrete. This is recorded, exactly as D-21 was, as a **deliberate security/usability tradeoff** — accepting the same disclosed, consent-gated, narrowly scoped risk already accepted for VWorld, for the Pl@ntNet case as well, in exchange for a field-usable identification workflow that does not require re-typing the key into QField for every generated project. This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-44 above, and does not alter Section 13's KTSN/probability-lookup/persistence requirements (FR-QPB-104–FR-QPB-113) in any way.

- **D-46** (mixed entry: **(1)** a corrected technical fact from direct research — not a stakeholder product decision, distinct in kind from a Category B/C item, and recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37's live-API-verification correction of FR-QPB-104; **(2)** Category C — an explicit, already-obtained stakeholder decision accepting a disclosed tradeoff. Corrects the FR-QPB-101 (revised; Decision Log D-45) text's claim that Pl@ntNet is called "via QML's own native `XMLHttpRequest` (confirmed available in QML's JavaScript engine — no separate QField networking component exists or is required for this)"; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-45 above):

  **(1) The corrected technical fact.** That claim is now confirmed factually incorrect in one specific respect: **reading the local attachment photo file's bytes** — not the Pl@ntNet network request itself, which remains an ordinary QML `XMLHttpRequest` POST — cannot be done via a plain QML `XMLHttpRequest` opening a `file://` URL. This was established via two independent pieces of confirmed research, not assumed:

  - Qt's own official documentation (`https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtqml-xmlhttprequest.html`) states verbatim: "By default, you cannot use the XMLHttpRequest object to read files from your local file system." Lifting this restriction requires the hosting process to set the environment variables `QML_XHR_ALLOW_FILE_READ=1`/`QML_XHR_ALLOW_FILE_WRITE=1` **before its QML engine starts** — something a generated project has no ability to control, since that is QField's own process, not this application's.
  - A direct GitHub code search of the real `opengisch/QField` repository (`gh search code "QML_XHR_ALLOW" --repo opengisch/QField`, corroborated by browsing the actual source) confirms QField's own application code never sets either environment variable anywhere. Qt's default restriction therefore applies inside QField, and a plain QML `XMLHttpRequest` genuinely cannot read a local attachment file there — independently corroborated by two real, identical on-device QField test failures ("Could not read any attached photo file for identification.") observed even after the file path itself was already correctly resolved via `@project_folder` (a separate, already-fixed bug, not reopened by this entry).

  The same GitHub source search also found QField's own purpose-built, native mechanism for exactly this need: `QfFileUtils::readFileContent(filePath)` (`src/core/utils/qffileutils.cpp`) — a C++ method (native file I/O, not JavaScript's sandboxed `XMLHttpRequest`) exposed to QML as a singleton registered under the QML module `org.qfield.core` (`src/core/qfcore.cpp`: `REGISTER_SINGLETON("org.qfield.core", QfFileUtils, "QfFileUtils")`), explicitly restricted to files within the current project directory via `QfFileUtils::isWithinProjectDirectory()` — which matches this application's own attachment files exactly, since they live inside the generated project folder. QField also ships its own custom `QfXmlHttpRequest` C++ class (`src/core/qfxmlhttprequest.cpp`) with built-in support for `file://` URLs in multipart form bodies, gated by a similar project-directory restriction — but this is used internally by QField's own app code and is not confirmed to be directly exposed/creatable from arbitrary project-plugin QML the way the `QfFileUtils` singleton is. `QfFileUtils.readFileContent(...)` is therefore the correct, confirmed mechanism for reading the local attachment file's bytes; `QfXmlHttpRequest` is not adopted here, for lack of confirmed accessibility. This is recorded, exactly as Decision Log D-37 recorded its live-API-verification finding, as a **confirmed technical fact from research, not a stakeholder product decision or a reversal of anything the stakeholder previously approved** — D-31/D-45's underlying architecture decisions (the `QML Widget` embedding, the project plugin, the Pl@ntNet-key retrieval mechanism) are unaffected and remain in force; only the specific, factually incorrect claim about not needing a separate QField mechanism for the file read is corrected.

  **(2) The stakeholder's tradeoff decision.** `import org.qfield.core`'s `QfFileUtils` singleton is registered only by QField's own native C++ application code; QGIS Desktop's plain PyQGIS-hosted QML engine never registers QField's custom types, and QML provides no conditional/optional import mechanism — if the widget's QML contains `import org.qfield.core` and that module cannot be resolved, as in QGIS Desktop, the **entire QML component fails to load**, the same class of total-failure symptom this application has already diagnosed and fixed for an unrelated bug (a zero-width root `Column` causing total QML load failure — `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`, `tests/unit/test_qml_plugin.py`). Adopting `QfFileUtils` to fix real, confirmed, on-device QField photo-reading will therefore very likely cause the *same widget* to stop rendering at all when opened in QGIS Desktop specifically — regressing a prior QGIS-Desktop rendering fix, for a platform that was never the primary, approved target for this specific capability: QField is the confirmed, approved target platform for the guaranteed-manual "Identify attached photos" baseline (Decision Log D-31); QGIS Desktop has only ever served as a secondary, exploratory test surface for this exact widget, not a requirement this specification imposes for the photo-identification network-request capability specifically.

  Presented with this exact tradeoff — informed, verbatim: *"this will likely make the widget fail to render at all in QGIS Desktop, in exchange for finally making Pl@ntNet identification actually work end-to-end in QField, the real target platform"* — the stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice: **"Yes, prioritize QField working correctly (Recommended)."**

  **What this decision changes.** FR-QPB-101 (Section 13.1) is further revised — correcting the photo-file-read mechanism and adding an explicit, disclosed QGIS-Desktop-rendering-scope caveat; the D-45 text above is retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted. AC-QPB-070 (Section 18) is further revised — scoping its criterion explicitly to QField and disclosing the same QGIS-Desktop caveat; the D-31 text above is retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted. No new FR-QPB-### number is added: consistent with how Decision Log D-37 handled a comparably narrow, confirmed technical-mechanism correction to FR-QPB-104 (a revision of the existing requirement, not a new one), this correction and its accompanying disclosed-tradeoff consequence are folded into a further revision of the existing FR-QPB-101 rather than a new requirement, since both concern exactly the same requirement's own execution mechanism. This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-45 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-102–FR-QPB-117's other substance (the KTSN/probability-enrichment, candidate-persistence, offline-queue, or Pl@ntNet-key-embedding rules) in any way.

- **D-47** (mixed entry: **(1)** a confirmed technical finding from real-device crash investigation — not itself a stakeholder product decision, distinct in kind from a Category B/C item, recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — an explicit, already-obtained stakeholder decision selecting among disclosed tradeoff options, following the same class of reasoning already established by Decision Log D-41 for a different large reference file — on-device practicality. Corrects, for the KTSN reference CSV specifically only, Decision Log D-35's original "no partial, cropped, filtered, or region-limited subset of either file/directory may be substituted" rule; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-46 above):

  **(1) The confirmed technical finding.** Real-device crash investigation confirmed that `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` — the file governed by FR-QPB-105, and originally required to be bundled complete and unmodified per FR-QPB-112 (original)/Decision Log D-35 — is 183 MB, 212,398 rows, and roughly 50 columns wide. The on-device runtime that actually consumes this file at QField runtime (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbLoadCsv`/matching logic, mirroring the Python reference implementation in `qfield_builder/ktsn_match.py`) only ever reads 5 of those ~50 columns: `ktsn`, `taxon_full_nm`, `taxon_kor_nm`, `taxon_jm_nm`, and `correct_list` — the same 5 columns FR-QPB-105 already requires to exist and validates. Loading and holding the complete 183 MB file as JavaScript-visible data inside a mobile QML engine is understood, on the evidence gathered, to very plausibly exceed practical mobile JS-engine memory/performance limits regardless of how efficiently any decode loop is written. This is recorded as the leading, well-evidenced working hypothesis for a reproducible real-device crash occurring during in-field identification — not as an independently confirmed root cause: no symbolicated crash trace was obtained during this investigation. The evidentiary basis for treating this as the leading hypothesis, rather than mere suspicion, is a strong, deterministic correlation: the crash occurs reliably on the specific code path that first attempts KTSN enrichment after a Pl@ntNet response is received, and never occurs on any code path that does not reach this file. This finding is recorded with the same honesty discipline already used for Decision Log D-36/D-46's technical-feasibility caveats — a well-evidenced, leading hypothesis, not an overclaimed certainty.

  **(2) The stakeholder's decision.** Presented with this finding and three options — (i) pre-extract a minimal lookup table containing only the 5 consumed columns at build time; (ii) defer full KTSN cross-referencing to a desktop-side sync step instead of running it in-field; or (iii) investigate further before deciding — the stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice: **"Pre-extract a minimal lookup table at build time (Recommended)."** This mirrors, for the KTSN CSV specifically, the same class of decision already made in Decision Log D-41 for the separate NIBR national-list xlsx file (extracting only the single `KTSN` column needed at runtime, rather than bundling the complete source file, for the same underlying reason: on-device practicality) — except here the on-device runtime needs 5 columns, not 1, so the extraction keeps all 5.

  **What this supersedes, precisely.** This corrects Decision Log D-35's original rule — "no partial, cropped, filtered, or region-limited subset of either file/directory may be substituted" — **for the KTSN reference CSV specifically, and only for the KTSN reference CSV.** D-35's own text above is left completely unchanged and is annotated, not rewritten, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-8/D-36, D-13/D-33, D-39/D-40). The probability-raster half of that same D-35 rule is **explicitly unaffected** and remains in full force: the complete, unmodified probability-raster set (every `.tif` file under `bce_inverse_corrected_probability_maps/`) must still be bundled into every generated project with no cropping, filtering, or region limiting, exactly as D-35 originally required.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-112 is revised accordingly (Section 13.3; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded for its KTSN-CSV clause only — the probability-raster clause is restated unaltered) to require bundling the new build-time-extracted `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` file (5 columns: `ktsn`, `taxon_full_nm`, `taxon_kor_nm`, `taxon_jm_nm`, `correct_list`) in place of the complete raw CSV. New FR-QPB-118 states the extraction step itself as an independently testable build-pipeline requirement, mirroring FR-QPB-113's structure for the analogous NIBR-list extraction (Decision Log D-41). AC-QPB-071 is revised accordingly (Section 18; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded for its KTSN-CSV assertion only — its probability-raster assertion is restated unaltered) to test for the extracted file's presence/column structure/row count in place of the complete raw CSV. New AC-QPB-083 makes FR-QPB-118's extraction requirement itself independently testable, mirroring AC-QPB-077's structure for the analogous NIBR-list bundling criterion (Decision Log D-41).

  **What is confirmed unaffected.** FR-QPB-105 (Section 13.3) and FR-QPB-106 (Section 13.4) are reviewed against this decision and confirmed unaffected in substance: FR-QPB-105 governs validation of the *source* scaffold file (`storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` as it exists before any generated project is built) and already scopes its required-column check to the same 5 columns this entry extracts — it says nothing about what gets bundled into a generated project, so this entry's change to the bundling step does not touch it. FR-QPB-106 governs the direct-KTSN-name-match algorithm itself (normalizing and comparing `species.scientificNameWithoutAuthor` against `taxon_full_nm`, displaying `taxon_kor_nm`) — a matching algorithm that operates on whichever 5-column dataset it is given, and is agnostic to whether that dataset is the complete raw CSV or the extracted `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`, since both carry the same 5 columns. Neither requirement is revised by this entry. Decision Log D-44's separate concern — how source reference data reaches the *distributed packaged application's* own build pipeline, as opposed to each *generated project's* own folder — is likewise unaffected: FR-QPB-112 (revised)'s own text already states that the packaged application's own bundle must still include the complete, unextracted `storage/reference/` tree, since the build pipeline needs the full source CSV locally to perform this new extraction step at generated-project build time; this entry does not restate that point beyond this cross-reference.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-46 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-113 (the separate NIBR-list extraction, Decision Log D-41), FR-QPB-106's matching logic, FR-QPB-107's resolution logic, or FR-QPB-108's raster-sampling logic in any way.

- **D-48** (mixed entry, extended in place, same entry, same date range, to its complete, cohesive **four-step** form before ever being shown to/approved by the stakeholder — no D-49 is created: **(1)** further confirmed technical history from real-device crash investigation and two subsequent, independent runtime-optimization remediation attempts made after Decision Log D-47's fix shipped — not itself a stakeholder product decision, distinct in kind from a Category B/C item, recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — four explicit, stakeholder-directed decisions (a Plantae-subtree row filter; a species-level-and-below rank filter; a vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist filter, added in this latest extension of this same entry; and a duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution-or-drop rule), together with concrete facts about the resulting filtered dataset at each step, verified by the orchestrator via one-off scripts run directly against the real raw CSV and the real NIBR xlsx workbook (cited here as confirmed ground truth; not independently re-verified by the spec-writer, who did not read either source file directly). Corrects, for the KTSN reference CSV specifically only, FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-47)'s extraction step, inserting four ordered build-time row-filtering steps before the existing 5-column extraction; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-47 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-112 (revised; Decision Log D-47)'s existing 5-column-selection/bundling requirement, which is confirmed unaffected and remains exactly as Decision Log D-47 left it):

  **(1) Continued crash history despite Decision Log D-47's fix.** Decision Log D-47 reduced the bundled KTSN reference file from the complete raw CSV (183 MB, 212,398 rows, ~50 columns) to a build-time-extracted, 5-column `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` (~36.7 MB), on the well-evidenced hypothesis that loading the complete file inside the on-device QML engine was the leading cause of a reproducible real-device crash during in-field identification. That fix did **not** resolve the crash: it recurred, 100% reproducibly, with the same test photo, at the exact same point in the identification flow. Two further, independent implementation-phase remediation rounds followed, each targeting a different candidate inefficiency in the on-device loader/matcher (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbLoadCsv`/matching logic, mirroring `qfield_builder/ktsn_match.py`'s Python reference implementation): first, replacing an eagerly-parsed, fully-materialized in-memory rows array with indexed O(1) lookups; second, eliminating retention of a full per-line-substring array entirely in favor of offset-based scanning, which also fixed a secondary quadratic-time bug discovered in that scanner. Neither round resolved the crash: it recurred at the same point, with the same reproduction steps, after each fix. Three independently-verified on-device optimization rounds have therefore proven insufficient to resolve this crash; the dataset's sheer row count (212,397 data rows, spanning every kingdom of life the source checklist covers — animals, fungi, bacteria, protists, and plants) is now considered a more likely contributing factor than the mechanics of how those rows are loaded or scanned.

  **(2) The stakeholder's directives — four, reconciled together in this same entry.** Given this history, the stakeholder directed a different, targeted fix, refined across a clarifying exchange the orchestrator conducted directly with the stakeholder into what is now four ordered steps (originally three; a fourth, narrower step was added in this latest extension of the same still-unapproved entry, described at (2c) below). As with the original Plantae-filter directive below, these are recorded honestly as paraphrases of stakeholder-directed instructions relayed to the spec-writer by the orchestrator, except where a specific verbatim choice is quoted below — no verbatim quotation was supplied for most of the steps' underlying rationale, unlike prior entries such as D-40/D-47, which quote the stakeholder directly for their core instruction; the new (2c) step below is the exception, for which a verbatim instruction was supplied and is quoted directly — and none of it is invented by the spec-writer.

  **(2a) Step 1 — Plantae-kingdom subtree filter (this entry's original directive, unchanged):** filter the bundled reference table down to only rows within the **Plantae kingdom** before the existing 5-column extraction (FR-QPB-118) runs, since the underlying reference dataset (a national species checklist) covers all kingdoms of life (animals, fungi, bacteria, protists, plants) but this application only ever needs plant species — Pl@ntNet, the identification API this feature calls (FR-QPB-104), identifies plants only.

  **Concrete verified facts for Step 1 (orchestrator-verified against the real raw CSV, `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv`, via a one-off script; cited here as confirmed ground truth, not independently re-verified by the spec-writer):**
  - The raw CSV is a self-referential hierarchical table: each row has its own `ktsn` (unique ID) and a `p_ktsn` column giving the `ktsn` of its immediate parent taxon (e.g. a species row's `p_ktsn` points to its genus row, a genus row's `p_ktsn` points to its family row, and so on up to kingdom-level rows).
  - The Plantae kingdom's own `ktsn` is the literal string `120000098391`.
  - Computing the full transitive closure of descendants reachable from `120000098391` via repeated `p_ktsn` lookups (a standard parent-pointer subtree/closure computation) yields exactly **32,251 rows** out of the raw file's 212,397 total rows (~15.2%).
  - A rank breakdown of those 32,251 rows: 21,584 Species, 4,406 Genus, 3,655 Variety, 1,018 Form, 653 Family, 397 Subspecies, 183 Order, 129 Subfamily, plus smaller counts at other ranks (Hybrid, Class, Subgenus, Subclass, Phylum, Subkingdom, Subphylum, Superorder, Supertribe), and a handful of malformed/quoted-string rank values that are a pre-existing data-quality artifact of the raw source file, not something this change attempts to clean up.
  - A phylum breakdown (via each row's own `r200_nm`/`r200_knm` lineage field) of those 32,251 rows confirms they are taxonomically sensible: Magnoliophyta 22,779 (flowering plants), Bryophyta 2,164 (mosses), Pteridophyta 1,923 (ferns), Charophyta 1,914 (stoneworts/green algae, classified under Plantae by this data source), Chlorophyta 1,874 (green algae, likewise classified under Plantae by this data source), Marchantiophyta 951 (liverworts), Pinophyta 296 (conifers/gymnosperms), Filicophyta 290 (ferns), Anthocerophyta 22 (hornworts), Glaucophyta 6, Lycopodiophyta 14 (clubmosses), Psilophyta 4, Sphenophyta 4 (horsetails), plus a small number of quoted-string-variant phylum names (a few rows total) — the same pre-existing data-quality artifact noted above.
  - The `ktsn=120000098391` row for Plantae itself does **not** appear in this species-detail table (it is presumably present only in a separate, not-currently-bundled kingdom-level table). The filter is therefore **"is this row a descendant of `120000098391` via the `p_ktsn` chain"** — not "is this row's own `ktsn` equal to `120000098391` or a descendant of it."

  **(2b) Step 2 — species-level-and-below rank filter (new in this extension of the same entry):** after Step 1, filter further to only rows whose raw CSV `rank_id` column, interpreted as an integer, is `>= 700`. The orchestrator independently verified `rank_id` is a taxonomic-rank code in this dataset (100=Kingdom, 110=Subkingdom, 200=Phylum, 210=Subphylum, 290=Superclass, 300=Class, 310=Subclass, 320=Infraclass, 390=Superorder, 400=Order, 405=Group, 410=Suborder, 420=Infraorder, 490=Superfamily, 500=Family, 510=Subfamily, 515=Supertribe, 520=Tribe, 530=Subtribe, 600=Genus, 610=Subgenus, 630=Section, 640=Series, 700=Species, 710=Subspecies, 720=Variety, 725=subvar, 730=Form, 740=Hybrid, 750=ab, 760=r, 770=st, 775=cf, 780=aff) — so `>= 700` keeps only species-level-and-below (infraspecific) entries, which is what Pl@ntNet's returned scientific names actually correspond to (FR-QPB-104/FR-QPB-106), and drops genus/family/order/etc.-level entries that could never be a direct match target. A row with a non-numeric or missing `rank_id` must be excluded (fails the `>= 700` test) — this matches the exclude-on-ambiguity/malformed-data posture Step 1 already establishes; this filtering pipeline never guess-includes a row. Orchestrator-verified result: applying Step 2 to Step 1's 32,251 rows yields **26,763** rows.

  **(2c) Step 3 — vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist filter (new in this latest extension of the same D-48 draft):** after directing Steps 1–2 above, the stakeholder gave a further, explicit direct instruction, quoted verbatim: **"filter out 선태류 [bryophytes]. I only need vascular plants."** The orchestrator disclosed to the stakeholder that this dataset's Plantae-kingdom subtree (Step 1's own result) contains not only the three bryophyte phyla named in that instruction (`Bryophyta`, `Marchantiophyta`, `Anthocerophyta` — mosses, liverworts, hornworts, collectively "선태류") but also three further phyla this dataset classifies under Plantae that are algae, not vascular plants (`Charophyta`, `Chlorophyta`, `Glaucophyta` — stoneworts/green algae), and asked the stakeholder, via a direct two-option question, to choose between: (i) excluding only the three named bryophyte phyla; or (ii) also excluding the three algae-related phyla, keeping vascular plants only. The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice was the broader, stricter option: **exclude both the bryophyte phyla and the algae-related phyla, keeping vascular plants only.** This yields an allowlist of exactly seven phyla — `Magnoliophyta` (flowering plants), `Pteridophyta` (ferns), `Pinophyta` (conifers/gymnosperms), `Filicophyta` (ferns), `Lycopodiophyta` (clubmosses), `Psilophyta`, `Sphenophyta` (horsetails) — filtered against the same `r200_nm` phylum-lineage field already used in Step 1's own concrete-facts phylum breakdown above (see the counts recorded there: Magnoliophyta 22,779; Bryophyta 2,164; Pteridophyta 1,923; Charophyta 1,914; Chlorophyta 1,874; Marchantiophyta 951; Pinophyta 296; Filicophyta 290; Anthocerophyta 22; Glaucophyta 6; Lycopodiophyta 14; Psilophyta 4; Sphenophyta 4). This step runs after Step 2 (the rank filter) and before what was previously labeled "Step 3" (the duplicate-name resolution step), which is renumbered to **Step 4** below as a direct consequence of this insertion. Orchestrator-verified result: applying this new Step 3 to Step 2's 26,763 rows yields **21,025** rows.

  **(2d) Step 4 — canonical-KTSN resolution for duplicate scientific names, using the NIBR xlsx already bundled at build time (renumbered from this entry's prior "Step 3"; the resolution rule itself is unchanged, but it now runs over the narrower row set surviving the new Step 3 above, which changes its specific counts from this entry's prior form):** after Steps 1–3, some `taxon_full_nm` values — after applying the same `<em>`/`</em>`-tag-stripping-plus-whitespace-collapsing normalization the runtime matcher already uses (`qfield_builder/ktsn_match.py`'s `_normalize`/`_EM_TAG_RE`) — appear on more than one surviving row, each with a different `ktsn`. The orchestrator verified this affects exactly **58 distinct scientific names (118 total rows)** out of the 21,025 rows surviving Step 3 — fewer than the prior form's 106 names/215 rows, because narrowing to vascular-plants-only in Step 3 already removed many of the bryophyte-genus duplicates that motivated this step in the first place (e.g. most of the `Jungermannia` liverwort duplicates), before duplicate resolution even runs. For each such duplicated name, look it up (after the same normalization) in the same NIBR xlsx workbook already required by FR-QPB-113/Decision Log D-40/D-41 (`storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx`) — but specifically its **`관속식물류`** sheet (vascular plants) this time, not the `62,604종` sheet D-40/D-41 already use — matching the duplicated name against that sheet's **`학명`** column:
  - If the name is found in `관속식물류`'s `학명` column with exactly one distinct `KTSN` value, **and** that `KTSN` value equals one of the `ktsn` values already present among that name's duplicate rows in the Step-3 output, then **keep only the one row whose `ktsn` equals that value; drop the other row(s) for that name.** The orchestrator verified this resolves exactly **7 of the 58** duplicate names this way — the same 7 names resolved in this entry's prior form, since they were already vascular-plant names and therefore survived the new Step 3 unaffected.
  - In every other case — the name is not found at all in `관속식물류`'s `학명` column (the orchestrator verified this is true for **51 of the 58** duplicate names, mostly species not native to Korea and therefore absent from this Korea-specific national checklist); or the name is found but maps to more than one distinct `KTSN` value there; or the `KTSN` value found there does not match any of the `ktsn` values among that name's duplicate rows — the resolution is inconclusive, and **all rows for that duplicated name must be dropped entirely from the output** (not just left ambiguous, and not resolved by any other heuristic such as file order or the `taxon_jm_nm` accepted/synonym-status field).

  This drop-entirely rule for the inconclusive case was the stakeholder's own explicit, direct choice between two presented options — keep-as-is-with-existing-runtime-tie-break (relying on the shipped matcher's first-occurrence-wins behavior) versus drop-entirely — made after the orchestrator disclosed that only 7 of 106 names (at the time this choice was made, prior to Step 3's later insertion) actually resolve via the `관속식물류` cross-reference rule. Separately, the scope of that cross-reference (`관속식물류` only, not also the `선태류` bryophyte sheet) was likewise the stakeholder's own explicit, direct choice: the orchestrator disclosed that checking `선태류` as well was available, and the stakeholder declined it, explicitly choosing to use `관속식물류` only, matching their original instruction literally. Neither of these two sub-decisions is invented or inferred by the spec-writer; both are recorded here as the stakeholder's own confirmed choices, exactly as D-48's Step 1 directive above is recorded — as a paraphrase relayed by the orchestrator, since no literal quoted sentence was supplied for either.

  This step is a build-time-only computation over the CSV rows and the xlsx sheet already present in `storage/reference/`; nothing about how the runtime QML matcher (`qpbLoadCsv`/`qpbMatchKtsn`) works changes — it still does first-occurrence-wins on whatever rows survive into `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`, but after this step there is at most one row per distinct (normalized) `taxon_full_nm` for every name this step was able to inspect, other than the deliberately-unresolvable ones, which are removed entirely rather than left duplicated.

  **Combined result across all four steps (orchestrator-verified; supersedes this entry's prior three-step, 26,555-row combined result):** Steps 1+2+3+4 together reduce the raw 212,397 rows to **20,914 rows** — 32,251 after Step 1 → 26,763 after Step 2 → 21,025 after Step 3 → 20,914 after Step 4 (7 names de-duplicated to 1 row each [−7 rows]; 51 names dropped entirely [−104 rows]) — a final result of ~9.8% of the raw row count, roughly a 10x reduction.

  **What this requires.** FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-47/this entry's own two-step and four-step prior forms, both retained above, struck through, marked superseded) is further revised below to require, before the existing column-extraction sub-step runs: **Step 1** (Plantae-subtree filter, unchanged from this entry's original form), **Step 2** (`rank_id >= 700` filter, unchanged from this entry's four-step form), **Step 3** (new in this latest extension: the seven-phylum vascular-plants-only allowlist filter against `r200_nm`), and **Step 4** (duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution-or-drop via the `관속식물류` sheet, renumbered from this entry's prior "Step 3," rule unchanged, counts recomputed over the narrower Step-3 output), each computed once, in pure Python, in `reference_bundle.py`'s build-time extraction step, and **never** at runtime on-device. New AC-QPB-084 (Section 18.6) makes Step 1 independently testable, unchanged in substance from this entry's original form. New AC-QPB-085 (Section 18.6) makes Step 2 independently testable (the 26,763-row result, and the exclude-on-malformed-`rank_id` rule), unaffected in substance or count by this latest extension. New AC-QPB-087 (Section 18.6) makes the new Step 3 phylum-allowlist filter independently testable (the 21,025-row result, and a synthetic multi-phylum fixture confirming only the seven allowlisted phyla survive). AC-QPB-086 (Section 18.6) is further revised (its prior "Step 3" framing retained, described, and updated in place) to make Step 4 independently testable, both via the real-fixture combined count (20,914) and via the same two synthetic fixtures as before — one in which a duplicated name resolves via a synthetic `관속식물류`-equivalent lookup (exactly one row survives, with the correct `ktsn`), and one in which it does not (zero rows survive for that name). AC-QPB-083 (post-MVP; Decision Log D-47/D-48's original and three-step forms) is further revised (its prior text retained, struck through, marked superseded) to state the full four-step pipeline's row-count assertion and the final 20,914-row combined count, rather than the prior 26,555-row figure. AC-QPB-071 (post-MVP; Decision Log D-47/D-48's original and three-step forms) receives the same extension to its own row-count sub-clause, for consistency, since it makes the identical claim about the same file.

  **Behavior-change tradeoff, disclosed and recorded, not silently absorbed.** Previously (per Decision Log D-47/FR-QPB-118, prior to this entry), the complete set of raw-CSV rows surviving only the 5-column reduction was eligible for on-device matching (FR-QPB-106), subject to the existing matching logic. Going forward, **only rows surviving all four of Steps 1–4 are bundled and therefore eligible for on-device matching at all.** Four distinct consequences follow, each a deliberate, accepted consequence of the stakeholder's directives, not an oversight: (i) a genuine species outside the Plantae subtree — which should not occur in practice, since Pl@ntNet (FR-QPB-104) only ever returns plant species names — would, if it ever occurred, now be reported as "KTSN match not found"/unresolved rather than potentially matching a non-Plantae row (Step 1's consequence, unchanged from this entry's original form); (ii) a genus/family/order/etc.-level `taxon_full_nm` can no longer ever be matched at all, which is expected and intended, since Pl@ntNet never returns a name at that rank (Step 2's consequence); (iii) a bryophyte or algae-related-phylum `taxon_full_nm` — bryophytes in particular being a real, if botanically distinct, category Pl@ntNet's own species catalogue might occasionally still name — can no longer ever be matched at all, per the stakeholder's own explicit, disclosed choice to scope this feature to vascular plants only (Step 3's consequence, new in this extension); and (iv) for the 51 of 58 duplicated scientific names Step 4 could not conclusively resolve, a photo whose Pl@ntNet-identified name normalizes to one of those names will now be reported "KTSN match not found"/unresolved by the existing matching logic (FR-QPB-106), rather than matching via the shipped matcher's existing first-occurrence-wins tie-break against an arbitrary one of the ambiguous candidate rows (Step 4's consequence, renumbered from this entry's prior "Step 3," with recomputed counts) — this prioritizes never guessing over maximizing match coverage, consistent with this project's existing ambiguity-flagging discipline (the `KTSN`/`KTNS` conflict rule, Decision Log D-4/15c; AC-QPB-043's general convention) applied here at the row-filtering level rather than the resolution level.

  **What is confirmed unaffected.** FR-QPB-112 (revised; Decision Log D-47)'s own 5-column-selection/bundling requirement — which file is bundled, under what filename, with what column set, and via what relative-path discipline — is unchanged and is not revised by this entry; this entry only changes which *rows* are eligible to reach that column-extraction step in the first place, a change fully contained within FR-QPB-118. FR-QPB-105 (source-scaffold validation) and FR-QPB-106 (direct-KTSN-name-match algorithm) are reviewed against this decision and confirmed unaffected in substance, for the same reasons Decision Log D-47 already gave when it made its own, narrower change: FR-QPB-105 validates only that the required 5 columns exist in the *source* file, independent of which rows are later filtered out of the bundled derivative; FR-QPB-106's matching algorithm operates on whichever 5-column dataset it is given and is agnostic to how many rows that dataset contains. FR-QPB-113 (the separate `62,604종`-sheet/`KTSN`-column-only NIBR extraction, Decision Log D-40/D-41) is likewise reviewed and confirmed unaffected: it continues to read only that sheet, for its own distinct, runtime multi-candidate `correct_list`-resolution purpose (FR-QPB-107); Step 4 above reads a *different* sheet (`관속식물류`) of the same already-bundled workbook, for a distinct, build-time-only row-deduplication purpose, and does not alter FR-QPB-113's own extraction, sheet, column, or bundled-file scope in any way. Decision Log D-44's distributed-application-bundle concern is likewise unaffected: the packaged application's own bundle must still include the complete, unfiltered, unextracted `storage/reference/` tree — the raw CSV in full, for Steps 1–3's transitive-closure/rank/phylum computations over every row, not only the vascular-plants-only subset; and the complete NIBR xlsx workbook, both sheets, for Step 4 and for FR-QPB-113's own separate use — locally to perform this filtering/extraction at generated-project build time.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-47 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-107's resolution logic, FR-QPB-108's raster-sampling logic, FR-QPB-113 (the separate NIBR-list `62,604종`/`KTSN`-column extraction), or any requirement outside FR-QPB-118/AC-QPB-071/AC-QPB-083/AC-QPB-084/AC-QPB-085/AC-QPB-086/AC-QPB-087's row-count/content clauses in any way.

  **Approval status (added after approval; read this note before any other language in this entry describing draft/approval state).** This entry, in its complete five-step form described above (Steps 1–5, including the pre-existing Step 5 column-extraction sub-step), was presented to the stakeholder in full and explicitly approved on 2026-08-23. The corresponding acceptance tests (AC-QPB-071/AC-QPB-083/AC-QPB-084/AC-QPB-085/AC-QPB-086/AC-QPB-087, in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/`) were likewise presented and explicitly approved on 2026-08-23. Both the specification revision and the acceptance tests are committed (`a95d465` and `0f509f5` respectively). Every phrase elsewhere in this entry, and in this document's status header, describing D-48 as a "still-unapproved draft," "before ever being shown to/approved by the stakeholder," or similar, is accurate only as a description of this entry's state *during* its multi-round drafting process (it was extended in place, without a new decision-log number, across several rounds before ever being shown to the stakeholder in complete form) — it does not describe the entry's current, approved status, which this note now records unambiguously for any later reader (including a fresh `reviewer` or `implementer` invocation) who has not seen the conversation in which that approval was given.

The entry below (D-49) is dated 2026-08-23 and records a confirmed technical finding from real-device testing, plus the stakeholder's explicit choice of how to respond to it, for FR-QPB-108 (occurrence-probability display) specifically. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-48 above.

- **D-49** (mixed entry: **(1)** a confirmed technical finding from real-device testing and follow-up investigation — not itself a stakeholder product decision, distinct in kind from a Category B/C item, recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47/D-48's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — an explicit, already-obtained stakeholder decision selecting among two disclosed options for how to respond. Adds a disclosed, QField-iOS-specific platform-limitation caveat to FR-QPB-108/AC-QPB-044 (Sections 13.6/18.6); does **not** allege or record any defect in this project's own `qpbReadPhotoGps`/`qpbReadExifTag` implementation (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`), which this same investigation independently confirms is correct; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-48 above):

  **(1) The confirmed technical finding, in two parts.** Real-device testing on QField 4.2.4 (iOS) reported that the application displayed "No photo GPS — probability unavailable" (FR-QPB-108's own already-specified no-GPS message) for a photo the stakeholder confirmed does contain GPS EXIF data. Investigating this report:

  - First, the orchestrator independently verified — via this project's own sanctioned QGIS-isolation probe (`scripts/qgis_isolated_probe.py`), not by inspecting or modifying any application source — that the `exif(path, tag)` QGIS expression function this project's QML (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbReadExifTag`/`qpbReadPhotoGps`, FR-QPB-108) already relies on works correctly: a synthetic JPEG built with real GPS EXIF tags (via Python `piexif`) correctly returned a plain decimal float (e.g. `37.5665`) when queried for `Exif.GPSInfo.GPSLatitude` — exactly the format `qpbReadPhotoGps` already expects and parses. This confirms the `exif()` mechanism itself, and this project's own parsing of it, are both correct; there is no defect in `qpbReadExifTag`/`qpbReadPhotoGps` to fix.
  - Second, the orchestrator asked the stakeholder how the GPS-containing photo had been attached to the observation; the stakeholder confirmed it was picked from an existing photo already on the phone's camera roll/gallery, not taken with QField's own in-app camera. The orchestrator then found a confirmed, matching public report — QField's own GitHub discussion #4246, "Photos missing geotag in iOS environment (attachment widget)" (`https://github.com/opengisch/QField/discussions/4246`) — in which a QField user reported testing three distinct photo-attachment methods on iOS: (a) the native iOS camera with geotagging enabled in iOS Settings; (b) QField's own internal camera; and (c) choosing an existing geotagged photo from the camera roll (the same method the stakeholder used). In every case, the GPS geotag was missing from the file QField actually saved into the project's attachment folder, confirmed in that report by inspecting the saved files directly with an external EXIF-reading tool (Geosetter); the same report states explicitly, "This does not happen on an Android device." Because that report tested and confirmed this failure across all three acquisition methods, and the confirmed root cause is QField's own file-saving step for attachments on iOS — not anything about how the photo was acquired — this is recorded as a QField-iOS platform limitation reproducible regardless of acquisition method, not something specific to the camera-roll-picker method the stakeholder happened to use.

  Combining both parts: `exif()` is confirmed working correctly, and a confirmed, independently-reported QField-iOS platform behavior explains the missing data at the source — QField's own attachment-saving step strips GPS EXIF metadata from the file before this project's generated QML ever gets a chance to read it, on iOS specifically. This project's own `qpbReadPhotoGps`/`qpbReadExifTag` implementation (FR-QPB-108) has no defect to fix: it is correctly reporting "no GPS" because the file it is given genuinely no longer contains GPS data by the time QField hands it over, on iOS specifically. Per the same report quoted directly above, this behavior is **reported not to reproduce on an Android device**; this project has not independently verified that on a real Android device, and this entry records it only as "reported not to reproduce," not as this project's own confirmed finding.

  **(2) The stakeholder's decision.** Presented with this finding and two disclosed options — (i) document this as a known limitation, with no code change (matching the existing "current behavior is already correct" pattern already used elsewhere in this specification, e.g. Decision Log D-30's confirmation that a mechanism already works correctly as specified); or (ii) add a new manual-GPS-entry fallback feature, letting the field user type in a coordinate when a photo's GPS is unavailable — the stakeholder's explicit choice: **document it as a known limitation only, with no code change**, declining the manual-GPS-entry fallback for now.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-108 is revised accordingly (Section 13.6; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted) to add the disclosed QField-iOS platform-limitation caveat: on QField running on iOS specifically, this criterion's GPS-present branch cannot be met for any attached photo, regardless of acquisition method, because of QField's own attachment-saving behavior — not a defect in this project's own EXIF-reading implementation. AC-QPB-044 is revised accordingly (Section 18.6; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted) to state the same disclosed limitation as an explicit, testable qualification on its own GPS-transform assertion. AC-QPB-045/AC-QPB-049/AC-QPB-050 (Section 18.6) and DR-QPB-070 (Section 13.6) are reviewed against this finding and confirmed unaffected in substance: none of them asserts that GPS-based probability lookup succeeds given a photo with EXIF GPS specifically (unlike AC-QPB-044) — AC-QPB-045 already covers the "no photo GPS" display path (which this finding confirms is, in practice, the path always taken on QField iOS, for a reason this specification did not previously record), AC-QPB-049/AC-QPB-050 govern the sampled-value/NoData/out-of-range handling once a sample is actually taken, and DR-QPB-070 restates that same sampled-value scale/NoData convention — none of these requires or asserts that a photo's GPS actually survives QField's iOS attachment-saving step. No manual-GPS-entry fallback feature is added by this entry, per the stakeholder's explicit choice above; if the stakeholder later wants that fallback built, it is a distinct, future Category C/B specification change, not something this entry authorizes.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-48 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-104–FR-QPB-107/FR-QPB-109–FR-QPB-118 or any other requirement outside FR-QPB-108/AC-QPB-044's own disclosed-limitation clause in any way. It does not allege that any acceptance test currently in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/` is wrong or must change — whether the existing GPS/EXIF acceptance-test fixtures need an added manual-QA placeholder or updated wording to reflect this platform-specific finding is left to a separate, future `test-designer` round, not decided here.

The entry below (D-50) is dated 2026-08-23 and records confirmed technical findings from real-device testing plus direct QGIS/QField source-code inspection, and the stakeholder's resulting decision, for FR-QPB-109 (candidate-selection/manual-entry attribute write-back, Section 13.7) specifically. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-49 above.

- **D-50** (mixed entry: **(1)** confirmed technical findings from real-device testing and direct QGIS/QField source-code inspection — not itself a stakeholder product decision, distinct in kind from a Category B/C item, recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47/D-48/D-49's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — an explicit, already-obtained stakeholder decision selecting among two disclosed options for how to respond. Resolves, for FR-QPB-109's attribute write-back specifically, the same class of "plausible but not confirmed" uncertainty Decision Log D-36 records for on-device raster sampling; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-49 above):

  **(1) The confirmed technical findings, in three parts.** FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-43) required both a real candidate selection and a manual identification entry to be "persisted," but the mechanism by which the embedded `QML Widget` attribute-editor (Decision Log D-31) could actually write that persistence back onto the current feature's attributes was, at the time, an unconfirmed, best-effort mechanism — the same class of uncertainty Decision Log D-36 records for on-device raster sampling: a speculative attempt at a `currentFeature.setAttribute(...)`-style call, falling back to an on-screen "not saved" disclosure if no such context property turned out to be present. Real-device testing (QField 4.2.4) confirmed this speculative mechanism never works: no `currentFeature`-style context property is ever exposed to the embedded widget's QML, on any device tested. The orchestrator then investigated alternative mechanisms across an extensive series of real-device feasibility spikes — all now fully reverted from the codebase, per this project's own documented commitment to keep such spikes clean-room and non-shipping until confirmed (orchestrator-cited commit ranges: `f9dffe6` through `c49b084` for the first spike lineage, `47d70bc` through `c55d676` for the second; not independently re-verified by the spec-writer, who did not inspect either commit range directly). That investigation established three findings, in order:

  - **Confirmed structurally impossible via the "QML Widget" attribute-editor itself, on any platform or QField version.** Direct inspection of QGIS core's own C++ source for `QgsQmlWidgetWrapper` — the class implementing the "QML Widget" attribute-editor type this feature is built on (Decision Log D-31) — shows it exposes exactly one context property to embedded QML: `expression`, with a single, read-only `evaluate()` method. No feature object, no attribute setter, and no signal path back into C++ is ever wired up for this widget type, in any QGIS/QField version — this is a structural property of the wrapper class itself, not a configuration or version gap that further investigation could close.
  - **Confirmed structurally possible, and confirmed working on a real device, via a genuine QField "project plugin"** (already shipped by this project as `<project_slug>.qml`, per FR-QPB-100/Decision Log D-31 — a different embedding mechanism entirely from the "QML Widget" attribute-editor above) — but only for a narrower case: **a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature, created via QField's own "Add feature" digitizing flow.** This was confirmed via direct source inspection: `FeatureForm.qml` declares `property AttributeFormModel model`; `OverlayFeatureFormDrawer.qml` — QField's own Add-feature drawer, reachable from a project plugin via `iface.findItemByObjectName('overlayFeatureFormDrawer')` — instantiates this type and aliases it as `featureForm`, exposing the live, editable model for the feature currently being created. This was then confirmed working end-to-end, repeatedly, on a real device: the embedded identification widget writes a small pending-request file — the new feature's UUID (every new feature's UUID primary-key field already receives a `uuid('WithoutBraces')` default value the moment its form opens, per `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`), the target field name, and the value — via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.writeFileContent()`; the already-shipped project plugin polls for this file on a short-interval `Timer`, and, when found, locates `overlayFeatureFormDrawer.featureForm.model`, confirms its current feature's UUID matches the pending request, and calls `changeAttribute(name, value)` on it. The value appears immediately in the still-open, unsaved form, and survives the user's normal save (tapping the checkmark) — confirmed by inspecting the real GeoPackage record afterward.
  - **Confirmed structurally impossible for the other realistic case — editing an existing, already-saved feature, reopened later (not a new "Add feature" session).** Direct source inspection of `FeatureListForm.qml` — the component QField uses for viewing/editing an existing feature, exposed app-wide as `objectName: "featureForm"` — shows it internally constructs its own per-feature `FeatureForm { id: featureForm; model: AttributeFormModel { featureModel: FeatureModel {...} } }`, but exposes only two top-level properties externally: `property alias model: globalFeaturesList.model` (a *different* object — a list/multi-selection model, not the per-feature `AttributeFormModel`) and `property alias extentController`. The inner `featureForm`/its `AttributeFormModel` has no alias and no `objectName` of its own, making it structurally unreachable from a project plugin. This was cross-checked against the complete list of every top-level named object in QField's main application QML (`qgismobileapp.qml`'s full `objectName:` list): `featureForm` and `overlayFeatureFormDrawer` are the only two feature-editing-related named objects that exist at all, and only `overlayFeatureFormDrawer` (Add-feature-only) exposes a usable, per-feature model. This is a structural limitation in QField's own source, not something further investigation could resolve.

  **(2) The stakeholder's decision.** Presented with these three findings — one confirmed-working mechanism, narrowly scoped to brand-new/unsaved features; one confirmed-impossible limitation for the existing/already-saved-feature case — the stakeholder's explicit decision: ship the confirmed-working mechanism as a real, permanent feature for the brand-new, not-yet-saved-feature case; keep the existing, already-disclosed "not saved" fallback message, now as a **confirmed, permanent limitation** rather than an open uncertainty, specifically for the case of editing an already-saved feature.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-109 is further revised (Section 13.7; Decision Log D-43's text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted) to require the confirmed, real mechanism described in finding (1)'s second bullet above for **real candidate selection** on a brand-new/unsaved feature specifically — the case the stakeholder's decision above was presented with and approved — and to state plainly, as a confirmed and permanent (not open) limitation, that write-back cannot occur, for either a candidate selection or a manual entry, once a feature is an existing/already-saved feature. AC-QPB-046 (Section 18.6) is correspondingly restructured into two independently testable branches: (a) for a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature, real candidate-selection persistence must actually succeed, testable via real-device manual QA following this document's existing convention for device-dependent criteria (Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072; mirroring the documented, honestly-skipped `device`-marked placeholder tests already in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/test_post_mvp_manual_qfield_runtime.py`); (b) for an existing, already-saved feature, the disclosed fallback message must be shown and the previously-saved value must remain unchanged — recorded as a confirmed, permanent limitation, not a gap awaiting resolution.

  **What is confirmed unaffected.** AC-QPB-078 (manual-identification `identification_status` distinction) is reviewed against this entry and confirmed unaffected in its own substance: it asserts which enum value/nulled columns a manual entry must be persisted with, not by what mechanism persistence itself is achieved, and remains correct regardless of feature lifecycle state.

  **Flagged, not silently resolved.** FR-QPB-109's own text has, since before this entry (Decision Log D-38/D-43), equally required a manual identification entry to be persisted, and the current implementation's manual-entry confirmation path (`qpbConfirmManualEntry`, `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`) is built on the identical best-effort write-back function this entry's finding (1) addresses for candidate selection (`qpbPersistIdentification`). The stakeholder's explicit instruction reconciled by this entry was framed around candidate-selection write-back specifically; this entry does not independently confirm, via its own real-device testing, that the identical pending-request-file mechanism works for the manual-entry path, and FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-50)'s new normative mechanism requirement is accordingly scoped to real candidate selection only, not extended to manual entry.
