See new Open Question O-20.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-49 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104–FR-QPB-108/FR-QPB-110–FR-QPB-118 or any other requirement outside FR-QPB-109/AC-QPB-046's own write-back-mechanism clauses in any way.

The entry below (D-51) is dated 2026-08-23 and records the stakeholder's explicit answer to former Open Question O-20 (a spec-writer finding raised while reconciling Decision Log D-50, not itself a stakeholder decision at the time it was raised), extending FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-50)'s confirmed write-back mechanism to manual identification entry on a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-50 above.

- **D-51** (Category C — an explicit, already-obtained stakeholder decision closing former Open Question O-20; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-50 above): Decision Log D-50 confirmed and required the pending-request-file/project-plugin-`Timer`-polling/`overlayFeatureFormDrawer.featureForm.model`/`changeAttribute()` write-back mechanism as a real, permanent feature for **real candidate selection** on a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature specifically, leaving open (Open Question O-20) whether the identical mechanism was also intended to govern **manual identification entry** (the path where the user rejects all three candidates and types a name manually, persisted with `identification_status = "manual"` rather than `"complete"`, per the existing, unchanged Decision Log D-38/D-43 rule) for a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature — noting that the current implementation's manual-entry confirmation path (`qpbConfirmManualEntry`, `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`) is already built on the identical best-effort write-back function Decision Log D-50's findings addressed for candidate selection (`qpbPersistIdentification`).

  **The stakeholder's decision.** The orchestrator asked the stakeholder directly: "Should the confirmed write-back mechanism also apply to manual identification entry (typing a name after rejecting all three candidates) on a brand-new/unsaved feature, not just candidate selection?" The stakeholder's explicit answer: **"Yes, extend it to manual entry too."** This closes Open Question O-20 (Section 20).

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-50)'s brand-new/not-yet-saved-feature branch (Section 13.7) is extended, not restated from scratch, so that the identical confirmed mechanism — the pending write-back request via `FileUtils.writeFileContent()`, the project-plugin `Timer` poll, the UUID match against `overlayFeatureFormDrawer.featureForm.model`, the `changeAttribute()` call, and the empty-content-overwrite clearing step — governs manual identification entry exactly as it already governs real candidate selection, for a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature. This branch's prior scope-limiting closing sentence ("scoped to real candidate selection specifically... not decided by this entry") is retained, struck through, and marked superseded, immediately in place, not deleted. AC-QPB-046 (further revised; Decision Log D-50; Section 18.6) branch (a) is correspondingly extended to assert both scenarios — real candidate selection and manual identification entry — as independently testable, each verifiable only via real-device manual QA, following the existing convention for device-dependent criteria (Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072); its own prior scope-limiting closing sentence is likewise retained, struck through, and marked superseded, in place, not deleted.

  **What is confirmed unaffected.** AC-QPB-078 (manual-identification `identification_status`/nulled-column assertions) is reviewed against this entry and confirmed unaffected in its own substance: this entry only confirms the mechanism by which a manual entry's persistence is achieved for a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature, not which enum value or nulled columns that persistence must carry, which AC-QPB-078 already governs, unchanged. The existing/already-saved-feature branch of FR-QPB-109/AC-QPB-046 (Decision Log D-50's confirmed, permanent limitation, which already applied identically to candidate selection and manual entry alike) is unaffected and unchanged by this entry.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-50 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104–FR-QPB-108/FR-QPB-110–FR-QPB-118 or any other requirement outside FR-QPB-109/AC-QPB-046's own write-back-mechanism clauses in any way.

The entry below (D-52) is dated 2026-08-25 and records a confirmed real-device HTTP 413 finding plus confirmed technical facts from Pl@ntNet's own public documentation and direct QField v4.2.4 C++ source inspection, and the stakeholder's resulting confirmation of one narrow parameter, for the Pl@ntNet photo-upload path specifically (FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104, Section 13.1/13.2). It closes a genuine specification omission (Category B) — no prior requirement anticipated or specified any photo resize/compression/size-limiting step. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-51 above.

- **D-52** (mixed entry: **(1)** a confirmed real-device finding plus confirmed technical facts from Pl@ntNet's own public documentation and direct QField v4.2.4 C++ source inspection — not itself a stakeholder product decision, closing a genuine specification omission (Category B), recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47/D-48/D-49/D-50's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — the stakeholder's explicit confirmation of one narrow parameter, the exact resize target, among the options this finding required disclosing. Does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-51 above):

  **(1) The confirmed finding, in four parts.**

  - **Real-device 413 rejection.** Real-device testing reported that uploading a 6 MB photo for identification (via the existing "Identify attached photos" action, FR-QPB-101) returned an HTTP `413 Request Entity Too Large` response from Pl@ntNet.
  - **The specification omission this closes.** Investigation confirmed the current implementation (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbRunIdentification`) reads each attached photo's raw file bytes via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.readFileContent()` and embeds them, completely unmodified, into the multipart request body sent to Pl@ntNet — there is no resizing, compression, or size-limiting step anywhere in the current photo-upload path. FR-QPB-104 (Decision Log D-37) and FR-QPB-101 (Decision Log D-31/D-45/D-46) each already specified various photo-upload rules (endpoint, auth, `organs`/`images` field pairing, "no more than five JPEG/PNG photos... per request," error handling for authentication/quota/timeout/malformed-response cases), but none of them, at any point in this specification's history, ever anticipated or specified a size-limiting step for the photo bytes themselves — a genuine specification omission, not a defect in any existing requirement's implementation.
  - **Pl@ntNet's own documented guidance, and the honest limit of what it states.** Pl@ntNet's own public API documentation (`my.plantnet.org/doc/getting-started/faq`) states, verbatim: submitted images are "resized to a maximum size of 1280 pixels on the large side, but smaller submitted images will never be upscaled," and recommends clients submit images already at approximately that size, at approximately 90% JPEG compression quality, as best practice. Pl@ntNet's own documentation does not state an exact byte-size limit anywhere the orchestrator could find — this is recorded honestly as **not found**, not invented as a precise number. A full-resolution, unmodified modern phone-camera photo (commonly 6 MB+) is confirmed, by the real-device report above, to trigger a 413 response somewhere in the request path — Pl@ntNet's own infrastructure, or an intermediate layer between the field device and Pl@ntNet — which of the two this entry cannot determine, since Pl@ntNet does not document an exact limit.
  - **QField's own confirmed native mechanism, and why it must run against a temporary copy.** QField itself exposes a real, native, confirmed method for exactly this need: `FileUtils.restrictImageSize(imagePath, maximumWidthHeight)`, confirmed via direct inspection of the real QField v4.2.4 C++ source (`src/core/utils/fileutils.h`: "Insures that a given image's width and height are restricted to a maximum size"). This method resizes the image file at `imagePath` **in place** — it has no separate output-path parameter and returns nothing — so it must never be called directly on the original attachment file, which would permanently destroy the field worker's original, full-resolution photo evidence stored in the project's GeoPackage/attachments. The confirmed, correct approach operates on a temporary copy only: write the original photo's already-read bytes to a new temporary file via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.writeFileContent()`; call `FileUtils.restrictImageSize()` on that temporary copy only; read back the now-resized bytes from the temporary file via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.readFileContent()`; use those resized bytes, not the original bytes, for the Pl@ntNet multipart upload; and clean up the temporary file afterward via `FileUtils.writeFileContent(tempPath, "")` — an empty-content overwrite, following this project's own already-established convention of never relying on `FileUtils.deleteFiles()` for cleanup, which Decision Log D-50 already found unreliable/silently-no-op on at least one tested device (that finding is reused here, not restated in full).

  **(2) The stakeholder's decision.** Presented with Pl@ntNet's own documented 1280-pixel server-side resize target as the self-evidently non-wasteful choice — sending anything larger achieves nothing, since Pl@ntNet resizes it down anyway, while unnecessarily risking a size-limit rejection and wasting the field worker's mobile data/upload time — the stakeholder's explicit confirmation: **1280 pixels** on the long side, matching Pl@ntNet's own documented server-side resize target exactly.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-101 (Section 13.1; post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-46's text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted) is further revised to require the resize-via-temporary-copy step described in finding (1)'s fourth bullet above, inserted between reading the original attachment file's bytes and submitting those bytes to Pl@ntNet, with a maximum dimension of 1280 pixels on the long side. The original attachment file itself — the one referenced by the feature's own photo-path attribute and stored in the project's GeoPackage/attachments — must remain completely unmodified and at its original, full resolution at all times; only the temporary copy actually submitted to Pl@ntNet is ever downsized. FR-QPB-104 (Section 13.2) receives a minimal new cross-reference note only, clarifying which bytes are submitted without duplicating FR-QPB-101's substance. New AC-QPB-088 (Section 18.6) makes this independently, structurally testable: the generated project's embedded identification widget QML must contain the resize-via-temporary-copy mechanism (temporary-file write, `restrictImageSize` call with the `1280` argument, read-back, empty-content cleanup, and never a direct `restrictImageSize` call against the original attachment path) — mirroring how AC-QPB-069/AC-QPB-070 make other FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-101 mechanism details independently testable via structural QML inspection, and how AC-QPB-046 (Decision Log D-50) made FR-QPB-109's write-back mechanism independently testable at the mechanism level. AC-QPB-040 (Section 18.6, top-three-results ordering) is reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance — it concerns result count/ordering, not the bytes submitted. No DR/schema change is required: this entry concerns only the bytes submitted to Pl@ntNet, not any persisted GeoPackage attribute.

  **Flagged, not silently resolved.** The resize step's `FileUtils` singleton naming (`FileUtils.writeFileContent()`, `FileUtils.restrictImageSize()`, `FileUtils.readFileContent()`) matches Decision Log D-50's already-established write-back-mechanism naming and this entry's own confirmed v4.2.4 source-inspection finding. This entry does not address or reconcile any naming difference between this and the `QfFileUtils`/`org.qfield.core` naming FR-QPB-101 (Decision Log D-46) uses elsewhere, in that same requirement's still-current text, for the original attachment-file read step — reconciling that naming question, if one turns out to be needed, is a separate matter outside this entry's scope and is not decided here.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-51 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-100/FR-QPB-102/FR-QPB-103/FR-QPB-105–FR-QPB-118 or any other requirement outside FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104's own photo-resize-mechanism clauses in any way. It does not allege that any acceptance test currently in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/` is wrong or must change — whether existing Pl@ntNet-upload acceptance-test fixtures need an added structural assertion or a new device-QA placeholder to reflect this mechanism is left to a separate, future `test-designer` round, not decided here.

The entry below (D-53) is dated 2026-08-25 and records a Category C stakeholder-directed change to **this application's own** local storage mechanism for the VWorld/Pl@ntNet API keys it collects from the field-tool operator (`qfield_builder/credential_store.py`'s "Remember this key" retention path) — it has nothing to do with, and does not alter, the generated QField project's own, separately governed key-embedding exceptions (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079 for VWorld; FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-117 for Pl@ntNet, Decision Log D-45), which remain exactly as before. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-52 above.

- **D-53** (mixed entry: **(1)** a confirmed real, well-known technical behavior of unsigned macOS applications and the `keyring`/Keychain mechanism — not itself a stakeholder product decision — presented to the stakeholder as the motivation for a decision; **(2)** Category C — the stakeholder's explicit, confirmed three-part decision, reported to the spec-writer by the orchestrator rather than reproduced here as a literal verbatim quote (flagged explicitly below, not silently smoothed over, since every other Category C entry in this log reproduces the stakeholder's own words); **(3)** a disclosed security trade-off, recorded honestly per this project's established pattern (mirroring Decision Log D-46's QGIS-Desktop-rendering-caveat disclosure). Does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-52 above):

  **(1) The confirmed real annoyance and its technical basis.** This application is currently distributed as an **unsigned** build (no Apple Developer signing identity is available, per the packaging script's own disclosure and the delivery context already recorded in Decision Log D-25). macOS ties a Keychain access grant to the specific code signature of the requesting binary; an unsigned or ad-hoc-signed build's effective signature is not guaranteed stable across rebuilds, so the OS's own Keychain permission prompt ("[App] wants to use your confidential information stored in [keychain]...") can reappear on every single rebuild/relaunch of this application, not just once at first use. This is a real, well-known behavior of the `keyring` package on macOS Keychain for unsigned applications — confirmed by the orchestrator as a genuine technical fact, not merely a plausible guess — and the orchestrator confirmed directly with the stakeholder that this repeated-permission-prompt annoyance is indeed the actual, motivating pain point behind the decision below, not a hypothetical concern.

  **(2) The stakeholder's three-part decision.** Presented with this confirmed annoyance, the stakeholder's confirmed decision — reported to the spec-writer by the orchestrator, which represented itself as having confirmed each part directly with the stakeholder, including one point (the first-launch prompt's scope) the orchestrator says it asked the stakeholder about directly — comprises three interdependent parts, reconciled together in this one entry because none of the three is a coherent, working mechanism without the other two:

  1. **Remove the OS-credential-store (`keyring`) mechanism entirely** for this application's own key storage — no more Keychain/Windows-Credential-Manager-based storage for the VWorld/Pl@ntNet "Remember this key" opt-in, and therefore no more OS-level permission prompt tied to this application's own key storage.
  2. **Add application-managed encryption** for any locally-persisted API key, replacing the OS credential store as the retention mechanism for the existing "Remember this key" opt-in. NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072's own consent-gated "remember across sessions" *behavior* is **not** being removed — only its underlying storage mechanism changes, from the OS keychain/credential manager to an application-managed, locally-encrypted file.
  3. **Prompt the user to set a password the first time the application is ever launched** (or whenever no such password has yet been established) — a one-time setup step, not a per-launch application-wide access-gate. The stakeholder explicitly confirmed, when asked directly, that this password is used only to derive the encryption key for locally-stored credentials, not as a general access-gate over the rest of the application's functionality.

  **Honest sourcing note, flagged rather than silently smoothed over:** unlike Decision Log D-21, D-40, D-44–D-52, and every other Category C entry in this log, this entry has no literal, verbatim stakeholder quotation to reproduce, because none was supplied to the spec-writer for this item — only the orchestrator's paraphrased report of what it says it confirmed directly with the stakeholder. This is recorded here as a transparency matter, not a defect in the decision's validity: per this project's clean-room workflow, the spec-writer works from what the orchestrator provides, and this specification's own mandatory stopping point (presenting this document to the stakeholder for explicit review and approval before any further role acts on it) is exactly the check that confirms this framing is accurate. If, on review, any of the three parts above does not match the stakeholder's actual intent, that is a correction to make at this review step, not something this entry can verify independently.

  **What this decision requires, precisely:**
  - `keyring` (and any OS Keychain/Windows Credential Manager access) must no longer appear anywhere in this application's own key-retention code path.
  - The existing "Remember this key" opt-in (unchanged, consent-gated exactly as NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072 already required) now persists the key in an application-managed, locally-encrypted file — `credentials.enc` — placed in this application's own local application-data directory: macOS `~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\`. **This directory/filename convention is newly introduced by this entry**, since no prior local, writable, per-installation application-state-directory convention existed anywhere in this specification (confirmed by review of this specification and of this application's own `qfield_builder/resource_paths.py`, which resolves only this application's bundled, read-only resources, never a writable local-state location) — see new A-QPB-005.
  - The encryption key is derived from a password the user establishes at first launch (or at any later launch where no such password yet exists), via a named, concrete key-derivation function — **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256**, with at least 600,000 iterations and a randomly generated, per-installation salt of at least 16 bytes (the salt itself need not be kept secret and may be stored alongside the encrypted file) — producing a 32-byte key. **KDF choice and reasoning:** Python's standard library exposes `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` directly, and the third-party `cryptography` package exposes an equivalent `PBKDF2HMAC` construction; either is a real, available, well-documented option, and this specification does not invent a novel KDF. This specification specifies the **`cryptography` package** (`cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.pbkdf2.PBKDF2HMAC` for derivation, `cryptography.fernet.Fernet` for the encryption itself) rather than hand-assembling `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` with a separately chosen cipher, because `Fernet` is a complete, fixed-format, authenticated symmetric-encryption scheme (AES-128-CBC plus HMAC-SHA256, with its own built-in versioning/timestamp/IV handling) that has already had its nonce/IV-management and authentication-tag details worked out and documented by that library — avoiding exactly the class of hand-rolled-crypto mistake (e.g. IV reuse, missing authentication) this project's own mandate warns against inventing. This is a deliberate choice of a complete, well-known combination, not a custom scheme.
  - **Decline path:** if the user declines/skips the first-launch (or any later, still-unestablished) password prompt, no password is established; "Remember this key" becomes unavailable/disabled for that application session; the application falls back to the existing session-only, in-memory retention NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072 already specify for the non-remembered case — no new fallback behavior is invented here, this is the same existing session-only path reused. The setup prompt is shown again at the next launch, since a password still has not been established.
  - **Forgotten-password path:** if the user later cannot supply the correct password, decryption of `credentials.enc` fails; any previously remembered key becomes **permanently unrecoverable** — this specification does not invent, and explicitly disclaims, any password-recovery mechanism, since none exists — and the user must re-enter their API key(s) manually and may establish a new password (and therefore new encrypted storage) to resume "Remember this key" behavior going forward.
  - **Flagged, not decided here:** the stakeholder's confirmed instruction establishes that this password is not a general access-gate over the rest of the application, but it does not specify the exact UX for when/how the application re-requests this same password during a *later* session, in order to decrypt an already-remembered key (e.g., a targeted prompt at the point of retrieving a remembered key, versus some other mechanism). This specification does not invent an answer; it records the narrowest reading consistent with the stakeholder's "not a general access-gate" confirmation as an explicit assumption (new A-QPB-006) and raises it as new Open Question O-21.

  **(3) The disclosed security trade-off, stated honestly.** Moving from the operating system's own credential store — which, particularly on macOS, benefits from OS-level access controls and, in many configurations, hardware-backed protections (e.g. Secure Enclave-backed keychain items on supported hardware) — to an application-managed, password-derived encryption-at-rest scheme is a real, non-trivial security trade-off, not a strictly-more-secure replacement. The new scheme's protection depends entirely on the strength of the user's own chosen password and this KDF's chosen work factor (600,000 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 iterations); it does not benefit from OS-level access-control enforcement or hardware backing the way the OS credential store did. This is recorded as a disclosed, accepted trade-off — mirroring this document's own established pattern for such disclosures (e.g. Decision Log D-46's QGIS-Desktop-rendering caveat, D-36/D-47's technical-feasibility caveats) — not silently assumed to be strictly more secure than what it replaces.

  **What this changes.** §14.1 NFR-QPB-012/NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072 are each revised (original text retained above, struck through, marked superseded) to require the new storage mechanism while leaving their existing consent-gating substance unchanged; new NFR-QPB-073 states the first-launch password-setup requirement, its decline-path fallback, and its forgotten-password consequence. NFR-QPB-017/NFR-QPB-019/NFR-QPB-071 were each reviewed against this entry and confirmed unaffected in substance and not textually altered beyond a brief cross-reference annotation — they govern the `MANIFEST.json` disclosure flag and generated-project embedding-exception scope-independence respectively, neither of which is this entry's storage-mechanism concern. §18.5 AC-QPB-058 and §18.6 AC-QPB-082 are each revised (original text retained above, struck through, marked superseded) and new AC-QPB-089–AC-QPB-093 (§18.5) make the no-`keyring`-in-the-retention-path, not-plaintext-on-disk, named-KDF-parameters, first-launch-prompt/decline, and forgotten-password behaviors independently testable. §16 new A-QPB-005/A-QPB-006 record, respectively, that the application-data-directory convention is newly introduced here and that the retrieval-time password-re-prompt mechanism is an assumption pending stakeholder confirmation. §20 new Open Question O-21 records the one genuinely unresolved interaction-design question this entry does not invent an answer for.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-52 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079/FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-117 (the generated-project key-embedding exceptions) or any other requirement outside NFR-QPB-012/NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072/NFR-QPB-073's own desktop-application-local-storage-mechanism clauses in any way. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective — this entry is a specification change to an already-approved requirement's storage mechanism, not a report of a conformance defect, and per this project's change-control discipline, updating `qfield_builder/credential_store.py`, its dependencies, and any affected tests is `implementer`/`test-designer` work that follows this specification revision, not something this entry performs itself.

The entry below (D-54) is dated 2026-08-25 and records a Category C stakeholder-directed feature addition — displaying a representative reference image alongside each of the three candidates shown by the embedded "Identify attached photos" `QML Widget` (FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104/FR-QPB-109, Section 13.1/13.2/13.7) — based on the orchestrator's own direct research into Pl@ntNet's own public API documentation, confirmed feasible and then explicitly directed by the stakeholder. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-53 above.

- **D-54** (mixed entry: **(1)** confirmed technical facts from Pl@ntNet's own public API documentation, researched and confirmed by the orchestrator directly — not itself a stakeholder product decision, recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47/D-48/D-49/D-50/D-52's confirmed-technical-fact findings; **(2)** Category C — the stakeholder's explicit decision to proceed with a feature the stakeholder had asked the orchestrator to investigate for feasibility. Does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-53 above):

  **(1) The confirmed technical findings, in four parts.**

  - **The `include-related-images` request parameter.** Pl@ntNet's own identify-endpoint documentation (`my.plantnet.org/doc/api/identify`) confirms the endpoint accepts an additional query parameter, **`include-related-images=true`**, alongside the already-confirmed `api-key`/`nb-results` parameters this specification already establishes for the real, live endpoint (FR-QPB-104, Decision Log D-37). Pl@ntNet's own documentation states, when this parameter is set, it will "return a list of most-similar images for each probable species."
  - **The returned image fields.** Pl@ntNet's own reference documentation for these images (`my.plantnet.org/doc/references/using-images`) confirms each returned image carries: `organ`, `author`, `license`, `date`, `citation`, and a `url` object with `o` (original)/`m` (medium)/`s` (small) size-variant URLs — e.g. `https://bs.plantnet.org/image/s/<image-id>` for the small variant — confirmed via Pl@ntNet's own documentation and corroborated by web search.
  - **The CC BY-SA attribution requirement.** These images are licensed CC BY-SA, and Pl@ntNet's own documentation states an explicit attribution requirement whenever they are displayed, verbatim: **"Photo(s): [Contributor Username] / Pl@ntNet, CC BY-SA."** This requires, specifically: (i) a Pl@ntNet app credit, (ii) the CC BY-SA license indication, and (iii) the original contributor's name. This is a real licensing/legal obligation, not merely a nice-to-have, and must be reflected in the application's UI whenever a Pl@ntNet-sourced image is displayed.
  - **The QML display mechanism.** QML's native `Image` element can load a remote HTTP(S) URL directly via its `source` property — standard, well-documented Qt/QML behavior requiring no special network-fetch code beyond setting `source: <url>` — consistent with this project's existing, already-confirmed pattern of using QML's `XMLHttpRequest` for the Pl@ntNet network POST itself (FR-QPB-101).

  **(2) The stakeholder's decision.** The stakeholder framed this as "investigate whether representative images can be added" for each of the three candidates shown by the embedded "Identify attached photos" widget (FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104/FR-QPB-109). The orchestrator's investigation, recorded in part (1) above, confirmed this is feasible using Pl@ntNet's own documented `include-related-images` mechanism; the stakeholder subsequently directed proceeding with it as a real feature.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-104 (Section 13.2; Decision Log D-37 text retained, struck through, marked superseded) is further revised to add `include-related-images=true` to the Pl@ntNet request's query parameters, alongside the existing `api-key`/`nb-results=3`. FR-QPB-109 (Section 13.7) receives a new, purely additive bullet (Decision Log D-38/D-43/D-50/D-51's own persistence-mechanism substance retained, unreworded, and not reopened by this entry) requiring each candidate card to display one representative image — using the small (`s`) size variant, a deliberate bandwidth-conscious choice consistent with Decision Log D-52's existing photo-resize precedent — when the API response supplies one for that candidate, together with the CC BY-SA attribution described above whenever an image is actually displayed, degrading gracefully (no broken-image placeholder, no attribution text) when no image is available for a candidate, and never letting an image-load failure block or corrupt the rest of that candidate's existing textual content. New AC-QPB-094 (Section 18.6) makes the outgoing `include-related-images=true` request-shape assertion independently testable, mirroring AC-QPB-040's request-shape-adjacent framing. New AC-QPB-095 (Section 18.6) makes the generated widget QML's structural per-candidate `Image`-element/attribution-text construction and graceful-degradation-when-absent behavior independently testable via the same structural QML-source-inspection pattern already established for AC-QPB-046/AC-QPB-088. New AC-QPB-096 (Section 18.6) records, as a manual-QA-only placeholder (mirroring Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072's existing convention), the one part of this feature that cannot be confirmed via structural inspection alone: that a real candidate image actually renders on a real device/QGIS Desktop when network connectivity is present, with the required attribution, and that the rest of the card's content remains undegraded when an image load fails after the initial response. AC-QPB-040 (top-three-results ordering) is reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance — it concerns result count/ordering, not any additional response field the request may also return. No DR/schema change is required: this entry concerns only the ephemeral display of the API response's own image URLs at candidate-selection time, not any persisted GeoPackage attribute, mirroring Decision Log D-52's own no-DR-change footnote.

  **Network-connectivity note.** Displaying a candidate image requires network connectivity to load, exactly as reaching the candidate-display step itself already required being online for the identify response in the first place (FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104). If an image fails to load for any reason after the initial identify response has already succeeded (a transient network hiccup, a since-unreachable image URL, etc.), the card's existing textual content (scientific name, confidence, KTSN/probability enrichment, etc., per FR-QPB-109) must remain fully displayed and unaffected — an image-load failure must never block or corrupt the rest of the candidate's display.

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-53 above, and does not alter FR-QPB-100–FR-QPB-103/FR-QPB-105–FR-QPB-108/FR-QPB-110–FR-QPB-118 or any other requirement outside FR-QPB-104/FR-QPB-109's own representative-image-display clauses in any way. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective — this entry is a specification addition, not a report of a conformance defect, and per this project's change-control discipline, implementing it and adding corresponding acceptance tests is `implementer`/`test-designer` work that follows this specification revision, not something this entry performs itself.

The entry below (D-55) is dated 2026-08-25 and closes Open Question O-21, raised by Decision Log D-53's own entry, by recording the stakeholder's explicit answer to a direct clarifying question the orchestrator put to them about the retrieval-time password-re-prompt UX that D-53 left open. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-54 above.

- **D-55** (Category C: the stakeholder's explicit, confirmed choice between two disclosed options, closing Open Question O-21. This entry confirms, rather than corrects, the narrowest-reading assumption already recorded in A-QPB-006 — the assumption's own content turned out to already match the stakeholder's answer. Does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-54 above):

  **The question put to the stakeholder.** Decision Log D-53/new NFR-QPB-073 established the first-launch encrypted-storage password-setup requirement (its decline path and forgotten-password consequence) but left one interaction-design detail unresolved, recorded as Open Question O-21: exactly when, during a later application session, the application should re-request this password in order to decrypt an already-remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key. The orchestrator asked the stakeholder directly, presenting two options: **(a)** only at the point of use — e.g., right when the wizard would otherwise auto-fill a remembered key; or **(b)** once per application launch, upfront, before any wizard step.

  **The stakeholder's explicit answer: option (a), only at the point of use.**

  **What this confirms.** This is the identical narrowest reading A-QPB-006 already recorded as an unconfirmed assumption, consistent with the stakeholder's earlier "not a general access-gate" instruction (Decision Log D-53). The stakeholder's answer here does not correct or contradict that assumption's own content — it confirms it was the correct reading all along.

  **What this changes.** §14.1 NFR-QPB-073 is revised (its first-launch-prompt, decline-path, and forgotten-password substance unchanged and restated; only its previously open, explicitly-flagged final clause is replaced) to state, as a decided requirement rather than an open question: the application must re-prompt for the encryption password only at the specific point where a remembered key would otherwise be auto-filled (e.g., the relevant wizard step that would use a remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key) — never at general application startup, and never as a blanket gate over any other part of the application. §16 A-QPB-006 is annotated in place (not struck through or removed, since its own content already matched the confirmed answer) to record that it is no longer a live, unconfirmed assumption. §18.5 new AC-QPB-097 makes the confirmed retrieval-time trigger point independently testable. §20 O-21 is marked CLOSED (a new sub-bullet appended after its existing open-question text; original O-21 text left completely unchanged).

  This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-54 above, and does not alter any other FR/DR/NFR/AC requirement outside NFR-QPB-073's own previously-open retrieval-timing clause. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective — this entry closes a specification gap explicitly flagged as open by D-53, it is not a report of a conformance defect, and per this project's change-control discipline, implementing this retrieval-time trigger and adding a corresponding acceptance test is `implementer`/`test-designer` work that follows this specification revision, not something this entry performs itself.

  2. New FR-QPB-119 (Section 9) states the alias-setting requirement itself, cross-referenced additively from FR-QPB-057 (FR-QPB-057's own text is otherwise unchanged — this is a purely additive cross-reference, not a supersession, mirroring the precedent set by Decision Log D-52's FR-QPB-104 cross-reference note). New Section 8.5 enumerates, per survey type and per table, every in-scope column's proposed Korean alias, built from three sources in order of authority: (a) this specification's own existing field descriptions (Section 8.1–8.4, `ColumnDef.comment` values in `qfield_builder/schemas.py`); (b) this application's own already-drafted Korean UI copy, specifically the Step 2 survey-type explanations (FR-QPB-024a/Decision Log D-27) and the Step 5 identification-toggle text in `qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py`, which independently establish several terms this entry aligns with rather than re-deriving from scratch — notably "사이트" for the `site` concept, "조사" for the `survey` concept, "조사구" for the `plot` concept ("고정 조사구" for the Type-3 permanent variant specifically), "관찰" for the `observation` concept, "군락" for the `community` concept, "피도" for `cover`, "우점종" for `dominant_species`, "현장 확인 여부" for `is_field_checked`, "출현 확률" for `occurrence_probability`, "식별" (not "동정") for the identification-subsystem term family, and "KTSN" left untranslated; and (c), only where neither (a) nor (b) settles the term, the spec-writer's own domain-informed best judgment, explicitly flagged Medium confidence. New AC-QPB-098 (Section 18.2) makes the alias/no-alias split independently testable once this entry is approved. New Open Question O-22 (Section 20) consolidates every Medium-confidence term for explicit stakeholder confirmation or correction.

  **Honest limits of this proposal, stated rather than smoothed over.** This entry's Korean terminology is the spec-writer's own reasoned proposal — informed by standard Korean ecological/biological survey usage and by this application's own existing, but not independently stakeholder-reviewed, wizard copy — not a translation supplied or verified by the stakeholder or by a domain expert at the institute. Every field flagged Medium confidence in Section 8.5/Open Question O-22 is flagged precisely because more than one common Korean rendering exists, because the exact institute-preferred register/phrasing could not be verified from any artifact available to the spec-writer, or because the term is a scientific/technical abbreviation (`KTSN`) with no single settled Korean rendering confirmed anywhere in this project. No field was found whose real-world referent is unclear — the underlying purpose of every field is already documented in Section 8/Section 13 — so no field is raised as an open question about *meaning*, only about *rendering*.

  **What this does not change.** This entry does not alter DR-QPB-005/DR-QPB-006/DR-QPB-002 (the existing hidden-UUID/foreign-key/physical-key rules), FR-QPB-057's own existing substance (only a cross-reference is appended), NFR-QPB-070/Decision Log D-28 (the desktop application's own separate UI-localization requirement, confirmed unaffected — it governs a different surface entirely), or any other requirement outside the new items listed above. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective — the current absence of field aliases is a specification gap this entry closes, not a conformance defect, and per this project's change-control discipline, implementing `setFieldAlias` calls and adding corresponding acceptance tests is `test-designer`/`implementer` work that follows this specification revision, not something this entry performs itself.

The entry below (D-59) is dated 2026-08-26 and records a Category B correction of a confirmed technical/factual error in DR-QPB-071 (Section 7) and Section 8.5's own scoping note (Section 8), discovered during implementation and review of the Korean field-alias feature (Decision Log D-56/D-57/D-58). It is not a stakeholder product decision and not a Category A implementation defect. It does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-58 above.

- **D-59** (Category B correction of a confirmed technical/factual error in the specification's own reasoning — not a stakeholder product decision, and not a Category A implementation defect to be fixed in code; recorded with the same rigor as Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47's confirmed-technical-fact corrections; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-58 above):

  **What was wrong.** DR-QPB-071 (Section 7) and Section 8.5's own scoping note (Section 8, immediately above the Type 1 table) each stated that the hidden GeoPackage physical key `fid` (DR-QPB-002) is excluded from this section's Korean-alias proposal "for the same reason" the geometry columns (`geom`/`site_geom`/`plot_geom`/`community_geom`) are excluded — because it is "never modeled as a `ColumnDef`... and is already excluded from the attribute-editor form tree entirely." By direct parallel to the geometry-column sentence immediately preceding it in each location — which explicitly states geometry columns "are not part of a QGIS vector layer's attribute-field collection (`layer.fields()`)" — this language implied `fid` is likewise absent from `layer.fields()`. **This implied claim is false.** `fid` is not modeled as a `ColumnDef` in this codebase's own Python schema classes (`qfield_builder/schemas.py`) — that narrower part was, and remains, true — but it **is** a genuine, real attribute field present in `layer.fields()` for every generated GeoPackage `QgsVectorLayer` in this codebase. It is only excluded from the visible attribute-editor *form tree*, which is a different, narrower thing than being absent from the layer's field collection entirely.

  **What is now confirmed correct, and how (four independent lines of evidence).**
  1. `qfield_builder/gpkg.py`'s table-DDL construction creates every domain table with an explicit `"fid" INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` column — a real, physical database column, required by the OGC GeoPackage specification's own named-integer-primary-key rule.
  2. `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_build_drag_and_drop_form` function, and its surrounding comment block (added by an earlier, unrelated implementer round), already documents that "QGIS pre-populates [the form] with a flat, ungrouped `QgsAttributeEditorField` for every field on the layer (including the physical `fid` primary key)," and that the function must actively clear and rebuild the form tree to achieve `fid`'s exclusion from the *visible form* — a step that is only meaningful/necessary because `fid` genuinely is a member of `layer.fields()` to begin with; if it were truly absent from `layer.fields()`, as the corrected text previously implied, there would be nothing present for this clearing step to exclude.
  3. `tests/unit/test_qgis_worker_drag_and_drop_form.py`, an existing, already-passing, real-PyQGIS-backed regression test, independently confirms exactly this distinction: `fid`'s absence from the *form tree* is not the same thing as its absence from `layer.fields()`.
  4. This also matches standard, well-documented GeoPackage/OGR/QGIS behavior: unlike a Shapefile, which has no genuine primary-key column and for which OGR synthesizes an ephemeral `FID` outside the attribute schema, a GeoPackage's OGC-required integer primary key is a real table column, and OGR/QGIS's GeoPackage driver exposes it as an ordinary attribute field.

  A newly written acceptance test, `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/test_korean_field_aliases.py::test_every_layer_field_is_accounted_for_by_exactly_one_alias_expectation`, which assumed the now-corrected (incorrect) claim, was found to fail against a real generated project with the concrete, reproduced assertion failure `extra=['fid']` — direct empirical confirmation, from outside this specification entirely, that `fid` really is present in `layer.fields()` and was simply missing an alias expectation.

  **What this changes.** DR-QPB-071 (Section 7) is revised in place: the clause equating `fid`'s form-tree exclusion with absence from `layer.fields()` is struck through, not deleted, and replaced with the corrected technical basis above, citing this entry. Section 8.5's scoping note (Section 8, immediately above the Type 1 table) is revised the same way: the sentence claiming `fid` is unlisted "for the same reason" as geometry columns is struck through and replaced with a corrected sentence clarifying that `fid`'s omission from Section 8.5's alias table rests on a different, unrelated basis than geometry columns' omission.

  **What this does not change.** This correction does **not** change the actual, substantive requirement that `fid` must receive no Korean alias — that conclusion remains correct and unaffected, and is restated (not reopened) by the corrected text: `fid` is not a domain-meaningful field a surveyor should see labeled, and it is already excluded from the *visible* attribute-editor form entirely by the pre-existing, unrelated, unaffected `_build_drag_and_drop_form` mechanism (DR-QPB-002). What changes is only the *reasoning*/*technical claim* about *why*/*how* `fid` is excluded from this section's proposal — not the exclusion itself, and not any other requirement's substance. This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-58 above, does not alter FR-QPB-119, AC-QPB-098, or any row of Section 8.5's per-field alias table beyond the one scoping-note sentence identified above, and does not allege that any application source file currently in `qfield_builder/` is defective — `_build_drag_and_drop_form`'s existing `fid`-exclusion behavior is confirmed correct by this same investigation, not questioned by it.

  **What remains out of scope for this entry.** This is a specification-only correction. `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`, `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/conftest.py`, the corresponding traceability file, and the one acceptance test found to fail against the corrected understanding (`test_every_layer_field_is_accounted_for_by_exactly_one_alias_expectation`, and any harness helper it relies on that enumerates `layer.fields()` without accounting for `fid`) each still assume the now-corrected claim and will need a corresponding `test-designer` round to reconcile them against this entry — that reconciliation work is out of scope for this specification-only correction and is not performed here. No test file or application source file is modified by this entry.

  **Approval status.** This entry records a confirmed technical/factual correction of the specification's own prior reasoning, not a stakeholder product decision, and therefore does not require the same kind of stakeholder sign-off a Category C entry does; it is presented, alongside the rest of this specification revision, for the orchestrator's/stakeholder's ordinary review.

The four entries below (D-60–D-63) are dated 2026-08-26 and record four independently classified, newly-requested stakeholder items (a fifth, factual question, was answered directly by the orchestrator and required no specification change). Each is its own separately traceable Decision Log entry, per this project's own change-control discipline. **None of D-60–D-63 has been reviewed or approved by the stakeholder; no `test-designer` or `implementer` work may proceed against any of them until that approval is given.**

- **D-60** (Category C — two related, verbatim stakeholder instructions extending the already-shipped KTSN direct-match/accepted-name-resolution mechanism (FR-QPB-106/FR-QPB-107, Decision Log D-37/D-39/D-40/D-42) and candidate-selection persistence mechanism (FR-QPB-109, Decision Log D-38/D-43/D-50/D-51/D-54); ~~**draft, not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder**~~ **CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (2026-08-26) exactly as originally proposed in this entry — see new Decision Log D-64 below**; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-59 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instructions, given together:**
  1. "After identification, when displaying the scientific and Korean names, do not use the scientific name as-is. Instead, display the standardized scientific name from the `taxon_full_nm` field in the `ktsn_lookup.csv` file."
  2. "After identification, the scientific name entered into the field upon selection must also be the standardized name from the `taxon_full_nm` field in the `ktsn_lookup.csv` file."

  **Investigation finding (grounds this entry; not itself a stakeholder decision).** `taxon_full_nm` is **already** one of the 5 columns bundled into every identification-enabled generated project's `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` (`REQUIRED_KTSN_CSV_COLUMNS`, `qfield_builder/reference_bundle.py`; FR-QPB-105/FR-QPB-112 (revised, D-47)/FR-QPB-118 (further revised, D-48)) — it is not merely present in the raw upstream source and dropped by the extraction pipeline. It is already read and used internally by both the Python reference matcher (`qfield_builder/ktsn_match.py`) and its line-for-line QML mirror (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbMatchKtsn`), which already compute an `<em>`-tag-stripped `accepted_scientific_name` field from a matched row's `taxon_full_nm` whenever accepted-name resolution succeeds (`taxon_jm_nm == '정명'`, or a single canonical `correct_list` entry is resolved per FR-QPB-107). **This item therefore requires no extension to FR-QPB-105/FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113/FR-QPB-118's reference-bundling/column-extraction pipeline** — contrary to the possibility this entry was asked to investigate, no new column needs to be added to the bundled CSV. What is missing is narrower: (a) the candidate-card display and the `selected_scientific_name` value persisted on selection currently use Pl@ntNet's own raw `species.scientificName` (`qpbHandlePlantNetResponse`/`qpbSelectCandidate`, `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`) unconditionally, never the CSV-derived name, even when a KTSN match exists; and (b) the match result exposes an accepted-name-derived scientific name (`accepted_scientific_name`) only when accepted-name resolution actually succeeds — there is currently no equivalent field exposing the *directly matched* row's own `taxon_full_nm` when a direct match is found but accepted-name resolution does not succeed (ambiguous, `correct_list` empty/malformed, accepted KTSN not found in the CSV, etc.), the same way `direct_korean_name` already exists alongside `accepted_korean_name`.

  **What this adds.** FR-QPB-106 (Section 13.4) is revised (further revised; this entry) to require the direct-match step to also expose the matched row's own `taxon_full_nm`, with `<em>` tags stripped exactly as `accepted_scientific_name` already is, as a new `direct_scientific_name` field on the match result — mirroring the existing `direct_korean_name` field precisely, so it is available regardless of whether accepted-name resolution (FR-QPB-107) succeeds. FR-QPB-109 (Section 13.7) is revised (further revised; this entry, purely additive) so that both the candidate-card scientific-name display and the value persisted to `selected_scientific_name` on selection use, in order of preference: **(1)** `accepted_scientific_name` when accepted-name resolution succeeded; **(2)** otherwise `direct_scientific_name` (new, above) when a direct KTSN match was found but accepted-name resolution did not succeed; **(3)** otherwise — no direct KTSN match found at all — Pl@ntNet's own raw `species.scientificName`, **exactly as today, unchanged by this entry** (see the open question immediately below). Pl@ntNet's own `scientificName`/`scientificNameAuthorship` remain read/preserved for audit purposes exactly as FR-QPB-104 already requires; this entry changes only which name is used as *the* displayed/persisted scientific name, not whether Pl@ntNet's own values continue to be read from the response.

  **What this deliberately does not decide (flagged, not silently assumed — new Open Question O-23).** The stakeholder's two verbatim instructions above are both phrased "after identification" and do not state what should happen when Pl@ntNet returns a candidate for which **no** KTSN match is found at all (case (3) above), nor whether case (2) above (a direct match exists but is not confirmed as the *accepted*, non-synonym name) should be treated the same as case (1), or should instead also fall back to Pl@ntNet's raw name. This entry's own drafted proposal takes the narrower, more literal reading — apply the CSV-derived name only when *some* KTSN match exists (cases (1)/(2)), leave the existing no-match fallback and its existing "KTSN match not found" disclosure completely unchanged for case (3) — because the stakeholder's instructions presuppose a matched CSV row to read `taxon_full_nm` from. This is recorded explicitly as this entry's own assumption, not as a confirmed stakeholder decision; see Open Question O-23.

  **What this does not change.** FR-QPB-107's own accepted-name-resolution logic (Decision Log D-40/D-42) is unaffected in substance — `accepted_scientific_name` was already `taxon_full_nm`-derived before this entry; this entry only makes it, and the new sibling `direct_scientific_name`, the values actually *used* for display/persistence in place of Pl@ntNet's raw name. FR-QPB-105/FR-QPB-112/FR-QPB-113/FR-QPB-118's reference-bundling/extraction pipeline is confirmed unaffected (see the investigation finding above) — no new column, no new bundled file. The Korean-name side of display/persistence (`korean_name_display`, `selected_korean_name`) is already `taxon_kor_nm`-derived via `accepted_korean_name`/`direct_korean_name` and is unaffected by this entry.

  **Approval status: ~~DRAFT. Not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder.~~ CONFIRMED (2026-08-26) — the stakeholder confirmed this entry's own drafted proposal exactly as written, including its explicit choice not to alter the no-KTSN-match fallback; see new Decision Log D-64, which closes Open Question O-23.** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-106 (revised)/FR-QPB-109 (further revised)/AC-QPB-099.

- **D-61** (Category C — new feature with real architectural implications; ~~**draft, not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder; the network-boundary portion additionally requires the stakeholder's own explicit decision among disclosed options, mirroring Decision Log D-24's precedent, before any part of it may be implemented**~~ **CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (2026-08-26), including the network-boundary decision — see new Decision Log D-65 below**; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-60 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction:** "Add a feature for configuring symbol styles for points and polygons, with minimalist default settings. For points, users should also be able to search for and download SVG icons directly from Tabler for use as symbols."

  **Investigation findings (ground this entry; not stakeholder decisions).** (1) The only existing symbology customization anywhere in this codebase is DR-QPB-051's rule-based renderer for the Type 4 `community` polygon layer (`is_field_checked` green/red hatch, `_apply_community_symbology` in `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`); every other point/polygon layer in every survey type currently receives QGIS's own built-in default symbol (`QgsSymbol.defaultSymbol(layer.geometryType())`), never a deliberately chosen "minimalist" style — there is no existing "default styling" requirement this item could be read as merely restating. (2) No SVG-icon or Tabler-related code, dependency, or network destination exists anywhere in this repository. (3) This application's network boundary (FR-QPB-011, revised by Decision Log D-24's narrow OpenStreetMap drawing-canvas carve-out) currently permits exactly three purposes: VWorld online-basemap tiles, VWorld offline-MBTiles tile downloads, and OSM tiles for the drawing-canvas visual aid. `tabler-icons.io` (or any other Tabler-project distribution host) is a **fourth, new network destination**, not covered by any existing clause, and — per this specification's own explicit governing rule (FR-QPB-011's closing sentence, "No other network access is permitted in the MVP," and NFR-QPB-002's parallel rule) — may not be added without its own explicit decision, exactly as D-24 required for the OSM case.

  **Draft proposal — symbol styling (points/polygons, minimalist defaults).** New FR-QPB-120 (Section 9; draft) proposes: every point layer receives a simple, single-color circular marker symbol, and every polygon layer receives a simple, single-color solid-fill-with-outline symbol, applied as each generated project's own default `QgsSymbol`/`QgsSingleSymbolRenderer` at build time (extending, not replacing, DR-QPB-051's existing rule-based renderer for the one already-special-cased Type 4 `community` layer, which is unaffected). "Minimalist" is not otherwise defined anywhere in this specification or this codebase; this entry's own concrete proposal — a single flat fill color with a thin, contrasting outline for polygons, and a small solid circle marker for points, with no gradient, pattern, label callout, or per-category color-coding by default — is offered as a reasoned starting point only, explicitly flagged for the stakeholder's own confirmation or correction (Open Question O-25), not asserted as the stakeholder's own specification.

  **Draft proposal — Tabler SVG icon search/download for point symbols.** New FR-QPB-121 (Section 9; draft) proposes a wizard-accessible (or post-build; see Open Question O-27) affordance letting the user search Tabler's published icon set by name/keyword and select one SVG icon to use as a given point layer's marker symbol, replacing the minimalist default marker for that layer. This is drafted as a narrowly scoped proposal only, mirroring Decision Log D-24's own carve-out structure, and is **not approved** — it requires the stakeholder's explicit decision among the disclosed options in new Open Question O-24 before any implementation may proceed, covering: which specific Tabler distribution/API mechanism is used (a static icon-metadata bundle fetched once vs. a live per-keystroke search endpoint — Tabler's own exact, currently supported machine-readable search mechanism has not been independently verified by this spec-writer round, since no live-research tool was available to it; this must be confirmed, not assumed, before FR-QPB-121 can be finalized); Tabler Icons' own current license terms and whether/how attribution must be disclosed in the generated project (commonly understood, but not freshly, independently reverified in this round, to be MIT-licensed); offline behavior when no network is available (the minimalist default must remain fully available and usable with zero network access, mirroring NFR-QPB-060(4)'s existing drawing-canvas discipline); and whether a downloaded icon is embedded into the generated project's own output (as a local file the `.qgs` symbol references, requiring its own relative-path/portability treatment per FR-QPB-091/DR-QPB-012) or is a desktop-application-only, UI-tool convenience that never appears in generated project output. New NFR-QPB-080 (Section 5.4; draft) proposes safeguards for this new network destination mirroring NFR-QPB-060's existing OSM safeguards (identifying `User-Agent`, no automatic-retry-storm behavior, and a permanently visible attribution/license notice wherever a downloaded Tabler icon is used) — itself provisional pending Open Question O-24. A purely additive cross-reference note is appended to the end of FR-QPB-011 (Section 5.4) pointing to this entry and O-24; FR-QPB-011's own approved clauses (a)/(b)/(c) and its "No other network access is permitted" closing sentence are **not** struck through, reworded, or extended by this entry — no new clause (d) is added to FR-QPB-011 until O-24 is resolved.

  **Further open questions raised, not silently resolved.** New Open Question O-26: does this styling feature apply per-layer, per-survey-type, or globally across every generated project (e.g., can two projects of the same survey type receive different point/polygon styles, or is styling fixed once per survey-type template)? New Open Question O-27: how does a user configure this in the wizard — a new, seventh wizard step (renumbering the existing Step 6 "Review and build," FR-QPB-040/041) inserted before review, or a post-build/settings-panel option exercised after project generation, or something else? This specification does not invent wizard UX unilaterally; both are offered as real options for the stakeholder to choose between, not decided here.

  **Approval status: ~~DRAFT. Not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder.~~ CONFIRMED (2026-08-26) — the stakeholder has explicitly resolved Open Questions O-24–O-27, including the network-boundary decision; see new Decision Log D-65 below.** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-011 (further revised)/FR-QPB-120 (revised)/FR-QPB-121 (revised)/FR-QPB-123 (new)/NFR-QPB-080 (revised)/AC-QPB-100–AC-QPB-102 (revised)/AC-QPB-104 (new).

- **D-62** (Category C — new feature with major, genuinely unresolved architectural implications; ~~**this entry is an investigation/proposal record only — no FR/DR/NFR/AC number is added by this entry itself; concrete requirement text is deliberately deferred to a future spec-writer round once the stakeholder has resolved the open questions below, mirroring this specification's own precedent for Open Question O-13 before Decision Log D-31 resolved it**~~ **The stakeholder has since resolved Open Questions O-28–O-32; the deferred concrete requirement text this entry anticipated is now drafted by new Decision Log D-66/D-67/D-68 below.**; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-61 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction:** "Connect a lookup table so that fields such as the Korean name and scientific name accept values only from a predefined range selectable through a dropdown menu. As the user types, dynamically filter the available options and display no more than five results. When a Korean name is entered, automatically populate the corresponding scientific name and KTSN. Conversely, when a scientific name is entered, automatically populate the corresponding Korean name and KTSN. If the entered name is a synonym or original combination, automatically replace it with the linked accepted name and notify the user—such as through a popup—that the name has been standardized. Since the lookup table contains a large number of rows, structure it to support indexing for efficient searches."

  **Investigation findings (ground this entry; not stakeholder decisions, and explicitly not asserted as confirmed QGIS/QField technical capability — see the caution below).**
  1. No KTSN lookup table exists anywhere in this codebase as a queryable database table today. `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` (FR-QPB-112 (revised)/FR-QPB-118 (further revised); 20,914 rows after Decision Log D-48's five-step filtering pipeline) is consumed only by hand-written JavaScript inside the embedded Pl@ntNet identification `QML Widget` (`qpbLoadCsv`/`qpbMatchKtsn`, `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`) — it is not loaded as a GeoPackage table, not added to the generated project's `.qgs` file (the "Reference" layer-tree group FR-QPB-055 already creates is currently never populated with any layer, `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`), and not referenced by any `ValueRelation`/`RelationReference` editor widget anywhere in this codebase. `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` (Section 8.1/8.2/8.3) currently receive no special editor-widget configuration at all in `_configure_widget_for_column` (`qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`) — they fall through to QGIS's own plain default text-edit widget, exactly like any other free-text field.
  2. This codebase already implements, but only inside that one embedded `QML Widget`'s own JavaScript, an in-memory indexed-lookup technique for exactly this CSV (`nameIndex`/`ktsnIndex`, built once per identification run, giving O(1) name/KTSN lookup instead of a linear scan) — a real, working precedent for "efficient search over this lookup table" that does **not** require a database index or a real GeoPackage table, but that is currently scoped to, and reachable only from, the identification action's own widget, not from the plain `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` fields themselves.
  3. Reading this same bundled `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` file from within embedded QML already requires QField's own native `FileUtils.readFileContent()` mechanism, not plain QML `XMLHttpRequest` (Decision Log D-46) — confirming that any reused/extended version of this technique inherits the same already-disclosed QField-only rendering caveat AC-QPB-070 (further revised)/Decision Log D-46 already establish for the Pl@ntNet identification widget: it would not be expected to render in QGIS Desktop specifically.
  4. **This spec-writer round has no live web-research tool available to it** (unlike prior rounds that produced Decision Log D-24/D-30/D-37/D-46, which relied on the orchestrator's own live research). It therefore cannot, and does not, independently confirm: (a) whether QGIS's native `ValueRelation` editor widget (or `RelationReference` with an embedded/filtered form) actually supports a live, as-you-type, filtered dropdown capped at exactly five displayed results, backed by a ~20,914-row table, in either QGIS Desktop or QField specifically; or (b) whether QField's own rendering of either widget type matches QGIS Desktop's behavior for this specific interaction. Per this specification's own hard-won discipline (Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-47/D-59 — each a case where an unverified technical claim reached this specification and had to be corrected later), this entry does **not** assert that either mechanism works as described; both are recorded below as **unverified hypotheses requiring independent, live confirmation** before implementation, exactly the posture this specification already takes for QGIS/QField internals elsewhere (Decision Log D-36's raster-sampling caveat is the closest existing precedent).

  **Two candidate architectural directions, presented as real, mutually exclusive options for the stakeholder to choose between — this entry does not pick one:**

  - **Option 1 — native QGIS/QField editor widget, backed by a real table.** Bundle `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` (or an equivalent projection of it) as a real table inside the generated GeoPackage, or a separate bundled lookup GeoPackage/layer, referenced by the generated project (populating the currently-empty "Reference" layer-tree group, FR-QPB-055). Configure `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` with a native QGIS editor widget (`ValueRelation`, possibly with a `FilterExpression`/`UseCompleter`-style configuration, or `RelationReference`) pointing at that table. Build-time `CREATE INDEX` statements on the relevant name columns, mirroring DR-QPB-009's already-established "ordinary indexes must exist on... commonly searched name fields" convention, would give this option a concrete, testable meaning for "indexing for efficient search." **Advantage:** if QGIS's/QField's native widget genuinely supports the required live-filter/max-5-result UX (unverified — see above), this option works identically in both QGIS Desktop and QField, unlike Option 2. **Risk:** the required UX (live filter, exactly five results, both-directions auto-population, synonym auto-replace-with-popup) may not be achievable through native QGIS editor-widget configuration alone; the synonym-auto-replace-and-notify behavior in particular likely requires custom logic beyond what a `ValueRelation`/`RelationReference` widget's own configuration provides, and QGIS's `QgsEditFormConfig` Python-init-function mechanism (a plausible desktop-side candidate for that extra logic) is **not confirmed** to execute at all inside QField's own runtime, which is JavaScript/QML-based, not a full PyQGIS Python environment — this is the same category of QGIS-Desktop-vs-QField capability gap already documented for a different mechanism at Decision Log D-46, and is flagged with the same rigor here, not assumed away.

  - **Option 2 — custom `QML Widget`, mirroring the already-proven Pl@ntNet identification architecture.** Build a new, dedicated `QML Widget` editor-widget (Decision Log D-31/D-46's already-proven mechanism, `QgsAttributeEditorContainer`/`QgsAttributeEditorField`, FR-QPB-057) for `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` specifically, reusing/extending the existing `qpbLoadCsv`/`nameIndex`/`ktsnIndex` in-memory-indexed-lookup technique to implement the live-filter/max-5-result/auto-populate/synonym-replace-and-notify behavior entirely in JavaScript, replacing the plain text-edit widget these fields currently receive. This reuses proven, already-working infrastructure (D-31/D-46/D-50/D-51) rather than depending on unverified native-widget capability, and the "synonym-replace-and-notify" behavior can directly reuse FR-QPB-107's already-implemented accepted-name-resolution logic (`accepted_korean_name`/`accepted_scientific_name`, and the new `direct_scientific_name`/standardized-display logic proposed by Decision Log D-60, if approved). **Risk:** inherits the same QField-only rendering caveat already disclosed for the identification widget (Decision Log D-46) — this dropdown would not be expected to render in QGIS Desktop. It also inherits the same category of write-back uncertainty this specification already spent three Decision Log entries (D-36→D-50→D-51) resolving for the Pl@ntNet candidate-selection case: **auto-populating a sibling field (e.g. writing `selected_ktsn`/the paired name field automatically when the user selects a dropdown result) is exactly the kind of "write to the current feature's own attributes from within an embedded `QML Widget`" problem D-50 found QGIS's confirmed `expression.evaluate()` context property cannot do at all, and which required a separate, real, working pending-request-file/project-plugin-polling mechanism to actually solve — for a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature only; write-back to an already-saved, reopened feature remains a confirmed, permanent limitation (D-50)**. This entry flags, rather than assumes past, that Option 2's "automatically populate"/"automatically replace... and notify" requirements would likely face this identical constraint, with the identical brand-new-vs-already-saved-feature split in what is achievable at all.

  **Further open questions raised, not silently resolved.** New Open Question O-28 (the architecture choice between Option 1 and Option 2 above, and the underlying unverified technical capability each depends on); new Open Question O-29 (scope: does this apply to `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` only, across all of Types 1–3, or also to other name-like fields such as Type 4's `dominant_species`, Section 8.4 — the stakeholder's own instruction says "fields such as," which is illustrative, not an exhaustive list); new Open Question O-30 (whether the synonym-auto-replace-and-popup-notify behavior is achievable in QField specifically, as distinct from QGIS Desktop, given the write-back constraint identified above); new Open Question O-31 (whether this feature's dependency on `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` means it is necessarily scoped to only those generated projects that already enable the post-MVP identification subsystem, per FR-QPB-112's existing conditional bundling rule, or whether the stakeholder wants this dropdown/autocomplete available even when Pl@ntNet identification itself is disabled — which would require bundling the reference data unconditionally, itself a change to FR-QPB-112 with project-size implications already flagged at Open Question O-17); new Open Question O-32 (whether "structure it to support indexing for efficient searches" means a literal, build-time SQL index on a real database table — meaningful only under Option 1 — or is already substantially addressed by the existing in-memory JS index technique described in investigation finding 2 above — meaningful under Option 2).

  **Approval status: ~~DRAFT — investigation/proposal record only.~~ RESOLVED (2026-08-26) — the stakeholder has reviewed this entry and explicitly resolved Open Questions O-28–O-32, selecting Option 1 (native `ValueRelation`/`RelationReference` widget backed by a real bundled table) and confirming a one-way-autofill/filter-to-accepted-only design for the synonym-handling sub-question. This entry's own investigation record and both candidate options above remain unaltered, for the historical record; the concrete requirement text it deferred is now drafted by new Decision Log D-66 (architecture/scope), D-67 (synonym handling/derived fields), and D-68 (bundling scope) below.** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against the new DR-QPB-072 and FR-QPB-124–FR-QPB-127 those entries introduce.

- **D-63** (Category B — closes a specification omission Section 8.5 had already explicitly identified as out of scope for that round, not a reversal of any existing requirement; ~~**draft, not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder**~~ **CONFIRMED by the stakeholder (2026-08-26) — see new Decision Log D-69 below**; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-62 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction:** "The 'Identification Status' field should be changed to allow selection from a predefined list of values."

  **Grounding.** `identification_status`'s complete, fixed set of values is already confirmed and unchanged by this entry: `not_requested`, `pending`, `complete`, `failed`, `manual` (`_IDENTIFICATION_STATUS_VALUES`, `qfield_builder/schemas.py`; enumerated in Section 8.1/8.2/8.3's field tables; `manual` added by Decision Log D-43; enforced today only by a SQLite `CHECK` constraint, `_identification_status_col()`). `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_configure_widget_for_column` currently applies a `ValueMap` editor widget only to the `organ` field (`{v: v for v in ("leaf", "flower", "fruit", "bark", "auto")}`) — `identification_status` receives no matching branch and therefore falls through to QGIS's own plain default text-edit widget, confirmed by a real-device screenshot showing a plain text box containing the literal string `not_requested`. This is precisely the gap Section 8.5 (Decision Log D-56) already named and explicitly declined to address in that round: "value-level Korean display (e.g. via `ValueMap`) is a related but separate, out-of-scope concern this section does not propose." This entry closes that exact, already-identified gap; it is unrelated in scope to Decision Log D-62/Section 13.9's much larger lookup-table/autocomplete proposal above — both are about constraining a name-like or status-like field to valid values, but this entry is narrowly scoped to one existing, fully-enumerated, already-fixed five-value field using the existing `ValueMap` mechanism this codebase already uses elsewhere, not a new lookup-table/dropdown architecture.

  **What this adds.** New FR-QPB-122 (Section 9; draft) requires `_configure_widget_for_column` to configure `identification_status` (Section 8.1's `inventory_observation`; Section 8.2/8.3's `observation`) with a `ValueMap` (or a functionally equivalent fixed-list-selection) editor widget listing exactly the five existing enum values as the only selectable options — no free-text entry. The value actually written to the GeoPackage on selection must remain exactly the existing raw enum string (`"not_requested"`, `"pending"`, `"complete"`, `"failed"`, `"manual"`) — this is a presentation/entry-constraint change only; it does not alter the column's existing SQL type, `CHECK` constraint, default value, or any of the values themselves, and does not alter which code path is permitted to write which value (FR-QPB-109's own `"complete"`/`"manual"` persistence rules, Decision Log D-38/D-43/D-50/D-51, are unaffected). The exact `ValueMap` dict key/display-label orientation is left as an implementation detail, mirroring how the existing `organ` `ValueMap`'s own internal dict shape is not specification-dictated either.

  **What this deliberately does not decide (flagged, not silently assumed — new Open Question O-33).** The stakeholder's instruction asks only that the field become a constrained selection instead of free text; it says nothing about display language. This specification's existing Korean-localization requirements do not, on their own terms, extend to this: NFR-QPB-070 (Decision Log D-28) is explicitly scoped only to "this application's own PySide6 desktop wizard UI," not the generated project's own QGIS/QField form content; and Section 8.5/DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119 (Decision Log D-56–D-58) governs only field *labels* (aliases), explicitly declining to govern enum *value* display. Whether the institute also wants each of the five `identification_status` values shown with a Korean-language display label in the dropdown (the existing `organ` `ValueMap` precedent uses identical English keys and values, `{v: v}`, so there is no existing in-repo precedent for a Korean-labeled `ValueMap` to follow either way) is therefore a genuinely open, unaddressed question, not something this entry assumes. This entry's own draft proposal, absent further instruction, keeps the dropdown's displayed option text as the existing raw English enum strings, unchanged from what technically already appears today — flagged explicitly as an assumption pending confirmation, not a decision.

  **Approval status: ~~DRAFT. Not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder.~~ CONFIRMED (2026-08-26) — the stakeholder confirmed this entry's own drafted proposal (constrain to a fixed-list widget; keep the existing raw English enum strings as displayed values, no Korean value-label translation) exactly as written; see new Decision Log D-69, which closes Open Question O-33.** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-122/AC-QPB-103.

The six entries below (D-64–D-69), all dated 2026-08-26, close Open Questions O-23–O-33, raised by Decision Log D-60–D-63 above.
