Each traces to an explicit stakeholder answer (a direct quote where one was given verbatim, or the orchestrator's own confirmed technical research where the stakeholder's decision was made in light of that research — each distinguished explicitly below, matching this project's existing D-37/D-46/D-49/D-50/D-52 convention). None of D-64–D-69 reopens, rewords, or renumbers D-1–D-63 or any existing FR/DR/NFR/AC; every revision below is a non-destructive strikethrough-and-annotation, mirroring D-40's superseding pattern where substance changes and D-42's pure-confirmation pattern where it does not.

- **D-64** (Category C — closes Open Question O-23 by confirming Decision Log D-60's own drafted proposal exactly as written; pure confirmation, not a reversal; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-63 above):

  The stakeholder confirmed Decision Log D-60's own drafted proposal exactly as written: the standardized `taxon_full_nm`-derived scientific name (Section 13.4/13.7, FR-QPB-106 (revised)/FR-QPB-109 (further revised)) is used for candidate-card display and for the value persisted to `selected_scientific_name` on selection only when some KTSN match exists for that candidate — an accepted match (`accepted_scientific_name`) or a direct match (`direct_scientific_name`), in that order of preference. When a Pl@ntNet candidate has no KTSN match at all, the existing fallback is **completely unchanged by this entry**: Pl@ntNet's own raw `species.scientificName` continues to be displayed/persisted, together with the existing "KTSN match not found" disclosure. This confirms, and does not reopen or reword, FR-QPB-106 (revised; Decision Log D-60)/FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-60)/AC-QPB-099 exactly as those entries already stated it; no requirement text changes in substance as a result of this entry — only the "draft, not yet stakeholder-approved" qualifier on each is removed, per the annotations above.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Closes Open Question O-23 (Section 20).

- **D-65** (Category C — closes Open Questions O-24–O-27, confirming and completing Decision Log D-61's symbol-styling/Tabler-icon feature; includes orchestrator-confirmed technical research into Tabler Icons' own distribution/licensing mechanism, distinct in kind from the stakeholder's own product decisions that follow it, mirroring Decision Log D-24/D-46's own "confirmed technical finding, distinct from a stakeholder product decision" framing; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-64 above):

  **Confirmed technical finding (orchestrator research, not a stakeholder decision; grounds the decisions below).** Tabler Icons' actual, current access mechanism was independently confirmed: source `github.com/tabler/tabler-icons` (the official repository), MIT license, confirmed directly from the source — no attribution is legally required; `tabler.io/icons` and `docs.tabler.io/icons/static-files/svg` confirm the icons are distributed as free, static SVG files with instant export, requiring no sign-up or API key of any kind to search or download. No official, machine-readable, live search API exists: the search UI at tabler.io is a client-side filter applied to the complete, static icon-name list, not a server-side search endpoint. This confirms and narrows Open Question O-24(a)'s two candidate mechanisms in favor of the static-index option, and directly answers O-24(b) (MIT, no attribution required) without needing the "commonly understood, but not freshly reverified" hedge Decision Log D-61 originally recorded.

  **The stakeholder's explicit sign-off, closing O-24(a)–(d) together:**
  - **(a) Network mechanism:** a static index of all Tabler icon names (~6,184, at time of research) is bundled with the desktop application itself at build time, giving instant, fully offline search-as-you-type in the wizard's icon picker. The actual SVG content for a specific icon is fetched from Tabler's public source only on demand, at the moment the user selects that specific icon — network access is required only at that point, never for searching.
  - **(b) License/attribution:** MIT license; no attribution disclosure is required anywhere in the generated project.
  - **(c) Offline behavior:** unchanged from Decision Log D-61's own original proposal — the minimalist default point symbol (FR-QPB-120) remains fully usable with zero network access at all times, regardless of whether the Tabler feature is reachable, mirroring NFR-QPB-060(4)'s existing drawing-canvas offline discipline.
  - **(d) Embedding:** a downloaded icon's SVG file must be embedded into the generated project's own output folder, referenced by a project-relative path (mirroring FR-QPB-091/DR-QPB-012's existing portability discipline) — not merely a desktop-application-only convenience — because QField itself needs the actual SVG file on-device to render the point symbol in the field.

  **FR-QPB-011 (further revised; this entry): a fourth network-access clause.** All rules from FR-QPB-011 (revised; Decision Log D-24) above — clauses (a)/(b)/(c) and the general MVP framing — remain correct and are restated here, unchanged in substance. ~~The purely additive cross-reference note appended by Decision Log D-61 above ("a proposed new network destination... is under consideration and is explicitly not yet an approved exception")~~ — **superseded, not deleted: the Tabler network destination is now an approved exception, per this entry.** A new clause **(d)** is added: fetching a single, specifically selected Tabler icon's SVG file, from Tabler's public source, strictly and only when the user has already selected that icon by name from the offline, build-time-bundled static icon-name index described above (FR-QPB-121, revised, immediately below) — this clause never authorizes any other Tabler network request (in particular, no live search/autocomplete request against any Tabler endpoint; searching is always offline). The closing sentence "No other network access is permitted in the MVP" now means: no network access beyond clauses (a)–(d).

  **FR-QPB-120 (revised; this entry; closes O-25/O-26): confirmed minimalist definition and per-survey-type scope.** All rules from FR-QPB-120 (Decision Log D-61) above remain correct; the following is now stated as confirmed requirement text rather than an open proposal. "Minimalist" concretely means: for every polygon layer (excluding the Type 4 `community` layer, unaffected, DR-QPB-051), a single flat fill color plus a thin, contrasting outline; for every point layer, a small, solid circle marker. No gradient, pattern, label callout, or per-category color-coding is applied by default. **Scope (closes O-26; stakeholder's verbatim reasoning: "because we can define the number of layers and types of layers only after determining survey type"):** styling is decided once per generated project, as a whole, at the point in the wizard where that project's survey type (and therefore its full layer set) is already known (Step 2, FR-QPB-023) — never before. Within one generated project, the resulting choice (the minimalist default, or a selected Tabler icon per FR-QPB-121) applies uniformly to **every** point layer of that project and, separately, uniformly to **every** polygon layer of that project — never a different style per individual layer within the same project. Styling is **not** a global, cross-survey-type, cross-project default: it is not persisted or reused automatically for a later, separately generated project, even of the same survey type — each generated project's build makes this choice fresh.

  **FR-QPB-121 (revised; this entry; closes remainder of O-24): confirmed Tabler search/download mechanism.** For point layers specifically, the wizard must let the user search, by name/keyword, the offline, build-time-bundled static index of Tabler icon names described above, with results filtered live as the user types (a simple client-side substring/prefix filter over the bundled name list — no network request). Upon selecting one icon, the application must fetch that icon's SVG content from Tabler's public source (the one network request this feature ever makes, per FR-QPB-011(d) above), and, on success, use it as the point-marker symbol for **every** point layer of the generated project (FR-QPB-120's per-survey-type/not-per-layer scope, above), replacing the minimalist default marker for that project, and embed the downloaded SVG file into the generated project's own output folder (e.g. a new `symbols/` subfolder of the project root), referenced only by a project-relative path from the `.qgs` symbol definition — never an absolute path, and never a path outside the generated project's own folder tree (FR-QPB-091/DR-QPB-012). If the fetch fails (no network, non-200 response, timeout) or the user does not select an icon, the minimalist default (FR-QPB-120) remains the project's point-marker symbol and project generation is not blocked.

  **NFR-QPB-080 (revised; this entry): confirmed safeguards, attribution clause removed.** All rules from NFR-QPB-080 (Decision Log D-61) above remain correct in kind, restated here as confirmed rather than provisional, with one removal: (1) the single SVG-fetch request permitted by FR-QPB-011(d) must carry a compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header; (2) that request must not retry automatically in an unbounded loop on failure — one attempt per user selection, surfaced as a clear, non-blocking failure to the user on error, per FR-QPB-121 above; ~~(3) a permanently visible attribution/license notice for the Tabler Icons project must be shown wherever a downloaded Tabler icon is actually used as a symbol~~ — **removed, not merely struck: per the confirmed technical finding above (MIT license, no attribution legally required) and the stakeholder's explicit sign-off to O-24(b), no attribution/license notice is required anywhere in the generated project or this application's own UI for a used Tabler icon.** (4) the minimalist default styling (FR-QPB-120) must remain fully available and usable with zero network access at all times, unaffected by whether the Tabler feature is reachable — unchanged.

  **New FR-QPB-123 (new; this entry; closes O-27): a new wizard Step 6.** The wizard must present a new step — **Step 6, "Symbol styling configuration"** — inserted immediately after the existing Step 5 (optional photo identification toggle, Section 6.5) and immediately before the existing Step 6 (renumbered **Step 7**, "Review and build," FR-QPB-040/FR-QPB-041, Section 6.6, renumbered Section 6.7 below), per the stakeholder's explicit choice of option (a) from Decision Log D-61's own Open Question O-27. At this step, for the survey type already selected at Step 2 (FR-QPB-023), the wizard must let the user: accept the minimalist default point/polygon styling (FR-QPB-120) with no further action, or search for and select one Tabler SVG icon (FR-QPB-121) to replace the default point-marker symbol for every point layer of the project being generated. ~~The wizard must present the following six steps in order, matching the Requirements Draft.~~ — **superseded, not deleted, by this entry: the wizard now presents seven steps in order — the original six (Section 6.1–6.5, and the renumbered Section 6.7) plus this entry's new Step 6 (Section 6.6) — the first five of which, plus the renumbered seventh, trace to the Requirements Draft exactly as before; the new sixth step (this entry) does not; the originally-sixth, now-seventh step (Review and build) is unaffected in its own substance, only its position/number.**

  New AC-QPB-104 (Section 18.5) makes the new wizard step and its per-project (not per-layer, not global) styling scope independently testable. AC-QPB-100/AC-QPB-101/AC-QPB-102 (Section 18.2) are each revised (draft flag removed; substance updated to match the confirmed mechanism above).

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-011 (further revised)/FR-QPB-120 (revised)/FR-QPB-121 (revised)/FR-QPB-123 (new)/NFR-QPB-080 (revised)/AC-QPB-100–AC-QPB-102 (revised)/AC-QPB-104 (new). Closes Open Questions O-24, O-25, O-26, O-27 (Section 20).

- **D-66** (Category C — closes Open Questions O-28, O-29, and O-32, resolving Decision Log D-62's central architecture choice and this feature's field/survey-type scope; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-65 above):

  **The stakeholder's explicit answer to O-28 (verbatim, as reported by the orchestrator): Option 1** — a native QGIS `ValueRelation`/`RelationReference` widget backed by a real, bundled lookup table, **not** Option 2 (a custom `QML Widget` mirroring the Pl@ntNet identification architecture). This is the central decision this feature's entire architecture now follows; Decision Log D-62's own investigation record and both candidate options remain unaltered above, for the historical record — this entry does not reopen or reword them, it selects between them.

  **The stakeholder's explicit answer to O-29 (verbatim, as reported by the orchestrator):** scope is exactly `selected_korean_name`/`selected_scientific_name` — and, by the stakeholder's own original instruction's "automatically populate the corresponding scientific name **and KTSN**," `selected_ktsn` as well (Types 1–3, Section 8.1–8.3) — the fields the stakeholder's original instruction explicitly named or directly implied. `dominant_species` (Type 4 `community`, Section 8.4) is **explicitly out of scope**; DR-QPB-050's existing exclusion of Type 4 from the Types 1–3 identification-field set is confirmed unaffected and is not extended by this feature.

  **New DR-QPB-072 (Section 7; new; closes O-32 together with the FR below): a real, indexed, bundled lookup table.** Every generated project for Types 1–3 must bundle a real, queryable, indexed database table — the "KTSN accepted-name lookup table" — containing at minimum the Korean name, scientific name, and KTSN identifier of every currently accepted (non-synonym) taxon (its exact row-derivation rule is stated by new FR-QPB-126, Decision Log D-67, below). This table must be added as an additional non-spatial table inside the generated project's own existing survey `.gpkg` file — **not** a second `.gpkg` file, preserving DR-QPB-007's existing "one local `.gpkg` file per generated project" rule — and must be loaded into the generated project's `.qgs` file as the first layer to actually populate the pre-existing, previously-always-empty "Reference" layer-tree group (FR-QPB-055), configured non-identifiable and read-only where appropriate, per FR-QPB-059's existing "Reference/extent layers" convention. **Closes O-32:** "structure it to support indexing for efficient searches" means a literal, real, build-time `CREATE INDEX` statement on this table's own Korean-name and scientific-name columns — mirroring DR-QPB-009's already-established "ordinary indexes must exist on... commonly searched name fields" convention — **not** the in-memory JavaScript index technique (`nameIndex`/`ktsnIndex`, `qpbLoadCsv`) this codebase already uses for the Pl@ntNet identification widget, which was relevant only to the now-rejected Option 2. This table is reference/lookup data, not a domain survey entity in DR-QPB-001's sense; its own key column is the source data's own natural `ktsn` identifier, not a newly generated UUID, and DR-QPB-001's UUID-identifier rule does not apply to it.

  **New FR-QPB-124 (Section 9; new): `ValueRelation` widget for `selected_korean_name`.** `selected_korean_name` (Types 1–3 only, per O-29 above) must be configured with a native QGIS `ValueRelation` editor widget referencing the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072), configured for a filterable, typeahead selection experience using QGIS's own `ValueRelation` "use completer"/filter-expression configuration, so the user can type to filter candidates rather than scrolling a flat list; where QGIS's widget configuration allows it, the number of simultaneously displayed matches should be capped at five, matching the stakeholder's original instruction. **Disclosed technical-feasibility caveat, mirroring FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-36's own "plausible, not yet confirmed" pattern:** whether QGIS's/QField's actual `ValueRelation` widget implementation supports a live, as-you-type filter capped at exactly five displayed results — as distinct from a filterable dropdown showing more than five, or a dropdown that filters but is not capped — is **not independently verified** by this specification (Decision Log D-62's own investigation finding 4(a); this spec-writer round has no live-research tool available to it, mirroring D-62's own disclosed limitation). The stakeholder's confirmed choice of Option 1 (above) is a decision to proceed with this architecture despite that uncertainty, not a confirmation that the exact five-result cap is achievable; verifying and, if necessary, adjusting the display-count behavior to whatever QGIS's real widget configuration actually supports is implementer work to report back, exactly as FR-QPB-111's on-device-raster-sampling caveat was handled. The value written to `selected_korean_name` on selection is the plain Korean-name text itself (the `ValueRelation` widget's configured "Value" column) — **this is a constrained-value-selection widget, not a true relational foreign key** in the DR-QPB-006/FR-QPB-056 sense: no GeoPackage-level foreign-key constraint and no QGIS project relation is created for it, mirroring how the existing `organ` `ValueMap` widget (FR-QPB-057) likewise constrains entry without creating a relation.

  Section 8.1/8.2/8.3's `selected_korean_name` field-table entries receive a purely additive cross-reference note (their existing "active in MVP" substance unchanged — only the entry mechanism changes, from free text to a constrained `ValueRelation` selection).

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against new DR-QPB-072/FR-QPB-124. Closes Open Questions O-28, O-29, and O-32 (Section 20).

- **D-67** (Category C, with confirmed technical findings that are distinct in kind from the stakeholder's own product decisions, mirroring Decision Log D-37/D-46/D-49/D-50's "confirmed technical finding, distinct from a stakeholder product decision" framing — closes Open Question O-30, the most architecturally consequential item in this round; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-66 above):

  **Confirmed technical findings (orchestrator research, not stakeholder decisions; ground the decisions below).**
  1. QGIS's native default-value mechanism supports an `applyOnUpdate` flag (`QgsDefaultValue.applyOnUpdate`; confirmed via the QGIS API reference, `api.qgis.org/api/3.0/classQgsDefaultValue.html` and `qgis.org/pyqgis/master/core/QgsDefaultValue.html`): when set, a field's default-value expression is re-applied **whenever the feature is updated, not only when it is first created**. QField's own documentation confirms this "live" behavior is explicitly supported when editing features (`docs.qfield.org/how-to/advanced-how-tos/live-default-value/`, "Live default value," toggled via "apply default upon update" in the layer's Attributes Form configuration, with a worked example of one field's value driving another field's auto-calculated value). **This mechanism is materially different from, and better suited to this problem than, the custom `QML Widget`/pending-request-file write-back mechanism Decision Log D-50 found permanently limited to a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature only: because `applyOnUpdate` operates through QGIS/QField's own standard attribute-form editing machinery — not a custom external write-back hack — it is not subject to D-50's brand-new-feature-only limitation. It works identically for a brand-new feature and for an existing, already-saved feature reopened later**, unlike every write-back mechanism this specification has examined for the Pl@ntNet candidate-selection case (Decision Log D-36→D-50→D-51).
  2. The same QGIS documentation is explicit that once a field's `applyOnUpdate` default-value expression is active, "any user input will be overwritten by the default value" — that field becomes effectively non-manually-editable while the mechanism is active on it. A field cannot simultaneously (a) be the field a default-value expression writes into, and (b) remain independently, manually typeable by the user. This is a genuine, confirmed constraint on any design that tries to make two fields mutually auto-populate each other bidirectionally.
  3. QField does not support Python: confirmed via QField's own attribute-form documentation (`docs.qfield.org/how-to/project-setup/attributes-form/`) and discussion (`github.com/opengisch/QField/discussions/3448`, "Form with python script in QField") — Python form-init scripts are a QGIS-Desktop-only capability, not available in QField at all. This rules out any Python-scripted "detect a synonym on entry, silently replace it, and show the user a popup notification" mechanism as achievable in QField specifically — the mechanism the stakeholder's original instruction literally described.

  **The stakeholder's explicit design decisions, given directly in response to these findings:**
  1. **One-way autofill only, not bidirectional.** When a Korean name is entered/selected, the corresponding scientific name and KTSN are automatically populated. The reverse (typing a scientific name auto-filling the Korean name) is explicitly **not** required. This resolves finding 2's `applyOnUpdate`-lock conflict cleanly, since only one field (the Korean name) needs to remain independently user-editable/selectable.
  2. **`selected_korean_name` is the single entry point; `selected_scientific_name` and `selected_ktsn` become fully derived, read-only fields.** The stakeholder's exact words, confirming this design: **"Please implement only one-way autofill: when a Korean name is entered, automatically populate the corresponding scientific name."** — with the KTSN-also-derived and scientific-name-becomes-read-only consequences confirmed via an explicit follow-up choice presented as "Fully derived, read-only (Recommended)" against the alternative "scientific name stays independently editable," which the stakeholder selected.
  3. **Synonym/original-combination handling: "Filter synonyms out of the dropdown."** Given the confirmed no-Python-in-QField constraint (finding 3), the stakeholder's explicit choice was to prevent the situation from ever arising, not to detect-and-fix it after the fact: the Korean-name `ValueRelation`'s underlying lookup table (DR-QPB-072) is filtered, at the source-data level, to include **only accepted/canonical names** to begin with, so a synonym or original-combination name can never be selected via this dropdown in the first place. No replace-after-the-fact logic and no popup notification are required or should be built. This is a deliberate, accepted narrowing of the originally-requested UX (the stakeholder's original instruction described a "replace and notify" flow; the now-confirmed design instead prevents the situation from arising at all) — and, unlike Decision Log D-46's disclosed QField-vs-Desktop tradeoff, this design is fully native and platform-uniform: identical behavior in QField and QGIS Desktop, with no platform-scope gap to disclose here.

  **Investigation into whether the existing reference-data pipeline already produces an accepted/canonical flag (per this round's specific instruction to check before inventing a new concept).** It does. `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`'s own `taxon_jm_nm` column is already, by this specification's own long-established and approved rule (Decision Log D-4/15b, restated unchanged through Decision Log D-40/D-47/D-48), the row's nomenclatural-status field: **`taxon_jm_nm == '정명'` means the row is itself the accepted KTSN record** (FR-QPB-107, further revised). A row that is a synonym or original combination does not carry `taxon_jm_nm == '정명'` — instead, per the same already-approved rule, it carries a `correct_list` pointing to a *different* row's KTSN, which is itself the `정명` row. This means the accepted/canonical flag this feature needs already exists, unambiguously, as a single, already-defined column-and-literal-value check on data this specification already bundles — **no new, unrelated concept is invented by this entry**; filtering to `taxon_jm_nm == '정명'` is the accepted-only filter.

  **New FR-QPB-125 (Section 9; new): derived, read-only `selected_scientific_name`/`selected_ktsn`.** For Types 1–3 (per Decision Log D-66/O-29), `selected_scientific_name` and `selected_ktsn` must each be configured with a `QgsDefaultValue` expression that has `applyOnUpdate = true` (finding 1 above; QField's "apply default upon update"), referencing `selected_korean_name`'s current value to look up, in the bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072), that row's own scientific name (for `selected_scientific_name`) and KTSN identifier (for `selected_ktsn`). Both fields' own editor widgets must be configured non-editable (read-only) — consistent with finding 2's confirmed "cannot simultaneously auto-populate and remain independently typeable" constraint, and consistent with the stakeholder's own confirmed "fully derived, read-only" choice above. This works identically for a brand-new feature and for an existing, already-saved feature reopened later (finding 1's confirmed distinction from Decision Log D-50's brand-new-feature-only limitation) — selecting or changing `selected_korean_name` at any time re-derives both fields via QGIS's/QField's own standard live-default-value re-evaluation, with no custom write-back mechanism, pending-request file, or project-plugin polling required.

  **New FR-QPB-126 (Section 9; new; states DR-QPB-072's own row-derivation/filtering rule): accepted-only lookup-table content.** The bundled accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) must be derived, at build time, as follows: (1) reuse the same deterministic, build-time-only Steps 1–4 row-filtering computation FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-48) already defines (Plantae-kingdom-subtree filter; species-level-and-below rank filter; vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist filter; duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution) — as a shared, reusable computation, invoked regardless of whether `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` output itself is written for a given build (see new FR-QPB-127, Decision Log D-68, for this table's own, decoupled trigger condition); then (2) apply one additional, new filter — **Step 5** — keeping only rows whose `taxon_jm_nm` value is exactly `정명` (the confirmed accepted/canonical flag identified above), and excluding every row for which it is not, including a row with a missing/blank `taxon_jm_nm` value (fails the `정명` test; matches this pipeline's existing exclude-on-ambiguity posture, Decision Log D-48). The resulting table's columns are, at minimum, `ktsn`, `taxon_kor_nm` (Korean name), and `taxon_full_nm` with `<em>`/`</em>` tags removed (scientific name, mirroring FR-QPB-106/FR-QPB-107's existing tag-stripping rule) — the same normalization already applied elsewhere in this specification, not a new one. **Row count is not asserted by this entry**: no orchestrator-verified count exists for this new Step 5 filter (unlike Steps 1–4, each of which Decision Log D-47/D-48 verified against the real reference CSV) — this is honestly recorded as **unconfirmed, requiring a build-time measurement** once implemented, per NFR-QPB-001's no-invented-numbers discipline, rather than estimated here.

  Section 8.1/8.2/8.3's `selected_scientific_name` field-table entries are revised (original "final user-selected/entered scientific name; active in MVP for manual entry" text retained, struck through, marked superseded for Types 1–3): direct manual free-text entry into `selected_scientific_name` is no longer possible once this feature is present — the field is now fully derived per FR-QPB-125. Section 8.1's `selected_ktsn` entry (and the equivalent Type 2/3 prose) is likewise revised (original "reserved; nullable/inactive until post-MVP identification subsystem ships" text retained, struck through, marked superseded): `selected_ktsn` is no longer inactive-until-post-MVP — it becomes an active, auto-derived field as soon as `selected_korean_name` is selected, independent of the post-MVP identification subsystem's own toggle (this is the same independence Decision Log D-68/O-31 confirms below; the two entries are complementary, not redundant — this entry changes *what* is derived and *how*, D-68 changes *when/whether it is bundled at all*).

  New AC-QPB-105 (Section 18.2) makes FR-QPB-124's `ValueRelation` configuration independently testable; new AC-QPB-106 (Section 18.1) makes DR-QPB-072's build-time index independently testable; new AC-QPB-107 (Section 18.2) makes FR-QPB-125's derived-read-only-field behavior and FR-QPB-126's accepted-only-filtering (no synonym ever selectable) independently testable, for both a brand-new and an already-saved/reopened feature, per finding 1's confirmed distinction.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against new FR-QPB-125/FR-QPB-126. Closes Open Question O-30 (Section 20).

- **D-68** (Category C — closes Open Question O-31, decoupling this feature from the post-MVP identification subsystem's own enablement toggle; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-67 above):

  **The stakeholder's explicit answer (verbatim, as reported by the orchestrator): "should be work even when Pl@ntNet identification is disabled. This function is independent."** The Korean-name/scientific-name/KTSN dropdown-and-autofill feature (DR-QPB-072/FR-QPB-124/FR-QPB-125/FR-QPB-126, Decision Log D-66/D-67), and the accepted-name lookup table it depends on, must be present and functional in **every** generated project for Types 1–3, regardless of whether `identification_enabled` (FR-QPB-037–039) is true or false. It is **not** gated behind the post-MVP identification subsystem's own toggle.

  **What this does and does not change.** This entry does **not** make FR-QPB-112 (revised; Decision Log D-47)'s own ~247 MB combined `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv`-plus-probability-raster bundling rule unconditional — that rule, and its existing `identification_enabled`-gated trigger, are confirmed **unaffected** and remain exactly as Decision Log D-47 left them; the probability rasters in particular are of no use to this feature and are not implicated by this entry at all. What this entry does is decouple only this new, much smaller feature's own bundling from that same toggle: **new FR-QPB-127** (Section 9; new) requires that, for every Types 1–3 generated project, the accepted-name lookup table (DR-QPB-072) and its build-time row-derivation (FR-QPB-126) must always run and always be bundled — independent of `identification_enabled` — reusing FR-QPB-105's existing source-CSV-presence/required-column validation and fail-early discipline, now applying to every Types 1–3 project build, not only identification-enabled ones (FR-QPB-105 receives a purely additive cross-reference note to this effect; its own substantive validation rule is unchanged). Decision Log D-44's confirmation that the *distributed packaged application's* own build always bundles the complete `storage/reference/` tree, regardless of any per-project toggle, is confirmed unaffected and is what makes this decoupling possible without any packaging change.

  **Honest, unconfirmed size disclosure (per this round's explicit instruction not to invent a figure).** No precise size figure exists anywhere in this specification's Decision Log for `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` itself (the 5-column, post-Decision-Log-D-48-filtering extraction) independent of the probability rasters — only the ~247 MB *combined* figure (Decision Log D-35, covering both the CSV and the rasters together) and the 183 MB *raw, unextracted* source-CSV figure (Decision Log D-47) are recorded anywhere in this document. The new accepted-name lookup table this entry makes unconditional is smaller still than `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` (a `taxon_jm_nm == '정명'`-filtered subset of it, per FR-QPB-126), and is very likely small in absolute terms — but this specification does not invent a number for it, consistent with NFR-QPB-001's discipline. This is recorded as an **unconfirmed figure requiring a build-time measurement**, not asserted as safe or risky either way; Open Question O-17's existing "not itself a size/transfer-risk concern" assessment (Decision Log D-41) was made about a different, unrelated extracted file (the NIBR `KTSN`-column-only list, FR-QPB-113) and is not extended by this entry to cover this new table.

  New AC-QPB-108 (Section 18.2) makes the unconditional presence/functionality of this feature — regardless of `identification_enabled` — independently testable.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against new FR-QPB-127. Closes Open Question O-31 (Section 20).

- **D-69** (Category C — closes Open Question O-33 by confirming Decision Log D-63's own drafted proposal exactly as written; pure confirmation, not a reversal; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-68 above):

  The stakeholder's explicit answer (verbatim, as reported by the orchestrator): **"not_requested/pending/complete/failed/manual"** — the `identification_status` `ValueMap` dropdown's displayed option text keeps the existing English enum strings as its values, with no Korean-language value-label translation required. This matches the existing `organ` `ValueMap` widget's own precedent in this codebase (identical English keys/values, `{v: v}`). This confirms, and does not reopen or reword, FR-QPB-122 (Decision Log D-63)'s own already-drafted assumption exactly as written; no requirement text changes in substance as a result of this entry — only the "draft, not yet stakeholder-approved" qualifier is removed, per the annotation above.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-26).** Closes Open Question O-33 (Section 20).

- **D-70** (Category B — closes a genuine specification gap a `test-designer` round found and explicitly reported while writing acceptance tests for Decision Log D-64–D-69/FR-QPB-124–127; closes new Open Question O-34, raised and closed within this same round; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-69 above):

  A `test-designer` round building acceptance tests for the Korean-name/scientific-name/KTSN lookup-table feature (Decision Log D-64–D-69) found, and correctly reported rather than silently resolved, a genuine environment-dependency gap that new FR-QPB-127/Decision Log D-68 created. The full finding is recorded verbatim in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder_ktsn_lookup_table.traceability.md`'s "Flagged interaction with this suite's own shared fixture defaults" section and the identical note in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`; summarized here: FR-QPB-126's accepted-name lookup-table derivation reuses FR-QPB-118's existing Steps 1–4 row-filtering pipeline, which reads the **raw** KTSN reference CSV (`storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv`, ~183 MB) and the NIBR xlsx directly — not a precomputed/cached file. FR-QPB-105's existing fail-early validation for this raw source data was, at the time of that round, scoped to trigger "only when the identification subsystem is enabled." Because FR-QPB-127 requires the lookup table's derivation to run **unconditionally** for every Types 1–3 build, this raw source data effectively needed to be present for every such build, not only identification-enabled ones — but this specification had never stated whether that is actually the intended operational precondition, and the raw data itself is excluded from version control (`.gitignore`'s "Runtime data under `storage/`: reference datasets, user uploads, work-in-progress" entry). That round correctly declined to guess and routed the question back through `spec-writer`, per this project's own change-control discipline; it also confirmed its own new tests do not depend on the ambiguity either way (each passes an explicit `_test_reference_data_dir` override) and that no existing shared fixture default was changed by that round.

  **Two orchestrator-verified facts, cited here as confirmed ground truth (not independently re-verified by this spec-writer round):** (1) `qfield_builder/reference_bundle.py` (its own module docstring, plus `_extract_ktsn_lookup_csv` and the five-step pipeline) confirms `reference/ktsn_lookup.csv` is derived fresh, from the raw source CSV, at every project-build time — it is not a precomputed, checked-in artifact. (2) `storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` (the raw 183 MB source file) exists on the orchestrator's own local development machine but is excluded from version control by `.gitignore` (confirmed via direct inspection of `.gitignore`'s "Runtime data under `storage/`..." entry) — it is not part of this repository and is not guaranteed present in a fresh clone or a CI environment.

  Given these facts, the stakeholder was presented with three options for what this actually means: **(a)** bundle the raw reference data into the repository/package itself so every environment always has it; **(b)** allow a Types 1–3 build to gracefully degrade when the raw source data is genuinely absent, relaxing FR-QPB-127's own "must always run and always be bundled" text; or **(c)** treat this as an accepted, already-established operational precondition (every environment that builds a Types 1–3 project, in development/CI or production, is expected to always have the reference-data scaffold present), mirroring Decision Log D-44's existing precedent, requiring only this test suite's own fixture housekeeping, not a specification change. **The stakeholder's explicit, final answer (verbatim, as reported by the orchestrator): "Use Option (c)."**

  **What this decision does and does not change.** This is confirmed as an accepted, known operational precondition: every environment that builds a Types 1–3 project — development, CI, or the distributed packaged application — is expected to have the raw reference-data scaffold (`storage/reference/`) present, exactly as Decision Log D-44 already established for the *distributed, packaged* application (which bundles the complete `storage/reference/` tree into every copy at packaging time). **FR-QPB-127's own requirement text is not relaxed or changed in substance by this resolution.** The only consequence is that this test suite's own **shared, pre-existing** fixtures (`make_base_config`/`built_project_by_type`/`isolated_project_by_type` in `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/conftest.py`, used by dozens of already-approved MVP acceptance tests) need to supply a small, synthetic reference-data override by default going forward, instead of relying on the real, gitignored `storage/reference/` scaffold being present on whatever machine runs the suite. This is `test-designer`/`implementer` housekeeping work for a future round; **this spec-writer round does not design or prescribe the exact fixture mechanics**, per the orchestrator's own explicit scoping of this task.

  FR-QPB-105 (Section 13.3) is revised (its Decision Log D-68 cross-reference sentence retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted) to state precisely that its fail-early validation now triggers on **either** of two independent conditions: `identification_enabled = true` (the original, unchanged trigger) **or** a Types 1–3 project being built at all (a new, independent, second trigger, per FR-QPB-127) — this is not a stricter validation rule in any new respect, only a second, independent condition under which the same, completely unchanged CSV-presence/required-column/encoding/JSON-validation checks are triggered. FR-QPB-112 (Section 13.3) receives a purely additive clarifying cross-reference confirming its own, separate ~247 MB combined bundle remains conditional on `identification_enabled`, unaffected by this entry — FR-QPB-112's own substance is unchanged. New AC-QPB-109 (Section 18.2) makes the new trigger condition independently testable.

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file. The shared-fixture-default change Option (c) itself calls for is explicitly out of scope for this spec-writer round and is left to a future `test-designer`/`implementer` round.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-27).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-105 (further revised)/AC-QPB-109; the shared-fixture housekeeping Option (c) itself requires is a separate, future `test-designer`/`implementer` task, not authorized or performed by this entry. Closes Open Question O-34 (Section 20).

- **D-71** (Category B — closes a specification omission regarding the three required layer-tree groups' own stacking/rendering order, found via the stakeholder's real manual testing of the built application; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-70 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction**, given directly in response to observing this defect on a real device: **"Basemap MUST be the last layer in layer order."**

  **The confirmed real defect this corrects.** FR-QPB-055 (original) required only that layers be grouped into `Survey data`, `Basemap`, and `Reference` groups — it never stated any required order among the three groups. In QGIS, layer-tree order is also rendering (z-)order: a layer/group listed higher (earlier) in the tree renders on top of (in front of) one listed lower (later). The orchestrator independently confirmed, via direct code reading, the current implementation: `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_add_reference_and_basemap_groups(project)` calls `root.addGroup("Basemap")` then `root.addGroup("Reference")`, both **before** `_add_domain_layers()` (called immediately after) adds `"Survey data"`. Because `QgsLayerTreeGroup.addGroup()` appends to the end of the parent's existing children, `"Basemap"` ends up as the very first (topmost) group in the tree, meaning it currently renders **on top of** both `"Survey data"` and `"Reference"` — the opposite of standard, usable GIS layer-tree convention, where a basemap must be the bottom-most group so the actual working survey data remains visible above it. This is recorded here as a specification omission (Category B), not as a Category A implementation defect to fix in code alone: the approved specification itself never told the implementer what order was required, so the existing code cannot be said to have violated an already-approved requirement — it simply implemented an unconstrained requirement in the one order that happens to be unusable.

  **Resolution.** FR-QPB-055 is revised (original text retained and extended in place, not struck through — a purely additive clarification, since the original sentence's own meaning, "the three groups must exist," remains true and unchanged) to state precisely, and independently-testably, that `Basemap` must be the last of the three groups by its own children-index within the root layer tree, and that this single children-index governs on-screen tree position, "last added"/list order, and rendering (z-)order together, so no future role is left to guess between those readings. See FR-QPB-055 (revised) above. New **AC-QPB-110** (Section 18.2) makes this independently testable against a generated project's `.qgs` file. This entry does not state, and does not resolve, any relative order between `Survey data` and `Reference` — the stakeholder's instruction addressed only `Basemap`'s position, and no other approved requirement in this specification (including DR-QPB-072's "Reference" layer-tree-group population text) states one either; that relative order remains unconstrained by this specification.

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file. The actual code fix to `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_add_reference_and_basemap_groups`/`_add_domain_layers` call order is `test-designer`/`implementer` work for a future round, now unblocked by this clarified requirement — it is not performed by this spec-writer round.

  **Approval status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-27).** Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may now proceed against FR-QPB-055 (revised)/AC-QPB-110.

The four entries below (D-72–D-75) are new, reconciling a rapid-fire, four-item feedback batch received in one session during real-device/UI testing of the built application (2026-08-28). Each item is independently classified per this project's own change-control discipline; items 1 and 2 are investigation/proposal records only (mirroring Decision Log D-61/D-62's precedent), items 3 and 4 trace to explicit stakeholder instructions and are recorded as decided.

- **D-72** (Category B/investigation — a genuine tension between an already-approved network-boundary requirement and a new stakeholder UX complaint, not yet resolved; mirrors Decision Log D-61/D-62's own "investigation record, not yet approved" precedent; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-71 above):

  **The stakeholder's direct report**, given during real-device/UI testing of Step 6's Tabler icon search results, quoted verbatim: **"Tabler에서 이미지를 검색할때 이미지 이름 뿐만 아니라 실제 이미지도 보여줘야 해"** ("When searching images in Tabler, it should show not just the image name but the actual image too") — prompted by seeing search results rendered as a plain list of names only (e.g. "flower", "flower-off"), confirmed by direct code reading: `SymbolStylingPage.results_list` (`qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py`) is a plain `QListWidget` populated only with the matched name strings returned by `search_bundled_tabler_icon_names()` (`qfield_builder/symbol_styling.py`) — no icon image of any kind is rendered in the results list today.

  **The real tension this report creates, not silently resolved here.** FR-QPB-011(d)/FR-QPB-121/NFR-QPB-080 (Decision Log D-65, already stakeholder-approved) permit exactly one network request per project build: fetching a single, already-selected icon's SVG, only *after* the user has chosen it by name from the offline, build-time-bundled name index (confirmed: `resources/tabler/icon_names.txt`, 5,130 names, no SVG content bundled at all — `qfield_builder/symbol_styling.py`'s own module docstring). FR-QPB-011(d)'s own text is explicit that this clause "never authorizes any live search/autocomplete network request against any Tabler endpoint." Showing a real image preview for every visible search result — as the stakeholder's report asks for — requires either fetching each visible result's SVG live during search (directly conflicting with the already-approved text above) or bundling actual SVG file *content*, not just names, so previews can render fully offline. Bundling actual SVG content for some or all of 5,130 icons is a materially larger, previously-undisclosed bundling commitment than the current name-only text file, and affects the packaged application's own size/build pipeline — Decision Log D-44's precedent (bundling `storage/reference/` into the packaged app, growing it from ~110 MB to ~379 MB) is the directly relevant prior reasoning for this class of tradeoff.

  **Investigation into a lower-cost middle ground: honestly inconclusive, not verified.** This spec-writer round has no live-research tool available to it (mirroring Decision Log D-61's own identical disclosure for its first Tabler investigation, later resolved by a subsequent round that did have research capability, per Decision Log D-65). Whether Tabler Icons' own repository (`github.com/tabler/tabler-icons`) offers a single, reasonably-sized combined asset (e.g. an SVG "sprite sheet," an icon font, or a similarly consolidated bundle covering many/all icons at once) that would let a search-result preview render offline without either the full-individual-file-bundling cost or a live per-result network fetch, is **not confirmed either way by this round** — recorded honestly as unconfirmed, not invented, per this document's own D-46/D-59 discipline for distinguishing confirmed facts from unconfirmed ones. If such a format exists and is a genuinely lower-cost option, it would need its own live verification (by the orchestrator or a future round with research tooling) before being presented as a real option with a known cost.

  **Four disclosed options, presented for the stakeholder's own explicit choice — none selected here:**
  - **(a) Status quo — name-only search results, no preview image.** Zero additional network access, zero additional bundling; does not address the stakeholder's report at all.
  - **(b) Live per-result SVG fetch during search** (e.g. fetching previews for the currently-visible/top-N filtered matches as the user types, debounced). Requires superseding FR-QPB-011(d)/NFR-QPB-080's already-approved "never authorizes any live search/autocomplete network request" text (a new Category C network-boundary decision, mirroring Decision Log D-24's OSM precedent for how such an exception gets disclosed and scoped) and reintroduces an always-online dependency for a feature Decision Log D-65 specifically designed to stay usable offline until the moment of final selection.
  - **(c) Bundle real SVG content for all (or a large subset of) the 5,130 bundled icon names**, so every/most search results can render a true offline preview with no additional network access at any point. Materially larger packaged-application size (Decision Log D-44 precedent); exact size impact not estimated here (would require knowing the SVGs' own total size, not established by this round).
  - **(d) Bundle a single, consolidated preview asset** (e.g. a combined sprite sheet/icon font/similar), if Tabler's own repository actually offers one at reasonable cost — **not confirmed to exist or to be practical by this round** (see "honestly inconclusive" paragraph above); if it does not exist in a workable form, this option collapses to (a) or (c).

  This entry adds no FR/DR/NFR/AC number of its own and changes no already-approved requirement text — new Open Question O-35 (Section 20) presents the stakeholder's choice among (a)–(d) above, mirroring Open Question O-24's own precedent (which disclosed a Tabler-mechanism uncertainty once before, in that case later resolved by a subsequent round).

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file.

  **Approval status: UNRESOLVED (investigation/proposal record only).** No `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against any preview-related Tabler-search behavior until the stakeholder has explicitly chosen among the options above (or a further-researched option not listed here). This does not affect the already-approved, unrelated FR-QPB-120/FR-QPB-121/FR-QPB-011(d) name-search-then-single-fetch-on-selection behavior, which is unchanged.

- **D-73** (Category B — closes a specification omission regarding the display name/label of an embedded relation widget, as distinct from an ordinary attribute-field alias; investigation plus a draft, not-yet-approved terminology proposal, mirroring Decision Log D-56's own precedent for how a first-round proposal is recorded before stakeholder confirmation; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-72 above):

  **The stakeholder's direct report**, quoted verbatim: **"Widget에 relation을 추가할 때 rel_observation_survey와 같은 이름으로 추가하지 말고 적절한 한국어 alias를 적용할 것"** ("When adding a relation to a widget, don't add it with a name like 'rel_observation_survey' — apply an appropriate Korean alias instead").

  **This is a genuine specification omission (Category B), not a reversal of anything approved.** DR-QPB-071/FR-QPB-119/Section 8.5 (Decision Log D-56–D-59) already establish that user-facing form elements must carry a Korean display name via QGIS's field-alias mechanism (`QgsVectorLayer.setFieldAlias`) — but that work covers only ordinary attribute *fields*. It says nothing about the separate `QgsAttributeEditorRelation` widget FR-QPB-056/FR-QPB-057 already require to be embedded in a parent record's own form to show its related child records (e.g. `site`'s form showing its child `survey` records).

  **Confirmed technical facts, from direct code reading (`qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`):** `_add_relations()` currently calls both `relation.setId(fk.relation_id)` and `relation.setName(fk.relation_id)` with the exact same raw string (e.g. `rel_observation_survey`) — the relation's own stable ID (required by FR-QPB-056, and by this document's own convention of never renaming an already-established ID) and its separate, human-facing "name" property are set to the identical value. `_build_drag_and_drop_form()` then embeds each parent's child relations via `QgsAttributeEditorRelation(relation, related_container)`, which is the mechanism the stakeholder's report reflects.

  **Disclosed, not-yet-independently-verified technical caveat, mirroring FR-QPB-111/FR-QPB-124's own "plausible, not confirmed" pattern:** whether the on-screen label QGIS/QField actually draws for an embedded `QgsAttributeEditorRelation` widget is drawn from `QgsRelation.name()` specifically (as opposed to some other override this specification has not identified) is not independently verified here — no live-research tool is available to this spec-writer round, mirroring Decision Log D-61's identical honest disclosure for its own initial Tabler investigation. This is recorded as the most plausible, code-grounded mechanism, not an asserted certainty; confirming it (and, if it turns out `QgsAttributeEditorElement.setName()`/an equivalent override is needed instead of, or in addition to, `QgsRelation.setName()`) is implementer verification work to report back, exactly as FR-QPB-111/D-36 already establish as this project's convention for this class of uncertainty.

  **Proposed resolution:** keep `QgsRelation.setId(fk.relation_id)` completely unchanged (the stable relation ID FR-QPB-056 requires, and the identifier `_identification_photo_paths_expression()`/`relation_aggregate()` calls already depend on by name, is untouched by this proposal). Change only the separate `QgsRelation.setName(...)` call (and/or whichever concrete mechanism implementer verification confirms actually drives the widget's displayed label) to a Korean-language display name instead of the raw relation ID string.

  New FR-QPB-128 (Section 9) states this requirement; new Section 8.6 records the draft, per-relation proposed Korean names (grounded in this specification's own already-confirmed Section 8.5 vocabulary for the child table each relation lists, but not itself independently confirmed, since a relation-widget group label is a different UI element from an ordinary field alias); new AC-QPB-111 (Section 18.2) makes the `id()`/`name()` split independently testable, separately from the disclosed rendering-mechanism caveat above. `rel_observation_photo_observation` is deliberately excluded from Section 8.6's proposal: Decision Log D-74 (this same round) removes the `observation_photo` table — and therefore this relation — entirely for Type 2/3, so a Korean name for it would immediately be moot. New Open Question O-36 (Section 20) consolidates the seven proposed terms for explicit stakeholder confirmation or correction.

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file.

  **Approval status: ~~DRAFT. Not yet reviewed or approved by the stakeholder.~~ CONFIRMED (2026-08-28) — the stakeholder has explicitly confirmed six of the seven proposed relation names exactly as proposed and corrected the seventh (`rel_observation_survey`: "관찰" → "식물관찰"); see new Decision Log D-77 immediately below.** No `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against FR-QPB-128/Section 8.6/AC-QPB-111 until the stakeholder has confirmed or corrected the proposed Korean relation names (Open Question O-36) — **this condition is now satisfied; see Decision Log D-77.**

- **D-74** (Category C — a stakeholder-approved product/schema change superseding Decision Log D-16/D-23's existing scope for Type 2/3's `observation` table specifically; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-73 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction**, given during real-device/UI testing: **"조사유형 2에서 Observation별로 추가하는 사진을 observation_photo에 별도 저장하지 않고 조사유형 1의 inventory_observation처럼 observation layer 자체에 잎 사진, 꽃 사진, 열매 사진 attribute를 추가하고 이를 identify attached photos와 연결하여 바로 식별이 가능하게 할 것"** ("For survey type 2, instead of storing photos added per-Observation separately in observation_photo, add leaf/flower/fruit photo attributes directly to the observation layer itself, like inventory_observation in survey type 1, and connect this to 'identify attached photos' so identification can happen immediately").

  **Two follow-up clarifications, reported by the orchestrator as the stakeholder's own confirmed, explicit answers — not inferred by this spec-writer round (no literal verbatim quote was supplied for either, unlike the primary instruction above; this is disclosed honestly, mirroring Decision Log D-53's own precedent for a relayed-but-not-literally-quoted confirmed decision):**
  - **Scope: both Type 2 and Type 3.** Despite the verbatim instruction naming only "조사유형 2," the stakeholder explicitly confirmed, when asked, that Type 3's `observation` table (which shares the identical `observation_photo` child-table pattern, per Section 8.3's own "same fields... as Type 2" cross-reference) receives the identical treatment.
  - **Cardinality: exactly matches Type 1's `inventory_observation`.** `observation_photo` (Decision Log D-23's "zero or more related `observation_photo` records" rule, DR-QPB-031/DR-QPB-042) is **removed entirely** for Type 2/3's `observation` table — replaced by exactly three optional, nullable, relation-free photo-path fields (`leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path`), mirroring DR-QPB-020's Type-1 design precisely, **not** kept alongside the new fields for additional/multiple photos.

  **Confirmed technical facts from direct code reading, cited as ground truth:**
  - `qfield_builder/schemas.py`'s `_build_temporary_plots()`/`_build_permanent_plots()` confirm `observation_photo` is used **only** by Type 2/3's `observation` table; Type 3's own `plot_photo` (a separate table, holding photos of the permanent `plot` itself, not of an individual `observation`) is a structurally distinct table, unaffected by this change.
  - `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `IDENTIFICATION_TARGET_LAYERS = ("inventory_observation", "observation")` already treats Type 2/3's `observation` table generically by name, regardless of survey type — so a single schema change to the shared `observation` table-building logic naturally covers both Type 2 and Type 3 at once, matching the confirmed scope above with no extra per-type branching needed.
  - `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`'s `_identification_photo_paths_expression()` currently branches explicitly: `table.name == "inventory_observation"` reads its three inline photo-path columns directly; every other table (i.e., today, only `observation`) instead reads via a `relation_aggregate()` expression over the stable relation ID `rel_observation_photo_observation`. This is the exact mechanism the stakeholder's instruction asks to be replaced.
  - `qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `render_identification_widget_qml()`/`qpbCurrentPhotoPaths()` treat the resulting `photo_paths_expression` as an opaque, pre-built string, and already submit every photo to Pl@ntNet with a hardcoded `organs` value of `"auto"` regardless of source table — confirming this change requires **no** change to the embedded QML itself, only to the expression-construction function above.
  - `qfield_builder/korean_field_aliases.py`'s `FIELD_ALIASES_BY_TABLE["inventory_observation"]` already carries the confirmed Korean aliases for `leaf_photo_path`/`flower_photo_path`/`fruit_photo_path` (잎 사진/꽃 사진/열매 사진, Decision Log D-56–D-58) — since Type 2/3's new fields reuse the identical column names, no new Korean-terminology decision is required; only `FIELD_ALIASES_BY_TABLE["observation"]` needs the same three entries added.
  - `organ` (the column DR-QPB-032 governs) exists, in this codebase's own schema, **only** on `observation_photo` — no other table anywhere has an `organ` column, confirmed by inspection of `qfield_builder/schemas.py`. Removing `observation_photo` for Type 2/3 therefore makes DR-QPB-032 moot everywhere it previously applied, not merely for Type 2/3.

  **Resolution.** New DR-QPB-074–077 (Section 8.2) state the replacement schema/behavior in full; Section 8.2/8.3's `observation` field-list prose and "Photo tables" bullet lists are revised (original text retained, struck through, marked superseded, not deleted); DR-QPB-031/032/033/042 are each struck through and annotated superseded/moot, not deleted or renumbered; Section 8.5's Type 2 `observation` alias table gains three new, High-confidence rows (reusing Type 1's already-confirmed aliases verbatim) and its `observation_photo` rows (Type 2 table and Type 3's cross-reference row) are annotated as removed/moot, not deleted. AC-QPB-009 is narrowed (struck through and annotated, not deleted) to remove its now-inapplicable `observation`-photo-record clause; new AC-QPB-112/113/114 (Sections 18.1/18.6) make the replacement independently testable.

  **Migration/backward-compatibility for an already-generated Type 2/3 project using the old `observation_photo` schema is explicitly not resolved by this entry** — see new Open Question O-37, which records that this specification has no existing precedent for this class of question (checked; the closest analogue, Open Question O-11, addresses a different, still-open migration question for VWorld layer-name spelling and does not resolve this one either).

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file. The actual code changes to `qfield_builder/schemas.py`, `qfield_builder/gpkg.py`, `qfield_builder/qgis_worker.py`, and `qfield_builder/korean_field_aliases.py` are `test-designer`/`implementer` work for a future round, now unblocked by this clarified/revised specification — they are not performed by this spec-writer round.

Open Question O-37 (migration/backward-compatibility) remains open and unresolved.

This entry's own text above is left completely unchanged and remains the accurate historical record of what was known and open when it was written; it is annotated, not reworded or deleted, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-8/D-13/D-57). - **D-75** (Category C — a stakeholder-directed workflow/UX change to the site-input wizard step and drawing canvas, not a geometry-schema change; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-74 above):

  **The stakeholder's verbatim instruction**, given during real-device/UI testing: **"Type 2, 3에서 site를 그려서 추가할 때, multipolygon을 추가할 수 있도록 변경. 각 폴리곤별로 사이트 이름을 수동 지정 가능하게 할 것"** ("When drawing and adding a site in Type 2/3, change it so that a MultiPolygon can be added. Make it possible to manually specify a site name for each polygon").

  **One follow-up clarification, reported by the orchestrator as the stakeholder's own confirmed, explicit answer — not inferred by this spec-writer round (no literal verbatim quote was supplied, disclosed honestly, mirroring Decision Log D-53's/D-74's own precedent above):** this is **not** a change to `site`'s own geometry column type — `site_geom` stays a single Polygon/MultiPolygon column exactly as DR-QPB-008 already states, unchanged. It is a **workflow/UX change**: the user wants to draw **multiple, separate polygons in one drawing session**, with each drawn polygon becoming its **own separate `site` GeoPackage record**, individually named by the user — not one `site` record with a multi-part `MultiPolygon` geometry, and not one shared name applied to all of them.

  **Confirmed technical facts from direct code reading, cited as ground truth:**
  - `qfield_builder/build.py`'s `_resolve_seed_sites()`/`build_project()` **already** accept `config["sites"]` as a **list** of `{"site_name": ..., "geom_wkt": ...}` dicts, validating each entry's geometry individually in a loop and raising a per-site-named error on failure — this is exactly the target end-state data model, and it requires **no backend/build-pipeline change whatsoever**: it is precisely how `_resolve_sites_from_upload()` (the existing GeoPackage/Shapefile upload path) already produces one `site` record per uploaded feature, each named from the user-mapped source attribute.
  - `qfield_builder/ui/map_canvas.py`'s `MapCanvas` currently supports drawing **exactly one** polygon at a time: `self._vertices`/`self.last_polygon_wkt` are singular, and `polygon_drawn` emits one WKT string; calling `add_polygon_vertex_at()` again after `finish_polygon()` re-opens the *same* shape for further editing (per the function's own comment) — it does not start a second, independent shape. This confirms today's actual single-polygon-only drawing behavior, as this round was instructed to verify before asserting it needs to change.
  - `qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py`'s `SiteInputPage` currently has exactly one `draw_site_name_edit` field and one `_drawn_site_wkt` value; the wizard's config-collection step builds `config["sites"]` as a **single-element** list, `[{"site_name": site_input_page.drawn_site_name(), "geom_wkt": drawn_site_wkt}]` — confirming the wizard/canvas layer, not the backend, is the sole place this capability is actually missing.
  - `SiteInputPage.validatePage()` already treats drawing as optional ("Drawing is optional, same as upload -- not every type needs sites") — zero drawn sites is already an accepted outcome today; this precedent is preserved by this entry (zero, one, or many named polygons in one session are all valid).

  **Resolution.** New FR-QPB-129 (Section 6.3) requires: (1) the drawing canvas must support finishing a polygon, assigning/confirming that specific polygon's own individual name, and then either starting a new, separate polygon or ending the drawing session entirely — producing a **list** of zero or more independently named, finished polygons per session, never merging them into one `MultiPolygon` geometry; (2) `SiteInputPage`'s config-collection step must build `config["sites"]` as a list with one `{"site_name", "geom_wkt"}` entry per named polygon, reusing the exact, already-existing list contract `_resolve_seed_sites()`/`_resolve_sites_from_upload()` already implement — requiring **no** change to `qfield_builder/build.py` itself. Exact UI mechanics (e.g. the precise button/label text for "finish this shape and start a new one" vs. "finish drawing entirely," and the exact default-name-per-polygon fallback string) are deliberately left to the implementer, mirroring Decision Log D-27's own precedent that this specification states the underlying capability and data-model behavior, not exact UI copy. New AC-QPB-115/116 (Sections 18.1/18.5) make this independently testable.

  **Scope, explicitly limited to what the stakeholder's instruction and its confirmed clarification state.** The verbatim instruction names only survey types 2 and 3; Type 4 (`vegetation_mapping`) also has a `site` layer and reaches this exact same `SiteInputPage`/`MapCanvas` mechanism (Section 8.4), but was not named by the stakeholder's instruction, and no follow-up clarification addressed it either. This specification does **not** decide, either way, whether Type 4's site-drawing step also receives this capability — see new Open Question O-38.

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file. The actual code changes to `qfield_builder/ui/map_canvas.py` and `qfield_builder/ui/wizard.py` are `test-designer`/`implementer` work for a future round, now unblocked by this clarified specification — they are not performed by this spec-writer round.

  **Approval status: DECIDED (2026-08-28)** for Types 2/3, as described above — traces directly to the stakeholder's own quoted instruction and confirmed follow-up answer. Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against FR-QPB-129/AC-QPB-115/116 once this specification revision itself has been reviewed and approved by the user, per this project's standard spec-approval gate. Open Question O-38 (Type 4 scope) remains open and must be resolved before any implementation decides Type 4's own behavior one way or the other.

  **Forward-pointing note (2026-08-28; Decision Log D-79):** Open Question O-38 has since been put to the stakeholder directly and explicitly answered — "Yes apply to Type 4 as well." FR-QPB-129/AC-QPB-115/AC-QPB-116's scope is now Types 2, 3, and 4. This entry's own text above is left completely unchanged and remains the accurate historical record of what was known and open when it was written; it is annotated, not reworded or deleted, per this project's non-destructive Decision Log convention (mirroring D-8/D-13/D-57). See new Decision Log D-79, immediately below.

The four entries below (D-76–D-79) are dated 2026-08-28 and record the stakeholder's explicit, final decisions on the four items Decision Log D-72–D-75 raised or left partially open. Each is independently classified per this project's own change-control discipline, mirroring the reasoning already recorded for D-72–D-75 themselves. None reopens, rewords, or renumbers D-1–D-75 above.

- **D-76** (Category C — a stakeholder-approved network-boundary change superseding one specific clause of FR-QPB-011(d)/NFR-QPB-080 (Decision Log D-65); resolves Open Question O-35/Decision Log D-72's own disclosed four-option investigation; mirrors Decision Log D-24's own precedent for how an OSM-style network-boundary exception is disclosed and scoped; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-75 above):

  **The stakeholder's explicit, final answer**, given a menu of exactly the four options Decision Log D-72 disclosed: **option (b) — live per-result SVG fetch during search** (e.g. fetching previews for the currently-visible/top-N filtered matches as the user types, debounced).

  **What this decides.** Decision Log D-72 itself already stated what choosing option (b) requires, and this entry adopts that requirement in full: superseding FR-QPB-011(d)/NFR-QPB-080's already-approved "never authorizes any live search/autocomplete network request" text, and reintroducing an always-online dependency for the Step 6 search-preview experience specifically — a feature Decision Log D-65 had specifically designed to stay usable offline until the moment of final selection. That underlying offline-until-selection design is **not** abandoned by this entry; it is narrowed, in the specific, scoped way described below, not discarded — offline search-by-name and offline selection remain fully required (see the graceful-degradation safeguards added to NFR-QPB-080 below and new AC-QPB-117).

  **What changes.** FR-QPB-011(d) (Section 5.4) is revised in place: its existing "this clause never authorizes any live search/autocomplete network request against any Tabler endpoint; searching the bundled icon-name index is always offline" sentence is struck through, not deleted, and annotated as superseded by this entry for the narrow live-preview-fetch case specifically — the underlying client-side name-filtering/search mechanism itself remains entirely offline and unchanged. A new, second permitted network-fetch trigger is added within clause (d) itself (not a new clause letter, so the existing "clauses (a)–(d) above are exhaustive" closing sentence remains accurate): fetching preview SVG content, live, for the currently visible/matched results of an in-progress search only — never an unbounded background prefetch of the entire ~5,130-name bundled index, and never for a result not currently rendered on screen. NFR-QPB-080 (Section 5.4) is further revised, adding new clauses (5)–(8), directly mirroring NFR-QPB-060's own OSM-carve-out safeguards as this specification's established structural template for every network-boundary exception it has ever granted: a compliant, identifying `User-Agent` header on every preview-fetch request (extending, not duplicating, the identical obligation clause (1) already imposes on the selection-fetch request — confirmed already present in the existing Tabler SVG-fetch-on-selection code, per Decision Log D-65); debouncing so a preview fetch does not fire on every keystroke; bounded, reasonable concurrency rather than one unbounded simultaneous request per visible result; and — critically — graceful degradation: search-by-name and the ability to select an icon by name must remain fully functional with zero network access at all times, and a missing/failed preview must simply show no image (or a name-only/placeholder row) for that one result, never block search, never block selection, and never crash. New AC-QPB-117 (Section 18.2) makes this graceful-degradation half of the decision independently testable; AC-QPB-101 (Section 18.2) is annotated, not altered in substance, to note that the fetch-on-selection mechanism it already describes is now one of two independently permitted fetch triggers, the other being this entry's new live-preview-fetch trigger.

  **What this does not change.** The final SVG fetch-on-selection mechanism FR-QPB-121/AC-QPB-101 already describe — a single fetch, triggered only once the user has actually selected an icon by name, embedded into the generated project's own output folder at a project-relative path — is completely unaffected by this entry and remains exactly as Decision Log D-65 approved it; this entry adds an *additional*, narrower permission for a preview-during-search fetch, it does not replace, alter, or duplicate the selection-fetch mechanism. The offline, build-time-bundled icon-name index and its client-side substring/prefix name-filtering (FR-QPB-121) are unaffected and remain fully offline. NFR-QPB-080's existing clauses (1), (2), and (4) are unaffected in substance (clause (3) remains removed per Decision Log D-65 — MIT license, no attribution required). No other requirement outside FR-QPB-011(d)/NFR-QPB-080/AC-QPB-101/new AC-QPB-117 is touched by this entry.

  This entry does not modify any test file or application source file. The actual code changes (a debounced, bounded-concurrency preview-fetch mechanism in the Step 6 search-results UI) are `test-designer`/`implementer` work for a future round, now unblocked by this specification revision — they are not performed by this spec-writer round.

  **Approval status: DECIDED (2026-08-28)** — traces directly to the stakeholder's own explicit choice among Decision Log D-72's four disclosed options. Per this project's change-control discipline, `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against FR-QPB-011(d) (further revised)/NFR-QPB-080 (further revised)/AC-QPB-101 (annotated)/AC-QPB-117 (new) once this specification revision itself has been reviewed and approved by the user, per this project's standard spec-approval gate. Open Question O-35 is **CLOSED** (Section 20).

  - `rel_plot_photo_plot` → **고정조사구 사진** (confirmed as proposed).
  - `rel_community_survey` → **군락** (confirmed as proposed).

For the one corrected row (`rel_observation_survey`), the originally proposed term "관찰" itself is struck through, not deleted, and replaced with the stakeholder-confirmed **식물관찰**, likewise marked **Confirmed** — mirroring Decision Log D-58's own precedent for how a stakeholder correction of a specific proposed term (as distinct from a plain confirmation) is recorded in place.   **What this does not change.** This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-76 above.
