- **D-81** (Category C — a stakeholder-directed product/branding rename, with a confirmed, directly-resolved consequential side effect; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-80 above):

  **The stakeholder's explicit, direct instruction:** "앱 이름을 QFieldKit으로 수정" ("Change the app name to QFieldKit").

  **A real, confirmed consequential side effect, already identified by the orchestrator and already put to the stakeholder for a direct answer:** this application's own display name, "QField Project Builder," is currently also the name of its own encrypted-credential-storage directory (NFR-QPB-018 (revised)/NFR-QPB-072 (revised), Decision Log D-53: `~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/` on macOS; `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\` on Windows). Renaming the application would silently orphan any already-remembered VWorld/Pl@ntNet key on a machine that already has one stored, unless migrated. **The stakeholder's explicit, confirmed answer: migrate automatically** — on first launch after the rename, the application must detect the old-named folder (if present) and migrate its contents (the encrypted `credentials.enc` file and its accompanying salt) into the new, ~~`QFieldKit`~~-named **`FieldBuild Kit`-named (corrected by Decision Log D-86)** folder, preserving any already-remembered key(s), rather than silently losing them or requiring the user to notice and move the folder manually.

  **What this confirms/changes.** New FR-QPB-131 (Section 5.1) states the application-rename decision itself: the application's own display name is now ~~"QFieldKit,"~~ **"FieldBuild Kit," (corrected by Decision Log D-86; see that entry for the correction)** superseding "QField Project Builder" as the name shown in this application's own UI, the README, and the packaging configuration's own bundle name. Locating and updating every remaining literal occurrence of the prior name is left as `test-designer`/`implementer` discovery work, not itemized file-by-file here. NFR-QPB-018 (further revised; Decision Log D-53's own directory-name text retained, struck through, marked superseded) and NFR-QPB-072 (further revised, same treatment) now name the new directory: macOS ~~`~/Library/Application Support/QFieldKit/`~~ **`~/Library/Application Support/FieldBuild Kit/` (corrected by Decision Log D-86)**; Windows ~~`%APPDATA%\QFieldKit\`~~ **`%APPDATA%\FieldBuild Kit\` (corrected by Decision Log D-86)** — the `credentials.enc` filename itself, the encryption mechanism, and the consent-gated "Remember this key" opt-in behavior are all otherwise completely unchanged. New NFR-QPB-081 (Section 14.1) states the required one-time migration behavior in detail. **The spec-writer's own reasoned judgment, stated explicitly, on what this migration does and does not do (mirroring this document's own precedent, e.g. Decision Log D-50's `FileUtils.deleteFiles()`-unreliability finding, for disclosing exactly what a mechanism does and does not do):** the old directory is left in place, untouched, after a successful migration — it is never deleted by this mechanism, a deliberate, conservative choice given this project's own documented history of an implementer incident that deleted a real user directory outside this application's own generated-project scope (the QGIS-profile-deletion incident recorded in `.claude/agents/implementer.md`, referenced in `CLAUDE.md`'s "Current status"); an automatic, unconditional deletion of a user's own Application-Support/AppData folder carries a real, avoidable risk for a small, one-time convenience gain. If both the old and the new directories already exist and each already has its own `credentials.enc` file (an odd, but possible, upgrade scenario), the new directory's own, already-present `credentials.enc` is treated as authoritative and is never overwritten or merged with the old directory's contents; the old directory is, again, left completely untouched. New AC-QPB-119–AC-QPB-121 (Section 18.5) make the fresh-install, populated-upgrade, and both-already-exist scenarios each independently testable.

  **What this does not change.** This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-80 above. It does not alter the consent-gated "Remember this key" opt-in behavior, the KDF/cipher choice, or the first-launch password-setup requirement (NFR-QPB-073, Decision Log D-53/D-55) in any way — only the directory's own name changes, plus the new one-time migration step. It does not touch the generated QField project's own, separately governed key-embedding exceptions (FR-QPB-073/FR-QPB-076–FR-QPB-079, FR-QPB-114–FR-QPB-117), which have nothing to do with this application's own local storage directory. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective.

- **D-83** (Category C — a stakeholder-directed feature addition, with confirmed technical grounding for part of its mechanism and one honestly disclosed, not-yet-confirmed technical question for the rest; does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-82 above):

  **The stakeholder's explicit, direct instruction:** "Develop a QField plugin that adds an 'Export HTML Report' button within QField. The report must be generated as a standalone HTML file."

  **Confirmed technical facts, from the orchestrator's own live research (cited in full):** QField's own official plugin API (`https://qfield.org/blog/2024/06/18/supercharge-your-fieldwork-with-qfields-project-and-app-wide-plugins/`, `https://api.qfield.org/`, `https://docs.qfield.org/reference/plugins/`) confirms `iface.addItemToPluginsToolbar(item)` adds a custom button to QField's own main toolbar, declarable directly inside the same, already-generated `<project_slug>.qml` plugin file this application already produces (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`) — confirmed, by direct code reading of this exact codebase, to already implement the identification write-back `Timer`-polling mechanism (Decision Log D-50/D-51) and to already register a toolbar button of its own via this exact API (`render_project_plugin_qml`'s existing "Identify attached photos" reminder button, `qpbToolbarButton`) — no separate/new plugin file or architecture is required. The button's `onClicked` handler can write an arbitrary file to the local filesystem via `FileUtils.writeFileContent(path, content)` — already a real, confirmed, in-use mechanism in this exact codebase (the identification widget's pending-request-file write-back, Decision Log D-50, and the photo-resize temporary-file mechanism, Decision Log D-52). Together, these two confirmed facts establish this feature is technically feasible using this application's own already-established architecture, with the same rigor as Decision Log D-46/D-50's own confirmed-mechanism findings, not an untested assumption.

  **Not yet confirmed by this research, disclosed honestly rather than asserted:** the exact QML/JS mechanism for constructing the actual HTML content from the project's GeoPackage data. Reading GeoPackage records from within the QML/JS execution context — as opposed to Python/PyQGIS, which this specification's own desktop build-time pipeline uses freely — is a different environment with different available APIs; whether QField's own QML environment can query the local GeoPackage's actual attribute data at the enumeration breadth a full "actual collected records" report needs (as opposed to the narrower, already-confirmed `expression.evaluate()`/`get_feature()`/`relation_aggregate()` precedent this codebase already uses for a single, currently-open feature's own attribute values, throughout the identification/KTSN-lookup features) needs its own implementer-verification pass. This is not asserted as definitely straightforward — it is flagged honestly as the next open technical question, mirroring FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-36's own "plausible, not confirmed" pattern, and recorded as new Open Question O-41.

  **Confirmed stakeholder decisions on scope, already obtained directly (not inferred):** **Report content — both required:** a project/schema summary (survey type; site/plot/observation counts; basic project metadata) **and** the actual collected field data (the real attribute values entered so far — site/plot/observation records — rendered as a readable HTML table). Photos and post-MVP identification-subsystem results (Pl@ntNet/KTSN data) were explicitly **not** selected for this round — noted as a possible future extension, not specified as required now. **Trigger and output — on-demand, saved to the project folder:** tapping the button generates the HTML file immediately, from whatever data currently exists in the project's GeoPackage at that moment, and saves it inside the project folder itself (so it travels with the project on transfer back to desktop) — not QField's own share sheet, and not any other destination.

  **What this confirms/changes.** New Section 13.10 houses this feature. New FR-QPB-133 states the button's location/label, its data scope (both required categories; photos/identification data explicitly out of scope for this round), its on-demand-only trigger, and its project-relative output location. New FR-QPB-134 states the confirmed toolbar/file-write technical grounding and honestly discloses the one open technical question above, without resolving it. New AC-QPB-123–AC-QPB-126 (Section 18.6) make what can be specified concretely now independently testable: the button exists and is reachable from the toolbar; the generated file is valid, well-formed, standalone HTML requiring no external network/resource to view; it is saved at a project-relative location; and it reflects the project's current data at generation time (the last of these a manual-QA-only placeholder, pending the disclosed feasibility question). New Open Question O-40 (whether the `<project_slug>.qml` sidecar's own generation trigger — currently gated behind `identification_enabled`, FR-QPB-090/FR-QPB-100 — must now be broadened so this independent report feature is available even when identification is disabled, since this feature does not itself depend on the identification subsystem any more than Section 13.9's lookup-table feature does) and new Open Question O-41 (the GeoPackage-read-from-QML feasibility question itself, and what this report's own required scope becomes — schema-summary-only, or a different technical approach entirely — if full record-level reading proves infeasible) are both left open, not decided here, mirroring FR-QPB-111/Decision Log D-36's own precedent for disclosing a genuinely unresolved technical/scope question without inventing an answer to fill the gap.

  **What this does not change.** This entry does not reopen, reword, or renumber D-1–D-82 above. It does not alter Section 13.9's own confirmed, independent-of-`identification_enabled` scope for the lookup-table-autocomplete feature (Decision Log D-68) — this entry raises a structurally similar trigger-scope question for a different feature (O-40); it does not answer it by analogy. It does not allege that any implementation currently in `qfield_builder/` or any test currently in `tests/` is defective — this is a genuinely new feature, not a fix.

FR-QPB-134's disclosed GeoPackage-read-from-QML technical question, and the plugin-generation-trigger-scope question ~~(Open Questions O-40/O-41), remain open and require implementer-verification and/or a further stakeholder decision, respectively,~~ — **the plugin-generation-trigger-scope question (former Open Question O-40) is now CLOSED, per the stakeholder's explicit "Yes" (Decision Log D-85): the `<project_slug>.qml` sidecar's own generation trigger is broadened to fire whenever either `identification_enabled = true` or this report feature is present/enabled. Accepted fields must be copied from the final terminal `정명` row, never an intermediate row. New AC-QPB-128 covers a multi-hop `이명`/`원기재명` chain and preserves NIBR disambiguation at intermediate hops. New AC-QPB-129 defines deterministic termination for cycles, missing or malformed data, invalid candidates, and a maximum of 64 `correct_list` transitions; these cases retain the direct match and mark accepted-name data unavailable/ambiguous rather than looping, guessing, or returning a non-`정명` row.

These facts identify two contracts that conflict with the later stakeholder instructions; they do not authorize a broader relaxation.

  **What this changes.** FR-QPB-136, E-QPB-018, and AC-QPB-135 are revised in place, with their D-91 text retained struck through. Present `Survey data` and `Basemap` layers, and present non-lookup `Reference` layers, remain visible/checked by default. The one registered `occurrence_probability_multiband` multiband raster remains in the project and available for lookup, but is default-hidden and excluded from the ordinary visible-layer assertion/validation. New FR-QPB-137 and AC-QPB-136 require an explicit supported offline VWorld layer selection and make the selected identity flow consistently through tile retrieval, MBTiles metadata, and the generated project's offline source record; missing, blank, stale, or unsupported selection fails before retrieval/promotion, with no implicit default. New A-QPB-008 fixes the exception's narrow identity and records that valid offline acceptance fixtures must carry an explicit supported selection.

  **Compatibility and boundaries.** This does not hide any ordinary user-facing layer: all present survey layers, basemap layers, accepted-name tables, uploaded reference/extent layers, and other non-lookup reference layers retain D-91's visible-by-default behavior. It does not alter layer-tree grouping or basemap stacking order (FR-QPB-055/AC-QPB-110), a user's deliberate post-open saved visibility choice, the offline no-key-delivery rule (FR-QPB-078/NFR-QPB-058), VWorld supported-layer discovery (FR-QPB-071), or online consent-gated key embedding. It adds no migration requirement for already-generated projects. Any later request to hide another reference layer requires its own explicit decision; a `Reference` group, raster data type, or test convenience alone is insufficient.

  **Acceptance/traceability status.** The existing D-90/D-91/D-93 acceptance test and its traceability currently assert that every present reference node is visible and construct successful offline scenarios without an explicit layer, relying on a test-harness compatibility default. Both assertions are superseded by this candidate specification only as described above. After explicit stakeholder approval, a fresh `test-designer` must revise that acceptance test and traceability so it asserts the registered lookup raster is hidden while every ordinary layer remains visible, and so every valid offline configuration includes an explicit currently supported VWorld layer. This spec-writer round modifies no test file or application source.

  **Approval status: APPROVED by the user on 2026-09-03.** `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against D-94.

- **D-95** (Category C — user-directed canonical-reference migration and report-enrichment change; approved by the user 2026-09-03):

  **Verified current-source context.** The repository currently contains three relevant reference inputs: the legacy 191 MB `tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv` (53 columns), the legacy 2025 national-list workbook, and `Rpt_2026-08-29_List.xlsx` (973,891 bytes). The latter has one `Data Sheet`, 23 columns, a two-row header, and 8,042 data rows. Its row-1/source columns are `No`, `관리분류군`, `정이명여부`, `학명`, `대표국명`, `명명자`, `명명년도`, `Phylum`, `Class`, `Order`, `Family`, `Genus`, `콘텐츠 여부`, `URL`; row 2 supplies each rank's `Name`/`국명` sublabels. The current fixture contains 4,673 `정명` and 3,369 `이명` rows, with `No = '-'` on synonyms and exact NIBR species-detail URLs. The existing implementation instead hard-codes the legacy CSV and `2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx`/`62,604종`, derives `correct_list`-based accepted names, and exposes only the old three-column accepted lookup. D-95 explicitly resolves this source/schema conflict rather than treating those observed code paths as the new contract.

  **Decision.** For new Type 1–3 builds, `Rpt_2026-08-29_List.xlsx` is the sole canonical source and the workbook's `관속식물류` scope, `정이명여부` status, accepted-before-synonym grouping, URL-derived KTSN, preserved raw `학명`, exact authority-stripping algorithm, canonical schema, provenance, candidate-preview/upload workflow, and fail-closed behavior are normative in DR-QPB-079/081 and Section 13.3a. The old CSV/old workbook and `correct_list` recursion are not fallback inputs. The accepted-name lookup remains only as a compatibility projection, while the new `ktsn_taxonomy_reference` layer is the source of truth. The distributed application includes the canonical workbook as a non-secret candidate; generated projects include only materialized tables/provenance, never the raw workbook.

  **Integration impact.** FR-QPB-140 adds the read-only `식물 분류 참조표` layer alongside `인정 국명 조회표`. FR-QPB-142 preserves existing survey fields and UUID relations while making synonym matching resolve to accepted KTSN and retaining authority-bearing raw scientific text for write-back. FR-QPB-141 extends the unconditional HTML report with accepted-row Phylum/Class/Order/Family/Genus aggregation, with no join multiplication and explicit missing/legacy limitations. Existing generated projects remain readable and are not migrated; old source-based acceptance clauses are historical and require replacement test coverage after approval. NFR-QPB-083 keeps the workbook local and prevents secrets or raw field/reference content from entering logs, reports, or external requests.

  **Trade-offs and unresolved items.** Preserving the raw `학명` and storing a second comparison key increases table width but protects auditability and prevents authority loss. The workbook has no official dataset version, so hash/schema/pipeline identity is used until O-43 is resolved. Exact report visual presentation remains O-44. No code, test, or Git file is changed by this specification-only round.

  **Approval status: APPROVED by the user on 2026-09-03.** `test-designer`/`implementer` work may proceed against D-95.

- **D-97 (APPROVED; 2026-09-04; Category B — iPhone-QField result-verification and toolbar-asset clarification):** New user evidence from iPhone QField exposed two omissions in otherwise approved outcomes: an online project selected as VWorld `Satellite` with a valid key showed a layer-load failure accompanied by a QField missing/repair warning; and the plugin toolbar showed blank icon targets alongside duplicate controls. The intended user behavior is unchanged — the selected online layer must work in QField, and the existing report-export/plant-identification actions must remain compact icon-only toolbar actions. This is therefore a clarification of required observable results and their verification, not a new map provider, an additional toolbar feature, a changed action callback, or a new credential exception. D-96 is already allocated by a separate post-D-95 artifact, so this entry uses the new stable identifier D-97 rather than reusing it.

  **What this clarifies.** FR-QPB-072 is supplemented so a valid-key, consent-accepted online `Satellite` selection must actually render in QField on iPhone without a missing/repair warning; structural URI/XML inspection and offline checks are expressly insufficient by themselves. New FR-QPB-143 replaces only the toolbar icons' reliance on QField `Theme` identifiers with self-contained project-local SVG assets: `icons/report-export.svg` always, and `icons/plant-identification.svg` only when identification is enabled. The existing project-plugin convention (`<project_slug>.qml` beside the `.qgs`), Korean accessible names, action callbacks, feature-form identification control, identification-content condition, and all VWorld/Pl@ntNet consent and key-storage boundaries remain unchanged. In an identification-enabled project, the active plugin toolbar has exactly two 48px icon-only `QfToolButton` controls, each registered once; in an identification-disabled project, only the unconditional report-export control remains, consistent with the pre-existing D-87/FR-QPB-100 boundary.

  **Acceptance and platform boundary.** New AC-QPB-146, AC-QPB-147, and AC-QPB-148 require both structural asset/registration coverage and recorded iPhone QField visual/manual evidence. No local test runner emulates QField iOS, so a URI assertion or QML/source inspection cannot by itself pass either iPhone-visible result. The device record may identify app/project build, QField/iOS version, selected layer, and pass/fail observations, but must not record VWorld or Pl@ntNet key values.

  **Approval status: APPROVED by the user on 2026-09-04.** A fresh `test-designer` must add acceptance coverage and traceability for AC-QPB-146–148 before any implementation work proceeds. This clarification changes no application source or test file.

This closes the "has a real key ever been supplied" portion of this question, but the substantive portion — verifying the exact authentication scheme, endpoint base URL, rate-limit/quota behavior, and response schema against Pl@ntNet's real API — is now unblocked implementer/test-designer work, not something this entry itself certifies as done. **Open, narrowed — blocks FR-QPB-104 implementation only until that live verification work is actually carried out.**
  - **O-14** — **CLOSED** (Decision Log D-37): that live verification has now actually been performed, not merely unblocked. A `test-designer` round, while building acceptance tests for Section 13's guaranteed-manual baseline, actually called the real Pl@ntNet API on 2026-08-15 using the real key already stored locally in `QPB_TEST_PLANTNET_API_KEY` (a gitignored `.env` value, never written to any tracked file), per `tests/acceptance/qfield_project_builder/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`'s "Post-MVP: Section 13" section (functions 7 and 8, and function 8's "Live-verification note"). This confirms, against the real API rather than the Requirements Draft's summary: the real endpoint is `https://my-api.plantnet.org/v2/identify/{project}` (POST, multipart form body, one `organs` field and one `images` file per photo) — `https://my.plantnet.org/...`, the domain the Requirements Draft's own citation implied, returns HTTP 404 and must not be used; authentication is the `api-key` **query parameter** (not an `Authorization` header); `nb-results` is also a query parameter, and `nb-results=3` is confirmed to return exactly three results; the success envelope's confirmed keys are `query`, `predictedOrgans`, `language`, `preferedReferential`, `bestMatch`, `results`, `version`, `remainingIdentificationRequests`, with each `results[*]` entry confirming the `species.scientificNameWithoutAuthor`/`scientificNameAuthorship`/`scientificName` field paths FR-QPB-104 relies on, plus `genus`/`family`/`commonNames`, already returned in descending-`score` order by the real API itself; the confirmed auth-failure envelope is HTTP `401` with JSON body `{"statusCode": 401, "error": "Unauthorized", "message": "Bad token", "attributes": {"error": "Bad token"}}`. See Decision Log D-37 for the full record, quoted verbatim from the source note, and for why this is recorded as a confirmed technical fact from live verification rather than a stakeholder product decision. FR-QPB-104 (Section 13.2) is revised accordingly, with the original text retained, struck through, and marked superseded/corrected, not deleted.

  - **Interaction check (2026-08-15; Decision Log D-36) — substance unaffected, recorded for traceability, not a closure:** Decision Log D-36 (which puts in-field, on-device probability-raster sampling in scope, closing O-18 below) does not change this question's substance. D-36 only decides *where the bundled data is used* (on-device vs. desktop-side), not *whether it is present* on the device, so the size/transfer risk this question raises is exactly the same size as before. O-17 remains open, unchanged, on its own terms.
  - **Interaction check (2026-08-16; Decision Log D-41) — non-issue assessed, recorded for traceability, not a closure:** Decision Log D-41 (new FR-QPB-113) adds one more small reference-data artifact — a lookup list containing only the extracted `KTSN` column (a single column of identifier values) from the `62,604종` sheet's 62,604 data rows — bundled into every identification-enabled generated project alongside the existing ~247 MB KTSN-CSV/raster bundle (Decision Log D-35/FR-QPB-112). Because this new artifact is a single column of plain identifier values, not the full 31-column, 62,604-row source xlsx, it is expected to be well under 1 MB as plain text (e.g. a several-digit numeric KTSN value per line across ~62,604 lines is on the order of tens to a few hundred kilobytes, not megabytes) — negligible next to both the existing ~247 MB bundle and DR-QPB-060's 900 MiB–1 GiB `.mbtiles` range. This specification records this assessment explicitly, rather than leaving the new artifact's size unaddressed, and concludes it does not materially change the size/transfer risk this question already describes. O-17 remains open, unchanged, on its own terms; this annotation does not close it, since O-17's underlying ~247 MB-plus-`.mbtiles` risk is unaffected by this small addition.

The item below (O-34) is new, raised by a `test-designer` round while writing acceptance tests for the just-approved Decision Log D-64–D-69/FR-QPB-124–127 (2026-08-27). It does not derive from a stakeholder decision; it records a genuine environment-dependency gap that round found and explicitly reported, rather than silently resolved, following this specification's own existing discipline (mirroring O-19's origin from Decision Log D-39/D-40, and O-20's origin from D-50/D-51) against silently inventing an answer to a gap a downstream role surfaces. Per the orchestrator's own explicit instruction for this round, it is raised and closed within this same round, rather than left open pending a later round.

- **O-34** (new; test-designer finding while writing acceptance tests for Decision Log D-64–D-69/FR-QPB-124–127, not a stakeholder decision): New FR-QPB-127 (Decision Log D-68) makes the accepted-name lookup table's build-time derivation (FR-QPB-126) — and therefore FR-QPB-105's reused raw-source-CSV-presence/required-column fail-early validation — run **unconditionally** for every Types 1–3 build, independent of `identification_enabled`. FR-QPB-126's derivation reuses FR-QPB-118's existing row-filtering pipeline, which reads the **raw** KTSN reference CSV (`storage/reference/tables/tb_leco_nib_ktsn_dtl_gat.csv`, ~183 MB) and the NIBR xlsx directly, not a precomputed/cached file. That raw source data is excluded from version control (`.gitignore`'s "Runtime data under `storage/`..." entry) and was, before this entry, never confirmed by this specification as an expected-present operational precondition for *every* Types 1–3 build (as opposed to only identification-enabled ones, or only the distributed packaged application's own bundle, which Decision Log D-44 already covers separately). This suite's own pre-existing, shared `make_base_config()`/`built_project_by_type()`/`isolated_project_by_type()` fixtures (used by dozens of already-approved MVP acceptance tests) default to `identification_enabled = false` and supply no reference-data override at all — meaning that, once FR-QPB-127 is implemented, every one of those pre-existing tests would begin failing FR-QPB-105's early-failure validation on any machine lacking the real `storage/reference/` scaffold, purely as a side effect of implementing FR-QPB-127. **Open — blocks nothing already approved in substance; blocks only confirming whether the raw reference-data scaffold's presence is an accepted operational precondition for every Types 1–3 build, and this suite's own shared-fixture housekeeping that follows from the answer.**
  - **O-34** — **CLOSED** (Decision Log D-70): the stakeholder, presented with three disclosed options (bundle the raw data into the repository/package itself; allow a Types 1–3 build to gracefully degrade when the raw data is absent, relaxing FR-QPB-127's own text; or treat this as an accepted, already-established operational precondition mirroring Decision Log D-44's existing precedent), gave the explicit, verbatim answer: **"Use Option (c)."** This confirms, rather than relaxes, FR-QPB-127's own "must always run and always be bundled" requirement: every environment that builds a Types 1–3 project — development, CI, or the distributed packaged application — is expected to have the raw reference-data scaffold (`storage/reference/`) present, exactly as Decision Log D-44 already established for the distributed, packaged application specifically. FR-QPB-105 (Section 13.3) is revised accordingly to state its now-dual trigger condition explicitly; FR-QPB-112 (Section 13.3) receives a purely additive clarifying cross-reference; new AC-QPB-109 (Section 18.2) makes the new trigger condition independently testable. This suite's own shared-fixture-default housekeeping (`conftest.py`) that Option (c) itself calls for is explicitly deferred to a future `test-designer`/`implementer` round, not performed or prescribed here. See Decision Log D-70.

| *(sixteenth reconciliation, 2026-08-22 through 2026-08-23, further confirmed technical history from continued crash investigation plus four Category C stakeholder decisions directing a complete, four-step targeted fix, not from the Requirements Draft; this single reconciliation round's own Decision Log D-48 draft was extended in place twice, before ever being shown to the stakeholder for approval, to reach the complete four-step form recorded here — no D-49 was created for either extension)* | Origin: Decision Log D-47's build-time 5-column extraction did not resolve the on-device crash — it recurred 100% reproducibly at the same point — nor did two further, independent runtime-optimization rounds (indexed O(1) lookups; then offset-based scanning eliminating per-line-substring array retention, which also fixed a secondary quadratic-time scanner bug). Given this history, the stakeholder directed (relayed by the orchestrator, not quoted verbatim in this entry for most steps' underlying rationale) a four-step, ordered row-filtering pipeline before the existing 5-column extraction runs, since Pl@ntNet (this feature's identification source, FR-QPB-104) only ever returns plant species names at species rank or below, while the underlying reference dataset spans every kingdom of life at every taxonomic rank, includes non-vascular-plant taxa the stakeholder does not need, and contains duplicate scientific names with conflicting `ktsn` values. **Step 1** (Plantae-kingdom subtree filter): rows that are transitive descendants of `ktsn=120000098391` via the `p_ktsn` parent-pointer chain, computed once at build time — orchestrator-verified: 32,251 of 212,397 raw rows (~15.2%) survive, with a rank breakdown (21,584 Species; 4,406 Genus; 3,655 Variety; 1,018 Form; 653 Family; 397 Subspecies; 183 Order; 129 Subfamily; smaller counts elsewhere) and a phylum breakdown (Magnoliophyta 22,779; Bryophyta 2,164; Pteridophyta 1,923; Charophyta 1,914; Chlorophyta 1,874; Marchantiophyta 951; Pinophyta 296; Filicophyta 290; Anthocerophyta 22; Glaucophyta 6; Lycopodiophyta 14; Psilophyta 4; Sphenophyta 4) both confirming taxonomic sanity; the Plantae root row (`120000098391`) itself does not appear in this table, so the filter is descendant-only. **Step 2** (species-level-and-below rank filter): keeps only rows whose `rank_id >= 700` (species/subspecies/variety/etc., per the orchestrator-verified rank-code table), excluding a row with a missing/non-numeric `rank_id` rather than guess-including it — orchestrator-verified: 26,763 of Step 1's 32,251 rows survive. **Step 3** (vascular-plants-only phylum-allowlist filter, new in this reconciliation's second extension of the same D-48 draft): per the stakeholder's explicit, verbatim instruction — **"filter out 선태류 [bryophytes]. I only need vascular plants"** — and a follow-up explicit choice, between two disclosed options, to also exclude this dataset's algae-related phyla classified under Plantae (`Charophyta`/`Chlorophyta`/`Glaucophyta`) in addition to the three bryophyte phyla (`Bryophyta`/`Marchantiophyta`/`Anthocerophyta`), which the stakeholder explicitly chose (the broader, stricter option), keeps only rows whose `r200_nm` phylum-lineage field is one of exactly seven vascular-plant phyla (`Magnoliophyta`, `Pteridophyta`, `Pinophyta`, `Filicophyta`, `Lycopodiophyta`, `Psilophyta`, `Sphenophyta`), excluding a row with a missing/blank `r200_nm` value rather than guess-including it — orchestrator-verified: 21,025 of Step 2's 26,763 rows survive. **Step 4** (duplicate-scientific-name canonical-KTSN resolution, renumbered from this reconciliation's first-extension "Step 3," rule unchanged, counts recomputed over the narrower Step-3 output): for the 58 distinct normalized `taxon_full_nm` values (118 rows) that remain duplicated after Steps 1–3 — down from the first extension's 106 names/215 rows, since narrowing to vascular-plants-only in Step 3 already removed many bryophyte-genus duplicates before duplicate resolution even runs — cross-references each against the same NIBR xlsx already bundled for Decision Log D-40/D-41 (`storage/reference/tables/2025년 국가생물종목록_v1.0.xlsx`) but its **`관속식물류`** sheet's **`학명`** column this time — keeping the one row whose `ktsn` is corroborated there (7 of 58 names resolved this way — the same 7 as before) and dropping every row for a name whose lookup is inconclusive (51 of 58 names, 104 rows, dropped entirely) — per the stakeholder's own explicit, directly-confirmed choice of the drop-entirely fallback (over keeping the runtime's existing tie-break) and of scoping the lookup to `관속식물류` only (declining to also check the `선태류` bryophyte sheet); orchestrator-verified combined result: 20,914 rows survive all four steps (~9.8% of the raw 212,397, roughly a 10x reduction), superseding the first extension's 26,555-row figure everywhere it appeared. §13.3 FR-QPB-118 (further revised; Decision Log D-47/this entry's own two-step and four-step prior forms, all retained, struck through, marked superseded) now requires all four ordered row-filtering steps before the existing, unchanged column-extraction step (now Step 5); FR-QPB-112 (revised; Decision Log D-47) reviewed and confirmed unaffected — its 5-column-selection/bundling requirement remains exactly as D-47 left it. §18.6 AC-QPB-083 and AC-QPB-071 (each further revised; Decision Log D-47/this entry's own original and three-step-pipeline forms, all retained, struck through, marked superseded) now assert the full four-step pipeline's row count and the final 20,914-row combined result; AC-QPB-084 (unchanged in substance, now explicitly scoped as "Step 1 of 5") and AC-QPB-085 (unchanged in substance and row count) remain the independently testable Step 1/Step 2 assertions; new AC-QPB-087 (Step 3's 21,025-row result and a synthetic multi-phylum-fixture assertion that only the seven allowlisted phyla survive) and further-revised AC-QPB-086 (renumbered from "Step 3" to "Step 4," now asserting the 20,914-row combined result over the narrower 58-name/118-row duplicate set, plus the same two synthetic-fixture assertions as before). §19 Decision Log new/extended D-48 (records the continued-crash history as a confirmed technical finding, distinct from the stakeholder's four Category C directives, and the disclosed four-part behavior-change tradeoff — only rows surviving all of Steps 1–4 are now eligible for on-device matching at all). FR-QPB-105/FR-QPB-106/FR-QPB-113/Decision Log D-40/D-41/D-44 reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance — FR-QPB-113/D-40/D-41's own NIBR extraction continues to read only the `62,604종` sheet for its own distinct, runtime `correct_list`-resolution purpose, unrelated to Step 4's build-time use of the `관속식물류` sheet from the same already-bundled workbook. Neither D-1–D-47 nor any other existing FR/DR/NFR/AC is reopened, reworded in substance, or renumbered by this reconciliation, beyond the explicitly marked, struck-through supersessions (FR-QPB-118's, AC-QPB-083's, and AC-QPB-071's predecessor forms). |

Investigation confirmed two things: (1) the `exif()` mechanism this project's QML relies on (`qpbReadExifTag`/`qpbReadPhotoGps`, FR-QPB-108) works correctly, verified via this project's sanctioned QGIS-isolation probe (`scripts/qgis_isolated_probe.py`) against a synthetic GPS-tagged JPEG; and (2) QField's own iOS attachment-saving step strips GPS EXIF metadata before this project's code ever reads the file, confirmed via a matching public report (QField GitHub discussion #4246), reproducible across all three photo-acquisition methods tested there, including the camera-roll-picker method the stakeholder used — reported (not independently verified by this project) not to reproduce on Android. This project's own `qpbReadPhotoGps`/`qpbReadExifTag` implementation has no defect. Presented with two disclosed options (document as a known limitation with no code change, vs. build a manual-GPS-entry fallback), the stakeholder's explicit choice: document as a known limitation only, no code change. §13.6 FR-QPB-108 (further revised; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded — adds the disclosed QField-iOS platform-limitation caveat; the sampling/NoData/validation logic itself is unchanged and restated), §18.6 AC-QPB-044 (further revised; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded — adds the same disclosed qualification to its GPS-transform assertion), §19 Decision Log new D-49. | *(eighteenth reconciliation, 2026-08-23, confirmed technical findings from real-device testing plus direct QGIS/QField source-code inspection, and one Category C stakeholder decision on how to respond, not from the Requirements Draft)* | Origin: FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-43) required persistence for both a real candidate selection and a manual identification entry, but relied on an unconfirmed, best-effort `currentFeature.setAttribute(...)`-style write-back mechanism (the same class of uncertainty Decision Log D-36 records for on-device raster sampling). Real-device testing (QField 4.2.4) confirmed that mechanism never works. Direct QGIS-core source inspection (`QgsQmlWidgetWrapper`, the "QML Widget" attribute-editor's own wrapper class) confirmed this is structurally impossible, on any platform or QField version — the class exposes only a read-only `expression`/`evaluate()` context property, never a feature object or setter. Further source inspection and repeated real-device verification confirmed a different, narrower mechanism — a pending-request file (`FileUtils.writeFileContent()`) polled by the already-shipped project plugin (`<project_slug>.qml`, FR-QPB-100) on a short-interval `Timer`, matching the current feature's UUID and calling `changeAttribute()` on `overlayFeatureFormDrawer.featureForm.model` — works end-to-end for real candidate selection, but only for a brand-new, not-yet-saved feature created via QField's "Add feature" flow; the same was confirmed structurally impossible for an existing, already-saved feature reopened later, because `FeatureListForm.qml` never exposes its internal per-feature `AttributeFormModel` outside itself (cross-checked against the complete `objectName` list of QField's main application QML). Presented with both confirmed findings, the stakeholder's decision: ship the confirmed-working mechanism as a real, permanent feature for the brand-new/not-yet-saved-feature, real-candidate-selection case; keep the existing "not saved" fallback message as a confirmed, permanent limitation for the existing/already-saved-feature case (covering both candidate selection and manual entry, since the underlying structural limitation is independent of which attribute value is being written). §13.7 FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-43 text retained, struck through, marked superseded), §18.6 AC-QPB-046 (further revised; Decision Log D-43 text retained, struck through, marked superseded; restructured into two independently testable branches (a)/(b) by feature save-state), §19 Decision Log new D-50, §20 new Open Question O-20 (whether/how this new mechanism extends to the manual-identification-entry path for a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature specifically, not resolved by this entry, since the current implementation routes manual entry through the identical write-back function this entry addresses for candidate selection but the stakeholder's instruction was framed around candidate selection). AC-QPB-078 reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance. Neither D-1–D-49 nor any other existing FR/DR/NFR/AC is reopened, reworded in substance, or renumbered by this reconciliation, beyond the two explicitly marked, struck-through supersessions (FR-QPB-109's and AC-QPB-046's predecessor forms). **Extended in place (2026-08-23, same round; no separate nineteenth-reconciliation row created, since this closes an open question the round itself raised) to close Open Question O-20:** the orchestrator asked the stakeholder directly whether this same confirmed mechanism should also govern manual identification entry (not just real candidate selection) on a brand-new/not-yet-saved feature; the stakeholder's explicit answer: **"Yes, extend it to manual entry too."** §13.7 FR-QPB-109 (further revised; Decision Log D-50's own brand-new/not-yet-saved-feature branch text retained, its prior scope-limiting closing sentence struck through, marked superseded) extended to require the identical mechanism for manual identification entry, persisted per the existing, unchanged Decision Log D-38/D-43 `identification_status = "manual"` rule; §18.6 AC-QPB-046 (further revised; Decision Log D-50's own branch-(a) text retained, its prior scope-limiting closing sentence struck through, marked superseded) extended to assert both the real-candidate-selection and manual-identification-entry scenarios, each verifiable only via real-device manual QA; §19 Decision Log new D-51; §20 O-20 marked CLOSED (a new sub-bullet appended after its existing open-question text; original O-20 text left completely unchanged). AC-QPB-078 reviewed again and confirmed unaffected in substance. |
| *(nineteenth reconciliation, 2026-08-25, a confirmed real-device HTTP 413 finding plus confirmed technical facts from Pl@ntNet's own documentation and direct QField v4.2.4 source inspection, and one Category C stakeholder confirmation of a single parameter, closing a Category B specification omission, not from the Requirements Draft)* | Origin: real-device testing reported an HTTP `413 Request Entity Too Large` response from Pl@ntNet when uploading a 6 MB photo for identification. Investigation confirmed the current implementation (`qfield_builder/qml_plugin.py`'s `qpbRunIdentification`) submits each attached photo's raw, unmodified bytes (read via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.readFileContent()`) to Pl@ntNet with no resize, compression, or size-limiting step anywhere in the path — a genuine specification omission never anticipated by FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104 at any prior revision. Pl@ntNet's own public documentation (`my.plantnet.org/doc/getting-started/faq`) confirms server-side resizing to a maximum of 1280 pixels on the long side and recommends clients submit at approximately that size/~90% JPEG quality, while stating no exact byte-size limit (recorded honestly as not found, not invented). QField's own native, confirmed `FileUtils.restrictImageSize(imagePath, maximumWidthHeight)` method (real QField v4.2.4 C++ source, `src/core/utils/fileutils.h`) resizes a file in place with no output-path parameter, so it must run only against a temporary copy — written via the already-confirmed `FileUtils.writeFileContent()`, resized via `restrictImageSize()`, read back via `FileUtils.readFileContent()`, and cleaned up via an empty-content `FileUtils.writeFileContent(tempPath, "")` overwrite per the existing Decision Log D-50 `FileUtils.deleteFiles()`-unreliability finding — never mutating the original, full-resolution attachment file. Presented with Pl@ntNet's own documented 1280-pixel target as the self-evidently non-wasteful choice, the stakeholder's explicit confirmation: **1280 pixels** on the long side. §13.1 FR-QPB-101 (post-MVP; further revised; Decision Log D-46 text retained, struck through, marked superseded) revised to require the resize-via-temporary-copy step between reading and submitting each photo's bytes, with the original attachment file required to remain completely unmodified and full-resolution; §13.2 FR-QPB-104 receives a new cross-reference note only, no duplicated substance; §18.6 new AC-QPB-088 (structurally testable against the generated project's embedded identification widget QML, no real device required) and AC-QPB-040 reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance; §19 Decision Log new D-52. Neither D-1–D-51 nor any other existing FR/DR/NFR/AC is reopened, reworded in substance, or renumbered by this reconciliation, beyond the one explicitly marked, struck-through supersession (FR-QPB-101's predecessor form). |
| *(twentieth reconciliation, 2026-08-25, one Category C stakeholder-directed change to this application's own desktop credential-storage mechanism, not from the Requirements Draft; does not touch the generated QField project's own, separately governed key-embedding exceptions)* | Origin: this application is distributed unsigned (Decision Log D-25 packaging context), so macOS ties Keychain access grants to a specific code signature an unsigned/ad-hoc-signed rebuild does not reliably preserve — a real, confirmed `keyring`/macOS-Keychain behavior, not a guess — causing the OS Keychain permission prompt to potentially reappear on every rebuild/relaunch; the orchestrator confirmed directly with the stakeholder this is the actual motivating annoyance. The stakeholder's confirmed three-part decision (reported by the orchestrator, not reproduced here as a literal verbatim quote — flagged explicitly, since this differs from every other Category C entry in this log): (1) stop using the OS credential store (`keyring`) for this application's own key storage entirely; (2) replace it with application-managed, locally-encrypted-file storage for the existing "Remember this key" opt-in, whose consent-gated behavior itself is unchanged; (3) prompt for an encryption-deriving password once, at first launch (or whenever none yet exists) — not a general access-gate over the rest of the application — with an honest forgotten-password consequence (previously remembered keys become permanently unrecoverable, no recovery mechanism invented) and a graceful decline-path fallback (session-only retention, reusing the existing non-remembered case). §14.1 NFR-QPB-012/NFR-QPB-018/NFR-QPB-072 (each revised; original text retained, struck through, marked superseded) now require an application-managed encrypted file (`credentials.enc`, a newly introduced application-data-directory convention: macOS `~/Library/Application Support/QField Project Builder/`; Windows `%APPDATA%\QField Project Builder\`), encrypted via a `cryptography.fernet.Fernet` key derived by PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (≥600,000 iterations, ≥16-byte random salt) — a named, concrete, non-custom KDF/cipher choice, reasoned about explicitly in Decision Log D-53; new NFR-QPB-073 states the first-launch prompt, decline-path, and forgotten-password requirements; NFR-QPB-017/NFR-QPB-019/NFR-QPB-071 reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance (brief cross-reference annotations only, no textual alteration to their rules). §18.5 AC-QPB-058 (revised) and §18.6 AC-QPB-082 (revised) (each original text retained, struck through, marked superseded), plus new §18.5 AC-QPB-089–AC-QPB-093 (no-`keyring`-in-path, not-plaintext-on-disk, named-KDF-parameters, first-launch-prompt/decline, forgotten-password), make this independently testable. §16 new A-QPB-005 (records the application-data-directory convention as newly introduced, not pre-existing) and new A-QPB-006 (records the retrieval-time password-re-prompt UX as an assumption, not a stakeholder-confirmed decision). §19 Decision Log new D-53 (a mixed entry: confirmed technical background, the three-part Category C decision, and an honestly disclosed security trade-off — moving from a well-vetted, OS-hardened, and on macOS potentially hardware-backed credential store to an application-managed encryption-at-rest scheme is a real, non-trivial trade-off, not a strictly-more-secure replacement, mirroring Decision Log D-46's own disclosed-trade-off pattern). §20 new Open Question O-21 (the exact retrieval-time password-re-prompt UX, not resolved by the stakeholder's own confirmed instruction, does not block the core requirements above). Neither D-1–D-52 nor any other existing FR/DR/NFR/AC is reopened, reworded in substance, or renumbered by this reconciliation, beyond the explicitly marked, struck-through supersessions (NFR-QPB-012's, NFR-QPB-018's, NFR-QPB-072's, AC-QPB-058's, and AC-QPB-082's predecessor forms). This entry does not allege a conformance defect in `qfield_builder/credential_store.py` or any test; updating that implementation and its tests to match is `implementer`/`test-designer` work following this specification revision, not performed by this entry itself. |
| *(twenty-first reconciliation, 2026-08-25, one Category C stakeholder-directed feature addition, informed by the orchestrator's own confirmed research into Pl@ntNet's public API documentation, not from the Requirements Draft)* | Origin: the stakeholder asked the orchestrator to investigate whether a representative reference image could be shown alongside each of the three candidates the embedded "Identify attached photos" `QML Widget` already displays (FR-QPB-101/FR-QPB-104/FR-QPB-109). The orchestrator's research confirmed Pl@ntNet's identify endpoint accepts a documented `include-related-images=true` query parameter, returning, per Pl@ntNet's own documentation, "a list of most-similar images for each probable species," each carrying `organ`/`author`/`license`/`date`/`citation` fields and a `url` object with `o`/`m`/`s` size-variant URLs, licensed CC BY-SA with a documented attribution requirement, verbatim, **"Photo(s): [Contributor Username] / Pl@ntNet, CC BY-SA,"** and confirmed QML's native `Image` element can load such a URL directly via its `source` property. Presented with this confirmed feasibility, the stakeholder directed proceeding with the feature. §13.2 FR-QPB-104 (further revised; Decision Log D-37 text retained, struck through, marked superseded) adds `include-related-images=true` to the request's query parameters; §13.7 FR-QPB-109 receives a new, purely additive bullet (Decision Log D-38/D-43/D-50/D-51's persistence-mechanism substance unchanged and not reopened) requiring each candidate card to display one representative image, using the small (`s`) size variant for bandwidth-consciousness (consistent with Decision Log D-52's photo-resize precedent), together with the required CC BY-SA attribution whenever an image is displayed, and graceful degradation (no placeholder, no attribution text, other card content unaffected) when no image is available for a candidate, with an image-load failure after the initial response never blocking or corrupting the rest of the card's content. §18.6 new AC-QPB-094 (outgoing request-shape assertion), AC-QPB-095 (structural QML-source inspection of the per-candidate `Image` element/attribution-text construction and graceful degradation, mirroring the AC-QPB-046/AC-QPB-088 structural-inspection pattern), and AC-QPB-096 (manual-QA-only placeholder for actual on-device/on-screen image rendering and post-response image-load-failure resilience, mirroring the existing Decision Log D-36/AC-QPB-072 convention); AC-QPB-040 reviewed and confirmed unaffected in substance. §19 Decision Log new D-54. No DR/schema change required (ephemeral display of API-response image URLs only, no persisted GeoPackage attribute).
